call_details.description:
Target amount: The workers have to complete the target amount 32 baskets.
Only people who have been there 7-10 years can complete it. In some lines, shrimp distribution is fair. Sometimes, if there are many people at shrimp peeling line, your supervisor will ask you to go and help another line (arranging shrimp) which have less worker, but when you go to another line, supervisor from another line will ask you: what are you doing here? And when you cannot say anything and go back to your original work station, other supervisor will found you are going around in the room without working then you got scolded again. There are 13 supervisors, so that the worker could not know which supervisor they are interacting with. 
Water flow system: Actually, you can turn on the water to flow automatically but the supervisor do not allow you to let the water flow all the time, so that you have to use one hand to press water and another hand to hold the shrimp. You also need to take care the shrimp not to fall. The room was very cold and the water is also very cold so that most of the worker cannot work there. If the worker shirt gets wet, they are not allowing to change it.
Working hour and Shift schedule: The working time still unstable and the worker have to stand by anytime they are calling if the shrimp arrived. Sometimes, the worker doesn’t have enough rest period especially, on the day that they have extra cleaning duty (2.5 hours). Normally, if you don’t complete the target amount, you cannot work for OT. However, if it is on the cleaning day, you don’t want to work OT because it will be too late, but you cannot refuse it because the cleaning to be done after the shift (8 hours + OT + 2.5 hours cleaning). In the next day, if you have to work on early shift, it is hard for the worker. Sometimes, if the line run out of shrimp/raw materials, the workers have to take meal break just after started working in 1 hour then take a meal break 1 hour and continue another 7 hours without break. So the worker got hungry and it is very hard to work in a very cold room 7 hours consecutively. The workers prefer a fixed work schedule if it is day or night. When the work schedule is changing every day, they could not manage their sleeping time and eating time so that it will affect their health. The roommates are also working in a different schedule so that you cannot have a proper rest in the housing, other people will cook and shower while you are sleeping and there is not quiet time within 24 hours. There are about 8-12 people in a room. The factory gives the reason that the working hour have to manage based on the arrival of shrimp: the workers feel that the factory does not value the human as much as they value the shrimp.  
No rights to refuse OT: It was very cold so that some of the workers don’t want to do OT but they cannot refuse it.
Dormitory: For female (single)dormitory, there is no enough bath room, no enough electric plug to cook. The worker were told that they cannot take shower more than 5 mins. Some bathroom and toilet lock are broken so that you cannot close the door. In some bed room the fan is broken but cannot ask for replacement. They complain it but nothing improved. The mattress are very old and there are bugs in it so the worker request to move it away but they were told that they cannot remove it because it will be a problem if the visitor found it. 
Electric cost: There is no clear system for electric bill. The worker got deduct the bills less if they earned less wages, and they got deduct more if they earn more.
Health care and sick leave: In order to take a sick leave, you need approval from factory clinic nurse, it is not easy. Sometimes, they will tell you to come back again for signature. It is not easy for the workers to find them again and again since the worker have to run from work. Sometimes, the worker got sick and go to see the nurse: if there is no interpreter at the nurse room, you have to wait for a long hour. The workers could not identify which nurse has bad behavior. They thought that all nurses behavior are the same. 
If you take sick leave and went to the hospital and come back with the medical certificate, you got pay only for a half day. The workers are told that they can still work for a half day.

The workers have to complete the target amount 320 coins in 8 working hours. Many workers cannot complete it. If the workers cannot complete the target, they have to sign warning at the Pujakan’s office, and they were told that they will be sent back to Myanmar. Building 3 Pujakan is good but Building 4 Pujakan is bad. 
They count the target amount in coins (arranging shrimp), it is not fair. However, if there are a lot of people in the line, you cannot get enough shrimp so you have to rush for getting shrimp. Sometime, there is no coins included in the shrimp basket, and when you complain about it , supervisor will scold the workers. When they collect the basket and record your target: if you say, I have done 3 baskets without coins, they will not record it as you said. They record whatever they want. The supervisor said they do not have enough coins at the moment, they will have it enough after April then, if the worker could not complete the target amount, they will be sent back Myanmar. 
The working time still unstable and the worker have to stand by anytime they are calling if the shrimp arrived. When the work schedule is changing every day, they could not manage their sleeping time and eating time so that it will affect their health. The roommates are also working in a different schedule so that you cannot have a proper rest in the housing, other people will cook and shower while you are sleeping and there is not quiet time within 24 hours.
The dormitory of building number 5 is new and good maintenance since visitor can see very often. Electric plug for cooking is not enough but since workers have different shift, they can manage rotation for cooking. The interpreter in nurse room shouted the workers. If you take sick leave without medical certificate, you cannot get daily wage. 
For the annual bonus, you will be able to get it only if do not take any single leave.

Unfair start-finish working hour calculation, the worker have to get ready and enter to the production line earlier, new restriction of fine for dropping shrimp or if the damaged/unqualified shrimp  1 shrim/2baht to be duducted, grievance mechanism is not properly handle the issue raised.

Misunderstanding of the nature of the work of raw material allocation

remediation_results: Issara is closing this case because the business has communicated to the workers that for those adversely affected by the night shift with the late start hour, they can make a request to change to the day shift.

The workers updated that the business did not make the official announcement regarding the workers' right to refuse OT since this is their right. No one can refuse OT through the supervisors now. The OT and leave requests are handled by the line manager from Building 2. When the workers want to refuse OT, they have to directly reach out to the manager. 

The manager asked so many questions, why did the worker refuse OT? Even if the worker has some family member's health issue, the supervisors ask, "Why do you need to send your mom to the hospital? call_details.description: The worker went to check the noticeboard in the morning of July 5 and did not see any announcement regarding the OT policy. When ANT shows the photo that the business sent to the worker, she said the current notice board is full of different announcements but she does not see the notice related to OT policy. She said she really wants to take a photo and prove it to us, but she does not dare take photos since there is CCTV nearby.

The worker updated that the OT announcement regarding refusing OT was posted on the small notice board on July 14, 2022. The interpreter asked the workers whether they could refuse OT or not. 

On July 16, 2022, the female translator made the verbal announcement regarding refusing OT in the production line. The workers were informed that they could refuse OT by informing the manager, and if they could not refuse, they were asked to come to the HR office directly.

The manager of the shrimp peeling line in building 2 has verbal and physical abuse issues. She can speak Burmese and yell out to the workers, "Don't you have a brain to think? Why don't you understand if I tell you?" While she is yelling out to the workers, she uses her hand to point them out, touching their heads and pushing their shoulders. In July, a female worker got an eye injury because the manager's finger attacked her eye. The worker was told, "If you are not satisfied, go report to the office." The manager did not say sorry for her fault.

The female worker feels insecure about raising the issue and reporting it to the HR office, even though the interpreter came to investigate. However, the other workers called Issara and raised the issue because this line manager's behavior is unacceptable for the whole production line.

This line manager sometimes does not provide lunch on time after working a maximum of five hours. The workers have to work for over five hours before taking an hour's break.

The eight working hours are mostly until 4:00 p.m., but the manager asks the workers to work until 4:30 p.m. and sometimes until 4:45 p.m. The workers do not get overtime for those extra working hours.

In the past, workers could change the needles and knives at any time. Now the workers are asked to inform the supervisor if they would like to change the materials. If three or four workers requested new materials at the same time, the manager would shout and yell.

A few years ago, this manager had an issue with workers from Building 2, and she was moved to Building 3. She has a bad record, and the workers do not want to work with that manager anymore. The workers requested that Issara discuss this issue with the supplier and take serious action against her.

Context: Workers from building 2 have reported that they have to use secondhand gloves which makes it more difficult for workers to complete the work of peeling shrimp so their productivity is affected. 

Talking points:
-Ask the business what is their policy about PPE distribution and the usage of disposable gloves? Is it acceptable according to the company policy to re-utilize this kind of gloves? 


Recommendations:
-If the business says that reusing disposable gloves is against their policy, recommend the business to investigate how gloves are being distributed at building 2 to understand who is violating the company policy and why workers are not getting new gloves when needed. Based on the results of the investigation, the business should take disciplinary actions towards those not following the company policy. 
-If the business says that according to the policy it is acceptable to wash and reuse disposable gloves, explain to the company workers feedback and how they are being impacted by having to use secondhand gloves. Recommend the company to revise its PPE policy to make sure workers' productivity is not affected by not having the PPE needed.

(Feb 3,2021)

Added recommendations

To explain how and when they can get new gloves, who is in charge of providing the gloves, and what are the grievance mechanisms channels workers can use in case they have issues accessing PPE. 

The company should also explain to the person in charge of providing PPE that workers should be provided with new gloves whenever they need them (according to their policy, if the globes are not in good condition anymore).

closed_notes: This is being rated as “fair” because, for the latest Issue, the business has conducted an investigation and found the issue. Disciplinary actions towards the staff who broke the business policy were taken and the business remediated workers that reported this issue to HR.  For the previous two issues, there was no proper communication, investigation, or remediation. The actions taken by the business for the most recent case shows that the business is trying to improve the system. However, this will need to be monitored from time to time.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
#Issue 1. May - 2020.
-The business should provide enough personal protective equipment to employees ( apron, Gloves, and ears cover).  
-Initiate remediation process: assess workers impacted (those who had to buy extra materials with their own money); make payments within 2 pay periods. The remediation plan should be communicated to all workers.
-Business to do an immediate investigation to identify the root causes of the issue and who is not following the company policy and take disciplinary actions accordingly.

#Issue 2. 12-07-2020.
Context: The issue with a couple of Cambodian workers not receiving enough and adequate PPE (gloves) in their working line (Pay TN, line Patong) where the workers have to cut the fish belly, and the line supervisor not approving glove replacements forcing workers to tape up gloves with holes in them for re-use. ILM ID - 9945

-The business should provide enough personal protective equipment to employees (such as aprons, gloves, and ear covers), and replace them according to a set schedule rather than leaving it to the discretion of supervisors to approve replacements.  
-Business to conduct an immediate investigation to identify the root causes of the issue and who is not following the company policy and take disciplinary actions accordingly.

#Issue 3- (13-Oct).
Context; The line supervisor collecting 5THB per worker for PPE.
(Internal note: the calculation of the amount owed to workers is only based on the report on call 11427, however, other workers have reported having to buy PPE but we do not have the amount workers had paid so it isn't included below)


                                                                                     **TALKING POINTS**
# Issue 1 
-This issue is happening at the cat Food Line 2 ( Cafe 6& 7 Line literally). They get new apron and gloves every 2 months while other workers are receiving new materials every week. 
-Workers have been spending their own money to buy the PPE from the shop. 
-The line supervisor from this line only provides the PPE when they have the visitors. Remind the business that safeguards should be in place while the investigation and remediation are being conducted. 
-Workers have reported this issue to the line supervisor (green hat) but never got the assistance/remediation.

#Issue 2 
**Internal Note for BHR**
-Please be reminded that this issue was reported at the same time as the issue with a Cambodian worker being treated poorly by one male abusive supervisor. 
-Please start the talking point by saying that we have been receiving calls regarding the PPE issue from different lines quite frequently. 
-How does the business monitoring the condition of the protective equipment of workers to make sure that all workers have adequate PPE for their work? 
-Does the business have a system to replace the protective equipment on a regular basis, according to a set standard?  If so, how often is the protective equipment (in this case, gloves) replaced? 
-Workers from this specific line have also reported more recently receiving new gloves.  However, what has the business done to ensure that this situation doesn't happen again in the future?

#Issue 3- 
-Please share the issue in detail with the business. 
-Please provide Issara's feedback as follows: 
-The business has not taken Issara's recommendations for the system change yet.
-The business neither communicated with the line supervisors nor took remediation actions for the issue with money that the workers have to pay for the gloves and no disciplinary actions were taken towards the supervisors who were not strictly following the business policy.  
-In the previous meeting, the business said that they do not have a cooperative market in their factory, several workers confirmed having this marked and still being collected the money for the PPE. Please give the following information to the business 1) Schedule for opening the market. 2) PPE that is being sold is exactly the same as the business materials. 3)Share the information (line) of the workers and the supervisor who recently collected the money for PPE. 
4) Provide the price of each material as mentioned in the worker voice call.  Please share the business that workers only get PPE whenever they have visitors.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
#Issue 1.
The business only explained its policy regarding PPE, however, did not commit to taking action. It was added that the workers can reach out to HR if they have any issues with the PPE. 

9 June  2020; Workers from Catfood Cafe 6&7 got new aprons, gloves, and shoes on 1st June. (CLOSED). 

#issue 2. (30-Jul-2020) 
The business agreed to have a meeting with the production manager and distribute the PPE to the workers. 

24/08/2020. The worker updated that the business has provided the PPE as they have required and also the supervisor in this specific line is allowing the workers to access the PPE whenever is needed. (CLOSED)


#Issue 3. 13 Nov,20; 
The business conducted the investigation and found the issue. The staff who used to sell the PPE received the written warning and workers were distributed the PPE as required. For the reimbursement, the business announced the workers to reach out to the HR office for the remediation, however, only 3-4 workers have done so. The business added that some workers simply refused to be remediated. 

27-Nov; Workers confirmed receiving PPE as required and also confirmed the investigation taking place. Workes also added that they do not want their money back but the system to be improved.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The company should explain to all workers what are the disciplinary actions for those who do not follow the company policy.   

Communication.  
-Effectively communicate to workers (verbally and in written) the company policy on PPE, and contact information of focal points, actions that will be taken by the business for investigations and safeguarding, and timeframes. 
-The business to produce a clear set of visual standards and post on notice boards and announce verbally to ensure workers have clarity on the policy of PPE on when and how they should apply for kits replacement. 

-The business to revise the PPE distribution and tracking system to make sure all workers in the production lines receive the same standard amount of PPE and that they are regularly replaced. 

-Issara can also provide tailored training to full HR teams on-site, and provide systems review with tailored recommendations to eliminate labour risks.

closed_notes:
Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have communicated with all workers about the post-vaccination process. The business added that once a worker is vaccinated, she/he will get a check-up by the nurse to make sure the workers are safe to get back to work. In case the worker presents side effects during their work in the production, they have to reach out to the nurse so that the nurse can confirm their symptoms and provide a medical certificate. The business argued that the workers who made a report to Issara might have been the ones who did not reach out to the nurse according to the business protocol. Once again, the worker updated the missing payment even though he had followed the business protocol.

Issara provided the information of the worker to the business as requested and the worker  confirmed the reimbursement of (640 THB) for his sick leave days. However it was not clear from the business whether the business conducted an investigation to find if there were more impacted workers or not.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the COVID vaccinations side effect. A worker reported not receiving medical certificates from the in-house medical staff to be paid for sick leave when they have vaccine side effects and wanted to take rest. In addition to that, a worker who received the vaccine and had side effects also reported not receiving a daily wage for his sick leave days even though he has followed the business protocol in order to take sick leave. 

Recommendations: 
-The business shall communicate with all workers including medical staff about the potential side effects those receiving the vaccine might experience in the next few days after getting the shot. The communication should inform workers that those experiencing some side effect symptoms that would not enable them to work properly can take medical leave according to the business procedure of informing the focal person about their leave. 
-Workers who took sick leave and were being asked to present a medical certificate issued by the medical staff should be reimbursed and paid according to the sick leave section from LPA.

However, it is the business's responsibility to make sure that all workers are paid all of their wages upon their departure. Having a debt to pay to the workers after they leave their job is against the local law. Issara is checking with the workers if they want the business to process their missing payment since they are free from business control. remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: A group of 11 workers who have submitted resignation a week ago and were preparing to depart are not being allowed to go by the business. The workers reported that their belongings were taken by the business when they were about to leave in a van and that they now do not have a place to stay since they have already given back their rooms. Workers reported the reason for leaving job is as follows:
(1) discrimination against nationalities at the workplace,
(2) the business not keeping the promise of paying double for the working hours during COVID-19 restriction as promised,
(3) translator not being helpful and being biased by just listening to the business and not the workers. 

Recommendations: 
-As it is a worker's right to resign and leave the company, the business shall immediately investigate why this group of workers were not allowed to leave. And then come to an agreement with workers for their departure from the company without restrictions.
-Since the business made the taxi driver leave without the workers, it will be challenging for workers to find a new driver, therefore, the business is suggested to help workers find a new taxi/van for workers safe return. -Since the vaccination is a workers personal health matter, the business should provide vaccination cards or any support documents as proof that workers have received vaccination. If the business does not have such documents, the business should coordinate with the health organization that provided the vaccine to make sure all workers receive the vaccination card. 
-The business should immediately check with all workers and provide their missing daily wages if any. 


Talking Points: 
-What is the reason why this group of workers were stopped by HR? 
-Is business aware of this issue? 
-Workers have reported several workers leaving the job because of several repeated issues in the workplace, what is the business understanding of this? Does the business seek workers' feedback and have done anything to improve the working condition rather than stopping workers from leaving? 
- What was communicated to workers as reasons for not being allowed to leave the company?
-What was the reason for the business calling the police and threatening the workers? 

Added TPs; 
Because workers have resigned and are asking to depart, this situation should be addressed in less than the 3-4 day timeline suggested by SCC.
No resigned worker can be held against their will, or coerced into returning to work
Resigned workers can be provided vaccine certificates and COVID tests to ensure there are no positive cases before departure
Workers can be clearly offered a return to work, with no coercion, and with clear communication on next steps
Because this situation has escalated, Issara can jointly speak with HR and the group of workers if desired, to support communication.
Issara also recommends we provide training to HR reps at SCC, on COVID and other protocols for workforce management.

ETI Base Code 1.2. Employment is freely chosen; workers not required to lodge deposits or documents with employer, and free to leave with reasonable notice

Workers off-shift should be free to leave their workplace and dormitories, with no threats or assertions of control over their movements. Workers should never be treated as the property of employers, recruiters, brokers, or agents; and, their movements should never be restricted by these actors. Workers should be free to leave their jobs with reasonable notice.

remediation_action:
Issara reached out to the business immediately.  The business explained that HR had communicated to the workers about the government's travel restrictions to prevent the spread of Covid-19, and that they are not allowed to travel outside Songkhla province because it is currently a Covid-19 red zone.  They said police had come to enforce the travel restrictions and the van driver left without taking the workers after talking to the police.  Regarding vaccination certificates that would be important for when the workers travel back to Myanmar, the business said the document issuance was delayed by the hospital and would be provided to the workers when issued.  For now, the business said the workers are still living in the private dorm and the workers can ask the landlord to stay in the same place. 

The business will get back to Issara with corrective actions within 3-5 days.

The business further updated Issara saying pictures of HR staff with negative comments regarding this incident had been posted on social media and they wanted the workers to remove the posts.

TU explained that they didn't want the workers leaving the province illegally given the current Covid-19 restrictions.  The Sustainability Director said they would escalate the matter to the factory MD.  The following day, TU completed the process of issuing official separation documents for the workers so that they can leave.

Regarding the wages, the business noted that they could investigate what had happened with workers wages and compensate workers accordingly.
remediation_validation:
Issara followed up with the workers and provided an update, explaining that the business had said they were following government rules of not allowing inter-provincial travel and that the business would get to Issara in 3-5 days about next steps.  

The workers did not want to stay there anymore; they felt pressured and forced to go back to work.  They were even willing to pay any government fines if there were any for crossing province lines.  Since they have resigned, they don't understand why the business is not letting them leave.  They just want to be able to travel back to Myanmar. 

Regarding the social media posts, the workers said they did not take any photos or videos during the incident nor did they post anything on social media or ask their friends to do so.

The workers have confirmed that they have officially resigned from their jobs and are free to leave.

Regarding the wages, workers noted not wanting to wait for the business to conduct an investigation, as they wanted to leave as soon as possible without waiting for any compensation.

call_details.description:
Target amount: The workers have to complete the target amount 32 baskets.
Only people who have been there 7-10 years can complete it. In some lines, shrimp distribution is fair. Sometimes, if there are many people at shrimp peeling line, your supervisor will ask you to go and help another line (arranging shrimp) which have less worker, but when you go to another line, supervisor from another line will ask you: what are you doing here? And when you cannot say anything and go back to your original work station, other supervisor will found you are going around in the room without working then you got scolded again. There are 13 supervisors, so that the worker could not know which supervisor they are interacting with. 
Water flow system: Actually, you can turn on the water to flow automatically but the supervisor do not allow you to let the water flow all the time, so that you have to use one hand to press water and another hand to hold the shrimp. You also need to take care the shrimp not to fall. The room was very cold and the water is also very cold so that most of the worker cannot work there. If the worker shirt gets wet, they are not allowing to change it.
Working hour and Shift schedule: The working time still unstable and the worker have to stand by anytime they are calling if the shrimp arrived. Sometimes, the worker doesn’t have enough rest period especially, on the day that they have extra cleaning duty (2.5 hours). Normally, if you don’t complete the target amount, you cannot work for OT. However, if it is on the cleaning day, you don’t want to work OT because it will be too late, but you cannot refuse it because the cleaning to be done after the shift (8 hours + OT + 2.5 hours cleaning). In the next day, if you have to work on early shift, it is hard for the worker. Sometimes, if the line run out of shrimp/raw materials, the workers have to take meal break just after started working in 1 hour then take a meal break 1 hour and continue another 7 hours without break. So the worker got hungry and it is very hard to work in a very cold room 7 hours consecutively. The workers prefer a fixed work schedule if it is day or night. When the work schedule is changing every day, they could not manage their sleeping time and eating time so that it will affect their health. The roommates are also working in a different schedule so that you cannot have a proper rest in the housing, other people will cook and shower while you are sleeping and there is not quiet time within 24 hours. There are about 8-12 people in a room. The factory gives the reason that the working hour have to manage based on the arrival of shrimp: the workers feel that the factory does not value the human as much as they value the shrimp.  
No rights to refuse OT: It was very cold so that some of the workers don’t want to do OT but they cannot refuse it.
Dormitory: For female (single)dormitory, there is no enough bath room, no enough electric plug to cook. The worker were told that they cannot take shower more than 5 mins. Some bathroom and toilet lock are broken so that you cannot close the door. In some bed room the fan is broken but cannot ask for replacement. They complain it but nothing improved. The mattress are very old and there are bugs in it so the worker request to move it away but they were told that they cannot remove it because it will be a problem if the visitor found it. 
Electric cost: There is no clear system for electric bill. The worker got deduct the bills less if they earned less wages, and they got deduct more if they earn more.
Health care and sick leave: In order to take a sick leave, you need approval from factory clinic nurse, it is not easy. Sometimes, they will tell you to come back again for signature. It is not easy for the workers to find them again and again since the worker have to run from work. Sometimes, the worker got sick and go to see the nurse: if there is no interpreter at the nurse room, you have to wait for a long hour. The workers could not identify which nurse has bad behavior. They thought that all nurses behavior are the same. 
If you take sick leave and went to the hospital and come back with the medical certificate, you got pay only for a half day. The workers are told that they can still work for a half day.

The workers have to complete the target amount 320 coins in 8 working hours. Many workers cannot complete it. If the workers cannot complete the target, they have to sign warning at the Pujakan’s office, and they were told that they will be sent back to Myanmar. Building 3 Pujakan is good but Building 4 Pujakan is bad. 
They count the target amount in coins (arranging shrimp), it is not fair. However, if there are a lot of people in the line, you cannot get enough shrimp so you have to rush for getting shrimp. Sometime, there is no coins included in the shrimp basket, and when you complain about it , supervisor will scold the workers. When they collect the basket and record your target: if you say, I have done 3 baskets without coins, they will not record it as you said. They record whatever they want. The supervisor said they do not have enough coins at the moment, they will have it enough after April then, if the worker could not complete the target amount, they will be sent back Myanmar. 
The working time still unstable and the worker have to stand by anytime they are calling if the shrimp arrived. When the work schedule is changing every day, they could not manage their sleeping time and eating time so that it will affect their health. The roommates are also working in a different schedule so that you cannot have a proper rest in the housing, other people will cook and shower while you are sleeping and there is not quiet time within 24 hours.
The dormitory of building number 5 is new and good maintenance since visitor can see very often. Electric plug for cooking is not enough but since workers have different shift, they can manage rotation for cooking. The interpreter in nurse room shouted the workers. If you take sick leave without medical certificate, you cannot get daily wage. 
For the annual bonus, you will be able to get it only if do not take any single leave.

If the worker requests leave in advanced, the supervisor do not approve it. So, the worker just took it as they need it then supervisor will scold them. If worker takes leave many days, then ask to sign warning at the office. Building 2, supervisor is bad, you cannot refuse to do OT. If your clothes get wet and you are not allowed to change it. Shift schedule is keep changing and it was very cold in this building. The worker plan to resign if she cannot move back to original work line (boiling shrimp line). The worker moved to building 4 (shrimp peeling line) in November 2017 and was told that she will be able to move back to previous line after Songkran.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue # 1. 
Context: The issue with the covid-19 preventions concern. Community members around the factory reported their concern regarding the infected cases in Seafresh. The caller said that they have heard that there are around 10 infected workers in the Factory, however, there are no clear prevention measures to prevent the community from larger impact. 

Talking Points: 
-How many workers have been infected and what have been the prevention measures so far? 
-How have the business communicated with the workers the measures being taken to control the spread to larger groups of workers? 
-Have there been any communication and coordination with the local government to implement preventive measures? 

Recommendations: 
-The business shall make a clear communication to the workers verbally and in writing about the action that the business has been taking to control the spread of virus and the long term plan to control the spread to larger groups. 
-The business is also recommended to encourage workers to use the internal grievance mechanism and/or contact Issara if they have any questions and/or concerns about the prevention measures.

Issue # 2. 

Context: The issue with the workers being told that if they  have COVID symptoms they should go  to the internal clinic and have Pah Talajone for three days and have home quarantine for three days and get Pah Talajones for another three days if they do not get better. Workers reported the business not conducting the COVID-19 tests and having options to go to the hospital if they tested positive. 

Recommendation: 
The business shall provide the options to the workers to get a  COVID-19 test if they have any symptoms. If workers test positive, the company should follow the health officials recommendations depending on the severity of the symphons, such as  hospitalization or home quarantine, and also follow up tests according to the government procedure in Chumphon province. 
If there are workers at risk, meaning that they have been in contact with a positive case, then workers should be asked to stay in quarantine and then do a COVID test before returning back to home. This test shall be facilitated by the business.  

Talking Points: 
How many workers have been tested positive at the moment? 
What has been the process to control the spread and also the treatment for the positive workers. 
What has been the communication with the government in this regard? 
Are there any workers in the government or the factory quarantine center? 
What has been the ATK test process? 
Workers reported receiving the announcement about the internal treatment with Pah Talajone, what is the business understanding of this?

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Ms.Nyein Lae Maw,from TUF fish peeling line reported that she and her colleague, Sandar Cho were unfairly dismissed on 29th August 2023. On 28th August Ms Nyein and Ms. Sandar were assigned to work as a pair in fish peeling tasks. In the nature of fish peeling tasks, the pair (two workers) usually have to do deboning and removing blood. For the morning session (before lunch), Nyein finished 18 kilos while Sandar finished only 9 kilos. In the afternoon like 1pm the office called both of them and asked the reason for the unrealistic kilo difference. The workers explained that this is the very first time for them that much kilo difference but they didn't do it intentionally and they can balance their work done in the afternoon session but the business didn't accept their explanation and accused them that the worker did the job unethically and deceitfully. On 29th August, both of them were dismissed. In this matter the workers thought that they were unfairly dismissed because they have never got warning nor never sign any warning letter for this type of mistake.

TPs:
- Two workers were recently dismissed.  What is the reason for the dismissal?  Is it according to the company's disciplinary policy and were there fair grounds for immediate dismissal, since these workers had not received warnings in the past?

Recommendations:
- Investigate this issue, and establish the reasons for the dismissal.
- Explain clearly to the workers why the company took such actions, if indeed there were clear grounds for immediate dismissal
- If the reasons for dismissal are not sufficient to merit immediate dismissal, the company hire the workers back immediately
remediation_business_steps_taken: K. Varrorat, HR manager, responded that they were unaware of this issue. She requests more information, asking if Issara can provide a specific production line number because the fish peeling ling is a large area, as well as the impacted two workers' ID numbers. They will, however, investigate and respond with corrective action within 7 working days.
remediation_notes: Workers reported being dismissed for something that the business said was unethical but they couldn't understand exactly they had done wrong. In addition, they had not received any warnings previously so they don't understand what they could have done to deserve immediate dismissal.
remediation_action:
Issara raised this with the business, and the HR manager was unaware of this issue. She requested more information, such as the production line number because the fish peeling section is a large area, as well as the impacted two workers' ID numbers. They will, however, investigate and respond with corrective action within 7 working days.

In the latest update, the business noted that workers working in pairs have been instructed to report equal number of fish trays processed as this affects the worker's performance and related incentives. In this instance, one worker reported 6 trays while the other reported only 1 tray, because the worker reporting only 1 tray was away from work for many days and so wouldn't be getting much in terms of incentives. The business sees this as workers trying to manipulate the numbers fraudulently to increase one's incentive pay, which the business decided is a serious offense meriting immediate dismissal

In the country escalation, the business noted that it will re-investigate this case and reconsider the decision to dismiss the workers.  Based on the investigation, the company confirmed that there had been communication to workers in April 2023 (which the workers acknowledged and signed) that not equally sharing the number of trays completed would result in immediate dismissal, and checked with workers to make sure they understood this policy in September 2023, which they said they understood.  The business will not change its decision to dismiss these workers but will have additional communication sessions with workers about this policy so that workers are reminded that non-compliance can lead to immediate dismissal.
remediation_validation:
Workers provided an update that they had not heard about this policy of needing to have equal weights of fish trays before and heard that it was only announced recently. They also noted they were threatened to sign consent on the dismissal letter.

In a further update, the workers accepted the business decision because she had given her signature to signal acknowledgement of the policy.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue. The workers accept the business decision and noted that they had signed acknowledgement of the policy.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: Review the company's disciplinary policy, and review how this is communicated to all workers.  This should be communicated, verbally and in writing, on a regular basis to refresh workers on what actions on their part can lead to disciplinary actions and in some cases to dismissal.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
# Issue 1
Context: The issue with the unresponsive grievance mechanism, and workers being asked to raise their issues with their supervisors by HR staff.

#Issue 2

The issue with a Cambodian worker being abused by a Thai worker after having an overwhelming workload being sent to the only Cambodian worker. ID - 11261. 

-The business to conduct an investigation immediately. 

-During the investigation process, four parties (victim, Supervisor, suspect, and the witness) should be interviewed. Safeguard should ensure that all the interviews would be done confidentially. 

-The investigation should identify the root cause that led to the conflict, including the role of the supervisor and whether the supervisor was effectively monitoring that the workers were doing their job. 

-Appropriate disciplinary action should be taken based on the result of the investigation, to ensure that bullying and physical assaults between workers are prevented in the future. 

-The worker who was abused by her colleagues should be given options to change a new working line upon worker requests.

Time frame - 1 week.



Talking points : 

Please share with the business about the workers feedback as follow:
_Several workers reported that they do not feel transparent or safe to access the grievances, the reason is many of the workers already experienced poor response, being rejected, action not being taken and being threatened for using grievances mechanism. 

_Please ask the business how do their grievance mechanisms work? What are the processes and channels workers can use to provide feedback, file complaints, express their queries and concerns? 

-How do they handle the complaints including time frame and how many of the HR staff are responsible for the GM and provide the recommendations for the system change.
-Are there any policies on disciplinary actions for those who suppress workers from using grievance mechanisms?

#Issue 2

Please share the story detail with the business. 

Please ask the following questions to the business. 

- What is the business policy for such cases (Physical assault)?.
- What is the role of the supervisor in this line, and what has the business done to make sure that the workloads are being distributed fairly and managed fairly?

remediation_action: The business said that they would conduct an internal survey to assess the situation and be able to find out the root cause of the issue and the actions needed to respond to the issue of line supervisors’ behaviour. However, the business later got back to Issara by saying that they were not able to conduct the survey at the moment because of the third wave of COVID-19 issue, but that the company had simplified the process of taking annual leave and the sick leaves by workers getting approval from HR staff instead that getting it from line supervisors.
remediation_validation: There is no update from workers, since 1) the business hasn't been able to take further actions to address the issues with supervisors, translation and grievance mechanisms and 2) the company has been closed due to the explosion that took place near the company.
remediation_results: Since there is no clarity on any further steps the company would take  and the timeframes for those actions given the new COVID-19 wave and the current closure of the factory, Issara has decided to close all of the cases related to this report at this point and will update it as needed once the company resumes operations and workers can confirm if the issues have been solved.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations; 
-To have open discussion sessions between  HR and workers to understand better what are the challenges being faced by workers and what is driving them to resign. During these discussions, the business is encouraged to share with workers what the business actions are to address these issues.
-The business could also conduct an internal survey to learn why workers want to resign and what can help them remain in Ladybird. Issara can help with the survey questionnaire. Surveys should be conducted in a confidential way where workers feel safe to share the issues that they are facing. 
-The business shall work on a plan to address the issues that are raised in the survey by the workers. 
-The business shall provide training to all supervisors including translators.
-The business shall revise the grievance channels that are meant for workers to raise their issues. The revision should focus on workers' confidentiality and the no retaliation policy. Workers have expressed their concern about raising issues with HR, out of fear of retaliation from their supervisors, therefore it is strongly recommended for the business to reinforce a no retaliation policy and make sure all supervisors are aware of the policy, follow it and face consequences if they commit any actions against such policy.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that a fellow worker was punished for making a mistake in her task of not putting in a wifi chip into a device. She was made to write "I will never forget to put the chip into the device" 5,000 times as punishment. Even after this, she was made to hold up a poster displaying her punishment for a whole day. She reported this to HR (factory 6), feeling that this punishment was extreme. The line leader (P' Nata) was called into the office and both this line leader and the worker ended up receiving warning letters. Afterwards, the line leader threatened the worker saying she as the line leader would never get dismissed even if the worker were to report her and the line leader made her keep standing and holding up the poster.  All the workers are afraid to use the grievance mechanism, given what happened to this worker.   


Recommendations:
- Investigate this matter to establish how this worker report was handled and why the worker was not protected from the line leader that she made a complaint about. HR should handle any worker complaints in ways that ensures their safety.
- Consider withdrawing the warning issued to the worker
- Train line leaders / supervisors on the company's disciplinary policy and what disciplinary measures are considered to be appropriate and not appropriate
- Clearly communicate what disciplinary measures workers should expect for what kind of mistakes they make.  
- Clearly communicate that the company has a non-retaliation policy, and how the company will make sure workers are safe if and when they report any issues
remediation_business_steps_taken:

description: Hazardous or unsanitary living/dorm/canteen conditions

call_details.description:
Target amount: The workers have to complete the target amount 32 baskets.
Only people who have been there 7-10 years can complete it. In some lines, shrimp distribution is fair. Sometimes, if there are many people at shrimp peeling line, your supervisor will ask you to go and help another line (arranging shrimp) which have less worker, but when you go to another line, supervisor from another line will ask you: what are you doing here? And when you cannot say anything and go back to your original work station, other supervisor will found you are going around in the room without working then you got scolded again. There are 13 supervisors, so that the worker could not know which supervisor they are interacting with. 
Water flow system: Actually, you can turn on the water to flow automatically but the supervisor do not allow you to let the water flow all the time, so that you have to use one hand to press water and another hand to hold the shrimp. You also need to take care the shrimp not to fall. The room was very cold and the water is also very cold so that most of the worker cannot work there. If the worker shirt gets wet, they are not allowing to change it.
Working hour and Shift schedule: The working time still unstable and the worker have to stand by anytime they are calling if the shrimp arrived. Sometimes, the worker doesn’t have enough rest period especially, on the day that they have extra cleaning duty (2.5 hours). Normally, if you don’t complete the target amount, you cannot work for OT. However, if it is on the cleaning day, you don’t want to work OT because it will be too late, but you cannot refuse it because the cleaning to be done after the shift (8 hours + OT + 2.5 hours cleaning). In the next day, if you have to work on early shift, it is hard for the worker. Sometimes, if the line run out of shrimp/raw materials, the workers have to take meal break just after started working in 1 hour then take a meal break 1 hour and continue another 7 hours without break. So the worker got hungry and it is very hard to work in a very cold room 7 hours consecutively. The workers prefer a fixed work schedule if it is day or night. When the work schedule is changing every day, they could not manage their sleeping time and eating time so that it will affect their health. The roommates are also working in a different schedule so that you cannot have a proper rest in the housing, other people will cook and shower while you are sleeping and there is not quiet time within 24 hours. There are about 8-12 people in a room. The factory gives the reason that the working hour have to manage based on the arrival of shrimp: the workers feel that the factory does not value the human as much as they value the shrimp.  
No rights to refuse OT: It was very cold so that some of the workers don’t want to do OT but they cannot refuse it.
Dormitory: For female (single)dormitory, there is no enough bath room, no enough electric plug to cook. The worker were told that they cannot take shower more than 5 mins. Some bathroom and toilet lock are broken so that you cannot close the door. In some bed room the fan is broken but cannot ask for replacement. They complain it but nothing improved. The mattress are very old and there are bugs in it so the worker request to move it away but they were told that they cannot remove it because it will be a problem if the visitor found it. 
Electric cost: There is no clear system for electric bill. The worker got deduct the bills less if they earned less wages, and they got deduct more if they earn more.
Health care and sick leave: In order to take a sick leave, you need approval from factory clinic nurse, it is not easy. Sometimes, they will tell you to come back again for signature. It is not easy for the workers to find them again and again since the worker have to run from work. Sometimes, the worker got sick and go to see the nurse: if there is no interpreter at the nurse room, you have to wait for a long hour. The workers could not identify which nurse has bad behavior. They thought that all nurses behavior are the same. 
If you take sick leave and went to the hospital and come back with the medical certificate, you got pay only for a half day. The workers are told that they can still work for a half day.

The client said, that she and her friends are not okay to work at the current fcatory. Because of these reason...Living condition is not good and not eough space,  12 workers have to stay at the small room  with different shift, working shif are not acceptable, the RA in not taking the proper action. So the client has left the job and trying to get the cancellation letter. The caller request Issara to get the cancellation letter for them.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; The workers said that the manager P’Bua is biased towards the workers. He selected only the workers who get along with him and have good performance. For those workers, they can get a regular job and even double OT like working on a day off. But for the other workers who didn’t get along with him, they have to work only one or two days per month.


-Discrimination issues should be taken seriously and should be handled with appropriate disciplinary measures. Thus, the business should investigate the line supervisor from line 103 and create a plan of action to address this kind of issue, noting that it is the business's responsibility to make sure all workers are treated fairly and ethically.


** talking Points**

-Please ask the business how are they making sure that all workers are assigned for the fair and equal assignment?
remediation_business_steps_taken:
"The business has the policy to select the skilled workers to work on regular job or OT. As TG1 policy regarding COVID-19 to operate and survive. For the OT the TG 1 has a system to choose the workers who have the ability to work and provide more profit to the Business. This is not discrimination and sometimes the line supervisor may not explain more clearly to the workers. 
However, The impacted workers can go to meet HR directly. The business would communicate case by case.

Workers updated the improved situation. They have reported receiving equal OT working hours.
remediation_business_steps_remaining: There had no clear commitment or agreement from the business side on the recommendation that Issara has provided for the investigation and remediation. The business did not provide any update about taking any action or conducting an investigation.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that a manager is biased towards certain workers - over time and double OT is regularly given to select workers; other workers only get 1 or 2 days OT per month.

remediation_results: No information was shared by the business regarding actions that they may or may not have taken based on workers' reporting and Issara's recommendations.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
"-The business should have a standard distribution system for the work load for each worker. In order to generate a plan of action, the business shall coordinate with production department to make sure workloads are balanced and fair. 

-The business to communicate with all workers, supervisors and manager about the business policy for any kind of disctiminations and workload. The communication should include information about workload, tasks and the discplinary measure for those who do not  follow the business policy.  The communication should be provided in writing and explained verbally to workers. 
 
-Training and planning sessions with Issara and HR on strengthening  the relationship with all workers and supervisors, then broader training for line supervisors and others."

remediation_issara_recommendation: A worker reported that 400 MOU workers were recruited by Ngwe Kyal Zin Hein (RA) and started working in Factory 10 & 11 on 9th Dec 2022. They signed the employment contract on 12th Dec 2022. However, on 12 Jan 2023, the Thai Agency No.62 (Thai Power) came to their housing and announced that all 400 workers would have to move to Cal-Comp in SMSK. On 15 Jan 2023, 30 workers moved to Cal-Comp SMSK willingly. On 17 Jan 2023, the Thai RA forced the rest of the workers and arranged for them to move. Now all 400 workers have started working in Cal-Comp SMSK and 370 workers settled down there but 130 workers weren't happy about this involuntary relocation. So the 130 went on strike on 20th Jan 2023. At that time, the Thai RA came and promised 130 workers to move them back to Cal-Comp Petchaburi by 23rd Jan 2023. However, this did not happen.
remediation_business_steps_taken: According to CC policy, all workers would agree if they were relocated to the SMSK site, according to K. Piyabutr, CSR. Concerning the Thai RA forcing workers to relocate, they will look into it and get back to us.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that 400 MOU workers were recruited by a Myanmar recruitment agency (RA) and started working in Factory 10 & 11 on 9th Dec 2022. They signed the employment contract on 12th Dec 2022. However, on 12 Jan 2023, the Thai recruitment agency came to their housing and announced that all 400 workers would have to move to Cal-Comp in Samut Sakhon (SMSK). On 15 Jan 2023, 30 workers moved to Cal-Comp SMSK willingly. On 17 Jan 2023, the Thai RA forced the rest of the workers and arranged for them to move. Now all 400 workers have started working in Cal-Comp SMSK and 370 workers settled down there but 130 workers weren't happy about this involuntary relocation. So the 130 went on strike on 20th Jan 2023. At that time, the Thai RA came and promised 130 workers to move them back to Cal-Comp Petchaburi by 23rd Jan 2023. However, this did not happen.
remediation_action: The business responded that according to company policy, any worker that is relocated would need to consent first before such a move.  Concerning the Thai recruitment agency forcing workers to relocate, HR will investigate and get back to us.
remediation_validation:
Issara followed up with the workers and they noted that the Thai recruitment agency had made an announcement on the workers to be moved to the Samut Sakhon facility. The workers said there was no official announcement from the business.  Staff from the Thai recruitment agency came to their housing to take the workers to Samut Sakhon.

The worker provided a further update on March 7th, 2023, that the business is now arranging to send back 138 workers to CC Petchaburi by 4th April. Out of 370, only 50 had moved voluntarily.

All the workers that had been relocated to CC Samut Sakhon were terminated after the workers at this site voted for the 2-shift system which resulted in the business then choosing to terminate more than 1,000 workers.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case.  The workers had no chance to even return to the Petchburi facility because they were fired from their jobs at the Samut Sakhon site.

call_details.description:
Name  Mr. Shanti Lal 
Age - Around 40. 
Passport - J 8122700
Work Permit - 10512559011758
Source Country address -  Dehradun province, Anthwal village.
Arrival Date - 6th, June 2016. 
Recruiter - He came to Thailand with a tourist visa and changed to non B. 
Employer - Taj Cafe Indian restaurant. 
Address of the Employer - 1/29-30 Sukhumvit soi 3, Bangko (Near Grace Hotel), Ph- +6622535560. 
Job title and position - Indian Chef. 
 
A helpless Indian victim with several exploitations by the employer. 
 
He came with a tourist visa and his employer applied for a work permit for him. 
Started working there from June 2016 till October 2020. His documents have been retained by the employer since he arrived. He had worked for his employer till October 2020. Since February 2020, the client did not receive wages. He worked there till September 2020 without getting paid (total 8 months of unpaid wages). Since the employer did not give salary for 8 months, the client requested his employer to return his document so that he can find another job. The employer refused to return his documents. That is the reason the client reported to the Indian Embassy and the local police. The local police visited the employer, the employer made his remaining workers lie to the police. It means that the employer and the remaining workers argued to the police that the employer has not retained his documents. Indian Embassy replied to the victim that his employer never picked their calls. In addition to that, one of the female staff of the Indian Embassy told the client that his employer might harm him, he better avoid him. As the victim did not have a job since then, the victim relied on and stayed with one of his friends in Phra Khanong. In the last week of February 2021, the employer contacted him and said that he will return his documents. The employer picked him up from his place of residence and put him in his car but badly physically abused and dropped him on the way at night. After a few days of being beaten, his friend also refused to stay with him.  The victim ended up on the street for one night. Fortunately, with the help of his old colleagues, the client is currently staying in Bearing next to my Soi with the help of myself and my friends from that area. We have rented a small room and have been supporting his living rental fees since the last week of February 2021.
 
The client wants to return back to India. 
 
As he could not get his documents back from the employer, the client approached the embassy and requested to issue out passes (the letter that can allow them to be returned). The embassy suggested the client report to immigration for the repatriation and pay the fine and buy a flight ticket so that the Indian embassy can issue the letter. As the client could not speak the languages, he paid 19000 THB to a broker name Mr. RanVijay Yadav on 17, Dec 2020. The broker has not done anything for him till now. The client has been following up with the broker but the broker lately said that the victim has to buy a flight ticket so that he can report to immigration. The client has no money to buy a ticket. It means that the broker is also cheating the client. 
 
Risk assessment.
The victim said that his employer has connections with the gang stars. He has very high risks so that he does not want to let his employer know about him being in Thailand. He is a working father of three children in India sending money back home when he was earning.

So, the workers contacted the Myanmar RA, raising the issues. The Myanmar RA asked the Thai RA, AAA, to come and solve the issues.

On the day the Thai RA came to them, the workers were asked to follow the employer's announcement. The workers' problems were not solved at all.

call_details.description:
Client traveled to Kuwait via Dubai under a free visa and ticket arrangement. The client was promised a basic remuneration of 110 Kd, which she received from her employer. However, she endured severe mistreatment at the hands of her colleagues during her three-month tenure, resulting in physical abuse and visible injuries. Despite her employer's adherence to promised services, the client was repatriated to Nepal after 16 months due to ongoing violence from her colleagues, compounded by her limited language skills and vulnerability as a newcomer. The client now faces significant financial debt, prompting the provision of counseling services to support her during this challenging period.
Key Facts:
1. The client traveled to Kuwait via Dubai on a free visa and ticket, with a promised monthly remuneration of 110 Kd.
2. Her colleagues subjected her to abusive behavior for three months, resulting in physical injuries and visible marks on her body.
3. The client was assaulted on two separate occasions for minor reasons, such as coughing while her colleagues were eating.
4. While the employer fulfilled their obligations and provided the promised services, they recognized the client's vulnerability and repatriated her to Nepal.
5. Due to her limited language skills and unfamiliarity with the country, the client became an easy target for abuse by her colleagues.
6. The client is burdened with substantial debt, necessitating counseling services to address her financial and emotional well-being.
As client was undocumented we could not take any other action but the client was provided with legal counseling

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The Issue with lack of security in the living dorms.

- i) the Business to provide better security, such as setting up Locker boxes in the factory and to have CCTV, gate doors, and security guards at the housing by coordinating with the landlord. 

ii) the business should help coordinate with the police for regular monitoring factory and accommodations areas to ensure safety to the workers.

iii) Business to coordinate and help the workers to apply for their lost documents.


Talking points: 

-Request the business to revise their policy on workers not being allowed to bring their documents to the facility. 

-Explain to the business that the migrant workers should be allowed to carry their documents with them

-Explain workers' rights and the risks they could face for not having their documents with them, such as risks on their way to work/home, in case of emergency etc.

systems_change_issara_recommendation:

the business should make sure that grievance mechanisms are in place for workers to be able to report security issues and robbery happening at their dormitory. remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: A worker from Sewing Line 2 reported that in the second week of February, her line supervisor announced that workers can’t get free Covid tests or Covid-related medical care at the hospital under social security coverage anymore.  From now on, the workers will have to pay 2,500 Baht for a Covid test. 

Talking  Points; 
-Workers have reported not having access to their SSF for Covid-related care. What is the business understanding on this issue? 
-Has the business checked the government regulations on what Covid-related care services are to be covered by SSO?  

Recommendations:
- The business should clarify with the SSO as to what Covid-related medical services are covered for those with social security coverage
- Communicate with all workers about their health care coverage including Covid-related care under the social security system
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have a policy where if a worker is feeling unwell, they have to approach HR and request the ATK test kit. If the ATK kit results positive, the workers will have to go to the Social Security Hospital for the additional test. If any workers want to do the PCR test by themselves, they have to pay. However, the business conducted an investigation and identified that the workers had misunderstandings about the process.

To solve the issue, HR has trained and communicated with the line supervisors and will communicate with the workers. Issara checked with the workers, and workers have confirmed not having issues anyfurther.
remediation_notes: A worker from Sewing Line 2 reported that in the second week of February, her line supervisor announced that workers can’t get free Covid tests or Covid-related medical care at the hospital under social security coverage anymore.  From now on, the workers will have to pay 2,500 Baht for a Covid test.
remediation_action:
Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have the policy where if a worker is feeling unwell, they have to approach HR and request for the ATK test kit. If the ATK kit result is positive, the workers will have to go to the Social Security Hospital for the PCR test. The business clarified that if any worker wants to do the PCR test by herself, this would be on personal expense.

The business conducted an investigation and found that the workers had misunderstood this policy to mean that Covid-related testing and medical care would not be covered any longer.  To solve the issue, HR has trained the line supervisors on how to communicate this to workers and has been working on the written policy. The written policy will be announced to the workers in early April. Issara is checking with the workers.
remediation_validation: Issara checked with the workers, and they have confirmed not having issues any further.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue after the business investigated the matter and clarified with the workers the process for getting Covid tests and what costs will be covered by the business.  Workers now understand and don't have any further concerns.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case because much time has elapsed and the business has made it clear that its sick leave policy is according to the law (the medical certificate is not needed for 1-2 days of sick leave) but it is only missing the final step of making the announcement to workers.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that on October 10th, they had received two announcements, one of which was that when asking for sick leave, a worker can inform his/her supervisor by phone for one day but if it is longer than that, the worker must present a Medical Certificate in order to get paid for that day.

Talking Points:
-Is HR aware that this announcement was made to workers?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Make a new announcement to all workers, with the clarification that medical certificates are not required for one or two days of sick leave.  MCs are required only when a worker is taking 3 or more consecutive days of  sick leave.
-Investigate what happened, and why this announcement, which is clearly against the labor protection act, was made to workers.
-Refresh the knowledge of supervisors or others that made this announcement, so that the correct policy according to the law is communicated to workers
remediation_business_steps_taken:
HR will consult with management regarding making an announcement to all workers, with the clarification that medical certificates are not required for one or two days of sick leave.

BHR followed up with K. Leena, HR manager. She responded that now she is drafting the announcement and in process of translation. All three issues will be verbally announced via the morning talk session and written announcements will be posted on the boards around the factory. She will finish these things and get back to us by this week.


K. Leena, HR manager, clarified that HR had already spoken with all supervisors and that the supervisors should inform all workers. She will, however, double-check with supervisors, and HR will directly communicate this matter to the workers.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that on October 10th, they had received two announcements from HR, one of which was that when asking for sick leave, a worker can inform his/her supervisor by phone for one day but if it is longer than that, the worker must present a Medical Certificate in order to get paid for that day.
remediation_action: HR will make an announcement to all workers, with the clarification that medical certificates are not required for one or two days of sick leave.
remediation_validation: Issara followed up with the workers to let them know that the business is likely to make an announcement about the sick leave policy
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case because much time has elapsed and the business has made it clear that its sick leave policy is according to the law (the medical certificate is not needed for 1-2 days of sick leave) but it is only missing the final step of making the announcement to workers.

call_details.description:
Around 6 Burmese assistant interpreters borrow money from the production workers. 

If the workers do not lend money to them, the workers are targeted to move from here to there in production and sometimes asked to work cleaning almost every day, etc. 

If the workers lend money, it is difficult to get them back. So the workers are not happy with it at all. 

They requested Issara to raise it to the business in order to stop these behaviors.

The worker was followed up to collect more information. He said the assistant supervisors who borrow money from workers are mostly from Line numbers 4113, 4114, 4115, 4116, and 4121. 
Ms.Mar Thein from 4121 is the worse one.

The worker from Seafresh informed Issara that he heard the employer had a warning with the assistant line supervisors and some had to return the borrowed money.
He thanks Issara for supporting the workers.

The manager of the shrimp peeling line in building 2 has verbal and physical abuse issues. She can speak Burmese and yell out to the workers, "Don't you have a brain to think? Why don't you understand if I tell you?" While she is yelling out to the workers, she uses her hand to point them out, touching their heads and pushing their shoulders. In July, a female worker got an eye injury because the manager's finger attacked her eye. The worker was told, "If you are not satisfied, go report to the office." The manager did not say sorry for her fault.

The female worker feels insecure about raising the issue and reporting it to the HR office, even though the interpreter came to investigate. However, the other workers called Issara and raised the issue because this line manager's behavior is unacceptable for the whole production line.

This line manager sometimes does not provide lunch on time after working a maximum of five hours. The workers have to work for over five hours before taking an hour's break.

The eight working hours are mostly until 4:00 p.m., but the manager asks the workers to work until 4:30 p.m. and sometimes until 4:45 p.m. The workers do not get overtime for those extra working hours.

In the past, workers could change the needles and knives at any time. Now the workers are asked to inform the supervisor if they would like to change the materials. If three or four workers requested new materials at the same time, the manager would shout and yell.

A few years ago, this manager had an issue with workers from Building 2, and she was moved to Building 3. She has a bad record, and the workers do not want to work with that manager anymore. The workers requested that Issara discuss this issue with the supplier and take serious action against her.  

The manager's name is P'Kyip.

A worker reported that the manager of the shrimp peeling line in building 2 is verbally and physically abusive. She can speak Burmese and yells at workers, "Don't you have a brain to think? Why don't you understand if I tell you?" While she is yelling at the workers, she will point at them, touching their heads and pushing their shoulders. In July, she poked a female worker's eye, for which she offered no apology. The female worker feels insecure about raising the issue, even though the interpreter came to investigate.

NOTE: A few years ago, this manager had an issue with workers from Building 2, and she was moved to Building 3. She has a bad record, and the workers do not want to work with that manager anymore. The workers requested that Issara discuss this issue with the supplier and take serious action against her. The manager's name is P'Kyip.

Recommendations:
- Investigate this matter, noting that this manager has had issues with workers in the past.
- There should be zero tolerance to physical and verbal abuse.  Discipline the manager according to the company's disciplinary policy
- Communicate to all workers about the definition of verbal and physical abuse, and what is appropriate vs. unacceptable physical and verbal behavior
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Naruemon, HR, responded that HR is aware of the issue and has investigated it; the line manager has received a verbal warning and was trained by HR to improve and communicate with the workers properly.


IDENTIFIED POSSIBLE ROOT CAUSES:
The line supervisor's expectation for employees to speed up their work in accordance with the plan has led to instances of inappropriate behavior both in terms of verbal communication and physical actions.

CORRECTIVE ACTIONS / REMEDY:
From July 13-15 Jul 2023, the employee retention team conducted observations within the production area. During this time, they addressed supervisors who did inappropriate behavior and provided verbal warning notices.

remediation_action:
HR is aware of the issue and has investigated it. The line manager has acknowledged that he has communicated harshly to workers, received a verbal warning, and was trained by HR to improve communication with the workers.

After the workers updated that the line manager's behavior has not improved, this was escalated to the management level.  On 26 September 2023, the factory manager had a second meeting with the line manager, will develop an improvement plan, and there will be an evaluation of his behavior at the end of September 2023. systems_change_issara_recommendation: Regularly train all supervisors about the company's zero tolerance policy against verbal and physical abuse, and communicate clearly about what is considered verbal and physical abuse, and the disciplinary measures to be taken against the abusers.
