call_details.description:
Name  Mr. Shanti Lal 
Age - Around 40. 
Passport - J 8122700
Work Permit - 10512559011758
Source Country address -  Dehradun province, Anthwal village.
Arrival Date - 6th, June 2016. 
Recruiter - He came to Thailand with a tourist visa and changed to non B. 
Employer - Taj Cafe Indian restaurant. 
Address of the Employer - 1/29-30 Sukhumvit soi 3, Bangko (Near Grace Hotel), Ph- +6622535560. 
Job title and position - Indian Chef. 
 
A helpless Indian victim with several exploitations by the employer. 
 
He came with a tourist visa and his employer applied for a work permit for him. 
Started working there from June 2016 till October 2020. His documents have been retained by the employer since he arrived. He had worked for his employer till October 2020. Since February 2020, the client did not receive wages. He worked there till September 2020 without getting paid (total 8 months of unpaid wages). Since the employer did not give salary for 8 months, the client requested his employer to return his document so that he can find another job. The employer refused to return his documents. That is the reason the client reported to the Indian Embassy and the local police. The local police visited the employer, the employer made his remaining workers lie to the police. It means that the employer and the remaining workers argued to the police that the employer has not retained his documents. Indian Embassy replied to the victim that his employer never picked their calls. In addition to that, one of the female staff of the Indian Embassy told the client that his employer might harm him, he better avoid him. As the victim did not have a job since then, the victim relied on and stayed with one of his friends in Phra Khanong. In the last week of February 2021, the employer contacted him and said that he will return his documents. The employer picked him up from his place of residence and put him in his car but badly physically abused and dropped him on the way at night. After a few days of being beaten, his friend also refused to stay with him.  The victim ended up on the street for one night. Fortunately, with the help of his old colleagues, the client is currently staying in Bearing next to my Soi with the help of myself and my friends from that area. We have rented a small room and have been supporting his living rental fees since the last week of February 2021.
 
The client wants to return back to India. 
 
As he could not get his documents back from the employer, the client approached the embassy and requested to issue out passes (the letter that can allow them to be returned). The embassy suggested the client report to immigration for the repatriation and pay the fine and buy a flight ticket so that the Indian embassy can issue the letter. As the client could not speak the languages, he paid 19000 THB to a broker name Mr. RanVijay Yadav on 17, Dec 2020. The broker has not done anything for him till now. The client has been following up with the broker but the broker lately said that the victim has to buy a flight ticket so that he can report to immigration. The client has no money to buy a ticket. It means that the broker is also cheating the client. 
 
Risk assessment.
The victim said that his employer has connections with the gang stars. He has very high risks so that he does not want to let his employer know about him being in Thailand. He is a working father of three children in India sending money back home when he was earning.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Shine Min Htet Factory 11 worker reported that starting from Dec 20th 2022, Cal-Comp practiced 3 shifts a day in Factory 10 & 11 and the reason given was low orders from the buyers. The 3 shifts are: 1) 5 AM to 1:40 PM, 2) 1 PM to 9:40 PM, and 3) 9 PM to 5:40 AM. As a result, the workers assigned to work in the 1st shift have to wake up very early (3-4am) to catch the shuttle bus. The 2nd shift workers have faced security issues during this late night commute back home, with workers getting attacked by gangsters, especially in Bang Kway area. The gangsters try to take the workers' phones, jewelry, or money. On 14th March, one of the night-shift workers was attacked by two local gangsters near the Bar Bar shop (Bang Kway area) and seriously injured. Women also face sexual harassment by the locals and gangsters during their late night commute, with motorcycle riders touching the hips of the women workers. In addition, the food at the canteen often has gone bad by the time the 3rd shift workers get their meal break. Many workers are feeling physically weak due to sleeplessness, not having fresh food, and mentally distressed due to the dangers during the commute. Now, the business has decided to extend 3-shift work arrangement for another 3 months.

TPs:
- What are the reasons for moving to a 3-shift system?
- Is the business aware of the negative effects this is having on the workers?

Recommendations:
- The business should provide working hours and conditions as stated in the employment contract
- Given the negative impact on workers, consider going back to the 2-shift system as was the arrangement previously and the working hours that the workers signed up for when they signed their employment contracts.
- Investigate any cases where workers may have been victims of robbery, assault, or sexual harassment during their commute to work
remediation_notes: A Factory 11 worker reported that starting from Dec 20th 2022, the business moved to a 3-shift system for Factory 10 & 11, with the following hours: 1) 5 AM to 1:40 PM, 2) 1 PM to 9:40 PM, and 3) 9 PM to 5:40 AM. As a result, the workers assigned to work in the 1st shift have to wake up very early (3-4am) to catch the shuttle bus. The 2nd shift workers have faced security issues during this late night commute back home, with workers getting attacked by gangsters that try to take their phones, jewelry, or money. On 14th March, one of the night-shift workers was attacked by two local gangsters near the Bar Bar shop (Bang Kway area) and seriously injured. Women also face sexual harassment by the locals and gangsters during their late night commute. In addition, the food at the canteen often has gone bad by the time the 3rd shift workers get their meal break. Many workers are feeling physically weak due to sleeplessness, not having fresh food, and mentally distressed due to the dangers during the commute. Now, the business has decided to extend 3-shift work arrangement for another 3 months.
remediation_action: The business responded saying that due to declining orders, they had to move to three shifts to retain all workers rather than having to terminate the contracts of many workers. In terms of the worker concerns such as transportation safety at night and quality of the canteen food for all shifts, the business has made improvements after receiving worker feedback internally. They have increased the security guard and patrols, and they are in discussions with the police to install CCTVs along the route.
remediation_validation: Workers were asked to vote whether they wanted to change back to the 2-shift system but with the knowledge that if that were to happen, many workers would be terminated but if they agreed to maintain the 3-shift system, no workers would be let go.  The workers voted to stay on the 3-shift system and have noted that conditions such as travel security and canteen food quality has improved.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case.  Although the workers wanted to return to the 2-shift system, the business said they would have to fire many workers if that were to be the case so the workers voted to stay on the 3-shift system with no workers losing their jobs.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
#Issue 1 Context: According to workers' feedback, they can now use the toilet throughout the working day, however, there are workers from a building 4 that still have issues with toilet breaks.

Recommendations: Allow workers to use the toilet throughout the working day instead of only allowing them to use the toilet during their 60-minute total break time.

4 Nov 2020
The workers from building 4, the circuit producing line, downstairs reported that they are still having difficulties accessing the toilet breaks.

Additional talking points: 
-Workers said that they have to find someone to replace them to access the toilet break, what has the business done to address this issue? 


#Issue 2. 
(14-Aug-20) 
Context; Long OT working hours with an insufficient break; The workers have to work for around 6 hours of OT but only 30 minutes of break for the whole 6 hours. This is the issue that comes from Building - 4 and Buiding 9. However, the workers also reported that there are some of the lines in the same building which has no OT at all.

Issara recommendations.

-The business should immediately investigate and to revise their OT policy and the breaks before and during overtime working hours. Base on the result of investigations, the business should take action should guarantee that the policy is aligned with Thai law and the buyer's CoC. And there should be disciplinary action towards those who do not follow the policy. 

-The break schedule should be aligned with the labor protection act (there should be a break after 5 consecutive hours and 20 minutes of break before starting more than 2 hours of OT work). 

Talking Points:

-Ask the business about their OT break schedule in general and specific to this building. Why are some workers in the same building receiving 6 hours of OT and some of them are not receiving any at all? Are these increasing OT hours happening because of increased production? 

-Is the business aware of the HP COC and the maximum hours of OT for workers during COVID-19? 

-Explain to the business that workers should not be working more than 5 hours without a break and only 30 minutes of break for 6 hours of OT is not enough for the workers health. 

-Explain the business that the workers should get 20 minutes of break after their normal working hours. 

Update Oct 4, 2020
-Share with the business that the workers are being asked to work more than 5 consecutive hours during the OT work, which is a violation of the law according to Act B.E.2541, Article 27.

Reference : 
Act B.E.2541, Article 27; 
On a Working Day, an Employer shall arrange a rest period during work for an Employee of not less than one hour per day after the Employee has been working for not more than five consecutive hours. An Employer and Employee may agree in advance that each rest period may be less than one hour but the total rest period per day shall not be less than one hour. Whereas an Employer and Employee agree to specify rest periods during work other than paragraph one, the agreement shall be applicable only if it is more favorable to the Employee. Whereas any Overtime Work after normal working time is more than two hours, the
The employer shall arrange for the Employee to take a rest period of not less than twenty minutes before the Employee commences the Overtime Work.

Time frame   
1 pay period.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue # 1 (Old and unresolved, CLOSED) 
The issue with physically abusive supervisors. 
#Recommendations for Issue 1
-Physical assault should be responded to with an appropriate disciplinary measure.  Typical disciplinary systems include written warnings for serious infractions, followed by dismissal. 

-Physical assault on the company premises, as a serious human rights violation and violation of the Thai Criminal Code, would be expected to be met with immediate dismissal. 

Talking points:

- Disciplinary action should be taken.  Reports of crimes against workers should be addressed seriously by the company, including safeguards for reporting workers, credible investigations, and appropriate disciplinary measures.

- Cal-Comp explained they documented the incident on file but did not give the supervisor a warning.  This does not constitute an "appropriate disciplinary measure" for a violation that is essentially illegal - a violation of the Thai Criminal Code, typically punishable by fines and sometimes imprisonment.

- The lack of any disciplinary action by the business to physical assault of workers creates an environment of impunity.  This can create a high level of uncertainty and fear amongst the workforce when they see that management allows supervisors to physically assault workers with no consequences.

CLOSED

call_details.description:
Focus group discussion: Annual leave Issue at C department (Line: O.H, BB, BL, Sanai)
Participants: 9 (7 from C department and 2 from SP)

As discussing the workers all of them raised about the difficulties in requesting the annual leave. A worker said she once requested the annual leave successfully because she got sick during her duty (Most workers do not prefer to use sick leave when they get sick because they will lose their due diligence fee). Workers mentioned that most line supervisors' behavior is very difficult to deal with whenever they request the annual leave they are not allowed if the workers haven’t worked during additional holidays (the day that the business added up by using the workers’ annual leave). And here are the additional information from the worker:
The annual leave is entitled 6 days as mentioned in the e-slip from the mobile application. And these numbers will be deducted automatically when there is 1 or 2 days added up to the public holiday but if they are working on the additional holiday the annual on the e-slip remains the same. 
There are 13 holidays that were announced annually but they suspect that these are the additional holidays in 2022 that the business use their annual leave: 
- New Year, 1-2 day extra
- Chinese New Year, 3 days
- Islamic day, 1 day
- Ork Phansa, 1 day
- Khao Phansa, 2-3 days
- Factory close due to lack of materials, 1 day
(we need to request the 2022 holiday list from the business to compare to the mentioned events which are not on the list)

These are the events where the workers hear the announcement for them to work to obtain their annual leave:
- International New Year
- Chinese New Year
- Ork Phansa
- Islamic day
- On the business demand
(All these events the workers were ask to work voluntarily)  

The workers’s request:
The business should not use the workers’ annual leave as their desire, workers should own and use it as their need. 
Special request for Issara to train the line supervisors
The 13 holidays are enough for the workers, they don’t need additional holiday by using their annual leave. 
When there is a lack of materials and the factory is closed, the business should not deduct worker’s annual leave.
call_details.next_steps: After clearly understanding the issue, an escalation call will be proposed to the business.

call_details.description:
O&E to clarify with workers the company's leave policy and that it's not up to the workers to work on a holiday and get to use annual leave on a day of their choosing. The business decides when workers will take the six annual leave days, and informs the workers at the beginning of each month. 
The worker confirmed that now he clearly understands about the annual leave set by the business and he will communicate with other workers at his production line about this policy as well. He thanks to Issara for making an effort in discussing with the business, at least now he could understand why he can't freely use the annual leaves.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue.  The worker now understands the company policy on annual leave.  BFI should re-consider its position on deciding for workers when they will take annual leave days.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
During the recruitment fee survey, a worker raised an issue about the annual leave. 
He said trying to use his annual leave days was very difficult even if it was mentioned on the pay slip that he has 6 days annual leave days. When he requests the leave from line supervisor or manager, they said he could use his annual leave days only if he worked during the public holidays without payment. Workers that agreed to work on public holidays were allowed to use annual leave days later.

In the C.OH line there are almost 300 workers. And specifically, the C line there is around 200 workers and the OH line there is around 100 workers. The line C and OH are under one department that's why it is called C.OH. The worker also mentioned this policy does not apply to all production lines but in Line C.OH, it is like that. Workers request to raise the issue generally but not specify the working line if possible.

TPs:
-What is the company's policy and process for approving annual leave for workers?
-Is HR aware that line supervisors are saying unless workers volunteer to work on a public holiday without pay, they cannot get approval to use their annual leave days?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Conduct an investigation to find out why workers are being made to work for free on public holidays just so they can get approvals to use their annual leave days
-If workers have worked on public holidays and not been paid, reimburse the workers immediately
-If line supervisors have been found to make workers to work for free on public holidays just so that they can get to use their annual leave, those supervisors should be disciplined according to the company's disciplinary policy
-Communicate verbally and in writing that workers can request annual leave as needed and this is not conditional on working on public holidays without pay.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Panida, HR, shared the findings of the investigation, which revealed that workers from production line C and OH and DE were chosen at random interviewed about the issue. It turns out that the workers claimed that no such incident occurred.

They had a meeting with the supervisors about the issue. Even so, the supervisor confirmed that there was no incident. However, HR trained the supervisors on the company's leave policy. This includes instructing and publicizing the supervisors on the production line in order to prevent such incidents from occurring.

Please see the photos of the the interview and training.
https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1zhf38B7UVrdswKxC86mVMlbNIs0A4Hco


K. Seubpon, HR, mentioned that they will communicate with the workers about the annual leave by next week.


K. Seubpong, HR mentioned that he will follow up with the HR in the factory and get back to us.
remediation_notes: A worker report that he tried to use his annual leave days was very difficult even if it was mentioned on the pay slip that he has 6 days annual leave days. When he requests the leave from line supervisor or manager, they said he could use his annual leave days only if he worked during the public holidays without payment. Workers that agreed to work on public holidays were allowed to use annual leave days later.  This seems to be what's happening to workers in the production line where he is working.
remediation_action:
HR shared the investigation results, which revealed that workers claimed that no such incident occurred.  The supervisors also replied that such instances did not occur.  Still, HR trained the supervisors on the company's leave policy.  

Issara escalated this issue with senior management providing the worker update that workers were not able to choose when they would take annual leave unless they worked on the days the company had already decided would be when workers used annual leave.

BFI responded saying that it is lawful for the company to decide when the workers will take annual leave and this is what BFI is practicing.  Workers are not able to work on those days designated as annual leave by the company so that they can use it at another time.
remediation_validation:
Issara followed up with the workers to clarify the issue and it was that the company had decided when workers would take annual leave and if workers wanted to take annual leave at another time, they thought they needed to work on those days designated as annual leave by the company but it was difficult for them to get approval for this.

After Issara shared the company's policy that the company decides when workers can use annual leave and this cannot be changed just because the worker wanted to work on those days.  The worker now understands the company policy.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue.  The worker now understands the company policy on annual leave.  BFI should re-consider its position on deciding for workers when they will take annual leave days.

The workers arrived at the construction site in Chumburi on November 23 after they were recruited by Lucky Employment Agency. When they arrived, the workers had to buy the PPE, such as boots, a helmet, etc., by themselves. On the first working day, the employer announced that the workers had to work Sunday with their regular daily wage. If the employer cannot provide a job, the workers won't be paid. The working hours are from 7:00 to 17:30 p.m., which is totally against the contract.

So, the workers contacted the Myanmar RA, raising the issues. The Myanmar RA asked the Thai RA, AAA, to come and solve the issues.

On the day the Thai RA came to them, the workers were asked to follow the employer's announcement. The workers' problems were not solved at all.

The employer would not allow them to stay at their construction site if they did not work as assigned. The Thai RA will rent a room for them, and they have to wait a few months without having jobs to get the cancellation letter.
The workers do not have enough money to stay without jobs.

As a result, the workers contacted Issara and received advice on what they should do. It was suggested that they contact the labor attaché and raise the issues.

The workers did not work in construction, and different workers tried to find new jobs. The six workers, including the client, did not look for any other jobs. They just waited for the job arranged by the Thai RA. 

Later, they were recruited by an employer from Samut Sakhon to work at the sticker factory. The client said they were lucky and are now working with that new employer. She thanks Issara for calling her back and asking about her condition.
The client went to Qatar through Green Hill Overseas Pvt.Ltd.

followup call
Followup calls to TUF worker.

closed_notes:
The worker that reported the issue asked for the case not to be reported to the business without learning first how would the business address such issues, what the process of investigation would look like and how safeguards would be put in place for workers. 

Issara approached the business to learn about their no retaliation policy and the process of investigation for such kinds of cases where there is a high risk for  workers to be identified as reporters and then being targeted by their supervisors. As a response, the business replied how their No-Retaliation policy has been introduced with the workers and that workers should feel safe to report their grievances. The business did not provide a clear explanation about the investigation process where there is a small number of workers in a working line that can easily be identified and targeted by their supervisors. The business just provided general information about different ways to conduct investigations depending on the situation. Since the business response was not clear for such cases and there was no information provided about the safeguards for workers, Issara could not raise this issue with the business, following the worker request given that he feared being targeted by his supervisor. Therefore, this issue is considered to be closed.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers from the Pla-Sud line reported about OT working hours not being informed in advance, workers not getting 20 minutes of breaks before starting OT hours, workload being discriminatively distributed against the nationality however, the worker did not give full consent to Issara to raise this issue with the business. 

Talking Points

-We understand that TU has a no retaliation policy that should be used to protect workers when they share their grievances through any channel. So we would like to learn more about TUF investigation processes whenever there is a case that is affecting workers on a small working line. 
-How would HR investigate a case, if the issue is connected to the line supervisors? How would sage guards be put in place to make sure workers on the small working line are not targeted or seen negatively by the supervisor or other employees? Can you please describe the process of investigation?
-When the business conducts an investigation involving a line supervisor, is the supervisor notified about the issue in that specific production line? Or how is that information handled?
-If workers have an issue from a small line but also have concerns about being retaliated by the supervisor, what is the business’s strategy to resolve such issues in such condition? 
-Has the TUF communicated about TUs no-retaliation policy to all workers and supervisors? If so, when and how? If not, any plan for that? 
Because workers express not being aware of the TUs’ no retaliation policy.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Since the worker did not give consent to share the issue with the business with the fear of being retaliated given the small number of workers in this specific production line, Issara approached the business to learn about their process of investigation for such kinds of issues which has risks for the workers being targeted by their supervisors. Issara checked with the business about their No Retaliation policy and investigation process for such small production. As a response, the business replied how their No-Retaliation policy has been introduced with the workers and the workers should feel safe to use it. The business did not clearly explain about the investigation process where it has a small number of workers. It is only said having different ways to conduct the investigation depending on the situation. Since the business response was not clear for the certain line issue, Issara could not raise this issue given the workers fear of being targeted by their supervisors. Therefore, this issue is considered to be closed.
remediation_business_steps_remaining: Issara was not able to raise this specific issue with the business since the business response did not address the Issara queries.
remediation_notes: A worker reported issue with OT working hours not being informed in advance, workers not getting 20 minutes of breaks before starting OT hours, and facing discrimination based on nationality in the distribution of workloads. The worker reported that these issues were impacting all workers in his working line which has around 20 workers. The worker asked Issara for the case not to be reported to the business without learning first how would the business address such issues, what the process of investigation would look like and how safeguards would be put in place for workers.
remediation_action: Issara approached the business to learn about their no retaliation policy and the process of investigation for such kinds of cases where there is a high risk for  workers to be identified as reporters and then being targeted by their supervisors. As a response, the business replied how their No-Retaliation policy has been introduced with the workers and that workers should feel safe to report their grievances. The business did not provide a clear explanation about the investigation process where there is a small number of workers in a working line that can easily be identified and targeted by their supervisors. The business just provided general information about different ways to conduct investigations depending on the situation.
remediation_validation: Since the business response was not clear for such cases and there was no information provided about the safeguards for workers, Issara could not raise this issue with the business, following the worker request given that he feared being targeted by his supervisor.
remediation_results: Issara has a meeting with TU Group and provided recommendation to conduct a worker satisfaction survey to identify companies strengths but also issues that should be addressed. TU Group has not provided a clear response regarding this recommendation. In addition, to the survey, Issara has offered to provide tailored training to HR staff, for which the details are to be discussed with TU Group.

call_details.description:
From the hotline call, the worker shared the issue that they were experiencing, and they also would like to ask for understanding from the business, such as:

The worker mentioned that whenever visitors come to visit the production line, there is always an announcement for the workers to be prepared and stay at the working place until the visitors leave. So, the workers need to be at their place for about 2–3 hours and can't go anywhere, even to the toilet. During that time, it is very difficult for some workers as they need to go to the toilet.

Moreover, these are some requests and concerns that the worker would like to raise with the business for consideration:
1. During working hours, some workers went outside to get some coffee and eat food. Now the business is very restricted because the workers used the toilet break time to do something else. The restriction makes sense to the worker, but they ask for understanding as the nature of work is hard for them; they need to stand for long hours and work a lot. They need to fill in more energy by eating or getting a cup of coffee to be awake, well-concentrated, and more productive. If the worker goes out for more than 15 minutes, they will accept that it is their fault.
2. The worker is happy to work in GFPT, but the business should consider motivating the workers more, such as by providing a due diligence allowance. By providing such an allowance, the workers will be more happy, and it is helpful to support the worker's lives in the inflationary moment (price increases in the market).
call_details.next_steps: BHR reach out to the business

call_details.description:
The business response:
K. Sarayuth stated that workers can use the toilets freely, even if they have visitors. However, the production might work as a good arrangement when hosting visitors. They will look into what was happening on the production line. They will also communicate clearly to workers about the use of toilets when needed by February 15th.

K. Sarayuth stated that GFPT allows workers to bring their own food. However, there are no shelves or food storage facilities for the workers to store it. Workers can bring their own food and eat it in the canteen using the utensils provided, but they cannot keep it. They will clearly communicate this policy to workers through verbal and written announcements by February 15th.

Adding some requests and concerns from the workers:
1. They stated that if workers request a toilet break, they must use the toilets as requested but not eat food and take too long time during working hours. GFPT provides coffee and snack breaks at different times.

2. HR is aware of the attendant incentive requested by workers. HR is currently meeting with the Worker Welfare Committee. And they will conduct a worker survey to gather useful information for discussing the attendant incentive with top management.

The validation call with the worker:

O&E explained all the business responses to the worker. But there are some additional points that the worker would like to express due to the business response, such as:
1. Toilet break restriction during visitor visits: How come HR doesn't know about this? because at the production line it was loudly announced by a microphone, and the information about visiting should be passed from the HR office first. The worker will wait and see the correction action from the business. 

2. Eating snacks and coffee during working hours, some workers reported fainting after long working hours before a lunch break. The workers mentioned at the Chin Soun production line need to work 5–6 hours before getting a lunch break, and as it is a hard job, most workers can't bear that. That's why workers sneak to eat something, and some workers even bring snacks to eat in the toilet. The business should carefully arrange and consider the workers well-being.

3. Regarding the lack of shelves or food storage for the workers, it is very hard because the workers said that for night shift workers, sometimes they ate food that the vendor had made earlier in the morning and it caused diarrhea. And some food at the canteen is unclean; how does the business expect the workers to eat foods at the canteen or just let the workers eat immediately before starting work, as they deserve to eat better and healthier foods many times to fill in the energy? If the business really wants to do that, please ensure the freshness and healthy foods and worker's national food are available at the canteen. Otherwise, it is very difficult for the workers.

4. Additional comment regarding the toilet break: in some production lines, the toilets are limited and workers need to line up. Before, it used to have chairs or seats for workers to sit and wait, but now they have been removed. Workers wonder why?

If the business does not consider all this carefully, many more workers will leave the factory.
call_details.next_steps: Get back to the business of additional info

call_details.description:
1. The complaint about the food quality:
O&E shares with the worker the video and picture from the business showing that the food vendor always heads the foods to ensure freshness and some pictures of the ingredients that are good quality products. 

The worker said it is better now, as she also saw that the food vendors are suing the heading port, but the business should pay more attention to controlling the food quality because she still recently found a small worm on the Nam Prik Kapik. 

2. Validate with the worker about the toilet break issue while visitors are visiting and the long working hours before lunch break at the Chinsoun production line:

Regarding the restriction on not allowing the workers to go to the toilet whenever visitors come, now the issue is improving as there is no pressure or such announcement anymore during this recent visit from the guest. The business only asks the workers to be more corporate with them. 

At the Chinsoun production line, there is better change as the business arranges a better schedule for the lunch break after 4 working hours, and some workers can have two separate break times for half an hour each every 3 or 3.5 hours if the production line is very busy (ex:at 10:30, a half-hour break, and at 2 pm, another half-hour break). And the line supervisor carefully manages the workers break. 

The worker confirmed to close the case.

Context; The issue with the workers not getting 20 minutes of break before starting OT for more than 2 hours. This Issue comes from TUM factory 1, Fish packaging line, 4th floor of the Main building. ID - 10723

Issara recommendations 

-The business to conduct an investigation to identify the root cause of the issue. 
-The investigation should be conducted ethically taking into account safeguards for the workers. 
-The business to make sure that all workers have a break before starting OT for more than 2 hours. 
-The break schedule should be aligned with the labor protection act. 
-Workers' OT working hours should reflect on the payslip. 

time Frame 1 pay period.

systems_change_issara_recommendation:

remediation_issara_recommendation:
There are around 400 Cambodian workers with additional new batches of MOU workers arriving but there is only one Cambodian interpreter at ITC. Workers shared examples about how this lack of interpreters at ITC has negatively affected them.  A worker who needed interpretation support at the hospital because his wife was sick couldn't get it because the interpreter had gone to pick up a new batch of MOU workers at the border. Also, the interpreter only works the day shift and so when night shift workers need interpretation support or workers need to go to the hospital at night, the interpreter says he cannot help.  The workers would like more interpreters to be available to support them in both the day and night shifts. 

TPs:
-Does ITC have plans to hire additional Cambodian interpreters, given that there is this additional need for the number of Cambodian workers in the day and night shifts?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Ensure that there is adequate interpretation support for the Cambodian workers during both the day and night shifts, with at least two interpreters each for the day and night shifts so there is a back-up if one interpreter is unavailable during each shift
-Hear directly from the Cambodian workers as to what kind of interpretation support needs they have for what kinds of instances and when so that the company can be responsive to their needs
-Communicate with the Cambodian workers the company's plan to increase the number of interpreters so that there is adequate support, and by when this will be in place
remediation_business_steps_taken:
There are currently 260 Cambodian workers. HR will communicate with all Cambodian workers in the following ways.
HR collaborates with the hospital interpreter and pays the fee service for workers who require help facilities at the hospital.
Inform the workers about the volunteer interpreter group that can assist them during the night shift.


Investigate Case:
Because at present, the total number of Cambodian workers is 230 people and most of them have been working for a long time and can understand Thai other than HR's interpreters.

Solution:
There will be a transportation service to take the worker to the hospital every day. If it's an emergency case, night shift, the supervisor would use the interpreter from the nationality interpreter register that HR regularly updates to inform the supervisors every month. Emergency sickness workers must be sent to the hospital and every time the worker needs an interpreter, the supervisor will look at the interpreter register to help communicate and explain the work in the area. In addition, the HR department will communicate with the interpreter registered in Messenger, and representatives of each dormitory, so that representatives, including Cambodian workers who are members, are informed.
remediation_notes: There are around 400 Cambodian workers with additional new batches of MOU workers arriving but there is only one Cambodian interpreter at ITC. The workers would like more interpreters to be available to support them in both the day and night shifts.
remediation_action:
HR noted that there are currently only 260 Cambodian workers and will communicate with all Cambodian workers about the interpretation services that is made available to them. HR collaborates with the hospital interpreter and pays the fee service for workers who require interpretation services at the hospital. The company also has a volunteer interpreter group that can provide interpretation support during the night shift.

Solution:
The business will also provide a transportation service to take workers to the hospital every day. If it's an emergency case or during the night shift, the supervisor would use the interpreter roster to assign an interpreter to the worker.

systems_change_issara_recommendation:

Name:                        Khin Cho Thet @ Cho

Issue:                        Missing sick leave payment


She broke her left index finger while she was out for meal break. She had to see doctor and took sick leave from April 25 to May 16. Subsequently, she took unpaid leave from May 17 to 29 as her finger was not completely recovered. After undressing the bandage, she was recommended by the doctor to take some more leaves which was from May 30 to June 12. She submitted all the medical certificates to HR.
She said that she has received the wage for 24 days. She thinks that there are 13 days more she has yet to receive. Although she went to HR to raise the issue, she didn’t receive any clear explanation apart from the suggestion that she needs to go to Social Security Office to claim the wage for the days that exceeded 30 days. She said it would be great if HR can clearly explain what is happening with the sick leave payment. She also mentions about the reason of reporting as there are many other workers who has the same issue of missing payment. She wants the fair and clear treatment from TUF for this type of issue. It’s not only about her. 
She also wants to request that TUF would find a suitable working line for her. As she injured her finger before, it’s getting painful and swollen after working for a few hours at her current line. She is willing to share her details.

call_details.description: The client is working at a soft drink factory named (Etica) located in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. He was contracted with the Golden Plant agency. The client worked in that factory on 15.8.2019. Ten months ago, the factory could not continue to employ them due to COVID-19 pandemic and they were not paid but they are staying at the factory and the factory provided the food daily. Earlier when they get paid, they cooked themselves for the meals because the food provided by the factory is not okay for them. Since the factory could not continue to employ them, they informed the employer that they want to go back to Myanmar but the employer didn't take action. So the client+ 11 workers contacted the Malaysia embassy and made the list for relief flight. Another issue is the employer kept their passport. When they are being informed of the 5 seats available on the relief flight, they requested the employer to buy the flight tickets for them but the employer refused and told them that the ticket fees are expensive. So the client called Issara hotline through viber. They would like to contact Golden Plant agency to explain the issue. Issara provided the contact number of Golden Plant agency and Issara also tried to contact the Golden Plant agency in order to inform the issue. The agency's landlines were not answered and mobiles are power off. Issara contacted MOEAF and checked about Golden Plant agency and came to know that the agency was closed during this time. So Issara tried to contact the labour attache of Malaysia through Myanmar hotline viber and connected with the officer U Win Min Soe. Issara informed labour officer about the issue and made the link between the worker and the labor officer. Now they are connected to each other. The labour officer committed that he would negotiate and solve the issue. The client informed Issara that he already provided the necessary information to the labour officer. The client said he will get back to us if he has any progress.
call_details.referral_notes: Issara referred the case to the labour attache and the labour officer U Win Min Soe accepted the case.

call_details.description:
Client traveled to Kuwait via Dubai under a free visa and ticket arrangement. The client was promised a basic remuneration of 110 Kd, which she received from her employer. However, she endured severe mistreatment at the hands of her colleagues during her three-month tenure, resulting in physical abuse and visible injuries. Despite her employer's adherence to promised services, the client was repatriated to Nepal after 16 months due to ongoing violence from her colleagues, compounded by her limited language skills and vulnerability as a newcomer. The client now faces significant financial debt, prompting the provision of counseling services to support her during this challenging period.
Key Facts:
1. The client traveled to Kuwait via Dubai on a free visa and ticket, with a promised monthly remuneration of 110 Kd.
2. Her colleagues subjected her to abusive behavior for three months, resulting in physical injuries and visible marks on her body.
3. The client was assaulted on two separate occasions for minor reasons, such as coughing while her colleagues were eating.
4. While the employer fulfilled their obligations and provided the promised services, they recognized the client's vulnerability and repatriated her to Nepal.
5. Due to her limited language skills and unfamiliarity with the country, the client became an easy target for abuse by her colleagues.
6. The client is burdened with substantial debt, necessitating counseling services to address her financial and emotional well-being.
As client was undocumented we could not take any other action but the client was provided with legal counseling
The family members have submitted the application file to Foreign Employment Board for compensation procedure.

call_details.description:
During the recruitment fee survey a worker raised a problem about the annual leave that the business always used without workers confirmation. For some holidays the business added 1 or 2 days extra for workers to rest by using their annual leaves, and if the workers ran out of their annual leave the business will use business leave (la kech) or unpaid leave instead. Even the workers could benefit from the leave but it's not what they want, they want to use the leave on their own especially for urgent matters. 

Beside the problem mentioned above the worker also would like to check with business about:
- Why do businesses have two terms of employment, one is a monthly paid worker and another one is a daily paid worker. For a daily paid worker they are earned based on the exact day that they worked and they didn't get paid on day off and they didn't receive a bonus as a monthly paid worker. *The worker is the walk in worker so that's why the business set them as a daily paid worker and get payment weekly.
- The canteen always has the same menu (five menus) and never changes even him been here for over a year. The worker wants to have the food menu changed from time to time. 
- When will the worker receive incentive (Beer Ka Yan) again, the business stop provides incentive since covid-19 outbreak starts until now.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case.  The business is maintaining its position that it can decide when workers take annual leave even though Issara has recommended that workers be given the choice of when they will take annual leave or at the least to consult and get consent from the workers when the business decides when workers will take annual leave.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that the business used their annual leave (1-2 days) to extend some long holidays such as the New Year or Songkran.  If the workers ran out of their annual leave, the business would use business leave or unpaid leave instead.  Workers wanted to use their annual leave when they needed to, especially for urgent matters. 

Beside the problem mentioned above, the worker had the following questions for general inquiry:
-The worker wanted to know what's the difference between a monthly worker versus a daily worker
-The worker wanted to know if the canteen food choice could be more diverse instead of the same five food choices offered.
-The worker wanted to know when the company would start paying diligence allowance again (bia kayan) which was stopped since Covid-19 started.


Recommendations for remediation
The worker should be able to decide when he/she will make use of the annual leave days available, rather than having it decided by the company
Consult with workers well in advance of any proposed extended holiday period and get their input on whether workers will want to use their annual leave for the extra holidays or whether they will want to work on those days
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Noppakao, HR mentioned that he will investigate this case and get back to us within one week.

Added
-The worker wanted to know what's the difference between a monthly worker versus a daily worker
Of course, the worker who work effectiveness will be promoted to be a monthly workers. There are some benefits are different.

-The worker wanted to know if the canteen food choice could be more diverse instead of the same five food choices offered.
This is also internal grievance, the company is aware of this case and try to address it.

-The worker wanted to know when the company would start paying diligence allowance again (bia kayan) which was stopped since Covid-19 started.
The company do not have the diligence allowance anymore. However, the company will come out with new incentive soon.


K. Sarayuth, HR, stated that the HR team was aware of the issue and had previously raised it with company management. The management interprets Section 30 of the LPA as follows: "..the Employer is obliged to fix the Holiday in advance for the Employee’ (this beginning) Actually, the sentence ends with '..or as agreed by the Employer and Employee.' So, according to company policy, the company is obliged to plan the annual leave (holiday) for its employees in advance. The company informs employees one month in advance that they will be on leave.

BHR recommended that the management consider the last part of the sentence, '..or as agreed by the Employer and Employee.' He responded that management will review the policy in mid-September to consider and revise it. He will bring this up to management for review at that time.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that the business used their annual leave (1-2 days) to extend some long holidays such as the New Year or Songkran.  If the workers ran out of their annual leave, the business would use business leave or unpaid leave instead.  Workers wanted to use their annual leave when they needed to, especially for urgent matters.
remediation_action:
Issara reached out to the business, and HR investigated this case.  The management interprets Section 30 of the Labor Protection Act as follows: "..the Employer is obliged to fix the Holiday in advance for the Employee...or as agreed by the Employer and Employee." So, according to company policy, the company is obliged to plan the annual leave (holiday) for its employees in advance. The company informs employees one month in advance that they will be on leave.

Issara has recommended that Section 30 be interpreted as the employer fixing the number of holidays but not to decide when the employee will choose to take those holidays.  At the very least, there should be agreement between the employer and employee because in this case, the employees do not agree with the business unilaterally deciding when the workers will use their annual leave days.  HR responded that management may review the policy in mid-September to consider and revise it.
remediation_validation: Issara has updated the workers that the company's policy to decide when workers take annual leave is remaining unchanged but may be reconsidered at a later date.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case.  The business is maintaining its position that it can decide when workers take annual leave even though Issara has recommended that workers be given the choice of when they will take annual leave or at the least to consult and get consent from the workers when the business decides when workers will take annual leave.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for systems change
Revise the company policy on extended holiday breaks for factory-wide closures, and make it optional for workers as to whether they want to use annual leave for the additional days or whether they want to work during those days.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The issue with the relocation of 70 workers to TU. 



-There should not be any coercion to sign the relocation agreement paper. Asking worker's consent should be involved at least one recruitment focal from HR. If workers consent to move, a new Employment Contract must be issued, which requires approval by both the Thai and Myanmar Governments. The Myanmar recruitment agency and Myanmar Government Labour Attache should be informed by being provided with a list of workers moving to another factory.

**Talking points**

-Is the company planning to relocate workers? If yes, how many workers and what is the process of informing workers about this option and finding volunteers to move? 
-How and who will explain the voluntary nature of the consent form signing process? Workers reported that the supervisors already selected workers to be sent to a different company, but they haven't been asked to sign any documents and workers were also not given information about the voluntary nature of being relocated. Thus, ask the business what is the process to explain workers their options, who is involved in the communication of this plan and the relocation of workers? Explain to the business the importance of making sure the relocation of workers should be completely voluntary and that the appropriate procedures should be followed for those workers that accept being relocated.
remediation_business_steps_remaining: The Business did not take any action that was recommended by Issara.
remediation_notes: A total of 70 workers at Okeanos were reportedly compelled to move to work at another facility owned by Thai Union.  Workers reported that they were not given a choice in the matter.
remediation_action: Okeanos stated that they investigated the issue and that workers were told that moving to the other facility is voluntary.
remediation_validation: Okeano's report conflicts with worker views. Workers stated that the communication did not take place. Workers believe that the process was not voluntary, that their names were simply being picked by their supervisors, and that the group of 70 workers were only briefed on the move and the nature of the work at the other facility.
remediation_results: Okeanos and Thai Union were not willing to take further action, re-investigate, or allow workers to return to Okeanos.  Issara therefore considers the case closed unsatisfactorily. Worker reports signal risk of forced relocation among Thai Union facilities.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business to clearly communicate regarding staffing needs in other factories and solicit volunteers to move, providing comprehensive info about terms and conditions in advance of seeking consent. Then, process EC changes legally.

-The business is suggested to explain to the workers about the 75% of wages for those days where there isn't any work for the workers, for those who do not consent to move and will stay at Okeanos.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
PSM Line-3 (night shift/Pet meal processing); The workers know this line supervisor name as "Wanna-Ni", wearing green cap. 

Workers reported that their supervisor is pressuring them to complete certain target outputs per hour, and will scold them if they don't meet those targets. When workers tried to explain to her about their challenges in managing the workload, she holds a grudge against them and will punish them by sometimes sending some workers to help in other lines or will throw the trays at them. As the workers are afraid that they will get scolded by the supervisor, they don't even feel free to take toilet breaks when needed.

Recommendations:
- Investigate this matter, with worker safeguards. Supervisors should not verbally abuse the workers or throw physical objects at workers which can potentially lead to bodily harm
- Discipline the supervisor as per the business disciplinary policy. There should be a clear performance improvement plan that is monitored over time, with further disciplinary action taken if no improvement is observed.

Deadline: 7 working days
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 4 Oct 2023

K. Kung, HR, asked for the date on which the supervisor threw the tray to the workers. They will examine the CCTV footage. However, according to the information provided by Issara, they will investigate this case with many issues, including worker safeguards, and get back to us within seven working days.

DATE: 20 OCT 2023

Investigate Case:
Based on the findings of the facts It was discovered that the supervisor admitted to having a loud voice and a fierce face, but he did not speak rudely. So when speaking to workers at work, loud voices and facial expressions are used.

Following an investigation of the facts, it was discovered that the supervisor denied throwing the tray at the workers. There could have been an incident at the QC department. It was discovered that the cup contained cat food with no toppings mixed in. He then placed the cup on the tray in front of the workers. He may have placed the cup too forcefully, leading workers to believe that the supervisor intended to throw the cup at them, but it did not hit them or injure them.

Solution:
HR trained the supervisor in accordance with guidelines for managing the use of ethical labor and closely monitored the supervisor's behavior to determine whether there was a change or not so that the incident did not reoccur. Have the supervisor at higher levels and workers in the area report directly to HR if the supervisor's behavior does not improve so that the incident does not happen again. If it happens again, If it happens again, you will be punished in accordance with the company's policies.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that their supervisor is pressuring them to complete certain target outputs per hour, and will scold them if they don't meet those targets. When workers tried to explain their situation, she will punish them by sometimes sending some workers to help in other lines or will throw the trays at them.
remediation_action: HR investigated and found that the supervisor sometimes speaks loudly to workers with an angry expression. HR trained the supervisor and is closely monitoring the supervisor's behavior.
remediation_validation: The line supervisor has been moved elsewhere and the workers now have new supervisors but they have raised the production targets so workers still feel pressured to meet the higher targets.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue.  Workers confirmed their situation has improved because the supervisor has been moved to another shift. However, the business investigated the wrong shift and therefore didn't identify the issue and the supervisor involved.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Performance appraisal of line supervisors should include worker feedback as part of a 360 appraisal

Line:                        Sushi
Shift:                        Night
Line supervisor:        Thai lady (Tom boy, she has a mole on her nose)

She, Shwe Wine Hlaing, reported that she was physically abused again. The incident happened on 11 June at Sushi line while working. At 11pm, the workers were at Sushi line were about to have meal break. SWH was given a large amount of shrimps by the line supervisor who abused her. Some of the shrimp dropped. She was asked to pick them up. She refused to do it as it was not her fault and she wanted to have a meal break. That’s when the line supervisor hit her arm with shrimp basket. It was witnessed by many other workers. When she told the line supervisor that she would report it to HR, the supervisor replied “I don’t care anyone. You can report it to anywhere you want”. 
SWH said, “Although I know that HR would not resolve the issue properly, I still want HR knows about the abuse.” I know that I have been targeted for so many times and no serious action was taken by HR. I have been asked to move across the different lines although I meet the target. I hope that Issara could help me. 
She thinks that it will be good for her to work at Cut Size lines (day shift), to get away from abuse.

call_details.next_steps: Issara to raise the issue with the business.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue because the business has issued a verbal warning to the supervisor and has moved her to a different line so the workers affected do not need to deal with her poor treatment anymore.  At the same time, the business didn't respond directly to the supervisor's discriminatory behavior towards Burmese workers and moving her to another line may result in another group of workers being treated poorly if she doesn't improve her behavior.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker called to report the behavior of the supervisor from the Production line called - RP - Pelu site. The supervisor ("P Dam") treats workers poorly, (i) Workers' sick leave not always being approved as requested, she makes the decisions based on her mood and relationship with that certain worker. (ii) In other production lines, according to the business policy, each worker has to do cleaning for 15 days in rotation; however, in her line she assigned the workers to do cleaning as she wants. If some worker takes sick leave and she does not like that person, she will assign that worker to do the cleaning for as many days as she wants. (iii) She discriminates against nationalities by saying you Burmese people do not follow the rules, only Thai people follow the rules and policy. Workers added that they have reported the issue of this supervisor via grievance boxes, however, they have not noticed any improvement.

Recommendations for remediation:
The business should conduct an investigation regarding the supervisor’s behavior, with worker safeguards to ensure that workers don’t face retaliation afterwards 
Based on the investigation, take disciplinary action against the supervisor and develop an improvement plan; identify the number of workers who were denied sick leave and remediate (return pay if it was considered unpaid leave)
The business should investigate why reports about this supervisor put into the grievance box went unheeded 
Communicate to the workers the actions that the business will be taking to solve the issue
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Business response: 
(i) The HR department randomly had 15 workers at the processing line where Mr. Dam was the supervisor to ask if the supervisor had ever refused to allow the workers to take sick leave. All workers randomly asked said that the supervisor never refused sick leave but only asked about the symptoms of illness.

The HR department and the factory manager called the supervisor "Dam" to ask more questions. Dam insists that he has never denied sick leave but only asked about the symptoms of illness with concern for the workers. However, Dam admits that he has some loud conversations with the workers but never scolded or spoke badly to them in this regard. The factory manager has verbally warned Dam about proper communication and dialogue with workers as well as to adjust the tone of speech not to be loud in order not to misunderstand workers. 

All supervisors are communicated, trained, and emphasized on communication methods. Continuously, treating workers appropriately and the company has always been given importance. 


(ii) The business noted that the cleaning process of the production area is part of the scope of duties and responsibilities of the workers. All workers are informed from the first day they join the company.

However, the supervisor will arrange manpower in each process to suit the amount of work by considering the amount of work, the number of workers, skills and abilities, the performance of each workers; workers are notified the workers at least 1 week in advance.

In addition, the production department is considering a change in the form of assignments. All workers are required to switch roles throughout the process, including cleaning the production line. All workers will be switched every 15 days, which the supervisors and factory managers plan to communicate to workers during 16-20 May and start implementation from 1 June onwards


(iii) After investigation, the business found that it received complaints from workers on April 18, 2022, and the HR department responded to the complaints by clarification through the company's public relations board at the canteen on April 28, 2022.

However, the HR department and supervisors will have an appointment to communicate with all the processing line workers about the assignment of cleaning work during 16-20 May.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that his supervisor treats workers poorly, such as 1) not approving sick leave for some workers and basing her decisions on her mood; 2) assigning some workers to do the cleaning duties more than other workers if she doesn't like them, instead of assigning duties by rotation, and 3) discriminating against Burmese workers, saying "you Burmese people do not follow the rules, only Thai people follow the rules and policy." The worker added that he had reported the issues with his supervisor via the company's grievance boxes but had not noticed any improvement.
remediation_action: The business investigated and reported that HR had randomly interviewed some workers working under this supervisor and none reported that their sick leave requests had been denied.  However, the business noted that this supervisor sometimes shouted at the workers, for which she has received a verbal warning.  In regards to assignment of duties, it is the supervisor's discretion to assign various roles, including cleaning to the workers but the business will change this to an automatic rotation of duties every 15 days starting in June 2022.  The business didn't respond to how the supervisor was discriminatory towards Burmese workers.  The business also stated that it had received the complaint about the cleaning duties and that it had posted on the bulletin board the company's policy about assignment of duties earlier; however, it will announce the new arrangement of automatic rotation of duties during the week of May 16-20.
remediation_validation: The worker provided an update saying that the supervisor had been moved to another different line.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue because the business has issued a verbal warning to the supervisor and has moved her to a different line so the workers affected do not need to deal with her poor treatment anymore.  At the same time, the business didn't respond directly to the supervisor's discriminatory behavior towards Burmese workers and moving her to another line may result in another group of workers being treated poorly if she doesn't improve her behavior.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for systems change:
Ensure capacity building training for supervisors include the correct implementation of the sick leave request process and the non-discrimination policy.  Issara can provide this training to the supervisors and the HR staff.

Workers also confirmed that they have seen the QR code. Since then, Issara has not received a complaint from the workers.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: the business has appointed two focal persons (P Kung and P Saung)from HR for workers to approach in case of having any issue. However, according to workers' feedback, the focal persons are not available most of the time since they have many meetings. Also, many workers indicated that they do not know to whom they should report if they have an issue. Workers also shared that there have to get permission from, line leader, supervisors, senior supervisors, and office translator to see this assigned person which is very hard for the workers.

Talking points: explain to the business what is the feedback from workers and the challenges they face to access the grievance mechanism. And provide recommendations for system change.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business to revise the assigned HR focal person and appoint other focal persons at HR to handled workers queries or to indicate what is the availability of the focal persons and have a backup for when they are not available. 

-Communication. Effectively communicate to workers what the grievance mechanisms are, the contact information of focal points and availability, actions that will be taken by the business for investigations and safeguarding, and timeframes. 

-Credible and safe grievance mechanisms should include transparency and safeguards for all workers.  

-Training and planning sessions with Issara and HR on strengthening grievance mechanisms, then broader training for line supervisors and others.
systems_change_business_steps_taken:
In order to reduce the workers from reaching out to HR for several kinds of information and issues, the business has introduced a QR code where the workers can learn the process for each inquiry or issue.  

Workers reported seeing a newly announced QR code. Since then, Issara has not received an additional report from the workers.
systems_change_business_steps_remaining: -Training and planning sessions with Issara and HR on strengthening grievance mechanisms, then broader training for line supervisors and others.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
#Issue 1
The business should immediately investigate and revise their lunch break schedule. The break schedule should be aligned with the labor protection act (there should be a break after 5 consecutive hours) 

-The business to immediately investigate these specific lines.  
-The business to make sure that all workers have rest after 5 hours of consecutive work.

1 week.

#Issue 2. (13-October). ID - 11457
Workers should not be asked to work for more than 5 hours without having a break. The business should be clear with line supervisors (and others responsible of break times) that workers should have break time no later than completing 5 hours of work. If this isn't followed, the business should take disciplinary actions towards those not following this regulation.

Context: Workers from a working line have been working for more than 5 consecutive hours. Workers indicated that their lunch break is very early so the working hours in the afternoon are more than 5 consecutively. This is happening at the Fish Peeling Line. Workers have their lunch break at 9 am and work till 4 pm without a break. 

Talking Points ; 

- Ask the business about their lunch break schedule in general and specific to this line.

-Explain to the business that workers should not be working more than 5 hours without a break 

-Provide recommendations for remediation and system change. When the business revise their lunch break schedule we can suggest the business to:
1. Have the lunch break of 1 hour later in the day 
or
2. Have 2 breaks one in the morning and one in the afternoon (but the total time of breaks should not be less than 1 hour) NOTE: To arrange a new schedule there should be an agreement between the employer and employee, so the business should consult with the workers how they want to take the break and come to an agreement. 

#Issue 2. (13-October). ID - 11457
Provide the feedback that the business has not taken Issara recommendations for the system change. This is a systemic issue that requires different actions from the business to address the root cause of it. 

-Share with the business that the workers from this line have been working more than 5 hours consecutively before having the lunch break, which is a violation of the law according to Act B.E.2541, Article 27; 

On a Working Day, an Employer shall arrange a rest period during work for an Employee of not less than one hour per day after the Employee has been working for not more than five consecutive hours. An Employer and Employee may agree in advance that each rest period may be less than one hour but the total rest period per day shall not be less than one hour. Whereas an Employer and Employee agree to specify rest periods during work other than paragraph one, the agreement shall be applicable only if it is more favorable to the Employee.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
25-Sep-2020
Business response 
The business admitted that there was a break issue (working
more than 5 hours before taking a break) because during that period they had an external audit visit to the factory. The workers need to prepare the line for the visit which caused some workers to work more than 5 hours before a break. For the resolution, The business scheduled the break for this line at 11.30 a.m., and in case if there is a visitor, they will take turns to take a break.

9 Nov,2020
 HR coordinated with the line to investigate the issue in the fish-peeling line, where the workers have to work longer than 5 hours before taking break. They found that there was an issue in the dau shift when the audit visit. There were 2 workers who reported that they have to work more than 5 hours before taking a break, to prepare the line, but this was happening a long time ago. After that, the supervisor arranges that break time at 11.00 a.m. for workers who clock in at 6.30 and 7.00 a.m. which is not over 5 hours. 

Business Solution: 
- Fish-peeling line in PF arranged the same break time at 11.00 a.m. for workers who clock-in at 6.30 and 7.30 a.m., The workers in another line will rotate to take a break which starts from 10.30, 11.00, and 11.30 a.m. No worker will work more than 5 hours under this arrangement. If there is an audit visit, the workers will take turns to take a break, which is not over 5 hours time cap. 

18 Nov-2020
Workers from Par Mint Aung and PF3 Line stated that the lunch break issue is improved. Now in these two lines, their lunch break is not too early and not too late. The latest time is 12:00

call_details.description: Call to report an issue

A worker, San Lwin Oo from Cal-Comp(Petchaburi), Factory 10, Line FATP-3 was caught smoking in the toilet on 23rd March. And the next day, he was brought to HR Office and had to sign warning letter. So the client tried to go back and work to his line but unfortunately, the foreman said that he is not allowed to work and asked him to go back home. After that the sub-recruiter ( 1-PS) brought him home and take his photo of passport and said it is for resigning from job. Since then he is not allowed to go work. Actually smoking is not a major offences that worthy to dismiss according to cal-comp policy. So the worker would like to ask Issara for help.

This is a follow up call to Unfair Dismissal client from Cal-Comp Petchaburi and it is to informed him the business decision and check if he know this policy earlier. The client said he aware that it is a non-smoking area but he didn't know it is immediate dismissal and in the past, no one was dismissed immediately for smoking. Presently he is trying to apply job in Iron factory nearby.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case given that the worker smoked in an area near highly flammable materials and the business is standing by its decision to dismiss the worker.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: A worker, San Lwin Oo from Cal-Comp(Petchaburi), Factory 10, Line FATP-3, ID - C17 C708 was caught smoking in the toilet on 23rd March. And the next day, he was brought to HR Office and had to sign warning letter. On that day when he checked with HR staff if the paper he signed is warning letter or dismissal letter, the HR staff clearly stated that it is just warning letter. So the worker tried to go back and work to his line but unfortunately, the foreman said that he is not allowed to work and asked him to go back home. After that the sub-recruiter ( 1-PS) brought him home and take his photo of passport and said it is for resigning from job. Since then he is not allowed to go work. According to the worker, smoking is not a major offences that worthy to dismiss according to cal-comp policy. 

Recommendations for remediation 
-Clarify the status of the worker.  Has he been dismissed?  Under what grounds?  Is smoking grounds for immediate dismissal according to company policy?   Has he been issued a warning?  Why has he not been permitted to return to work?
-If there was a miscommunication between HR and the foreman, conduct an investigation as to why this happened.
-Communicate clearly with the worker about his status, whether it is a dismissal or a warning
-If he was given a warning but mistakenly kept from returning to work, the business should immediately inform him to return to work and pay for the wages of the days he wasn’t allowed to work.
-If he was dismissed in compliance with company disciplinary policy, it is suggested that the business issue him with a job changeable cancellation letter in order to help the work to be able to find a new employer in Thailand 


Talking points; Please share the details of the story ( and ask the following questions). 

-When the worker was called to the HR office, he was informed that he was receiving a warning and was asked to sign the written warning.  Is HR aware that the foreman communicated a different message saying he was dismissed and did not allow him to return to work since March 23rd?  Why was there a discrepancy in the communication provided by HR and the foreman?
-What is the business policy for immediate dismissal? Is smoking in the toilet grounds for immediate dismissal? How are these policies being communicated with the workers? 
-What is the current status of the worker?  Has he been dismissed?  If so, what has HR communicated to the worker? 
-Ask the business not to report the dismissal of this worker to DOE until there is a clear investigation and the company can guarantee that the company policies, buyers' CoC, and workers' rights are followed.
-If there was any investigation that has taken place, what was the investigation result? What has the business done to prevent such issues in the future? Any communication? 

Time frame within 1 day.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara raised this issue with the business, the CSR team member who joined the meeting was not aware of this issue, the business agreed to conduct the investigation and get back to us.

CSR, shared the findings of the investigation, which revealed that, according to the rules and regulations, the workers smoked in the bathroom, which is near to the storage of flammable materials or objects containing fuel. And this worker was aware that this area was restricted previously. So this is a very serious case, and the disciplinary action is dismissal, according to the disciplinary measure.

Issara is checking with the business.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that he was caught smoking in the toilet on 23rd March 2022. The next day, he was called to the HR Office and had to sign a warning letter. He reported back to work but the foreman said that he is not allowed to work and asked him to go back home. After that, a broker that arranged for his recruitment asked for his passport photo saying it was for his resignation process.  He understands the company policy that smoking in a non-smoking zone is not grounds for immediate dismissal, and wants to know why he has been dismissed.
remediation_action: Issara raised this issue with the business, and the business agreed to conduct the investigation and get back to us.  The findings of the investigation revealed that, according to the rules and regulations, the workers smoked in the bathroom, which is near the storage of flammable materials and fuel. And this worker was aware that this area was a restricted non-smoking area. So this is a very serious case that could have led to a workplace fire, and the disciplinary action is dismissal.
