remediation_results: Issara is closing this case given that the worker smoked in an area near highly flammable materials and the business is standing by its decision to dismiss the worker.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: -The business is recommended to communicate to all workers, including supervisors and foremen, what the company rules and regulations are regarding smoking in the working area and the disciplinary actions to be taken towards those that violate the policy.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
This call is from Zu Zu, a worker from TUF (Frying shrimp Line) reported that since April 2023, the business didn't allow workers to keep prescription medicine and water bottles in their lockers outside the production line. Workers that need to take medicine and drink purified room-temperature water for health reasons are finding this regulation difficult to follow. The business often does unannounced locker inspections, which they did on 16th June, 2023. If they find prohibited items such as sweets, tiger balm, lipstick, or water bottles in the locker, the worker will be suspended for 3 days. If they find betel nut, cigarettes, drugs, or knives, the worker will be dismissed. The worker had to skip taking medicine that she supposed to take every 4 hours. Some of her friends that need to drink warm water had to drink iced water from the tank. The worker would like more flexibility regarding prohibited items.

TPs:
- Why does the business prohibit some items from being kept in lockers by the workers?
- Why has this list been updated in April 2023 to include prohibition of medicine and water bottles?
- If workers cannot keep certain items in their lockers, is there somewhere else that they can keep important items such as medicine that they have to take during the day?
- What is the policy on disciplinary measures if certain items are found in a worker's locker?

Recommendations:
- The business should allow access to necessary items such as medicine and water bottles since workers need to take them for health reasons, whether it is in their lockers or an alternative place where such items can be stored safely and easily accessible by workers
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Root Cause:
- With the company being a food factory therefore must comply with various relevant criteria such as strictly since the beginning of production of products such as Methodology for safe food production (GMP), Food Safety Management System (HACCP), and customer requirements which are International standards for consumers to eat quality and safe food.
-During April 2023, the company reviewed the aforementioned standards and practices by having a training and public relations campaign for employees Including reviewing regulations on the use of lockers, which is considered One of the requirements, emphasizing the prohibited items entering the company. Items that cannot be brought are stored in the locker, including the storage of medicines and water bottles.
- Medicines: according to the regulations, establishing codes of practice on the carrying of drugs and prohibiting the storage of drugs
in the locker, where, if ill, the employee can ask for permission from the supervisor to come in for service at the infirmary which has 
professional nurses and basic medicine as required by law to provide services to employees, except for heart disease and asthma medicines, which are considered a group of medicines that are permitted for employees to carry. By employees bring medicine to be registered at the infirmary. Based on these requirements, the drug is considered a foreign thing that can be mixed with water and food products. which if slipping may contaminate the product which may be harmful to customers who eat contaminated food.
- Food and beverages: according to the regulations, there are guidelines for prohibiting employees from bringing
All kinds of food, beverages, glass bottles, candy, chewing gum, gloves, or equipment used in the production area, come to store in the locker to prevent animal carriers of germs such as cockroaches, flies, and rats from entering different areas and may cause contamination of the product
- Measures to randomly check lockers is one of the steps to control, prevent, deter, and bring items that are forbidden to be brought into the factory or stored in a locker including actions that may result in contamination with the products, which the company has communicated with employees and conducted random checks of lockers continuously. Employees would be aware of random checks but would not know the schedule and without prior notice on the day of random inspection, the company notified and invited the locker owners and supervisors to the locker area by asking the locker owner who opened, which the company checked in front of such employees.


Corrective/Prevention:
- On 25 July 2023, communicated further under Food Safety & Quality Culture to make employees aware of the production of safe food by the emphasis on medicine and bottle storage water, including random measures check-in such activities as well


K. Sukrid, HR, responded that HR made verbal and written announcements about the locker measurement to all employees. He will share with us the written communication that is posted on the locker room bulletin board.


DATE: 5 Oct 2023

K Prad emailed the corrective action table as per the link below.
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/18w_cHkTFDYU98DN9MkRiwKnAHvjHfj9g

- Communication by relevant departments and supervisors: During April 2023, the production department and product Refresh Training activities have been organized for employees in every department of the product production division and related to product production by inviting employees to a meeting in the conference room with the lecturer is the person responsible for GMP work including various quality systems at the company. The company holds and practices this training including discussion and opportunities for employees.
Q&A and review of locker use regulations, which is considered one of the requirements, emphasizing the items prohibited from entering the company, the things that cannot be kept in the locker including storing medicines and water bottles.

- A nursing room is provided in the common area of the company: TUF Rong Kung has provided a room. Nurses provide services to employees who need services, such as consulting about illnesses. Basic steps to receive medicine, treat disease, provide first aid, deposit medicine for personal illnesses, including a hot water service point, etc. The nursing room is open all the time, 24 hours a day on business days, with professional nurses on both shifts continuously. The nursing room is located on the 2nd floor of the building, which is the same building as the production building. It is the same area as the cafeteria which is an area for selling and storing food. For employees who have rice boxes from home to eat at the company, including drinking water points and a dining area for all employees.

- How to get to the nursing room: From the locker area, employees can use the stairs from the production area or stairs outside the building going up to the 2nd floor of the building is the cafeteria area and keep walking on the left, approximately 20 meters further, will be the location of the nursing room.
remediation_notes: Issara received a report that since April 2023, the business didn't allow workers to keep prescription medicine and water bottles in their lockers outside the production line but many workers need to take medicine and drink purified warm water several times daily for health reasons.
remediation_action:
The business responded that it was following various food safety standards, which include prohibition of the storage of water bottles and medicines in workers' lockers for reasons that it may contaminate the food being processed in the production line. 
This has already been communicated to workers but the business has made an additional announcement regarding this food safety policy. After the worker update saying he hadn't heard the announcement, HR made verbal and written announcements again about the locker measurement to all employees.

In the latest update, the business will check how the worker can take the medicine as needed and is able to access the clinic where the medicine is supposed to be kept, which is far from the production line. 

The business has set up a nursing room, which is close to the cafeteria and upstairs from the locker area. It is staffed by nurses for both shifts, accessible 24 hours a day. The workers can keep their medicine there, and a hot water service point is provided as well.
remediation_validation:
Regarding the locker issues, a worker updated Issara saying that he saw the written announcement about items prohibited from being stored in the lockers but it is not very clear and also there was no the verbal announcement.

In the latest update, the worker understands the new policy and will go to the nursing room to keep her medicine there.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue.  The workers understand the new policy and can access their medicines at the new nursing room.

remediation_issara_recommendation: Context: The issue with 15 days of OT wage being paid 15 days after the payday. Workers that resigned and go back to their home countries do not have access to their Thai accounts, so the business is using informal channels to pay the OT wages to workers after they go back to Myanmar.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Business explanation on their payment system (Aug 2019): for daily wage workers, the payment is done 15 days delayed because GFPT needs that time to check sick leave, absences, or other leave and then GPFT can make the correct payment. And for OT for monthly workers, they need 1 month to check with line supervisors if the OT hours are correct. Line supervisors have records of approved working hours. GPFT does not use the scanning system because there is no way for them to cross-check if the workers leave the factory after fishing working or not. When workers resign they can get their money through a friend or family member, GFPT recognizes that this is not the best way to do it but that is the practice right now. Issara recommended GFPT to reconsider their payment system and to find ways to pay workers on time. GFPT will discuss internally with the HQ to find a way to improve efficiency.

Since several months have passed and there has no improvement, this issue is considered to be closed at this point.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that Seafresh announced that starting on January 28, there will be more days when the factory shuts down due to no production, and has decided workers will use their annual leave for these days. The workers are not happy about this and would rather get paid 75% of wages if the employer cannot provide a regular job. The workers are pushed to use annual leave, and new workers will need to borrow annual leave from next year to use now.

Recommendations:
- The business should allow workers to choose when to use annual leave and at least get workers' agreement if the business is going to propose specific dates that workers should use their annual leave
remediation_notes: Workers reported that Seafresh announced that starting on January 28, there will be more days when the factory shuts down due to no production, and has decided workers will use their annual leave for these days. The workers are not happy about this and would rather get paid 75% of wages if the employer cannot provide a regular job. The workers are pushed to use annual leave, and new workers will need to borrow annual leave from next year to use now.
remediation_action:
Issara raised this with Seafresh, and the business HR stated that Seafresh is currently experiencing problems with low customer orders and a lack of raw materials. They are attempting to get all employees paid, so this announcement applies to all employees in Seafresh (all staff and all workers), and they have decided when workers will use those 6 annual leave days. Furthermore, according to the LPA. HR also noted that the Labor Protection Act allows the employer to fix holidays in advance for the employee.

Issara escalated this issue to the Managing Director.  The MD noted that production at Seafresh is currently only at 50-60% and so the business will have to reduce the production days.  It’s a difficult time for the company and it’s requesting the workers that they use annual leave so that at least they can get 100% pay rather than just 75%. Seafresh is mindful that they pay workers fully because cost of living has increased and they don't want workers to have money issues (they even increased wages for workers by 5% in Oct 2022). Usually, Seafresh will allow workers to choose when they would like to take annual leave and will in most cases approve their leave requests.  But this is a special year and the company has decided to prioritize workers getting full pay and have asked the workers to use annual leave days when the factory has no production.  If there are more days of no production after annual leave days are used up, then Seafresh will use 75% compensation pay for those days. Seafresh will meet with workers to explain why the business is doing this and hear from them as well, informally surveying their preferences.
remediation_validation: Workers have been updated on this business decision, and that the business will not revert on its decision despite Issara's recommendations.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue.  Seafresh has stated that this is decision it has had to make this year in order to not operate at a loss. Seafresh decided the annual leave days for all employees across the board, and has done this to pay full wages to workers rather than 75%.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
In some production lines, the line supervisors implicitly pressure the workers to reach the daily target within 8 hours by promising them OT hours if the workers hit the target but actually the supervisors didn't give them OT even when the workers reached the target.

TPs:
- What daily production targets are set for workers, how does this affect their pay or working hours (i.e. is OT work given based on ability to hit targets during the regular shift?), and how are these targets communicated to the workers?

Recommendations:
- If OT hours are offered to workers based on some performance criteria, the criteria should be fair and the system the business uses to select workers for OT should be clearly communicated to, and understood by workers
- Investigate how workers are feeling pressure to reach targets, whether the conditions for getting OT hours is being to apply this pressure, and why the conditions (giving OT work if workers meet the target) are not being met
- Communicate clearly to workers, verbally and in writing, the business' practice of having production targets, how they are set, and that they are not coercive

The issues related to workload, line supervisors and interpreter behavior: 

The day shift from production calls Yakik where the worker slices chicken meat and makes the skewer. There are 6 lines and each line has around 50-60 workers which are supervised by 2 line supervisors. The new workers were set to work in a line and they will be moved out to another line when they could do work better so, the new coming workers are easy to be target and closely monitor by the line supervisors. 

The worker raised that all the workers in Yakik generally were oppressed by the line supervisors to complete the target as they called "Yort", in an hour workers need to finish 100-150 kg meats (depend on which part of the chicken they do the skewer) and if workers can't complete the task the line supervisor will shout and scold to them by calling their ID number and sometimes even threat to the workers "If you can't do the job well just go back to your home country, please resign". Additionally, to make the skewer there is a rule to weigh the meat properly not to be over or less than the determined standard but to follow the rule workers can not complete the target as they want. 

Here are the consequences and difficulties workers face:
1. To complete the target, workers (mostly new workers because they have not gotten used to with the job yet) do the skewers without the proper weight as it takes time and when it were caught by the line supervisor, the line supervisor asked workers to sign on warning letter. 
2. When workers can't complete the target, the line supervisor shouts out their ID, scolds the workers by saying "If you can't do the job well just go back to your home country, please resign" and sometimes insult workers on the microphone. Moreover, workers were also asked to sign on the warning letter.  
3. By receiving the warning letter, workers'annual bonuses will be cut off and workers could be terminated if they received many warning letters.
4. Workers feel depressed and frightened from the managing of the line supervisors in oppressing the workers to complete the target. And some workers even skip the toilet break even if they need to because they are afraid the target will not be completed. 
5. Most workers dare not to raise issues because they are concerned about being targeted by the line supervisors. Only when the workers decide to go back home, they dare to raise the case. 

Due to #5, some workers used to raise the issue to the interpreter for her to reach out to the HR but it seems less effective and worker thought the interpreter don't deliver their complaint to the HR. The interpreter's behavior is rude and careless. The interpreter said everyone can do why you can't, and blame the worker. The worker feels disappointed and never wants to raise the interpreter again. The interpreter name Chiva. 

What the worker wants: No oppression to the workers to complete the target, treat the workers fairly with respect; no shouting, scolding and don't ask workers to resign. And the interpreter should change her behavior by treating the worker nicely and be helpful.

The worker called to inform o&e to withdraw the case as she had already moved to another line. 
The worker said, she had told the line supervisor that she couldn't work to complete the target as the line supervisor want so now they moved her to another line that she can work without the oppression of the target but there is no OT available. The worker mentioned that she is no longer at the reported line, worker request not to raise the issue to the business.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case because the worker has requested we not raise this issue with the business.

Context: The issue with fifty workers who were involuntarily relocated to TUF from Okeanos wanting to resign from TUF as they are not happy with their new working conditions. They added that they wanted to make sure that they received job changeable cancellation letter to find the new job somewhere else. 

Issara recommendations:

-It is strongly recommended for the business to provide departing workers cancellation letters that state the reason for departure as the business cannot provide sufficient work for them, which will allow the workers than to find new employers. 

-it is recommended for the business to make sure all these fifty workers who were involuntarily relocated have the options whether they want to continue working with TUF, return to Okeanos or want to find another job.

Talking Points:

-Please ask the business how many workers from this group have already left and what was the remark that was given in their job cancellation letter if there are some workers that have already left. 
-Please suggest the business to make the correction if some workers have already received improper job cancellation letter. 
-Please share with the business that this is the responsibility of the Okeanos and TUF to make sure these fifty workers have proper job cancellation letter to continue work in Thailand. (If needed).
-Please share with the business that several workers who left TUF are ending up becoming undocumented and working with improper documentation such as invalid and incorrect work permit. This situation is happening because workers are having difficulties to find an employer that accepts the cancellation letter provided by TUF, so workers have to find an employer that do not follow the right procedures to hire workers.  
-Explain the process that the employer can follow to amend the cancellation letter remark, to help workers be able to apply for another job. 
-Explain to the employer the other way they can help workers. By signing the 'Certificate of Responsibility for expenses from hiring foreign workers of former employers’. Share with the business for the supporting documents that can help the workers to apply for a new employer. 


Conditions for changing employers for MOU workers.

1. The employer terminated / the employer died.
*2. The employer goes bankrupt. Or reduce production capacity because there is no work for the workers
3. The employer or the employer representative or the supervisor has abused or attacked the employee
4. The employer does not comply with the employment contract.
5. Employees work in working conditions or working environments that may cause damage to employees’ life, body, mind or health.
*This is the preferred reason to be given, that the business has no work for the workers
remediation_business_steps_taken: The business did not take any recommendations that Issara had provided for this case. The business responded that the workers consented to be relocated to another TUF facility. Issara escalated to the Strategic Partners, however, no changes had been made. The business did not even agree to issue a job changeable cancellation letter for those workers who wanted discontinuing working for TUF.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business to make sure that the workes who are being relocated have full consent and voluntary. TUF is also recommended to have their own voluntary consent form and pre-departure communication to explain the working condition and also to seek the voluntariness. 

-The business to clearly communicate with the workers about the process of receiving job cancellation letter including the time frame.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
When the Issara team conducted canteen outreach and housing outreach in August 2022, many workers did not approach Issara staff in front of the Seafresh interpreter, HR staff, and dorm in-charge. Many workers felt uncomfortable when Issara staff approached them; they were guarded in their speech and did not respond openly and when Seafresh staff were nearby, the workers hid their face from the Seafresh staff. When Issara staff had moments with the workers without being observed by Seafresh staff, some workers said that they had heard second-hand information from previous workers that the line supervisors and HR staff did not like workers contacting Issara and that workers were targeted afterwards for doing so.  That's why they felt uncomfortable interacting with the Issara team.

Talking points:
- Is HR aware that the workers are feeling this way?
- How is HR communicating to workers to make it clear to them that Seafresh has a non-retaliation policy and that the business protects the right of workers to use worker voice channels, including Issara's?

Recommendations:
- Post a fresh announcement and make a verbal announcement to all workers that all have the right to express themselves without fear of retaliation by using any worker voice or grievance channels, including Issara's.
- Train all line supervisors about the non-retaliation policy and the disciplinary measures that will be taken if any supervisor attempts to suppress worker voice.  Use case studies to illustrate how and in what circumstance workers might be afraid to use worker voice channels, and how supervisors should promote rather than suppress worker voice.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A workers from the Ban Kyu line reported that the business doesn't usually give OT break even when they have to work 3 OT hours. Personally for him, on 22nd and 24th November, he had to work 3 OT hours OT but he didn't get any OT break. He said this is a common issue especially in this line. As the workers don't get an OT break, they can't even have a snack while working 3 hours consecutively so this can have a negative impact on their health.

Recommendations:
- According to the law, workers are entitled to 20 minutes break for any OT work exceeding 2 hours.  This should be implemented properly by the line supervisors and monitored by management.
- Line supervisors should be re-trained for proper implementation; disciplinary measures to be taken by the company as per its disciplinary policy
- HR and production to communicate this to all workers, verbally and in writing, so that it is clear to both workers and line supervisors about the required break time.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 30 Nov 2023

K. Chonticha, VP - HRM&GA, will investigate this production line, and if this occurs, PFI will ensure that workers receive a 20-minute break for any OT work that exceeds 2 hours. In addition, the supervisor would receive a verbal/written warning in accordance with the disciplinary measure and would be re-trained for proper implementation. And HR will make it clear to all employees about the break time before beginning the OT. She will get back to us next week with the corrective action.

DATE: 14 Dec 2023
K. Chonticha, HRM emailed the corrective action as follows.

Root Cause:
1. According to company policy and practice, workers must rest for 20 minutes before working on OT for more than 2 hours.
2. According to the investigation with the production, the OT work was scheduled for 2 hours on that day, but the machinery broke down and the OT work time had to be increased by 1 hour, so the production did not plan for rest time on that day.

Corrective Action:
HR discussed and trained production/line supervisors on the importance of communication with workers. In the case of OT work was planned but did not occur as planned. If this is the case, the production will arrange for workers to rest appropriately during OT time without interfering with their work.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that they don't get a break even when working 3 hours of overtime even though the law requires that breaks are provided to workers when overtime exceeds 2 hours.
remediation_action:
The business investigated and found that there was one day where OT was scheduled for two hours but the machinery broke down and so the OT time was increased by one hour. HR trained the line supervisors on the importance of arranging for a break period if the OT time gets longer than planned and to communicate this clearly with workers.

The business has issued an internal memo announcement (in Thai) that workers must be given a 20-minute break when working more than two hours of OT.
remediation_validation: Workers reported that since the business investigated this matter, the issue has recurred, on Dec 23, 2023 and January 16, 2024 where workers had to work 3 overtime hours with no break.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
- Conduct periodic training so that line supervisors understand all the company policies and procedures and can implement them properly
- Monitor line supervisor performance on a regular basis, with direct feedback from workers

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with three supervisors ( 2 assistant and 1 senior, ลำใย  LB2 and เรณู  LB4 blue cap and เพียงพอ จัยจัย with green cap) being abusive with the workers. A group of workers has reported being constantly and verbally abusive with aggressive behavior and rude words by the supervisors. 

Talking Points. 
-Workers reported to Issara that they have reported the issues they are facing with these two assistant supervisors to the senior supervisor but there has been no improvement in these supervisors’ behavior. What is the role of the senior supervisors if some workers report such issues? Is the senior supervisor responsible to report workers' grievances to HR, or how should they handle such cases?
-For the past few years, workers’ grievances have been well handled by SEAPAC, and Issara noticed the improvement throughout those years, so we would like to know what has been the process in the past and if anything has changed in the grievance mechanisms processes from the company.  
-Does the company have any systems or processes to assess workers' experiences at the workplace, such as surveys or open talks? 
-Are there any activities or any training that the business has not been able to conduct recently which might have led supervisors to behave poorly? 
-Is HR aware of this issue? And if so, how is it being handled? 

Recommendations
-The business shall conduct an immediate investigation about the three reported supervisors. 
-The investigation should make sure safeguards for the workers are in place and that there would be no risk of retaliation. The investigation should be confidential, meaning that workers’ identities should not be exposed in order to mitigate the risks of being targeted. 
-The business shall take disciplinary action based on the business policy and the investigation results. 
-Workers should be treated humanely and this should be followed by all company staff. 


Time Frame - 2 weeks.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue # 1.
Context: The issue with the recruitment fees being charged by the recruitment agency representative who is stationed outside of the Cal-Comp factory area. The person who collects the money is being known as a huanna-sub (sub-supervisor in English). The worker reported that they have contacted a person whose name was included in a job announcement to work at Cal-comp. After contacting the phone number from the announcement, the worker was asked to contact another person, a huanna-sub (sub-supervisor in English) who told the worker that she has to pay 2,500 THB for the job application.  

The worker did not mention the channel through which the announcement about the job vacancy was done nor the name of the huanna-sub who asked her to pay. In addition to that, the worker added that one of her friends was charged 3500 THB to get a job in Cal-Comp in the past. NOTE: So far, Issara knows about 2 workers being impacted however there could be many more.

Recommendations for remediation: 
-The business to do an immediate investigation to assess the number of impacted workers and identify the people involved in the recruitment process that has been charging workers. Safeguards should be in place throughout the investigation, and workers should not be targeted by the sub-supervisor or recruitment agency representative. 
-The investigation should also cover the staff from the recruitment agencies to identify the root causes of the issue and understand who was involved in the collection of the money.
- Actions should be taken towards those who collected the money, and the business should clarify with the recruitment agency that no fees should be charged to workers and what are the consequences for not following that policy, such as termination of the contract or disciplinary actions if those involved are Cal-Comp  employees. 
-As part of the investigation and remediation process, the business shall assess how much money new workers have paid and reimbursed them those recruitment fees. 

-The business should set a plan of action with the recruitment agency involved, such as revision of the contract and the penalties for not following the company policy about “zero recruitment fees for workers”, and the actions the agency will take to avoid this from happening again. 

-The business should cross check through different means with the recruitment agency and workers being recruited, how are the services being provided to job seekers, what is the communication like about the job and the recruitment process, etc. 
-One way of conducting the investigation and a vetting process is for Cal-comp to check all the announcements about job vacancies and verify that there are no fees being charged, that the process is handled legally and ethically and that all the recruitment agencies being used work professionally. 

Past history of this case:

Last year (2020) there was a similar case reported and the business conducted investigations for all issues and remediated the impacted workers which is considered a good step made by the company to address issues with recruitment. However, the process took several months and the business did not share with Issara the details of the last investigation conducted regarding walk-in workers being asked to make monetary donations to the Thai RA staff, and only one worker received compensation for that issue. In addition, the company did not follow Issara's recommendation on system change to have communication sessions with all workers and Thai RAs about the company policy of recruitment fees.

Timeframe 1 pay period


Issue # 2. 

Context: the issue with the workers who were recruited by the Thai RA being charged for the transportation and the recruitment fees. The experiences that the workers shared about their recruitment process are as follows: 
Three groups of workers were recruited by a broker from a Thai RA Number 17 and 64.
Ms. Than Than Soe and her business partner,  Ko Min ( Sub-recruiter of Thai RA No.17) were the recruiters. 
Workers were charged 5500 THB (3500 for service fees and 2000 for transportation fees). 
The workers gave 3500 for transportation and 2000 for recruitment fees) to  Ms.Than Than Soe on the day they arrived at Phetchaburi.
Workers have issues with the housing, they are staying somewhere very far from the factory. The recruiter arranged a track for them. The place they live has an issue with the internet, shopping, and emergency medical assistance problem
There are around 50 workers recruited by these recruiters very recently. 


Remediation recommendations:

-The business to do an immediate investigation to assess the number of impacted workers and identify the people involved in the recruitment process that has been charging workers. Safeguards should be in place throughout the investigation, and workers should not be targeted by the sub-recruiter or recruitment agency representative. And the business staff conducting the interviews should make sure that workers are explained and guaranteed safeguards and that their jobs will not be at risk, and that the information they share will be anonymized to make sure workers do not encounter any retaliation or risks from informal brokers and/or RA staff. 
-The investigation should also cover the staff from the recruitment agencies to identify the root causes of the issue and understand who was involved in the collection of the money.
- Actions should be taken towards those who collected the money, and the business should clarify with the recruitment agency that no fees should be charged to workers and what are the consequences for not following that policy, such as termination of the contract, penalties or disciplinary actions imposed by the recruitment agency towards the staff involved in such practices, etc. 
-The business should set a plan of action with the recruitment agency involved, such as revision of the contract and the penalties for not following the company policy about “zero recruitment fees for workers”, and the actions the agency will take to avoid this from happening again. 
-As part of the investigation and remediation process, the business shall assess how much money new workers have paid and reimburse them those recruitment fees. 
-The business should cross-check through different means with the recruitment agency and workers being recruited, how are the services being provided to job seekers, what is the communication like about the job and the recruitment process, etc. 

Talking Points: 

-How is the recent recruitment being handled? How many workers have been recruited recently? 
-How does the business work with the Thai recruitment agency? What is the definition of a recruitment agency with different numbers such as 64, 17, and so on? What is the position of the recruiters Ms. Than Than Soe and her business partner,  Ko Min from recruitment agency 64 and 17? 
-Have there been any recent communication with the Thai recruitment agency based on the previous issue? 

Expected meeting format: 
Business: HR Department, Recruitment Department, Translator. 
Issara: BHR, Involved O & E, Ma Chaw, Sandy, Ana, and John?
HP: K Narisa 

Note* we do not say that these workers are from Songkhla to avoid the risks of workers being targeted.

A worker from Cal-Comp Building 9 (HP product) and Building 10 (apple product) reported that workers had to pay 1,000 THB for renewing their passports for their 4-year MoU extension. It was collected by sub recruiter #34 who said that if workers do not want to pay 1,000THB, they would have to go to the embassy by themselves for the extension. He said that all workers have paid already.

Talking points:
Is the business aware that workers are being charged for their MOU extensions?
How is the business checking to ensure recruitment agents don’t charge any fees to workers?

Recommendations for remediation:
The business to investigate this matter immediately
Issue a warning to the recruiter for having violated the employer pays policy and require the recruiter to return the money it charged to the workers
Return the money that workers paid to the recruiter
remediation_business_steps_taken:
-Issara raised this issue with the business, the business agreed to conduct a vetting process to find out about the announcement that had been made and workers being charged and then get back to Issara.
-The business responded that they have been investigating to find out the person who collected the money from the workers and they have some suspected person for further investigation. It is added that once the business competes for the investigation process, the impacted workers will be reimbursed. 
-The business updated that they have conducted the survey with the newcomer in the past last month but did not find any issue from the survey. The business also reported conducting the survey with the workers who were recruited in August, however, only one worker was found being impacted.

Issara raised this issue with K Narisa (HP focal). She responded that she is aware that the factory is understaffed, however, she will try her best to push the business to work on this issue by the 15th of November.
-The business updated that they have interviewed 171 workers who were recently recruited and found workers being charged 5000-53000 THB by the recruitment agency Number 17. The HP suggested the business conduct interviews with 100% of workers and conduct the reimbursement within December.

Issara had another escalation call with the business, the business responded that they have investigated the original case and repaid the worker.  CC is in the process of interviewing all workers hired since August 2021, 470 total workers of which 210 were hired for production supplying HP.  This is expected to be completed in January 2022 and workers reimbursed.  CC noted there is an issue with hiring of walk-in workers.  Recruitment agencies are using sub-agents.  CC has taken the following actions: they trained the 13 RAs on zero fees, helped them review the job advertisements, and set up the policies/procedures for compliance and RAs not in compliance will be penalized in a 3-step process.  First time, CC will decrease demand of workers from the RA; second time, CC will decrease the demand further, and third time, CC will cancel the service agreement with the RA.

Apart from that, the HP focal, K Narisa suggested Issara to conduct the recruitment fee survey with the worker. Issara will have follow up discussion with the HP and conduct the survey.

The business response:
K. Piyabutr, CSC and K.Big, HR department mentioned that the company paid the passport fee for all workers and the agency that handled it. The Myanmar embassy issued 200 passports per day, according to information from the CC HR team. There is no need to do it in person for visa extending workers, but it depends on the number of extending workers. According to HR's investigation, the agency has not collected money from the worker. According to HR, some workers would like to do their own document extension. It could be the case, but in the CC process, the worker is not required to pay anything. Issara can assist in communicating to workers that they must follow the CC process and not pay it themselves.

BHR recommended conducting the communication session. They added, they have conducted worker communication to all workers and encourage workers to use the CC process for document extension. The CC was communicated by verbal announcement (PA), via line supervisors and HR team. The CC said all workers know no one needs to pay for document extension and the employer will pay for it all.
remediation_notes:
Case #1: 
Two workers reported seeing a job advert for jobs at Cal-Comp and contacted the broker about getting a job as a walk-in worker.  The broker told the workers to contact one of the "wanna-said", a representative of the recruitment agency, based in the factory about getting a job. One worker was asked for a payment of 2,500 Baht and the other was asked to pay 3,500 Baht to be able to get a job.

Case #2:
Around 50 workers recently recruited by a Thai recruitment agency reported that they had to pay 5,500 Baht for the transportation and the recruitment fees.  When they arrived, they were provided with housing in a location far from the factory, which meant they have to pay for transportation to and from work.  In addition, they have limited internet, shopping options for essential goods, banking, and medical services.

Case #3:
A worker from Cal-Comp Building 9 and Building 10 reported that workers had to pay 1,000 Baht for their 4-year MoU extension. It was collected by the sub-recruiter #34 who said that if workers do not want to pay 1,000 Baht, they would have to go to immigration by themselves for the extension. He said that all workers have paid already.
remediation_action:
Case #1-2: 
The business said that they outsource hiring to 7 recruitment agencies, and would investigate this matter. It is noteworthy that last year (2020) there was a similar case reported and the business conducted investigations, eventually partially remediating impacted workers, which was considered a good step made by the company to address issues with recruitment. However, the process took several months and the business did not share/collaborate with Issara regarding addressing root causes, to avoid the same issues from arising in the future (as they are now) - for example addressing corrupt supervisors conducting exploitative recruitment, or conducting communication sessions with all workers and supervisors about the company's ethical recruitment policy and prohibition of informal brokering with recruitment fees.

The business is in the process of investigation and have identified certain suspected persons that may have charged recruitment fees from the workers. 
Once the business competes the investigation, impacted workers will be reimbursed.  The business surveyed new employees that joined in August 2021 but found only 1 worker had paid recruitment fees. 

The Strategic Partner (SP) has requested that Issara conduct a recruitment fee survey on behalf of the business to verify recruitment fees paid.  The SP is in the process of securing agreement on the part of the business to move forward with this.

Case #3:
The HR department mentioned that the company paid the passport fee for all workers and the agency that handled it. The Myanmar embassy issued 200 passports per day, and there is no need to do it in person for visa extending workers. According to HR's investigation, the agency has not collected any money from the workers.
remediation_validation:
Case #1-2:
These issues have been discussed additionally with the Strategic Partner, who has been working with CalComp on escalating issues and CalComp developing a more responsible recruitment process and implementation.  However, issues with current in-country recruitment practices continue to be uncovered, with concerning behavior by Thai recruitment agencies engaged by CalComp and fees being reported by workers.  There is a need to both immediately investigate and repay fees charged to workers in this recruitment, but also develop a more comprehensive plan to address structural issues and resources dedicated to worker recruitment - moving beyond internal company investigations and audits of contracted agencies.  This is particularly pressing given continuing worker reports, continued worker recruitment, and planning for working with Myanmar recruitment agencies for the potential reopening of cross border recruitment.

Issara has conducted the recruitment fee survey with the workers that were hired in 2021. The survey results will be shared with the business and the Strategic Partner for further action to remediate fees paid and improve the recruitment system.

Case #3:
Issara followed up with the workers and learned that this was not about the business charging workers for the passport renewal but workers choosing to pay a broker to expedite the passport renewal.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue.  For the first two cases, Issara conducted the recruitment fee survey to determine if any recruitment fees were paid by the workers.  For the third case, the workers clarified that it was not the business that charged for the passport renewal but something some workers chose to do by paying a broker.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Issue # 1. 
-The business is encouraged to use the Golden Dreams Job MarketPlace to have a more direct recruitment process and avoid these kinds of risks of fees being charged to job seekers. It is a high risk for the company who will ultimately be responsible for any fees being charged against the company policy and the buyer code of conduct. 
-The business is also encouraged to promote Golden Dreams Marketplace in their social media and other channels to let job seekers know that they can directly apply through the app and no at all will be charged. 

-Effective communication in a wide range should be conducted in the written and verbal post including disciplinary action for those who break the business's recruitment policy or do not follow accordingly.

Issue # 2. 
System change recommendations:
-The business is encouraged to use the Golden Dreams Job MarketPlace to have a direct and transparent recruitment process and avoid these kinds of risks of fees being charged to job seekers. It is a high risk for the company who will ultimately be responsible for any fees being charged against the company policy and the buyer code of conduct. 
-The business is also encouraged to broadly promote Golden Dreams Marketplace through  their social media and other channels to let job seekers know that they can directly apply through the app without having to pay any recruitment fees. The business is also encouraged to promote the Golden Dream application broadly with their current workers, so that workers can also share it with their relatives and family members interested in applying for a job at Cal Comp. 

-Effective communication in a wide range should be conducted in the written and verbal post including disciplinary action for those who break the business's recruitment policy or do not follow accordingly. The communication should clearly state that no recruitment fees will be charged to the job seeker for Cal-Comp.

Issue # 3
Recommendations for systems change:
Review the current MSA with Recruiter #34, and 1) clarify expectations that it doesn’t charge workers any fees in the future or 2) discontinue working with this recruiter

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context : The issue with over workload due to less workforce as the workers from Ingredient Line are being shift to different line to fulfill the workforce in the other lines. Workers reported facing challenges to complete their workforce with less workers since the work load is remain same event he workforce is decreasing. 10171, 9677. 

Issara recommendations 

-The business to conduct an investigation ethically taking into account safeguards for the workers. The investigation should aim to understand why the workers are being asked to do the same amount of work in their line with fewer workers than before? The investigation should include workers' voice. 

-The business should coordinate with the production department to develop a corrective action plan to make sure workloads are balanced, fair, and do not affect workers health. Workers should not be asked to work or cover for their co-workers if they are rotated to other lines or are absent. 

-The business to communicate with impacted workers, supervisors and manager the plan of action to address this issue. The communication should include information about workload and tasks in the written and should be explained verbally to workers. 

Talking Points : 

Please ask the business following questions ; 

-What is the nature of work in this ingredient line? What are the workers expected to do in this line? 
-What is the recent turnover rate of this line/factory? If the current turnover rate is high, what has the business done to make sure that workers are not overworked?
-How does the business calculate incentives whether it is based on the number of workers in a line and their production target? And what system does the business uses to track workloads and to make sure incentives are being paid accordingly? 
-Are there standards for the minimum number of workers that should be in each line and the amount of work required for certain production levels?


Time frame 1 pay period

closed_notes:
Workers reported that they used to receive an incentive up to 2000 baht per pay period but they have not received it since they have a new line supervisor. They additionally reported they were not able to get further information on the change from the line supervisor or HR.
HR investigated the issue but focused on providing workers with a reason they did not get the incentive (not meeting a target, quality of work). The investigation on the incentive payment found that the incentive was given to eligible workers according to the rule which was communicated to all workers.

The business investigation did not include any focus on the conduct of the line supervisor and how incentives are calculated and communicated to workers. The business is not taking any further actions to address this issue and workers continue to report that they do not understand how incentives are calculated. 

Issara team has recommended the business to clarify to line supervisors and workers how incentives are calculated and what actions the business is taking to respond to workers’ concern on incentives and also the actions to improve their grievance mechanisms systems. In addition, Issara has recommended  to Thai Union group to have tailored training to this site staff and to also have a worker satisfaction survey in order to identify systemic issues and work on a plan of action to address those issues.

Context; the issue with the incentive that the workers are not receiving since they have a new supervisor in their production line. Workers reported that they used to receive intentive up to 2000 per pay period but they have not received it since they have a new line supervisor. 
Working Line; Cut Site" (In the Thai language) where the raw prawns firstly arrived and the workers have to sort them out by size and take out those which are not fresh anymore.

Recommendations: 

-The business to conduct the investigation on this working line to assess how incentives are being calculated and recorded, and what could be the reasons for workers not receiving incentives recently.

-The investigation should include production (whoever is responsible for setting targets and calculating the incentives amounts and the line supervisor who records the workers' work) and also feedback from workers.

- Based on the results of the investigation and analysis of the targets the business should compensate workers accordingly if needed. 

-Disciplinary actions should be taken towards the supervisor if the investigation found an issue of misconduct by the supervisor. 

-It is recommended for the business to clarify to line supervisors and workers how incentives are calculated and what actions is the business taking to respond to workers concern on incentives and also the actions to improve their grievance mechanisms systems to make sure there are actions taken when workers report a case to HR or to any other grievance mechanism channel.

-What is the incentive process for this line?

HR communicated with the workers who didn’t receive the incentive because it didn’t reach the target and some infected pawn (not good enough quality). However, HR will investigate and check the payroll, production, etc. which are involved with the incentive system.

remediation_business_steps_taken:
Business responses: 

Issue: Workers PR (processing) night shift said that the supervisor named "Morn" when the workers ask for sick leave, the supervisor does not allow it, but if it is a Thai workers, easier to allow.

cause/action: 
The HR conducted survey by randomly selected 8 workers at the night shift processing line where Pi Morn was the supervisor to ask if the supervisor had ever refused to allow workers to take sick leave. The workers were randomly given feedback that the supervisor never refused.

The HR department and the factory manager called the supervisor "Morn" to ask more questions. Khun Morn insists that he has never refused sick leave for both Thai and Burmese workers. He acknowledged the non-discrimination policy and considered approving leave according to the same rules for both Thai workers and Burmese workers.

However, in the case of some workers with taken sick leave often, Khun Morn would ask for more details about the sickness of the worker because he worried if the worker had chronic illnesses. 

HR trained all supervisors and they are communicated, taught, and emphasized on communication methods on how to communicate and treat workers appropriately and it has always been a matter that the company has given importance to. If the worker faces a case where the supervisor speaks badly, the worker can report the matter through the company grievance channels as usual.

Status: Done 
Responsibility: Production and HR
remediation_notes: A supervisor is discriminating against Burmese workers. She threatens the Burmese workers who take sick leave by telling them to go to the office to meet with the manager. However, she does not say anything to Thai workers who do the same.
remediation_action: Issara has raised this issue with the business, and the business investigated the matter.  The business found that the supervisor had not denied sick leave to any workers; however, for workers that were taking sick leave frequently, she asked detailed questions about their health condition out of concern that they might have a chronic illness.  The business has always placed great importance on training supervisors to communicate effectively with, and behave appropriately towards, the workers.
remediation_validation: Issara followed up with the workers and provided the business update that supervisors were asking questions about the health of those taking sick leave frequently and it wasn't about preferential treatment to Thai workers.  The workers understand this and have not observed the supervisor discriminating against Burmese workers since the incident.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case. remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that they had received the announcement that the business will no longer arrange for the interpreters to accompany them to the hospital when needed.  When workers are sick, they would have to go to the factory clinic first to get checked out, and if the factory nurse determined that the worker needed to go to the hospital, she would write the illness on the paper and the worker would have to go to the hospital without an interpreter. The business would provide interpretation support via phone if needed.  If workers use external interpreter on their own will, the business will not reimburse the cost. The business said that this is a trial period and if this process does not work, the business will try to find an official interpreter. Workers know that the single interpreter the business employed just resigned and so are depending on informal volunteer interpreters to provide workers with this interpretation support.

Talking Points:
-Is the business changing the policy on providing interpretation services to workers because of the lack of an interpreter?
-Is this a short-term change or is the business considering to continue without hiring adequate, qualified interpreters?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Recognizing that workers need the interpretation support when getting medical care, and it is something the business has been providing in the past, the business should hire 1 or more qualified interpreters as soon as possible
-Announce to all workers that this is a temporary measure during the interim period when there is no interpreter

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Case 1)The issue with the pregnant workers not having enough help to carry heavy load and (case 2) not having enough chairs to sit during the lunch break. ID; 9776.

Issara recommendations : 

-The supplier to investigate if there are enough "helpers" (bo ri can) to assist pregnant workers so that they do not have to carry heavy loads (Note that according to workers, there used to be 2 "helpers" but there is only one now, which is not enough to cover the work). The business to make sure there are enough helpers for this task.

-The supplier to make sure that the pregnant workers are not carrying more than 15 Kg of heavy materials at the workplace.

- The supplier to check the number of chairs being provided during lunch break and have priority sitting arrangements for pregnant workers.  

Legal References. 

Section 39 of the LPA, it is expressly prohibited for employers to allow pregnant employees to perform the following work:

(1) Work concerning vibrating machinery or engines;
(2) Driving, moving, or travelling on vehicles;
(3) Lifting, carrying, or bearing on the shoulders or head, or pulling or pushing, loads that weigh more than fifteen 
    kilogrammes;
(4) Working on waterborne vessels; and
(5) Other work prescribed by the ministerial regulations.

Code: ETI Base Code 3.1. Working conditions safe and hygienic; employer provides a safe and hygienic work environment and minimizes hazards and accidents

Description: A safe and hygienic working environment shall be provided, bearing in mind the prevailing knowledge of the industry and of any specific hazards. Adequate steps shall be taken to prevent accidents and injury to health arising out of, associated with, or occurring in the course of work, by minimizing, so far as reasonably practicable, the causes of hazards inherent in the working environment

Time Frame: 1 pay period

- Please share to the business about the working line information. 
- Please ask the business if they are aware of this issue or not, and if so, are there any actions being taken? 
- As noted by workers, there used to be 2 helpers and now there is only one, so check with the business if they are planning to replace this helper and if so, when.
- Since Issara is receiving several calls regarding Borican being reduced by the business, could you please explain what is the purpose and how is this impacting the workers? 
- Please ask the business what is the weight of the materials in that line that pregnant workers have to carry and type of work that they are being asked to do. 

Talking points for case 2:
-Share with the business what is the pregnant workers experience during lunch time and recommend the business to arrange a priority sitting for pregnant workers.
-
systems_change_issara_recommendation:

-Encourage workers to use grievance mechanisms. The business to have a communication session to encourage pregnant workers and other to raise their issues and concerns whenever is needed.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1:
Six Cambodian workers were charged fees by a sub-recruiter to issue their pink cards (1,300 THB).  They were hired as walk-in workers. At first, they had only their passports and they were referred by their friends to the sub-recruiter who is able to process the pink card, work permit and visa for workers. They paid 13,000 THB each for the whole process. However, six months later, they have only received their work permits but they haven't received their pink card yet. 

Note: This issue was raised during in-person outreach.  The workers that reported these issues did not want to share their identities.

Talking points:
How is the company handling the hiring of walk-in workers?  
Is there a recruitment agency involved?  If so, what is its role?

Recommendations for remediation:
Investigate this issue, include worker voice in the investigation and ensure worker safeguards
Identify the recruiter that has received money from the workers, and require this money be returned
The business should follow the employer pays policy, identify the amount paid by workers for the recruitment, and repay them
Communicate to all workers that the company has an EPP and that workers should not pay for any recruitment fees, including work permit, visa, 90-day extensions


Case #2:
One worker mentioned that for the Cambodian and Burmese workers who received the wages from the sub-contractors, 3% of their wages were being deducted.

Talking points: 
- Is the company aware that some workers are being paid their wages via a sub-contractor and not directly by F&D?
- Is the company aware that the sub-contractor is deducting money for the workers' wages?

Recommendations for remediation:
- All wages of F&D workers should be paid directly by the company and through a sub-contractor, with pay slips provided to the workers in their languages
- Any deductions of workers' wages should be repaid to the workers
- The practice of the sub-contractor deducting a percentage of the workers' wages should be discontinued immediately

call_details.description: The group of 32 U-Turn migrant workers called to Issara Yangon hotline to ask for help for their problems. They are the U turn workers from Pataya food Industry from Mahachai. Although they arrived back Myanmar since March 2023 and have been waiting for 5 months already. But there is no response from employer yet and they could not go back to factory in U-Turn process yet. That is why, they called to Issara to report the problem.
call_details.referral_notes:
The group of 32 U-Turn migrant workers called to Issara Yangon hotline to ask for help for their problems. They are the U turn workers from Pataya food Industry from Mahachai. Although they arrived back Myanmar since March 2023 and have been waiting for 5 months already. But there is no response from employer yet and they could not go back to factory in U-Turn process yet. That is why, they called to Issara to report the problem.
Ma Kay Thi Soe who called to Issara hotline said that the employer "Pataya Food Industry" told them that the factory will call the workers back within one month. But it is over 5 months already and there is no contacts and response from the employer side yet. So, they would like to get the update information from Pattaya Food industry. At first, they heard the news that Myanmar RAs Ngwe Sin Kabar agency will send them back to factory by U-Turn. But there is no response from the agency too. When they contacted to the agency, the agency said that they cannot do anythings as the employer did not provide any info to them and did not contact to agency at all. The agency said employer did not give any workers information to the agecny and no guidance from the employers side. So, they cannot tell anything to workers about that. 
So, the workers asked for help from issara to contact with the employer from Thailand. Do we have any connection from that Pataya foods?
The workers said that they all have the valid passports and all the passports are being updated and ready to go.
But as they did not hear any information from the employer for 5 months, and being in trouble as they do not have any income for long time. 
The workers provided employer info and agency info.
Ngwe Sin Kabar agency is in Official list but it is new agecny and we never had any contact with them before. So, Wint told the workers that I will report it to BKK team and ask whether how we can help for them.
The workers also sent the hand-written letter to ask for help from Issara too.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1
In the production line “chin suon”, the line supervisors pressured workers to meet increased targets.  For the past six months, the production targets have been increased based on the type of piece of meat (for chicken wing or leg, increased from 10 to 14kg per hour, for big pieces, increased from 25 to 30kg). When some workers can’t complete these targets, the line supervisor will notice those producing less and not offer them OT work in the future. Until now, but workers did not dare to raise this concern. 

Case #2
A worker reported that in his line with around 60 workers, he received a lot of pressure from the line supervisor to reach a certain target, to finish 100 kg/person within 5 hours before the 1-hour break.  That means workers have to slice 20kg of chicken meat per hour, which normally a worker completes around 10-15 kg only. If the worker does not complete the target, the line supervisor stares and says to the workers that "they are lazy and always going on toilet breaks". Workers feel they are being paid by piece rate, and feel pressured and irritated by the line supervisor's behavior. 

The detail info:
- There are around 60 workers on the production line
- Production line: Prer Roub - Kirami S3
- Line supervisor: Female; Monyrat

TPs:
-Have hourly production targets been increased in the past six months?  What is the reason for increasing the target?
-If workers are seen to not meet the target, line supervisors are denying them OT hours (Case #1).  Is OT work offered to workers on a conditional basis?
-If workers are seen to not meet the target, a line supervisor is using degrading language and calling workers lazy (Case #2).


Recommendations for remediation:
-Assess how the company determines production targets, and evaluate whether they are realistic and appropriate for the workforce.  Include workers' perspectives as part of this evaluation.
-Communicate to all workers, verbally and in writing, the company's production targets and how they are set (or increased) so that workers understand why they may be asked to increase efficiency
-Communicate to all workers, verbally and in writing, the company's policy regarding OT work, and how workers are selected for OT

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Marine Gold recently introduced a new policy verbally last week, which pertains to overtime (OT) restrictions for employees who take leave, regardless of the type of leave. Under this policy, any worker who takes leave is not eligible to work OT for one week following their return to work.

TPs:
- What is the intention behind this policy?
- If any type of leave, does this also include sick leave, business leave?
- Why should workers be penalized for taking leave?

Recommendations:
- Taking any type of leave is a right of the worker that should be protected
- There should not be conditions that are attached to leave; remove this policy where OT is withheld from workers for the week following workers taking leave
- Communicate the revised policy, verbally and in writing to all workers.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 25 Sep 2023

K. Pattsa and K. Juthamas, HR have no information about this issue. They will need to talk with the production manager to get more information and get back to us within one week.

DATE: 3 Oct 2023
K. Juthamas, HR, explained that production considers workers who are on sick leave or taking business leave because they care about the worker's ability to work more than 8 hours per day. That is why this reason is considered to give the worker OT hours. Another reason is based on production forecasting for OT hours. Not every worker works overtime. Some days are 50% or 30%. O&E and BHR explained that this should not be the reason for each worker's OT contribution. Workers should receive OT in the same way and without bias. K. Yaovapa, HR, added that as Issara noticed, the company has provided OT to workers who meet the standard or high performance each day. So, let's do this. HR agrees to discuss the OT contribution to the worker with the production manager and consider only the worker's performance, with no regard for any leave from the worker. By October 13, they will also clearly communicate this to the workers, both verbally and in writing.


DATE: 20 Oct 2023

K. Juthamas, HR
K. Yaovapa, HR

HR had a meeting with the production manager on Oct 4, and after that, they had a communication session with the workers on all the production lines by Oct 13 so that if a worker takes any leave, the worker can still work OT, but it depends on the worker's health condition and performance on that day.
remediation_notes: Issara received a report that the business recently introduced a new policy that for workers that take any type of leave would not be eligible to work OT for one week following their return to work.
remediation_action:
HR was not aware of this issue. They will discuss with the production manager and get back to us within one week.

HR agreed to offer OT hours to workers based on their performance, and will not penalize workers for being on leave. If a worker takes any leave, the worker can still work OT, but it will depend on the worker's health condition and performance on that day. HR will clearly communicate this to the workers, both verbally and in writing by Oct 13, 2023.
remediation_validation: Workers confirmed that they have heard the announcement saying taking leave would not affect their OT hours but rather OT would be offered to workers based on performance.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue.  Workers have confirmed they understand the updated policy regarding OT and taking leave will not affect their OT hours.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
In the fish inner organ cleaning room (Compoda Room) is a sub-room of the raw fish room. Mr.Kyaw Hla reported that 6 workers from Compoda room was moved to the fish trimming line without the workers' consent. 

Since the time these workers started applying for jobs in TUF, they were assigned for this specific line and the workers like the nature of this working line and they agree to work in this line. But in the second week of August 2023, these 6 workers were temporarily moved to the fish trimming line, since that time these workers clearly stated that they can only work temporarily in fish trimming line. 

On 8th September 2023, the chief line-supervisor of Compoda room asked these 6 workers again to move to the fish trimming line by 11th Sep permanently. The workers don't understand why the chief line-supervisor keeps trying to move them to the fish trimming line. The business said they are moving these 6 workers to fish trimming line because of lesser work in Compoda room but the other line workers keeps moving to Compoda room and new workers have many tasks to do in Compoda room.

In TUF working nature, Compoda Line is more busy and more OT than other lines, in this particular event, the chief line-supervisor of Pla Sot (Raw Fish Line), Phee Myuu and new Chief Line supervisor who moved from PH-1 Phee Moo are intentionally manipulate the workforce by playing favoritism. They welcomed their favorite workers to Compoda where there is more OT but they moved the workers they don't like to fish trimming lines where there is no OT. In this particular workforce shifting, the chief supervisors told the 6 workers that we will have no more OT in Compoda room, so we moved the workers regardless of OT opportunities.

TPs:
- What is the company policy in terms of moving workers from one line to another?  Is it based on the nature of work?  How are such re-assignment decisions made?  Are workers consulted and able to consent before the move?

Recommendations:
- Workers feel they are being moved from the line that has more OT and this is directly affecting their income.  The business should provide a clear rationale as to why this decision was made. If the re-assignment was not a fair, transparent decision with the workers' consent, the business should consider to assign the workers back to where they have always been working.
- Communicate clearly to workers how work and production line assignments are made, when changes might be made for what reason, and have a transparent process where workers consent to such moves.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 5 Oct 2023

K Prad emailed the corrective action table as per the link below.
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/18w_cHkTFDYU98DN9MkRiwKnAHvjHfj9g

The investigation discovered that the Compoda room is a Co-Product work point where 6 employees were transferred to work at the actual scrapping site. The supervisors met on September 8, 2023, and the transfer will be effective on September 11, 2023, at the point where the Co-product job is scraping and packing fish maws. This product will not be manufactured all year.
Customer orders will be fulfilled by the production line. Employees will be transferred to assist in other areas if there is no production. If the product is manufactured again, the employees will return to work at the same point (without the replacement of other employees from other lines, such as cold room 4). As a result, the employees can have work to do with the company although in some periods there will be no order at this line. Regardless of the matter of the assignment of overtime work, the company has determined it as appropriate depending on the production capacity of each production line.

remediation_action: The business investigated and responded that the particular line the workers were working in doesn't have production all year so workers are moved to other lines when there is no production here. When the line restarts production, these workers will return to work in that line again.
remediation_validation: Issara updated the workers and they now understand the situation regarding the production line and the changes they have experienced.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case, as the workers confirmed they now understand the reason they were moved to another line.

call_details.description: 2 female Lao MOU workers recruited as domestic workers in Thailand who were taken by the Thai employer to take care of her mother, children, and house in San Marino, Los Angeles County, California, USA on what are now expired passports and the wrong visa.  The women, during the raid, explained to Issara and the police that their phones were taken away from them as punishment for talking to men via Facebook.  They were also told that the employer had to hold their passports; they questioned none of this.  They seem to know very little about their rights and seem to have been easily led by the Thai employer to believe that she is caring for them and when they are in the wrong, they deserve the punishment and isolation they get.  The women were very scared to leave the home when the employer all of a sudden came home during the raid, after being gone for almost 1 week (ie she took the womens' phones then left the home for days).
call_details.referral_notes: Victims in the custody of the San Marino Police Dept and connected to support from CAST-LA
call_details.next_steps: Monitor and ensure communication with family, also ensure that it's not forgotten that they are owed lost wages and possibly more - but that service providers understand that they may not know all their rights or feel confident to assert them
