call_details.description:
The female worker (Thet Thet Htwe) has had a hand injury at the workplace since 2019. Again in February 2022, she had to be hospitalized for a month and take medical leave for three months from March to May. For one month in the hospital, the supplier provided daily wages, but for the other three months of leave, the supplier said the workmen's compensation had been submitted to the social security office. She followed up several times with the HR office, and the staff kept saying that it was in the process.

She will have to return to Myanmar in May 2023 because the four-year MoU is coming to an end. This morning, on April 21, she asked HR staff, and they said it will not be received until she arrives back in Myanmar. She was told to go back and keep her bank card with her friend. When the social security office pays the compensation, the supplier will transfer the money to her bank account, and then her friend can transfer her money. 

It is impossible for her to keep her bank account with her friends in Thai. She would like to get the compensation before she goes back to Myanmar. She requested that Issara help discuss her issue with the supplier.

The business had a communication session with the workers on April 20 and informed the workers who ended their MoU contract for 4 and 6 years to return to Myanmar on May 3.

For those who will renew their MoU U-Turn, each worker has to pay 5940 THB for the recruitment fees and 900 THB (transportation)to the HR office by Apr 24th and 300,000 Kyats to the Golden Sea Myanmar RA.

In 2022, the business collected 6500 THB to apply for a new passport and promised them that their visa and work permit would be extended in Thailand.

Since the business gave short notice, the workers feel unhappy about that.

Most of them do not want to go back to Myanmar and get the documents' extensions here.

Some do not have money for the MoU U-turn.

Some do not want to go back on May 3. They would like to continue working until their visa ends and will come back with a U-turn. For U-Turn as well, they would like to hear how many months they have to wait in Myanmar. They would like to get a clear timeline from the business.

The worker was explained about the workmen compensation according to the business response. The workers went back to Myanmar on 3rd May and they were provided the contact number of Yangon Issara office in case they would like to know something about it.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue.  In both cases, the workers now understand what the business will provide (facilitation of the U-turn process, receipt of Social Security compensation upon return, etc.) to the workers. The business is not changing its position to put on hold its responsible recruitment policy and paying for most of the workers' recruitment costs.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1: A female worker (Thet Thet Htwe) injured her hand in a workplace accident back in 2019. In February 2022, she had to be hospitalized for a month, and took medical leave for three months from March-May 2022. For the month in the hospital, the supplier paid daily wages as sick leave days, but for the three additional months of medical leave, the supplier submitted an application for workmen's compensation with the social security office. She followed up several times with the HR office, and the HR staff kept saying that it was in the process. She will have to return to Myanmar in May 2023 because her four-year MoU contract is coming to an end. This morning, on April 21, she asked HR staff, and they said she will not receive the compensation from social security before she leaves to return to Myanmar. HR told her keep her Thai bank card with her friend and when the social security office pays the compensation, the supplier will transfer the money to her bank account, and then her friend can transfer her the money. She would like to get the compensation before she goes back to Myanmar.

TPs:
- Why has there been such a delay in getting the compensation for her medical leave from the workmen's compensation fund if this took place almost a year ago?

Recommendations:
- The business to follow up with the social security office and expedite the request to process this payment from social security, which is already grossly overdue
= Ensure that the worker receives this compensation prior to returning to Myanmar
- Communicate clearly to the worker the status update in terms of processing the compensation payment and when the worker can expect to receive it

Case #2 (April 21, 2023): A worker reported that the business had a communication session with the workers on April 20th and informed the workers whose 4-year or 6-year MoU contracts are ending will need to return to Myanmar on May 3rd. For those renewing their contracts (MoU U-Turn), each worker has to pay 5,960 THB for the recruitment fees to the HR office by May 24th and 300,000 Kyats to the Golden Sea Myanmar RA. In 2022, the business already collected 6,500 THB for passport renewals and at that time had promised them that their visa and work permit would be extended in Thailand. The workers feel unhappy because the business has changed what they had announced earlier, and most do not want to go back to Myanmar given the current political situation. Some do not have the money for the MoU U-turn process. Some would like to continue working until their current visa ends. For others, they would like to know how many months they have to wait in Myanmar for the U-turn process.

TPs:
- Seafresh has a policy where the business will pay for the recruitment costs, except for the passport fees and any travel related costs to the point of departure (Yangon).  Workers reported they have been asked to pay 5,960 Baht to HR and another 300,000 Kyats to the Myanmar RA.  What is this for?

Recommendations:
- Clarify with workers what the fees are, for which workers have been asked to pay
- Clarify the timeframe for the U-turn process, so that workers know when they can expect to get back to Seafresh to resume work
- Clarify with the workers about the safety of the U-turn process and that Seafresh and the Myanmar RA can ensure that the workers will be able to return with renewed MOU contracts.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Case 1:
BR: 2295: According to Seafresh and SSO, in 2019, the worker received medical costs and compensation in excess of the SSF's maximum limit of 50,000 baht. However, in 2022, the injury flared up again and she needed additional medical attention, and Seafresh paid 40,281 Baht in advance (24,000 baht for transportation and miscellaneous + 16,000 for medical costs). SSO must consider this case because it involves an injury sustained in the first accident of 2019. It will be released in July 2023, according to SSO. In 2022, Seafresh paid for 30 sick days. In July, the worker will receive an 18,000 baht reimbursement (money order) from SSO for 96 days of work. The worker agreed to extend the MoU process and receive the reimbursement when she returned to Thailand in July. 

Case 2:
BR: 2295: Seafresh responded that they have consulted with DOE that the Thai Government would announce the MoU extension. They keep in touch with DOE and then DOE responded that there is not extension announcement so the workers must go back to Myanmar. Workers can pay 5,940 Baht between April 24 and May 3 (the majority of workers' visas expire on May 6). They combine May and June for workers whose visas expire because a few workers' visas expire in June. Seafresh would like to arrange this transportation at the same time for saving the cost for the workers. So there might be the case that short notice but this is voluntary for the workers. If the workers do not want to extend this MoU process, the workers can work until the work permit ends. Currently, there are 40 of 133 workers agreed to extend. In Myanmar, the timeline for U-Turn is three months. The workers who do not want to extend their MoU. They can work until their visa expires. Seafresh agrees to that and Seafresh can keep the worker status for another 2 months in case that the Thai Government announces amnesty. 

Seafresh had a communication session with the cost breakdown of 5,940 Baht to all workers on Apr 20. However, Seafresh will have another session to make a clear explanation to those whose visa will end in June. Seafresh will share the cost breakdown and Issara can also communicate with the workers as well. 

BR 2299: Seafresh shared the breakdown of U-turn costs and communications with the workers.
remediation_notes:
Case #1: A female worker injured her hand in a workplace accident back in 2019. In February 2022, she had to be hospitalized for a month, and took medical leave for three months from March-May 2022. For the month in the hospital, the supplier paid daily wages as sick leave days, but for the three additional months of medical leave, the supplier submitted an application for workmen's compensation with the social security office. She followed up several times with the HR office, and the HR staff kept saying that it was in the process. She will have to return to Myanmar in May 2023 because her four-year MoU contract is coming to an end. On April 21, 2023, she asked HR staff, and they said she will not receive the compensation from social security before she leaves to return to Myanmar. HR told her keep her Thai bank card with her friend and when the social security office pays the compensation, the supplier will transfer the money to her bank account, and then her friend can transfer her the money. She would like to get the compensation before she goes back to Myanmar.


Case #2: The business had a communication session with the workers on April 20, 2023 and informed the workers whose MoU contracts are ending that they would need to return to Myanmar on May 3, 2023. For those who will renew their contracts through the MoU U-turn process, each worker has to pay 5,940 THB for the recruitment fees and 900 THB for transportation costs to the HR office by Apr 24th and 300,000 Kyats to the Myanmar RA. In 2022, the business had already collected 6,500 THB to apply for a new passport and promised them that their visa and work permit would be extended in Thailand. Since the business gave such a short notice of needing to return to Myanmar, the workers feel unhappy about this. Most of them do not want to go back to Myanmar and would prefer to get their documents extended in Thailand. For U-Turn as well, they would like to hear how many months they have to wait in Myanmar. They would like to get a clear timeline from the business.
remediation_action:
Case #1: The business noted that the worker received medical costs and compensation in excess of the SSF's maximum limit of 50,000 baht in 2019. However, in 2022, the injury flared up again and she needed additional medical attention, and Seafresh paid 40,281 Baht in advance (24,000 baht for transportation and miscellaneous + 16,000 for medical costs). The Social Security Office must consider this case because it involves an injury sustained in the first accident of 2019. In 2022, Seafresh also paid for 30 sick days. In July 2023, the worker will receive an 18,000 baht reimbursement from SSO for 96 days of work. The worker agreed to extend the MoU U-turn process and will receive the reimbursement when she returns to Thailand in July. 

Case #2: Seafresh responded that they consulted the Department of Employment (DOE) and determined that workers would need to return to Myanmar for the MOU U-turn process. Workers will pay 5,940 Baht, and Seafresh will arrange transportation for the workers. If the workers do not want to extend this MoU process, the workers can work until the work permit ends. Currently, 40 of 133 workers agreed to do the U-turn process. In Myanmar, the timeline for U-Turn is three months. Seafresh had a communication session with the cost breakdown of 5,940 Baht to all workers on April 20, 2023. However, Seafresh will have another session to make a clear explanation to those whose visa will end in June. Issara escalated this to the Seafresh MD because according to its responsible recruitment policy and agreement with the recruitment agencies dated May 31, 2022, Seafresh would be covering these recruitment fees for workers.  The MD noted that there was a new policy dated December 5, 2022, which notes that "Seafresh is implementing a stepped plan for eliminating recruitment fees by January 2024" and this replaces the May 31, 2022 policy.  He said this "stepped plan" means that in 2023 Seafresh is putting a hold on covering all recruitment fees for workers and will move to full implementation of covering all fees starting in January 2024. However, Issara is of the position that the December 5, 2022 policy shouldn't cancel out the May 31, 2022 policy but rather build on it because it states a "stepped" plan. In practice, the May 31, 2022 agreement states almost full coverage of recruitment fees (except for the passport and the travel costs from home village to Yangon) and the Dec 5, 2022 policy says it is implementing a stepped plan to eliminate all fees but in practice they are going backwards and are making workers pay for the U-turn process costs 2023.  In the latest update, the MD noted that 31 workers went for the U-turn process in May 2023 and another 60 will do the U-turn in August 2023.
remediation_validation:
Case #1: The worker has agreed to return to Myanmar for the MOU U-turn process and understands that she will receive the Social Security compensation when she returns to Thailand. She went back to Myanmar on 3rd May and Issara provided our Yangon office contact number so she can stay connected and ask any questions she may have.

Case #2: 31 workers have returned and arrived safely in Myanmar for the U-turn process.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue.  In both cases, the workers now understand what the business will provide (facilitation of the U-turn process, receipt of Social Security compensation upon return, etc.) to the workers. The business is not changing its position to put on hold its responsible recruitment policy and paying for most of the workers' recruitment costs.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers sick leave and the medical certificate during their home quarantine. Workers reported an increasing number of COVID positive cases in the factory. The factory does the ATK test and asks the workers to take 10 days of home quarantine if they have tested positive and have no severe symptoms. However, it is not clear what will happen with their wages since they do not have the MC from the doctor as they are taking home quarantine. The factory interpreter said not to worry about the MC, however it was not clear if they will get fully paid without having MC. Workers wanted to hear from the business about how their Covid-related quarantine days will be handled. All workers in the factory have received booster doses of the COVID-19 vaccine. 

Recommendations: 
-The business should clearly communicate with the workers about how their Covid-related quarantine days will be processed and whether they will be considered sick leave days, with or without a medical certificate, and the workers paid accordingly for those days.
- If the business’ policy requires workers to present a medical certificate for taking sick leave for more than 3 days, the business should facilitate COVID-Positive workers to visit the hospital to get an MC, even if they are self-isolating at home. However, if the business does not require MC and an ATK test is sufficient, this should be clearly communicated to the workers. 

Talking Points; 
-How many workers have tested positive and are in-home quarantine at the moment? 
-What is the business policy for the workers’ wages when they do not have MC from the hospital for the quarantine period?  Will the Covid-related quarantine period without a medical certificate be considered sick leave? 

Time Frame ; within 1 week.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue #1. 
Context: The issue with the public holiday. Workers reported that they were being asked to sign a consent form which was written in Thai without an explanation and later realized it was the consent to agree to work for a public holiday (13th Oct). It also happened on 23rd Sep. Workers added that they were asked to sign the document first only after the workers signed the documents did the line supervisor explain the purpose. Workers want to take a rest and be well explained about the documents before they sign.

Recommendations; 
The business  shall immediately make an announcement to all workers noting that the consent received earlier is void because workers did not understand what they were consenting to, request the voluntary consent of workers that are willing to work on the upcoming public holiday on Oct 13th, and provide the consent forms to work on Oct 13th in the languages of the workers, without pressure to sign
The business is to make sure that all communication documents are in the native language of the workers, especially those documents requiring their informed consent
The business is to make sure that workers understand what the business is requesting, and that the worker has the right to voluntarily consent to the request by fully explaining the nature of the request in a language the workers understand, prior to asking for the workers’ consent.

Talking Points: 
Is the business aware that the consent form that the workers had to sign was only in Thai and not in Burmese (Khmer) and that the line supervisors that were tasked to get the consent from workers only explained what the workers were consenting to after the worker had already signed? 
What is the production plan for 13 Oct? Is the business planning for full production on that day?
How many workers have agreed to work on 13 Oct? 
Have there been any workers that have reported to HR or through the grievance channels about this issue?

Issue#2. Closed

Context: The issue with a worker who has been suspended from working OT hours for seven days for missing work on the business’s public holiday. The worker said that she missed her job because of the translator’s announcement that working for a public holiday on (23rd) is optional. In addition to that, the worker added not receiving OT for several days since she took sick leave for 4 days with the proper Medical Certificate. The worker added that it has been 23 days in total that she has not to received OT working hours. Worker information: Working ID; C 105033, Nwe Nwe Win. 

Recommendations: 
The business should conduct an investigation on this issue to find out why this work has not received OT hours for 23 days and why she was suspended from working OT for seven days for not working on a public holiday. If the investigation finds an issue with the worker being punished for not working on a public holiday, the worker should be remediated with the OT hours or wages that are equal to the 7 days of OT hours. The worker should not be punished for not working on public holidays. 
The business should communicate with the worker specifically and also all workers generally about the company’s OT policy, including that withholding OT is not used as a form of punishment and clear guidance on why OT might be reduced immediately after a worker has returned from sick leave for the worker’s health.
The business should provide training to all supervisors and clerks on appropriate ways to grant OT hours to workers so it is based on the voluntary consent of the worker and not used in any way to punish workers.  

Talking Points:
Is the business aware of this case?
In a previous escalation meeting related to this issue, the business has agreed to revise the consent form and conduct more investigation, what has been the investigation result and the action plan? Has the consent form been revised? 
What is the business OT policy for sick workers? If there is a policy for sick workers and OT hours, has this policy been communicated with the workers? 
How often does the business provide training to supervisors on how to properly implement company policies, such as those related to OT hours for workers?
remediation_business_steps_taken:

Isara raised this issue with the business, and the business initially noted that the consent form that workers need to sign was already in workers' native language and the workers were notified one month in advance.  However, the consent form that the worker provided showed that the form did not provide sufficient information to help the worker understand what he/she was voluntarily signing up for. remediation_issara_recommendation:
The issue with the workers being asked to work on Sunday but not getting double wages. The employer provides the workers with compensation day-off on weekdays.
Recommendation. 
-The business to conduct an investigation to find out the impacted workers and pay them back. The investigation process should include workers' voices. 
-Workers should not be forced or pressured to work on Sundays. 
-Workers should receive a fixed day off to let the workers have their plans for their personal activities.
-The business to make sure that all workers fully consent to work on Sundays. 
-HR to involve in the consent form process along with the supervisors. 
Time Frame - 1 pay period

Talking Points 

Please give the detail of the story and ask the following questions. 

-What are the terms and conditions of the day off in the contract? 
-Workers said that they are being questioned and forced to agree to work on Sundays by the super supervisors. How does the business make sure that all of the consent forms that the workers signed really consent? 
-What is the reason only this specific line's workers having this issue?
remediation_business_steps_taken:
15-Oct-2020
The investigation found that there is a necessity to change working hours to clean the working station, which workers have to work on Sunday (which is their day off). Therefore, the business provides a compensation day to the workers and also asks for a consent form. The business also added that they can not simply ask the workers to work for 7 days and provide 8 days of wages because of buyer COC and working hours. The business added that working for the workers day off happens only sometimes. Workers confirmed the communication taking place and also the voluntary process that was explained by the business.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business to clearly communicate to all workers about their policy for working on Sundays.

-The business to encourage the workers to reach out to HR if they have any issues.

closed_notes:
Workers reported being asked to complete the same amount of work with only 32 workers whereas previously there used to be 50 workers on this line.

The business investigated and found that there were 26 workers in the segregation line, and noted that the raw material in that line was also halved, decreasing the ratio of workload per worker.


Workers provided an update saying the number of workers had reduced further to 26. Also, the workload before New Year was around 50 tons of prawn on average per day but now it was reduced to 40 tons, only a 20% decrease.  The workload was still too high for the number of workers available.

Workers continue to report the heavy workload and the business is not taking any further steps to address this issue. This issue along with other unresolved issues has been raised in a meeting with TU group.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; Workers being asked to do excessive workload with only 32 workers where it used to be 50 workers. Workers have reported to a supervisor about this issue but the supervisor said that they can leave the job if they can not manage it. Workers reported having callouses on their hands due to heavy workload.
-working line; Cut Site" (In the Thai language) where the raw prawns firstly arrived and the workers have to sort them out by size and take out those which are not fresh anymore.

Recommendations; 

-The business conducts an investigation ethically taking into account safeguards for the workers. The investigation should aim to understand why the workers are being asked to work a heavy workload with fewer workers.

-The investigation should include workers' voices. In order to generate a plan of action, the business shall coordinate with the production department to make sure workloads and targets are balanced, realistic and fair (based on the number of workers), and that they do not affect workers' health.
 
-Workers should have a humane environment in their working line. Workload should not impact workers health. 

Talking Points;

-What is the standard amount of prawns for a worker per day? What is the maximum amount of Kg for this production line? Please report the business that the workers have reported having asked to do 800KG to 1500KG per day. Is the business aware of this amount?  
  
-What is the system that the business uses to track workloads and to make sure that workers are being distributed with a fair workload? 

-What is the recent turnover rate of this line? If the current turnover rate is high, what the business has done to make sure that works are not overworked? is there any plan to recruit more workers? 

NOTE FOR BHR; 
Please remind the business that Issara receive workload issue frequently from the TUS workers, which highlight the TUS's system need to be more strong when addressing this issue. 

Time Frame 2 weeks.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara had several meetings with the business, the business argued not having a heavy workload and less number of workers as reported by the workers. The business also added having decreased orders since the first quarter of the year. Issara followed up with the workers, the workers updated that the business response to Issara is completely different from the ground situation. Workers added having excessive heavy workload with less number of workers than before. The business did not take any action to resolve this issue rather argued the worker's report.

Issara; 
The business response is not addressing the worker's issues. since Issara received such issues continuously, Issara has prepared the PowerPoint and presented all of the worker's issues with the Thai Union groups. Issara suggested systemic improvement and proposed to provide training with the HR and conduct the worker satisfactory survey.

Issara also checked with the workers to learn if there are any improvements after Issara's Issues presentations with the business, the workers updated still having this issue in their production lines.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker Than Than Myint reported that HR has not been responsive to their request for help in accessing their bank account. 8 MOU workers (including her) who came in 2018 as a first MOU batch for TG-1 is having problems with accessing their bank account and withdrawing money. As their passport and visa expired in Nov 2022 and they have been working as pink-card workers until now, they can only withdraw their money from bank with business recommendation until 2023 August. After August 2023, the bank didn't allow them to withdraw their money anymore. As a result, their 1.5 months salary was stuck in the bank and now they are facing problems with their rent and food. 

TPs:
- Is the business aware of this new bank regulation?
- Has the business made an announcement to workers to explain the new bank regulations and how workers will be able to access their money?

Recommendations:
- Assist the workers to access their bank accounts immediately, by coordinating with the bank to understand what's required and to take action to re-open workers' access to their bank accounts
- Communicate with workers about any updated bank regulations and how the business is supporting them to access their bank accounts
- Communicate with workers about how the business will process the U-turn process for MOU workers given the new government announcement stating that MOU workers should do the U-turn process by April 2024
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 19 Oct 2023

K. Tunlaya, HR, will need to check the workers' status for this specific case and will get back to us as soon as this week or early next week.


DATE: 20 Oct 2023

K Tunlaya, HCM Director, explained that after investigating this case, the workers' passport extensions are being delayed due to the government and embassy processes. However, the company has a solution for its workers, which is as follows On Oct 19, the company contacted Thanachart Thai Military Bank. On Oct 20, The interpreter will ask for the workers' expired passport documents. And HR will prepare an explanation letter for the bank. It will take another two weeks after the above process for workers to be able to withdraw cash from a bank counter. Then if the workers could not get the new passport, the company will help this process for the workers again.


DATE: 24 Oct 2023

8-9 Migrant workers cannot withdraw money at their bank.
Because of Covid’s situations, there are some migrant workers who has their expired documents and Thai government has not yet announce when they can renew their documents.
Last time, Bank allowed our migrant workers to withdraw their money via bank counter until Aug’23. We are going to wait for announcement from government to renew their documents.
Today (Oct 24), TG1 proposed the letter to Bank  for 9 migrant workers to withdraw their money via bank counter until Dec’23 which they can withdraw since Nov 10, 2023.
remediation_notes: Issara received a report that MOU workers are not able to access their bank accounts given that their passports and visas expired and are currently working as pink card workers. remediation_validation: Workers updated that the HR interpreter made an announcement to workers with the bank issue to provide their passports and other documents and HR will liaise with the bank to allow the workers access to their bank accounts.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that the shuttle bus to PT housing is overcrowded, with the bus carrying 60-70 workers when the maximum capacity should be 40 persons.  He thinks that it is very dangerous to have to commute to work in these overcrowded buses. 

TPs:
-How is ITC's current shuttle bus service set up?  How many buses are made available to workers at what times and to what locations?  What is the maximum capacity that should be allowed on these vehicles?

Recommendations for remediation:
-ITC should investigate the current shuttle bus arrangements and find out why more than the legal limit of the number of persons allowed in the vehicle are being packed into the buses, making it overcrowded and unsafe.  
-Ensure that adequate vehicles are provided so that workers can use the service to commute to and from work and that they are safe and not overcrowded.  
-Communicate to the workers clearly about how the arrangement will be improved, with the shuttle service schedule and increased number of the shuttle buses
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The shuttle bus picks up and drops off workers on the same route several times. And the maximum number of workers per shift is 40 passengers. They will investigate the existing shuttle bus arrangements and get back to us.


Due to more new workers staying as members of PT dormitories, including other dormitories in Tha Nang Hom zone. Therefore causing the need to increase the running round in the run to receive more workers who enter the work in the morning in time to enter the workplace at 6.30 a.m. The shuttle bus will pick up at 5.40, 6.00, and 7.00. The inspection found that there are workers who should enter the work at 6.30, do not get on the shuttle bus on time at 5.40, but will go on the bus at 6.00, combined with many workers who enter at 7.00, which makes the number of workers plus the 7.00 shift workers are too many workers in the bus which get to the factory in the time 6.20 - 6.25 am crowded because the workers refused to get on the bus on the first trip. Causing the number of workers per bus in the first trip just 15-20 workers and the second trip normally 40-50 workers increased to 50-60 workers in the second round, causing the workers to feel crowded in the car.

Solution:
The company announced for workers to board the bus according to the timetable. Because the workers start work at 6.30, if the workers get in the car at 6.00, they may sometimes be late because the bus in the round takes 20-25 minutes, with the bus running at a safe normal speed and walk into the factory 10-15 minutes to scan the card. In order to avoid problems with workers not getting on the bus on the lap time, the company will make a sticker separating shift colors between 6.30 and 7.00 hours, informing the Master to let the driver observe and remind the workers to get on their own round. Also, the interpreter will be asked to go to the area to communicate and distribute dormitory cards with color-coded stickers indicating the entry time.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that the shuttle bus to PT housing is overcrowded, with the bus carrying 60-70 workers when the maximum capacity should be 40 persons.  He thinks that it is very dangerous to have to commute to work in these overcrowded buses.
remediation_action: The business investigated and found that due to more new workers staying in PT housing, the shuttle bus at certain pick-up times have been overcrowded.  The business announced to the workers the shuttle bus timetables again and issued color-coded stickers to indicate the time that each worker can get on the shuttle bus. The business also increased the number of shuttle buses to accommodate the demand.
remediation_validation: Workers confirmed that the shuttle buses are not overcrowded with the new sticker system indicating the time when workers can get on the buses.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case. The business has taken action to solve the overcrowding issue and workers have confirmed that their commute by shuttle bus is now much improved.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case.  The workers are not being pressured to hit unrealistic targets anymore in both Lines 5 & 6, and HR has trained the supervisors on how to communicate targets without threatening workers.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers from sewing line 6 reported having a hard time dealing with their line supervisor because she asks for the high demand of up to 40 pieces per hour, it used to be 15-20 in the past. Workers reported being pressured to work faster, the supervisor shouts and put pressure on them to work faster, and threatened them by saying that they will be moved to a different production line or sent to HR if they can not reach the target. Workers reported since the news increased wages, the business is putting pressure on workers to work faster, there was also an issue at line 5 where all workers left the production yesterday and went home as they could not bear the pressure to complete the expected workload.

Talking points:
-Are there changes in the production demands and are workers being asked to reach double the previous target?
-Is HR aware that line supervisors are threatening punishment to workers for not meeting targets?
-What are the incentives if the workers meet the target?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Investigate this matter, whether line supervisors have been unprofessional by shouting at workers and threatening punishment for workers not meeting increased targets
-Train supervisors on how to communicate production targets without the use of shouting and threatening punishment to workers
-Review the production targets set by the company, as workers have expressed that there's too much pressure from the increased workload
-Communicate clearly with all workers the company's target system, and the reason for any adjustments in the targets made
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Line 6, K. Leena, the HR manager will investigate this matter and get back to us next week. She mentioned that currently, the company does not have an incentives policy.
Line 5, She was aware of this issue, she investigated and the root cause is the line supervisor of line 5 was on sick leave for a week. Then another supervisor came to help but he didn't know how to communicate or care for the workers. That is why workers walk out and do not work overtime. However, HR trained supervisors on how to communicate production targets without shouting and threatening workers with punishment. Simultaneously, HR communicated clearly with the workers' Line 5 and the reason for any changes to the targets made. Line 5 is currently functioning normally.
remediation_notes: Workers reported having a hard time dealing with their line supervisor who was demanding they complete up to 40 pieces per hour, whereas the target used to be 15-20 in the past. remediation_action: HR will investigate this matter and get back to us next week. She mentioned that currently, the company does not have an incentives policy. HR conducted the investigation and found that in Line 5, the line supervisor was on sick leave for a week and another supervisor filled in but he didn't know how to communicate effectively or care for the workers. This resulted in Line 5 workers walking out and not working overtime. HR trained the supervisors on how to communicate production targets without shouting and threatening workers with punishment. HR also found that there was confusion among Line 6 workers and so HR communicated clearly with them about the reason for any changes to the targets.
remediation_validation: Issara followed up with a worker who confirmed that the issues in Line 5&6 were about unrealistic targets. In line 6, the workers have been working on swim suits, with the target of 15-20 pieces per hour in the past but in the third week of September, the line supervisor asked workers to finish 40 pieces per hour. In the same way, in line 5, they have been working on striped skirts (children's wear), producing up to 9 pieces per hour but when the supervisor asked for 10 pieces per hour, the workers went home. The worker noted that these days, both issues have been solved. In line 6, the workers are now working on zipped trousers and the target is not too high. In line 5, the business accepts any amount the worker can produce.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case.  The workers are not being pressured to hit unrealistic targets anymore in both Lines 5 & 6, and HR has trained the supervisors on how to communicate targets without threatening workers.

closed_notes: Issara escalated this issue with the business and recommended investigation into the poor treatment of the line supervisors toward two workers that have been retaliated and lack of response from the ER office when the workers reported the maltreatment from their supervisor. The business responded that the ER staff have been instructed to respond more appropriately to worker grievances and that there would be a training on implementing grievance mechanisms conducted by Verite in the Q1 or 2 of this year. However, the business did not address the line supervisor’s mistreatment of the workers, simply noting that the workers had not received permission from the line supervisor prior to going to the ER office and therefore had received warnings.  The workers noted that they had informed their supervisors before going to ER and so refused to sign the warning letters they had received.   This shows that the company’s grievance mechanism is not working effectively and workers are losing trust that their reports will be responded to appropriately.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with workers being treated poorly by their line supervisor and the line manager regarding their holidays. Workers added that they were being asked to switch their day off from Sunday to weekdays as needed as the business wants to avoid paying double for working on Sundays. Workers added that the line supervisor and the manager threaten them by saying that they can be fired, moved to a different working line which has poor working conditions, or workers to find buyers if they refuse to work on Sunday and have a rest during weekdays. 

Added on 17 Dec, 2022. 
Context: In regards to this issue, 2 female workers who refused to switch their day off reported being moved to a different line as retaliation. Since the business has ceased/solved this issue, for the time being, those workers want to come back to their original working line.

Regular shift hours and wages should be respected at all times, in line with contractual agreements. Changes in shifts should be made with the consent of workers and with reasonable notice, ensuring that total weekly working hours are in compliance with national law, and extra hours are paid at a premium rate. Workers should not be forced or coerced to agree to the changes. Shifts should not be changed in order to avoid paying premium overtime and holiday rates.
The business shall conduct an investigation to find out the root cause of the issues and remediate the workers if the result found workers being forced to change their day off. 
The business is recommended to have conversation with the workers and come to an agreement for a fixed day off. 
The process that the business has been practicing should be on a voluntary basis. No workers should be forced to change or switch their day off against their will.
The business should coordinate with the production and come up with a plan where workers' days off are not being switched or changed often. Workers have rights to have a fixed day off so that they can make their personal plans for the activities. 
If there is work during the days off of workers, the business shall ask workers if they would like to work on that day, and if so, the business should pay the wages according to the LPA 2x and 3x for OT during day off. 
The investigation with the line supervisor and the manager should be taken to investigate the treatment that they had with the workers and provide the training and disciplinary measure according to the business policy. 
Workers should not be threatened with being moved to a harder production line, getting fired from their job or having to find a new buyer for not agreeing to switch their day off.
After the investigation process, the business should conduct communication in written and verbal with all workers who have been impacted by this issue.


Update from workers (14 Jan 2022) : 

The two female workers who were sent to a different line for speaking up during the business communication session updated that they do not want to come back to their original line given that they have been treated poorly by the line supervisor but the business did not conduct any proper action to address the issues. In detail, these two workers did not receive overtime working hours like other workers for two weeks because they refused to switch their day off as requested by the business. The workers approached the ER as they were left out from the OT working hours. The ER staff did not conduct an investigation against the line supervisor but simply asked the workers if they wanted to change to new lines. Workers accepted to work for the new line as they did not have any other options and have been working in that line. Last week, these two workers were provided with a warning letter by their original working line supervisor (P Yat) for going to the HR office during working hours. Workers were called to the officer to sign the warning letter, but the workers did not sign because they had informed their supervisor about their visit to ER and they only took around 30 minutes which contrasted with the accusation of the supervisor who said that they took around one hour going out without her permission. 

Note: 
In summary, these two workers do not want to go back to their original, however, Issara wants to highlight how workers' issues are being handled improperly by the ER without a proper investigation to find out the root cause. This is to explain to the business how the grievance is not working effectively which drives workers reporting to Issara and losing trust of using internal grievances. 


Recommendations: 
-For the two workers, investigate the line supervisor and the manager’s treatment of the workers (OT hours not given, warning letter given for going to ER); provide the training and disciplinary measure according to the business policy. 
-After the investigation process, the business should provide an update on the investigation results to the impacted workers. 
-For the four workers, reassign them to their original lines, since they did not consent willingly to switch lines 
-The business should focus on the safeguard for the workers and clearly communicate with the supervisors that there should be no reprisals against these workers after relocation to their original line.
remediation_business_steps_taken: For two workers that had refused to work on their day-off, their line supervisor targeted them and denied them the opportunity to work on future Sundays when pay would be double wages after the company had made the policy change to keep Sundays the day-off and pay workers double if worked.  When they went to Employee Relations to report this issue, they were just told they could move to a different line if they wanted rather than addressing the line supervisor’s retaliatory behavior.  On top of that, they received warnings for having gone to the ER office without receiving permission from their line supervisors beforehand.  Issara re-escalated this issue with the business and recommended a further investigation into the poor treatment of the line supervisors toward these workers and lack of response from the ER office when the workers reported the maltreatment.  The business responded that the ER staff have been instructed to respond more appropriately to worker grievances and that there would be a training on implementing grievance mechanisms conducted by Verite in the Q1 or 2 of this year. However, the business did not address the line supervisor’s mistreatment of the workers, simply noting that the workers had not received permission from the line supervisor prior to going to the ER office and therefore had received warnings.  The workers noted that they had informed their supervisors before going to ER and so refused to sign the warning letters they had received.   This shows that the company’s grievance mechanism is not working effectively and workers are losing trust that their reports will be responded to appropriately.
remediation_business_steps_remaining: The business to conduct proper investigation to access the behavior of the supervisor and take proper action.
remediation_notes:
Workers in the “Pla Sod” line reported being asked to work on Sunday (the typical day off for workers) to meet production demands, and switch their day off to another weekday day. Some workers reported this was not voluntary or communicated in advance, and workers reported not being paid the 2x legal rate for Sunday work.  This was reported for Nov 7 and 14, and some workers noted this practice had been long-standing.  Worker contracts provide for one rest day a week, and Thai labor law establishes a 2x daily wage for Sunday work, and 3x daily wage for official holiday day work.
 
For two workers that had refused to work on their Sunday day-off, their line supervisor targeted them and denied them the opportunity to work on future Sundays after the company made the policy change to keep Sundays the day-off and pay workers double if worked on Sundays.  When the workers went to Employee Relations (ER) office to report being denied work on Sundays, they were just told they could move to a different line if they wanted rather than the ER staff addressing the line supervisor’s retaliatory behavior.  On top of that, they received warnings for having gone to the ER office without receiving permission from their line supervisors beforehand
remediation_action:
This issue was escalated to TU corporate HR and to the Sustainability Director.  The business conducted an investigation and noted that it has followed company policy to notify employees in advance to make sure that employees voluntarily agree to work, and they will sign consent for it.  To solve the issue, the business said it would pay double wages to the workers when they are asked to work on their weekly day-off on Sunday in the future and make sure that workers understand that it is voluntary.  However, the business did not say whether it would reimburse workers the double wages for days-off worked in the past.  

Issara conducted a follow-up escalation call and shared further details on the 2 workers that had experienced retaliation for refusing to work on their day off.  These 2 workers had already moved to a different line and did not want to return to their original line but the Employee Relations (ER) office had not responded to their grievance about being denied work on Sundays. The business responded that the ER staff have been instructed to respond more appropriately to worker grievances in the future and that there would be a training on implementing grievance mechanisms conducted by Verite in the Q1 or 2 of this year. However, the business did not address the line supervisor’s mistreatment of the workers, simply noting that the workers had not received permission from the line supervisor prior to going to the ER office and therefore had received warnings.
remediation_validation:
The workers confirmed that the business announced that they would receive double wages for working on their day-off from December onwards. However, they did not hear anything about reimbursement for working on Sundays in the past.

The two workers noted that they had informed their supervisors before going to ER office and so refused to sign the warning letters they had received.
remediation_results:
The business' investigation did not the address the issue of workers being targeted and being denied Sunday work opportunities to receive double pay. 
 The investigation report only noted that the supervisor had not granted permission to these workers to go to the ER office and therefore had been given warning letters.  It does not take into account that the workers have stated clearly that they informed their supervisor that they were going to the ER office.  Also, the business has not taken any steps to investigate the line supervisor's punitive behavior and seek to redress the problem.  This shows that the company’s grievance mechanism is not working effectively and workers are losing trust with the system and fear their reports will not be responded to appropriately.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
The business should provide training to production staff and HR on fair and ethical treatment towards workers. 
HR shall work closely with production to make sure workers rights are respected, that they receive the right payment according to the LPA, and that the company policies are clearly communicated and followed by all relevant staff. Workers should not be forced or coerced to work during their day off.
systems_change_business_steps_taken: For the Verite training, K Prad noted that he had spoken to Verite about collaborating with Issara on grievance mechanism training for two groups, the line supervisors group and HR/ER/interpreters group.  He will inform us after having received Verite's response on their position as to whether they would be willing to conduct the training together with Issara.  K Prad noted it would happen in Q1 or Q2 of this year.
systems_change_business_steps_remaining: The business to conduct proper investigation to access the behavior of the supervisor and take proper action.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with workers being charged a different amount of fees compared to past years for their document extension process. 

Issara recommendations remediation:

-The business to clarify what are the fees being collected for document processes, what is the breakdown of those fees, and why are the fees that high? And to explain to all workers how the process will be done during this time (COVID 19). 

-The business to charge workers only the legal amounts allowed by the government for workers' document extensions. 

-Workers should be remediated for any fees they paid above the legal amount. 

-The business to coordinate with the recruitment agency to return the money to the different batches of workers who were impacted. It is the responsibility of the business to make sure that all workers received their money back regardless of the recruitment agency agrees to pay back or not. 

-Workers should receive their money back within a pay period.



Talking Points 
-Ask the business how is the process of document extension for four years of MoU workers being handled? How much do workers have to pay and to whom? 

Please ask for the cost break down. 

-Who is the focal person for the document extension process from the business? Is a Thai RA handling this process, if so, what is the name of the RA and what is the agreement between the RA and GFPT? 

-How many workers are going through this process at the moment, how many have done it this year and how many more would need to extend the documents?

-Please ask the same questions for 2 years of document extension. 

-Please ask the business about the 14500 B that the workers paid in May and whether that will be returned to workers.

-Please share with the business the official amount that can be charged to the worker for the one-year extension. 

-Share information about the August 2020 Cabinet Resolution, that allows workers to complete their 4 years of the MOU contract to register to work in Thailand until March 2022.


Additional talking points Nov 30, 2020
Recommendations for remediation:

Ask for the cost breakdown of these fees (the breakdown that GFPT shared after the last meeting is for Fresh MOU, so that is not applicable/relevant for this case). Explain that the fees workers have reported having to pay are much higher than the official fees. 

Provide the details of the official fees as follows:
MOU 2 years document extension: 1,900THB (work permit) + 500THB (medical check-up) + 1,900 THB (visa for 1 year)+ 80THB (registration fee): 4,380THB. Workers should be reimbursed for any amount they have paid that is above the official cost. 
MOU 4 years extension (as per the Cabinet Resolution 4 August 2020): 1,450 THB (work permit)+500 (medical check-up)+1,900 (visa from Aug/Oct to March 2012)+ 80 THB (registration fee): 3,930 THB. GFPT said during the last meeting that this process is still ongoing for 200-300 workers, ask where exactly is the process, how many batches or number of workers are covered under the Cabinet Resolution of Aug and how many are not? What is the process and what are the fees for those who may not be covered with the Cabinet resolution (maybe those that completed the 4 years before Aug)? The business to share the details of the process being followed for workers completing 4 years of MOU. If GPFT says that they do not know and that it is all being handled by the Thai RA, explain the importance of GFPT being aware of the full process and the cost breakdown. Recommend GFPT to work with the RA to get all the detailed information to be shared with workers. 
The business should communicate with all workers what is the cost breakdown, how would the process be handled by GFPT and the RA(s), and how long would the process take to be completed. 


Recommendation for the plan to prepare for Tesco Zero fees policy that will enter into force in March 2021:

Explain to GFPT that we can provide guidance and recommendations to help them prepare for the enforcement of Tesco Employer Pays Policy that will be going into effect in March 2021
According to Tesco Employer Pays Policy :

All suppliers must obtain a clear understanding of the processes and costs associated with migrant worker recruitment. This should be presentable as a recruitment map, timeline and/or flowchart and include all the fees and costs incurred for migrant worker recruitment in origin, transit (where applicable) and destination countries.
Action plan and migrant worker recruitment policy of suppliers should be in line with the employer pays principle and the ILO definition on recruitment fees and costs. Thus, it is very important for GFPT to understand those definitions and revise service agreements with RAs as needed. As noted on Tesco policy, the employer should also cover fees happening in the source country, thus the service agreements with RAs should be revised accordingly. 

-Share with Issara any existing service agreement so that we can provide recommendations to increase transparency and clarity between all parties. 
-Share with Issara the recruitment plans, so that Issara-GFPT-RAs can work together to improve the recruitment process and mitigate the first mile risks. 
-Issara can support with training for RAs and GFPT, provide technical support to improve systems and documents and support job seekers throughout a CSO network in the source countries to mitigate first mile risks.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Workers reported their annual leaves being used by the business for quarantine days if workers were found positive or at high risk from COVID. 

Talking Points; 

Workers have reported their annual leave being used for the quarantine days, could the business explain what is the current practice for this issue? 
How many workers are in this situation and what has been the process for them so far? How many days of quarantine are required for close contact and positive cases? Who pays for those quarantine days? 
Has the business checked the government regulations on what Covid-related care services are to be covered by the business and/or SSO and whether and how quarantine days for Covid close contacts are to be paid?  

Recommendations:
The business should confirm the latest government regulations related to quarantine periods for Covid close contacts and how pay for missed working days due to quarantine is to be handled We have received the update that the government regulations are as follows:  If a worker is found to be positive at the factory, she/he is supposed to be sent to the hospital for the PCR test and if confirmed as positive, receive the medical certificate and recommended to quarantine. The worker should get paid sick leave during those days. 
If a worker is in close contact, s/he should visit the hospital and report why she/he is at high risk and get the recommendations from the hospital. The regular recommendation for vaccinated people is to take 10 days of quarantine and do another test on the 10th day. 
If the result is negative, then the worker can start working. In terms of the wages for the high-risk workers who have a medical certificate for their quarantine days, the employer can submit the worker information to the SSF for 62% of wages. 
If the worker is not allowed to go to the hospital but the employer orders the worker to take quarantine, it is the responsibility of the employer to pay the worker wages. 
The business should communicate with the workers about how to quarantine days for close contacts and positive workers will be paid. 

Time Frame; 1 week.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
TUM explained that the business policy is as follows.  For close contacts (living in close quarters with Covid-positive persons) and Covid infected workers: TUM will use 2 annual leave days first, then 3 business leave days second, and then to use sick leave for the remainder.  The business made it a point to say that the workers will receive full wages during the quarantine period, including their incentives and bonus pay.  This is applied to all nationalities.  Used to be 14 quarantine days; this year, it’s 7 quarantine days, and then ATK before returning to work for close contact cases.  For Covid-positive workers, it’s 10 quarantine days; after 7 days ATK, and then on the 10th day.  The business provides a separate quarantine area for such workers.  For quarantine days, no MC is required.
This policy has been communicated to all workers.

The business noted that their current policy pays the workers fully including incentive pay for all quarantine days whereas the government policy allows for 62% of wages from SSF for close contact cases.

TUM to make the public announcement again about this policy next week.  TUM will send the written policy in three languages to Issara as well.  TUM will consider with management whether they can be flexible with the Covid quarantine policy, to accommodate requests from workers that wish to use their annual leave at another time and not be required to use annual leave for quarantine days.

The business is working on a new policy update for the worker's annual leave related to Covid-19 quarantine. it will be announced soon and effected on the first of June 1st, 2022.

6 June 2022 follow up 
the worker's annual leave optional policy 

Business response: K Prad said he is following up with TUM and waiting for the written new annual leave policy if he received it will share it with Issara soon.
remediation_notes:
Workers reported their annual leave days were being used by the business for quarantine days if workers were found to be positive or at high risk to COVID-19.

The latest Thai government regulations regarding Covid-19 measures are as follows: 
- If a worker is found to be Covid-positive at the factory, she/he is to be sent to the hospital for the RT-PCR test and if confirmed as positive, receive a medical certificate and recommended to quarantine. The worker should get paid sick leave during those days. 
- If a worker is comes in close contact with a Covid-infected person and is a "high risk", s/he should visit the hospital and report why she/he is at high risk and get the recommendations from the hospital. The regular recommendation for vaccinated people is to take 10 days of quarantine and do another test on the 10th day. If the test result is negative, then the worker can resume working. In terms of the wages for the high-risk workers who have a medical certificate for their quarantine days, the employer can submit the worker information to the Social Security Office to receive 62% of wages. 
- If the worker is not allowed to go to the hospital but the employer orders the worker to quarantine, it is the responsibility of the employer to pay the worker's wages.
remediation_action:
Issara escalated this issue with the Sustainability Director.  TUM explained that the business policy is as follows.  For close contacts (living in close quarters with Covid-positive persons) and Covid infected workers: TUM will use 2 annual leave days first, then 3 business leave days second, and then to use sick leave for the remainder.  The business made it a point to say that the workers will receive full wages during the quarantine period, including their incentives and bonus pay.  This is applied to all nationalities. This policy has been communicated previously to all workers but the business will make the announcement to workers again about this policy.

The business is working on a new policy update for the worker's annual leave related to Covid-19 quarantine. it will be announced soon and effected on the first of June 1st, 2022.  Issara received the policy announcement from TUM, which still states that for quarantine periods for high-risk persons, the company will use annual leave and then sick leave for those quarantine days rather than allowing the workers the option to choose whether they want to use their annual leave days for this or not.
remediation_validation: Issara followed up with the workers, and they noted that the business did not just take 2 annual leave days; rather, all their annual leave days were used up for their quarantine days.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case because the business has decided to continue its policy to mandate annual leave days be used for workers that need to quarantine for Covid prevention reasons, rather than making it optional and allowing workers to choose whether or not to use their annual leave days for the quarantine period.

Requesting annual leave also the same. They try to finish the target as much as they can and they help each other when they have the sewing pieces accumulated in the line. Because of her loud voice, some workers, who do not understand Thai, thought that she was scolding them in front of the public. She can communicate in a soft way and pleasant way as the workers are also trying their job the best. For Thai workers, she used her voice softly and for Burmese workers, her voice tone is so hard. call_details.description:
Client updated about the abusive behavior of the line supervisor. 
The client name is Zin Mar Wai, ID:721626. She is currently in PU-4, in line no.67 managed by the line supervisor P'Pa-Yin. 
It's been about a week since the supervisor is finding a mistake on her. She has been working in this line for three years. As she has a problem with her digestive issue, she has to go to the toilet every morning for a week. Sometimes, one time, sometimes two times in the morning. But, she can still handle her points. Although there are two workers in other lines, she handles that task alone. But, she can manage it although she has to go to the toilet because of her health problem. Today, the supervisor called and blamed her for going to the toilet for a long time. Then she told the supervisor that there are many people queuing in front of the toilet this morning and she has to wait. But, the supervisor blamed her for giving the excuse. Then she talked back to the supervisor about why she is telling her like that because she can still handle her points and it's a health problem. Then they argued with each other and finally they asked the translator, Ko Soe Naing, to go and help her to translate for her. She would like the translator to help her translate. Please let the supervisor change the line if she doesn't like her. But, the translator didn't translate all that she said and he told her that she cannot change the line because there is nowhere that needs other workers to support. And he asked her to listen to what the supervisor suggested to her instantly. Actually, she came and joined the business as a sewer and she was asked to do trimming and punch the button hole. Now, it seems like they are asking her to do small tasks and assign her to unimportant roles. Whenever there is not much work, she is asked not to work and gets only 75% of daily wage.
So she became so upset, not only from the supervisor, but also from the translator, and then she decided to leave the job. Then she requests the resignation letter and she signs. The translator reminds her that you will not get a job changeable cancellation letter if you decide to leave by yourself. But, at that time, she cannot make a decision   and change her mind. 
In the evening, she called Issara and explained about this. She is wondering if the business can swift her the line, she will continue to work. She is wondering if we can help her discuss the business although she has submitted the resignation letter. If they don't want her anymore, she requests to provide her job changeable cancellation letter.
call_details.next_steps: Have to alert ILM team in email.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue # 1
Context; The issue with two repeatedly reported supervisors in the respective production lines. Supervisors are reported being verbally abusive, discriminative, and providing preferences towards Thai workers only, complaining to Burmese workers for any request they make. Supervisor name  P'Lei, in Line no. 110. and P'Bua, in Line no. 405.  

Previously Provided Recommendations; 

-The business to conduct an investigation with this specific supervisor. In order to assess the behavior of the supervisors, the business can conduct a survey where workers can rate their supervisors confidentially. Given that workers may not know their supervisors' Thai names, it is recommended that the business arrange an org-chart with all supervisors' names and titles. 
-There should not be any coercion or retaliation towards workers during the investigation and survey processes. The investigation process must be confidential, workers should not be needing to provide any of their personal information, such as working IDs, their names, etc.
-The business should create a plan of action based on the results of investigations and surveys. Such actions should include training and disciplinary actions (if necessary).
-To communicate to workers the actions the business is taking to respond to workers' grievances, would help the business to strengthen the trust of workers in the business grievance mechanism.


Business actions for the previous report; 
-The business conducted an investigation, then took disciplinary actions towards the line supervisor and provided training on fair and ethical treatment of workers. 
-The business didn't share the details of the investigation with Issara.

Recommendations that are missing to follow by the business. NOTE FOR BHR; Please suggest the business follow the following missing recommendations.
- Recommend the business to take disciplinary actions towards these supervisors following the company protocol. Since  this is the second time these supervisors are reported, please ask the company what would be the appropriate disciplinary actions in this case? Is it a written warning?
- Workers reported that the previous actions taken by the business helped improved the situation for a while, but now the supervisors are having abusive behaviors again. For this reason, it is recommended for the business to have a monitoring plan where they can hear from workers directly what the situation is and if further actions are needed. 
-The monitoring plan could be done by creating safe spaces for workers to share their feedback (e.g. morning talks) or the company could also conduct confidential survey with all workers under these two supervisors.

There should not be any coercion or retaliation towards workers during the investigation, open dialogue sessions and survey processes. The investigation process must be confidential, workers should not be needing to provide any of their personal information, such as working IDs, their names, etc. and workers should receive an explanation of the no retaliation policy that would guarantee safeguards. 
-To work on a plan of actions based on the result of the survey/investigation/dialogue with workers. 
-To communicate to workers the actions the business is taking to respond to workers' grievances, would help the business to strengthen the trust of workers in the business grievance mechanism.

Talking Points.
-What is the business action for such repeated issues? 
-Please propose to the business that Issara is happy to provide training to all supervisors and the HR after the business investigation.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; The issue with a worker being targeted by two clerks and one blue cap supervisor after she raised the issue with the business.

-The business to investigate with the staff involved in the issue and with the rest of workers in the working line to find out the root cause of the issue. 
-The business to make sure that the workers feel free to raise any issue they face and that the reported issues should be handled anonymously and confidentially. 
-The business to make sure that transparency is in place when making any decision towards the staff involved. 
-Issara can help with the online tri parties investigation if needed. 


**Talking Points**

Please share the issue detail including the worker's feedback on the business grievance not being anonymous. 
Ask the following questions with the business. 
-Is HR aware of this issue? If yes, what was the root cause of the issue? 
-How did they receive this issue and from whom? 
-How did they conduct the investigation and what made them decide this worker be moved to a different line? 
-What had the business done to make sure the safeguard for the workers. 
-Did the business aware that the worker was being targeted by the blue cap and the clerks after she raised the issue with the green cap about their poor behavior? 
-What has the business done to make sure that all supervisors are aware of the business's no retaliation policy and follow accordingly? 
-Has the business ever received any complaints about the blue cap and clerks in the past? If yes, what was the action that had been taken towards them?
-What are the grievance channels for the workers to raise their issues anonymously and how were they being introduced to the workers? 
-How often does the business receive the issues from those channels if any available.

Thet Thet Aye said that it is not sure, even if you should get , she will have to wait two years. On 7th May she went to Office to discuss about the compensation from SSF with P. Kont. As soon as she arrived to Office, the translator, Ko Myint Swe asked her " why are you coming to office very often". So the client had to explain that she came to office yesterday for missing payment and she is coming office today to discuss about the compensation from SSF with P. Kont. Finally Ko Myint Swe ( translator) let her see P. Kont. In her discussion with P. Kont , P. Kont said she didn't know about this incident and sorry to hear that. However, P. Kon't didn't let her know what is the plan of SCC to help her getting compensation from SSF. After meeting with P.
