description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: violation of law

call_details.next_steps: To coordinate with BHR
call_details.source_recruiter_name: International Focus General Services Co., Ltd

closed_notes:
Issara had several meetings with Okeanos about this issue, including an
escalation call. Okeanos responded that they had consulted with their lawyers and that TU maintains that the Thai Labor Protection Act allows businesses to allocate when workers would take their annual leave days. Issara has sent a report to the Strategic partners with the request of having a try parties call to strengthen the system. However, the try parties call has not taken place yet and no further actions will be taken by the employer. Therefore, this case is being closed as there have been no improvements or changes for several months.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
4-Jan-2020

The issue with the workers being deducted 4 of their annual leaves by the business for the new year (2), Chinese new year (1), and Songkran (1). This is for the year 2020. The business does not ask for any consent. This is set by the business without asking for the worker's consent. The reason that the workers shared the issue now is that they do not want this issue to be continued in 2021. 


Talking points:
-Ask the business what is their policy about annual leave to check what is their understanding of LPA Section 30. 
-Ask the business how was workers annual leave from last year handled. Ask if the business asked workers consent to allocate the annual leave on specific dates.  1) If the business says that they did not ask for consent because their interpretation of the law is that they can allocate annual leave, please explain to the business the actual interpretation of the law and the nature of the Labour Protection Act. 2) If the company says that they asked workers consent and that it was voluntary, shared with the business the conflicting information coming from WV channels where workers reported not being aware of the allocation of annual leave, thus the process was not voluntary. 

Remediation recommendations:
-The business should restate workers annual leave if the decision of using annual leave during those days was not voluntary. This means that, all workers should receive 4 days of annual leave back. 
-Workers should are entitled of 6 days of annual leave per year, and they can request to the employer when they would like to use it, and the business shall approve the days requested by the worker. But the business is not entitled to allocate workers annual leave. 

-In order to avoid misunderstanding regarding public holidays and business closure dates, it is recommended for the business to share the 13 public holidays for the years of 2021 with all workers and Issara. 

LPA; Section 30.An employee who has worked for an uninterrupted period of one year, is entitled to annual holidays of not less than six working days in one year, to be determined by the employer in advance for the employee or as agreed by the employer and employee.  In the following year, the employer may determine annual holidays exceeding six working days for the employee.  The employer and the employee may agree in advance to accumulate and carry forward any unused annual holiday to be included in the following year.  For the employee who has not completed one year of service, the employer may set annual holidays for the employee on a pro rata basis. 
The Employer and the Employee may agree in advance to accumulate and postpone any annual Holiday that has not yet been taken in a year to be included in the following years. For the Employee who has not completed one year of service, the Employer may set annual Holidays for the Employee on a pro-rata basis.

Time Frame ; 2 weeks.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara had several meetings with
Okeanos about this issue, including an
escalation call. Okeanos responded that
they had consulted with their lawyers, and that TU maintains that the Thai Labor Protection Act allows businesses to determine when workers would take their annual leave days. The Thai LPA (section 30) language on this matter is unclear and comes down to an
interpretation of the word “or”. The
the fundamental underlying issue, however, is if an employer selecting a worker's annual leave is ethical and meets international standards and global buyer’s supplier requirements/expectations - not just if it is legal under Thai labor law or not.
remediation_business_steps_remaining: The business did not take any of Isasra's recommendations for the remediation.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that 4 out of 6 of their annual leaves are being used by the business without their consent.
remediation_action:
Issara had several meetings with Okeanos, including an escalation call with the Thai Union Asia Sustainability Director. Thai Union responded that, after consulting with its lawyers, they maintain that the Thai Labor Protection Act allowed their business to determine when workers can take annual leave days. 

Issara’s position is that the Thai Labor Protection Act (LPA) does allow workers to choose when they would like to use their annual leave days. The language of LPA is not well-worded, opening the door for different interpretations. At a minimum, from an ethical stance alone, Issara believes the employer should consult the employee about when the employee would take annual leave.
remediation_validation: Workers believe it is improper for their employer to determine the dates of their annual leave without their consent.
remediation_results: Issara considers this case closed unsatisfactorily as the business is not willing to take any further steps on this issue.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Communication:

-The business to make written and verbal announcements to all workers regarding the annual leave policy (which should follow LPA) and clarify to workers what is the internal process for them to request annual leave. 
-The business should also communicate to workers when would their annual leave from last year (2020) would be restated. 

-Issara to provide training on labour rights to HR if needed.
systems_change_business_steps_remaining: Okeanos did not take any action for system improvements. Okeanos responded that they had consulted with their lawyers and that TU maintains that the Thai Labor Protection Act allows businesses to determine when workers would take their annual leave days.

2. She can no longer work at KOTO as she applied CI book. (She received the CI book already. ) She has submitted the resignation letter since March 10th. She is hoping to get the resignation letter soon as requested by her new employer. She is worried that she won’t get the letter in time. 3. Our informant suspects that she and her friends are being targeted by Arkar, the translator, for being informant to Issara. Last Thursday, 2 girls (Purpule passport holders) had to beg Arkar to help them with visa extension. Arkar told the girls that they should go by themselves for visa extension. The girls said, “We don’t know where to go and how to do it. We just know the market place around this area.” The girls pleaded him to accompany and help them with the extension. call_details.description:
Informant being targeted
This informant is the daughter of ex-informant who left KOTO already. She said that her mother was targeted by Akar, the bad translator, for being an informant to Issara. That’s why she has a huge concern being an informant to us. She doesn’t want to end up with the situation like her mother did. This is one of the main reasons Issara has not been receiving as much worker voice as it should. It would be great if Business must ensure the safe guard for the worker is one of the COCs required by the Buyer. 
Sick Leave
Workers are being barred from getting OT for 6 days, if they take sick leave. For example: a worker gets sick during work. And she meets the nurse at the clinic inside the factory compound. The worker would be asked to stop doing OT for a week. For the workers who take sick leave a day or two also would be asked to stop doing OT for a week. It would be great if KOTO can clarify how OTs are being provided to the workers. 
Foul smell
Workers are unable to sleep well due to the foul smell from the sewage pools near the housing. It smells worse when receiving raw shrimps. Closing all the windows and doors doesn’t help. Issara team had such experience, getting the foul smell, during the housing visit last year. 
Clinic
Workers claim that the clinic provide the same medicine most of the time. A worker, patient, wanted to measure blood pressure to check if the blood pressure is normal. The patient doesn’t know how to speak Thai. So he pointed his finger to sphygmomanometer, hoping the nurse would understand what he wants her to do. Unfortunately, the nurse couldn’t understand what he was trying to say. And he left the clinic without knowing her blood pressure. Although there is a translated chart for basic sickness, the clinic still need an interpreter to provide comprehensive service to the patients. 
 
Housings
This is an old issue which has not been solved yet. Some workers went back to Myanmar as they are not comfortable with the current housing arrangement. 4 to 8 workers, including married couples, sharing the same room while it is not the case for Thai workers. Workers have to pay for water and electric city bill. Both Thai and Myanmar workers don’t have to pay for the room. The informant said, Akar, the translator is sharing his room with his wife only. Even Akar’s brother is allowed to share the room with his wife. KOTO may want to clarify the housing arrangement for both Thai and Myanmar workers without discrimination across the two nationalities, the translator and his brother. 
Visitor regulation
Workers also want to know more about receiving visitors. The informant heard that Arkar asks for money from some visitors. It’s not clear why and how much he asks for money. KOTO might want to investigate the case if they are willing.

description: Issues with rent/utilities/other housing costs and how these should be paid

call_details.description:
Target amount: The workers have to complete the target amount 32 baskets.
Only people who have been there 7-10 years can complete it. In some lines, shrimp distribution is fair. Sometimes, if there are many people at shrimp peeling line, your supervisor will ask you to go and help another line (arranging shrimp) which have less worker, but when you go to another line, supervisor from another line will ask you: what are you doing here? And when you cannot say anything and go back to your original work station, other supervisor will found you are going around in the room without working then you got scolded again. There are 13 supervisors, so that the worker could not know which supervisor they are interacting with. 
Water flow system: Actually, you can turn on the water to flow automatically but the supervisor do not allow you to let the water flow all the time, so that you have to use one hand to press water and another hand to hold the shrimp. You also need to take care the shrimp not to fall. The room was very cold and the water is also very cold so that most of the worker cannot work there. If the worker shirt gets wet, they are not allowing to change it.
Working hour and Shift schedule: The working time still unstable and the worker have to stand by anytime they are calling if the shrimp arrived. Sometimes, the worker doesn’t have enough rest period especially, on the day that they have extra cleaning duty (2.5 hours). Normally, if you don’t complete the target amount, you cannot work for OT. However, if it is on the cleaning day, you don’t want to work OT because it will be too late, but you cannot refuse it because the cleaning to be done after the shift (8 hours + OT + 2.5 hours cleaning). In the next day, if you have to work on early shift, it is hard for the worker. Sometimes, if the line run out of shrimp/raw materials, the workers have to take meal break just after started working in 1 hour then take a meal break 1 hour and continue another 7 hours without break. So the worker got hungry and it is very hard to work in a very cold room 7 hours consecutively. The workers prefer a fixed work schedule if it is day or night. When the work schedule is changing every day, they could not manage their sleeping time and eating time so that it will affect their health. The roommates are also working in a different schedule so that you cannot have a proper rest in the housing, other people will cook and shower while you are sleeping and there is not quiet time within 24 hours. There are about 8-12 people in a room. The factory gives the reason that the working hour have to manage based on the arrival of shrimp: the workers feel that the factory does not value the human as much as they value the shrimp.  
No rights to refuse OT: It was very cold so that some of the workers don’t want to do OT but they cannot refuse it.
Dormitory: For female (single)dormitory, there is no enough bath room, no enough electric plug to cook. The worker were told that they cannot take shower more than 5 mins. Some bathroom and toilet lock are broken so that you cannot close the door. In some bed room the fan is broken but cannot ask for replacement. They complain it but nothing improved. The mattress are very old and there are bugs in it so the worker request to move it away but they were told that they cannot remove it because it will be a problem if the visitor found it. 
Electric cost: There is no clear system for electric bill. The worker got deduct the bills less if they earned less wages, and they got deduct more if they earn more.
Health care and sick leave: In order to take a sick leave, you need approval from factory clinic nurse, it is not easy. Sometimes, they will tell you to come back again for signature. It is not easy for the workers to find them again and again since the worker have to run from work. Sometimes, the worker got sick and go to see the nurse: if there is no interpreter at the nurse room, you have to wait for a long hour. The workers could not identify which nurse has bad behavior. They thought that all nurses behavior are the same. 
If you take sick leave and went to the hospital and come back with the medical certificate, you got pay only for a half day. The workers are told that they can still work for a half day.

The client said, that she and her friends are not okay to work at the current fcatory. Because of these reason...Living condition is not good and not eough space,  12 workers have to stay at the small room  with different shift, working shif are not acceptable, the RA in not taking the proper action. So the client has left the job and trying to get the cancellation letter. The caller request Issara to get the cancellation letter for them.

description: Unsafe or hazardous working conditions (OSH issues)

call_details.description: Shift schedule: The worker informed Issara that the working hours translated by Issara is not working in reality. They have to feed the chickens five times after the 21 days of chicken cycle; at 4 am, 9 am, 2:30 pm, 6:30 pm, and 9 pm. The men only left the farm at 9:30 am, 4:30 pm to have meals. The women had extra time to get back to the dormitory at 6 or 7 am and 2:30 pm or 3 pm to cook for meals. Their reason for not leaving the chicken farm except from meal times is that all the chicken will be dead if the electricity is off and no one is there to turn on in advance. -The pay slip should be in the language of the worker and understandable to the worker

-Provide the pay slips in Burmese as well so that the Burmese workers can understand the details of the payments and deductions for each pay period.

They just said the temperature is normal, but the workers are not fine with the temperature. Plus, not being provided food yesterday, made the workers weaker too.

call_details.description:
Follow up call with the client about 1. Polluted water issue, Drinking water Issue and 3. No access to ATM Issue.

1. Pollution Water Issue: Not fixed yet. The worker in Zone-C informed me that no technician came. So they just used that water and applied powder ect. The workers went to work all day and just came back. They thought everything was fixed, but not yet. 

2. Drinking water: This issue too. The informant said he didn't see any new water buckets yesterday after we talked with HR. As there are many zones (A,B,C,D,E), sometimes, they don't know if some workers from different zones have taken the bottle as the business just left the water buckets in the entrance of the dorn. Would be great if the business can allocate like 4 or 5 buckets per zone, so that they also can know who has taken and carried it to their room etc. For the water pump, I am checking with my informant in Zone-C and he said, he never saw that.

3. For the ATM issue in hotel quarantine: The informant said, the direct informant hasn't sent him the photo yet, so he cannot send it to me now. I asked the direct informant number and I just finished talking with the informant. He said it's near Siranakhon Hospital (5 min drive from the factory). It's kind of like an apartment. There are around 40 Burmese workers there and there are 4 babies who are under one year olds. While they are in hospital quarantine, the hospital quarantine provides everything, including mile power, baby meal or diapers. But now, when they were being moved to those apartments, they asked the business (P'Kyi Ya, male Burmese representative sitting in HR office), and told him that we will not take any responsibility for our baby. He just asked the workers to give money or give an ATM card to the focal so that he will buy it for the baby. But, I think they still have the responsibility to take care of the worker's baby too since their parents have to follow the business practice. 

4. Male workers have to take care of the babies: And the business managed only the father to take care of those babies and not the mother. The mothers are allocated back to MOU dorm and have to go back to work. The workers do not know why the business did like that. Actually, babies should be with the mother. They talked with P'Kyi Ya and he said the mommy work site required manpower so that they cannot let them taking care of the babies.

call_details.description:
Checking with the client how they are being communicated to relocate back to the yellow building based on BHR update on business response 1461. 
(The TUS HR said TUS paid for the Sealight room rental cost in advance for the workers and TUS will arrange free transportation for them to go back and work until the end of B&S. This group of workers said if the business would like them to go back and work the business must allow them to stay close to the factory, if not they won't go back to work because the Sealight hotel and TUS are very far and the worker said they don't want to take long transportation. This part is correct. But the business didn't communicate with them that they had to stay in a yellow building and paid the room cost after one month. They just thought they would be sent back to their own room. 
To solve the problem, workers requested the TUS discussed with the Songkhla Public health care to include the Yellow building in the TUS B&S policy. The Songkhla Public health care agreed to it and allowed 9 rooms under TUS B&S. The TUS already pays for the room rental cost for the workers. The HR said workers will have to pay for the room rental cost next month because the business already arranged for the worker at Sealight Hotel and paid the rental cost in advance already but the worker doesn't want to stay there.  
 
The HR said they have communicated with the worker many times but this group of workers are still saying that they would like to go back to their room. They don't understand B&S policy and are not interested in it. O&E check with the worker how the business communicates to you for relocation back to the yellow housing? 
The client responded that the translator called the focal persons who are assigned in the SEALIGHT Hotel to buy the kid stuff and withdraw cash. The translator called those persons to let the workers know who finished quarantine and had to go back to work. As the workers refused because of the time limitation and there is a problem with the limited bathroom in the hotel, they told those assigned persons to request the business to relocate them back to their room.   
The HR said TUS B&S policy, TUS arranged 4 people in each room during B&S, the worker can choose who they would like to stay with and send the list name of the room member to HR. All local or Burmese workers have to follow the same. 
This 20 workers group is also the same, the workers choose their room members by them self and send the name list to the HR team. The HR said the HR team did not select the people and send them to the same room.)The next day, a van arrived at the hotel and they were asked to board. At that time there was one Thai lady who came and picked them up. When the workers were about to board, she asked please raise your hands if you stay in the Yellow building in front of the building, there were 8 workers there and she asked them to please choose your friends who you think can stay with you in your rooms for only 14 days. As the workers thought only for 14 days, they chose their friends. But, the translator and that Thai lady also involved suggesting or advising the workers too. For example, if there are two couples who stay in that building, they ask them to temporarily stay like only the wifes stay with another two female workers and the two husbands stay with another two male workers. 

On that day, there were also still about 50 workers being sent to other housing near Sunday Market. But, those workers are now relocated back to their own room near near the Yellow Building. That building is called "Rakkhine Housing" and the room are more spacious. The informant who has to stay with her friends in the Yellow housing is also staying there.
Further Update:27 Sep: Yesterday, around 2 PM, the Burmese Translator (Arr Don) and P' Dium (HR) came into Yellow Housing and asked some workers to do a night shift. Since the workers have to share the room with some workers who have babies and some are leaving the job, working the night shift will make them annoyed. So they asked them to relocate them back to their own room. Then they agreed and they asked the workers to sign a paper as an agreement if they are ok to work on night shift. But they have to follow  business policy and they cannot commute except to the building to work. The landlord will strictly manage this. The workers agreed and signed and they started working the night shift. And they told the workers that you cannot go back to your room by yourselves. We have to manage you by transferring you to your room.

28 Sep,  this morning, as no one came up, the workers called the translator and asked them when they could come. The translator and P'Dium came back at 8 AM again. They told the workers that you are not able to relocate now as you have agreed to stay here and we have paid for this room. If you leave now, you have to pay the room fee for this month. The workers said, yes, we will pay. But, they said they still need the approval from management.
The workers said why they did not keep the promise and they manipulated the workers like that. They asked why another 50 workers being sent to Sunday housing and now they can go back to their room "Rakkhine Housing" and not them, the translator didn't translate it back to P'Dium. They are also not happy with the behavior or performance of the translator too.  

O&E asked the following three questions to the workers:
1. Have you been told that you have to pay that room cost after one month? 
Ans: The workers said no.

2. Did you know that you can go back to the SEALIGHT hotel if you don't want to stay here? The workers said no. Even the workers who will finish quarantine in the SEALIGHT hotel will be sent back to their housing (Rakkhine Housing) soon.

3. How long were you being communicated to stay there?
Ans: The translator and P'Dium told them as long as B&S policy.
The workers also added, not only the room cost, but also sharing the room with other workers is not a good practice. Plus, they have to work the night shift, the babies crying, and a lot of distractions.
call_details.next_steps: Have to Update ILM team to check with business why other workers from other housing and the workers in the yellow housing are not being sent back to their room yet.

closed_notes:
Issara raised this issue with the business several times including escalation calls. The business argued that they have been following the government's instructions to control the spread of the virus, but that the main causes of these issues were miscommunication. Therefore, the business formed a special team and assigned one focal for each Bubble & Seal housings in order for the workers to seek and access their basic needs and report any issues that they face in their bubble and seal dorms. Despite these changes made by the business, workers continue to report several repeated issues for several weeks even though the business had assigned a  focal for each housing. After several weeks and several meetings with the business and Issara, the business was eventually able to improve and address all of the issues that have happened in the bubble housing and workers confirmed not having issues anymore.

After the business took actions to solve the issues: 
- workers no longer reported being pressured to return to work earlier than the 14-day quarantine period since the factory was shut for the period of Sep 3-15, 2021.
- the workers confirmed that they no longer have any issues with meals.  They are receiving all meals, and the quality and quantity of the meals have improved as well.
- the workers confirmed that now there is adequate drinking water for all in the dorms and water pumps have been provided so they can dispense the water into their drinking bottles easily.
- the workers confirmed that the polluted tap water has now been solved and they have a clean tap water supply
- the female workers in the hotel quarantine have been able to buy necessary items for their babies with the help of HR making the cash withdrawals on their behalf and purchasing the requested items
- those in the hotel quarantine that had not received adequate bedding have now reported receiving bedsheets and so are satisfied with the sleeping conditions
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue #1 

Context: the issue with the COVID-19 infection. Workers reported the spread of the virus and increasing infected workers in the factory, however, they are still being asked to continue working. Workers raised their concerns about getting infected and requested clear communication about the business plan to control the infection rate and also to test 100% of the workers in the factory. In addition to that, the workers reported being threatened of not receiving their wages and of not having access to basic needs supplies such as water and food, and losing their job if they do not come to work before completing their quarantine. Workers added that they were suggested to stay 14 days of quarantine by the doctor but the business asked them to work after a few days (5 -8 days) of quarantine. 

Added Context: Workers updated that around 20 workers who have been tested positive and staying quarantined in the business quarantine center continued not receiving meals and water on (1 Sep 2021). In addition to that, the workers also have reported being forced to work OT in order to receive dinner.

Added Context: Workers updated not having purified drinking water on the 14th and 15th of September. In addition to that, workers added having polluted tap water for their daily use which causes allergics on their skin.

Recommendations: 
-The business to clearly communicate with the workers about the business plan to control the spread of the virus to a bigger number of workers in the factory and in the community.
-The business should also clearly communicate with the workers i) why they are being pushed to get back to work before completing the 14 days of quarantine, which is against the doctors’ recommendation, ii) what are the measures being taken by the business to make sure that those that have been exposed and in closed contact with positive cases do not spread the virus at the workplace if they are being asked to work before being able to confirm if they are positive or not. 
-The business should assign focal and introduce the vocals with the workers for the workers to reach out to them whenever they have questions and concerns related to COVID-19. 

Talking points:
-Is the business aware that the workers are being asked to get back to work before completing their 14 days of quarantine suggested by the doctor?  
-Workers reported being threatened of not receiving regular meals, not receiving wages for quarantine days, and even getting fired from work if they do not follow the business suggesting to get back to work before completion of 14 days of quarantine. What is the business understanding of this? 
-What has been the business action to control the number of impacted workers? 
-How many workers have been tested for COVID-19 so far and what is the testing process? 
-Are the COVID-19 regulation measures applied equally for Burmese and Thai workers, if not how so? According to the workers' report, there are different regulations for Thai, for instance, they have fewer restrictions of movement. This creates a feeling of insecurity among Burmese workers to work along with Thai workers who could have greater exposure to the virus. So what is the company policy, what is the plan to deal with these issues, and are the regulations applied equally for all workers?  


Issue #2. Added issues on 16th September 2021. 

(1) The issue with insufficient drinking water: This issue happened on 14th September, Issara raised this issue with HR in the evening of the same day, the HR responded that they were going to take immediate action, however, there were only 5 bottles of water added to only one Zone. At the rest of the Zones, workers reported not receiving water. On the 15th, workers again reported the same issue and Issara informed HR on the same day. In addition, workers have reported the issue to the focal person, however, the issues haven’t been resolved. Despite all the reports made by workers about the issue with water, which is a basic need, the business hasn’t addressed it and workers continue to experience difficulties accessing clean water. 

Recommended next steps: 
To conduct the investigation and provide enough drinking water to all of the workers with the ratio of at least two liters of purified water per worker per day. 
To introduce the focal person from HR for workers and the housing focal to reach out if they have issues. And have clear communication with workers about the actions the business will take to solve the issues and the timelines of those actions. 
To set up an emergency group to work on such issues immediately. 
Set up the system so all workers have access to adequate drinking water and water containers are not taken away by some workers to their rooms. The system should guarantee access to clean water and it should be effective and hygienic. 

(2) The issue with polluted tap water: Issara received the issue on 14th and reached out to the business immediately, however workers updated the situation on 15th September evening. Workers said that they have to use other medicines or powder to alleviate the rushes they got from the polluted water. Despite all the reports made by workers about the issue with water, which is a basic need, the business hasn’t addressed it and workers continue to experience difficulties accessing clean water. 

Recommended next steps: 
The business to closely work with the maintenance team and find out the root cause of the issue and take action immediately. 
Workers should be given a time frame for the issue to be solved and the other options if any available. 


 Workers reported not having dispensers on the provided water container and workers having difficulties using drinking water. The business responded that they have provided the pump which the workers can use to transfer the water to their small bottles, however, workers updated not having seen those pumps. 
To have easy access to the water, the business shall provide the water containers with the appropriate dispenser so that the workers can access them as needed without having to lift the heavy container. 

(4) The issue with not having an ATM: Workers who have been placed for quarantine in the SEALIGHT hotel have reported not having access to an ATM. There are 4 mothers with around one-year-old babies who need basic needs. They said that they have to give their ATM card to the focal when they want to buy any goods or baby sanitary stuff. 

Recommended next steps: 
Workers having to give their ATM card is not safe and secure, therefore, the business should find a way to solve this problem. 
The business to find a way where workers can do the online transaction when they order the product via focal or the business to arrange cash and exchange with the online payment from the workers. 

(5) The issue with lack of bed sheets: Eight workers who are in the SEALIGHT hotel for quarantine reported not having bedsheets to sleep. It is reported that they are provided with only a mat without a mattress. Workers said that they have reported to  P'Kyi Ya from HR about this a few days ago, however, no action has been taken. Workers added that it gets cold in the morning and they are not able to have a good rest at night. 

Recommended next steps:
The business should immediately investigate why workers haven’t received proper items for their beds and work closely with the hotel to make sure that all workers in the hotel quarantine receive proper mattresses, blankets, and bedsheets.

preparing accommodation for workers in the factory, the workers who wish to continue working shall stay in the compound. They could not commute between their dormitory and factory. remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara raised this issue with the business several times including escalation calls. The business argued and said that they have been following the government's instruction to control the spread, however added that the main causes of these issues are because of miscommunication, therefore, the business formed a special team and assigned one focal for each Bubble & Seal housings in order for the workers to seek and access their basics needs and report any issues that they face in their bubble and seal dorms. However, workers additionally reported several repeated issues for several weeks even though the business has the focal for each housings. After several weeks and several meetings with the business and Issara, the business was eventually able to improve and address all of the issues that have happened in the bubble housing and workers confirmed not having additional issues.

After the business took actions to solve the issues: 
- for workers pressured to return to work earlier than the 14-day quarantine period have not reported any further issues after the factory was shut for the period of Sep 3-15, 2021.
- the workers confirmed that they no longer have any issues with meals.  They are receiving all meals, and the quality and quantity of the meals have improved as well.
- the workers confirmed that now there is adequate drinking water for all in the dorms and water pumps have been provided so they can dispense the water into their drinking bottles easily.
- the workers confirmed that the polluted tap water has now been solved and they have a clean tap water supply
- the female workers in the hotel quarantine have been able to buy necessary items for their babies with the help of HR making the cash withdrawals on their behalf and purchasing the requested items
- those in the hotel quarantine that had not received adequate bedding have now reported receiving bedsheets and so are satisfied with the sleeping conditions
remediation_notes:
Workers reported that Covid-19 was spreading among the workers in the factory but they were still being asked to continue working.  Workers that were in quarantine reported that the business expected them to report back to work after only 5-8 days of quarantine, rather than the 14 days recommended by Thai health officials. The business had told them they might not receive their wages, not be provided with basic necessities such as water and food during quarantine, and might even lose their jobs if they did not report back to work as the business instructed.  One group that tested positive and were in quarantine did not receive meals or water. 

Workers have reported not receiving adequate drinking water in their dormitories during the bubble & seal period, with a lack of proper water dispenser and workers have to lift big water containers to pour water into water bottles with small openings.  Also, the tap water in their dorms was polluted, which the workers couldn't use for their cooking or showers.
  
In addition, some female workers in a hotel quarantine could not use their ATM cards to withdraw money to buy necessary items for their babies.  Some other workers in hotel quarantine did not receive bedsheets in their rooms.
remediation_action:
Issara raised this issue with the business and also escalated the issue to TU's Director of Sustainability. 

The business responded that in terms of when a worker was allowed to return to work, they were following the recommendations of the local health officials.  Regarding the provision of meals, the business said there was miscommunication with the workers, and committed to making sure that all workers received proper meals. 

The business also took action to provide adequate drinking water at designated stations, and communicated to workers how the drinking water would be provided so that all workers would be able to access it.  The business also fixed the issue with the contaminated tap water.

Finally, the business coordinated with the hotel staff so that the workers in quarantine could request TU HR staff to withdraw cash and get supplies on their behalf.  The business also notified the hotel about the amenities that the workers said was lacking in their rooms and the hotel staff provided the missing items.
remediation_validation:
Workers confirmed that they didn't receive meals on the day they reported the issue and also their electricity was cut off as punishment for not reporting to work as instructed by the business.  After Issara reported the worker issues regarding drinking water and polluted tap water to HR, the workers initially confirmed the next day that they had not received any remedies yet.  

After the business took actions to solve the issues: 
For workers pressured to return to work earlier than the 14-day quarantine period have not reported any further issues after the factory was shut for the period of Sep 3-15, 2021.  The workers also confirmed that they no longer have any issues with meals.  They are receiving all meals, and the quality and quantity of the meals have improved as well.

The workers confirmed that now there is adequate drinking water for all in the dorms and water pumps have been provided so they can dispense the water into their drinking bottles easily.  The workers confirmed that the polluted tap water has now been solved and they have a clean tap water supply

The female workers in the hotel quarantine have been able to buy necessary items for their babies with the help of HR making the cash withdrawals on their behalf and purchasing the requested items.  Those in the hotel quarantine that had not received adequate bedding have now reported receiving bedsheets and so are satisfied with the sleeping conditions
remediation_results:
After Issara had several meetings with HR and also escalated these issues to TU's Sustainability Director and corporate HR, the business took action to resolve them.

For the quarantine period, TU noted that they were following protocols given by the government health department.

TU responded that the issue with the provision food was due to problems of mis-communication with workers and an inadequate food distribution plan but that they had taken immediate actions after getting the workers report from Issara. 

The business also set up water stations so that all workers would be able to access it, and fixed tap water problem. 

The business also coordinated with the quarantine hotel staff so that the female workers in quarantine could access what they needed from outside, and those missing bedsheets got them supplied. 

After the business took actions to solve the workers' issues, most have been resolved with worker validation

systems_change_issara_recommendation:

call_details.description:
The fishermen worked on the boat number TM1338E location at Hartlek,Klorng Yai,Trat Report a problem, on  the boat owner didn’t approved the cancellation letter (Bai Jang Ork) for him and warning him not to work with other employer. 
He been working with that boat 2year. The reason that he want to change the employer because the work condition and the wage that he received from this boat was not accurate. 
-process payment: Normally, every trip there should be 11 crews. They pay for 6-6500/1person/ for 2 trips (24days). All the fisherment having bank account but the boat owner withhold everything. So the process of payment is by cash. No payslip. 
- Workering condition: it’s depend on there are a lot of fishes. The working period should 8pm-1am and sometime until morning. 
- Document: All document were keep by boat owner. The fisherment allow to hold only 1/ inspector come 2/ when they need to go hospital.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue. Workers confirmed they understand that the production line interpreter is acting in an informal capacity and so when they need interpretation support and this informal interpreter can't provide it, they should go to the HR interpreter.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The line interpreter U Maung Pu is also not helpful in the production line if the workers requested him to support for some interpretation. He only interpreter what the supervisor would like to say to the workers and he asked the workers to talk to the supervisor by themselves if the workers would like to communicate with the line supervisor. He even mocked to the workers that even you report those case to the office, it will be in vain.

TPs:
- What is the role of the interpreter on the line?  Is this his full-time role or is he working on the line but also helping the others with interpretation?  What is expected of this interpreter and does he receive additional salary or other benefits for this interpretation role?

Recommendations:
- Interpreters should have the skills to be able to accurately interpret between the employer and employees, and to be objective and neutral in this role. He should be responsive to requests by the workers to interpret what they wish to communicate to their supervisors and any other staff. He should not neglect his duties nor verbally abuse or harass workers using his position of relative authority as compared to other workers who have to rely on him for interpretation support
- Ensure the interpreter understands his role and train the interpreter to be able to do his job effectively
- Assess and monitor the performance of all interpreters on a regular basis
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 24 Oct 2023

K. Somchoke, HR manager, explained that U Muang Pu is the production line interpreter, not an HR official interpreter. ITC has promoted this worker to help communicate with the Burmese worker on the PF3 production line. K. Rachade, HR, added that they are aware of this case because when Issara reported the issues in the PF3 line, they interviewed the workers and received feedback from the workers regarding this case. So they are investigating and trying to solve this case. They will respond with a corrective action plan within 7 working days.

DATE: 14 Nov 2023

On the follow-up remediation call according to K. Rachada, HR, the interpreter on the production line is a volunteer who works on the translation. There is no incentive or additional compensation for the interpreter. HR also provided interpreter training. They will, however, communicate all translations that the workers require, and the workers can contact the HR interpreter directly. They plan to communicate this clearly to all workers by the end of November 2023.

They shared the corrective action via email.
Investigation Result:
From the investigation of the facts Mr. Mongpu who is a volunteer interpreter in the production line provided information that in the case of language translation, he helps the supervisor communicate with workers. Sometimes too many workers struggle to speak, resulting in not being able to communicate every sentence. As a result, the supervisor was unable to listen to all workers at the same time. This makes the workers think that the interpreter is not impartial and refuses to help workers and the interpreter insists that there was no verbal abuse to workers or that the supervisor asked him to translate the scolding of the workers. The interpreter stated that he was not on anyone's side but he just helped to translate from the supervisor to communicate with co-workers. He has no problems or bias with any co-workers in particular.

Corrective Action:
HR will arrange for a team to go to the area to help communicate the rules and regulations. Guidelines for workers in the area to know together for mutual understanding and understand every nationality. Reduce the pressure on interpreters in the area as follows: 
1. Communication about requesting to take a restroom break, the workers must notify the supervisor so that it does not disappear from the line without informing anyone. The supervisor will be able to adjust the work schedule when many workers go out to the bathroom and many do not go out. Please be informed that the workers will be switched and the workers will understand that some Muslim workers need to pray as religious. Due to the Thai people in the area, most are Muslims and will request to pray at a time of approximately 15-20 minutes. The supervisor will acknowledge the time. It is not a matter of discrimination. 
2. Arrangement of rest time, and work to know the status of both working at the department and helping in other departments. 
3. Notification of defects in the case of workers working incorrectly. Do not blame them collectively. Talk individually. If there is a written warning, you may ask for an interpreter from HR to help communicate. 
4. Scanning the card when the worker is about to leave work. and after this. HR will inform workers of the role of the interpreter in the production line who helps with basic communication and general work, taking them to the nurse's room in case workers are sick with their supervisors. But if it is training in new procedures or regulations or a serious emergency accident including if there are complaints or if the worker doesn't understand the supervisor and feels frustrated, please contact an HR interpreter.
remediation_notes: The interpreter in the production line only conveys messages from the line supervisor but doesn't help workers to interpret what they want to say to the supervisors and even mocks them saying their requests will not be heeded.
remediation_action: HR explained that this production line interpreter was informally helping with interpretation and was not the HR official interpreter. The business has announced to the workers that this production line interpreter is acting in an informal capacity and so workers should come directly to HR to get interpretation support from the HR interpreter as and when needed.
remediation_validation: Workers updated that HR clearly announced that the workers can come to office and communicate directly with the interpreter in HR office as the interpreter in the production line not officially assigned as a focal interpreter and is not obligated to interpret everything as per the workers' requests. The workers are now clear on where to go for interpretation support.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue. Workers confirmed they understand that the production line interpreter is acting in an informal capacity and so when they need interpretation support and this informal interpreter can't provide it, they should go to the HR interpreter.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
- Have a training program for interpreters on the production line so that they have clear expectations of their role and responsibilities
- Have a clear job description and appropriate salary and benefits to recognize the additional responsibilities the workers are fulfilling, both working on the line and providing interpretation support to his/her co-workers

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker in a production line for descaling and deboning fish reported that there are different incentive being paid to workers.  They work as a team of 8, with one descaling while the other 7 debone, and the de-scaler gets daily incentive of only 10 Baht while the de-boners get 60 Baht per day. The worker said they work together as a team and don't think they should receive different incentives. 

TPs:
- How are incentives calculated? Is there a reason why workers working as a team receive different daily incentives?

Recommendations:
- The incentive system should be fair and incentive pay should be reviewed and revised accordingly. As per this case, it is questionable as to why one team member gets 10 Baht and the others get 60 Baht as daily incentive pay.
- The incentive and bonus system should be clear to all workers and perceived to be fair; communicate, verbally and in writing, what incentives and bonuses are paid for what reasons so that workers fully understand what they can expect to receive.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 25 SEP 2023

K Wichai, HR manager, responded that the incentive scheme is based on the ability of workers to work in different ways. They will, however, investigate this matter first and get back to us within 7 working days.

DATE: 1 Nov 2023

K. Wichai, HR Manager, explained that each employee has his or her own job description as well as an agreement for hiring. As was mentioned in the previous call, the incentive scheme is based on workers' ability and skill to work in different capacities. However, the worker may change and shift to another job description depending on the job vacancy and how the worker performs to get the job, as well as the incentive in that position. He confirmed that HR is working on this issue's communication with workers and will share the corrective action with us next week.


DATE: 13 Nov 2023

Investigation Detail:
Before beginning work, the worker did not understand. Because HR did not communicate with workers to ensure that they understood first.

Corrective Action:
On 11 Nov 2023, HR and the Production Manager held a communication session with the workers about the incentives and explained clearly that the incentive varies depending on the order specification and fish material, so the incentive also varies.
remediation_notes: Issara received a report that workers in the production line for descaling and deboning fish were getting different incentives even though they work as a team.
remediation_action: The HR manager, responded that the incentive scheme is based on the ability of workers to work in different ways. HR found that workers didn't understand the incentive scheme and HR did not communicate this clearly with workers. On 11 Nov 2023, HR and the Production Manager held a communication session with the workers to explain how the incentives are calculated and how the incentive pay might vary per worker, depending on the order specification and fish material.
remediation_validation:
Workers updated Issara that there has been no action or any communication about the different incentives provided to workers in the same team.

In the latest update, the workers confirmed that they received the communication about incentives and how different job roles get different incentives.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue. Workers have confirmed that they now understand that different job roles get different incentives
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Institute regular formal reviews of the incentive and bonus system, with direct input and suggestions from the workers and considered by management.

call_details.referral_notes: Have to discuss in SC meeting and prepare talking point to check with business and pass the case to O&E focal.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case as "fair" because the company has clarified with the workers the company's policy regarding quarantine days for Covid high-risk persons, that workers needing to quarantine as high-risk persons can take annual or business leave, or otherwise apply for Social Security compensation of 50% of wages for those days.  It is not providing allowances for workers to use sick leave or special Covid leave for such instances.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; Workers reported that the business would not provide paid sick leave or   COVID special leaves for high-risk quarantine workers.  It was not clear for the workers as well.  Workers sought clarification.


Talking Points; 

Workers reported not being paid for quarantine days as Covid high-risk persons, what is the business understanding on this issue? 
How many workers are in this situation and what has been the process for them so far? How many days of quarantine are required for close contact and positive cases? Who pays for those quarantine days? 
Has the business checked the government regulations on what Covid-related care services are to be covered by the business and/or SSO and whether and how quarantine days for Covid close contacts are to be paid?  


Recommendations. 
The business should confirm the latest government regulations related to quarantine periods for Covid close contacts and how to pay for missed working days due to quarantine is to be handled
We have received the update that the government regulations are as follows:  If a worker is found to be positive at the factory, she/he is supposed to be sent to the hospital for the PCR test and if confirmed as positive, receive the medical certificate and recommended to quarantine. The worker should get paid sick leave during those days. 
If a worker is in close contact, s/he should visit the hospital and report why she/he is at high risk and get the recommendations from the hospital. The regular recommendation for vaccinated people is to take 10 days of quarantine and do another test on the 10th day. 
If the result is negative, then the worker can start working. In terms of the wages for the high-risk workers who have a medical certificate for their quarantine days, the employer can submit the worker's information to the SSF for 50% of the wages. 
If the worker is not allowed to go to the hospital but the employer orders the worker to take quarantine, it is the responsibility of the employer to pay the worker wages. 
The business should communicate with the workers about how to quarantine days for close contacts and positive workers will be paid. 

Time Frame; 1 week.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara shared this issue with the business, the business will check with the HR team and get back to Issara.

K. Alisa, Director of Quality System responded and clarified the policy as follows.
1. High-risk colleagues who work together do not need to be quarantined.
2. But if the workers live in the same house, in the past, the workers had to quarantine for 7 days and show APK results before came to work.
3. Now adjusted to a 5-day quarantine, showing APK results before coming to work, adjusting according to the government

In conclusion, if the workers work together but wear a mask all the time, the workers don't have to quarantine.

Those who need to quarantine, can take any leave. For example, annual leave and business leave to get the full wage or Social Security 50% of wage which a reimbursement from SSF but it will be slow because SSF required the certificate of quarantine from Provincial Public Heath.

Therefore, this is an optional and provides the form for workers to select.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that they had heard that the business would not provide paid sick leave or COVID special leave for workers needing to quarantine as high risk or close contact persons.  They wanted clarification on the company policy on this.
remediation_action: Issara shared this issue with the business, and the Director of Quality Systems responded that the company policy allowed for high-risk persons to continue working if the whole group working together were all high-risk.  For high-risk persons that needed to quarantine for five days, they would not get sick leave or Covid special leave.  They could either choose to use annual leave or business leave to get full pay during those days, or claim Social Security compensation for those days, which would be paid at 50% wages.
remediation_validation: The worker confirmed that the business has posted the announcement in Burmese about how to apply for social security compensation.  For now, he doesn't know anyone who has the quarantine payment issue.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case because the business has made the announcement and clarified with workers what kind of leave they can use for quarantine days for Covid high-risk persons, and the process for getting Social Security compensation as needed.

Need to get back to the business and get further clarification

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker called to say that he was dismissed for one incident where he was due to work the night shift but left after a few hours (he went for a dinner break then fell asleep for several hours and decided to go home). The next day, the HR manager asked him to come for an 8am meeting but he missed the meeting as he only went there at 10am. He went to the office again at 5pm and the HR interpreter asked whether he had gotten drunk and asked why he had missed work so he explained what happened. He was dismissed for the reason that he had been absent from work very often. The worker thinks this is unfair because in the past, whenever he needed to be absent from work, he had sought permission from the line supervisor but it was the supervisor that had not approved his request. 

TPs:
- What is the reason for this worker's dismissal?
- Has he received a warning about being absent in the past?
- What is the company's disciplinary policy for this kind of offence (being absent from work)? Is it verbal warning, written warning, suspension, and then dismissal?

Recommendations:
- Workers should be disciplined according to the company's disciplinary policy; he should be issued a verbal warning, written warning, suspended, and then dismissed, not dismissed immediately without having previously received such previous warnings
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 15 Feb 2024

K. Yaowapa (Gae) HR, explained that the worker's behavior is not good. He used to pee in the locker area. He slept 00.30-3.00 am. on the night of 2 Feb until the morning of 3 Feb. On the same day, he slept on the soccer field. He also took a lunch break longer and came to work not on time. When HR inquired he said he worked normally not take a nap or break longer. But the CCTV showed him sleeping. He said that he just took a nap not a serious issue. HR investigated and interviewed the coworkers and found out that this worker also got drunk often. HR appointed him to meet at 8 am and he missed the appointment. First, HR gave a verbal warning and then he still did not improve so tried to give me a written warning but he didn't sign and admit. He just only said to HR 'You wanna fire me' He defied HR and He didn't want to improve his behavior.

Reasons for dismissal
1. He lies and not admitted and he chooses to not listen and understand
2. This impact on the production capacity and the business
3. He got drunk and worked often.
4. He refuses to admit and sign the warning letter according to the disciplinary 
5. He had a chance to come to explain but he missed the appointment
6. He defied HR and refused to improve his behavior
Note: HR communicates through the interpreter and he also can understand the Thai language.

Timeline:
On 5 Feb, he got a verbal warning about the he slept during working time.
On 6 Feb, he missed the appointment at 8 am. He was communicated by HR about his behavior. So HR tried to give him a written warning but he refused to sign and ignored HR communication.
On 7-9 Feb, he didn't come to work for 3 days consecutive without notice to the supervisor or HR. HR also communicated to the worker if he wanted to work or leave please notify HR but he didn't.

Next, K Gae needs to check the clock-in clock-out system to ensure his last work day. HR will issue the cancellation letter to him. However, if he has any queries or clarification, he can come to meet HR.

remediation_action: Issara raised this issue with the business, and HR responded that this worker had a history of disciplinary issues and he lied about his missing work and sleeping when there is video evidence about this. He was given a verbal warning, then a written warning which he refused to sign, and most recently missed the meeting with HR to discuss his behavior. Therefore, the business has dismissed him.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case because the business has paid the amount agreed with the workers for the separation.
remediation_issara_recommendation: Workers were asked to resign without severance pay. The main issue is that workers are terminated without having a documented extension and no severance pay.
remediation_business_steps_taken: For this case, SFP consulted with a lawyer. The lawyer proceed according to the law with the court and agreed to consider and decided to pay as the worker requested. On May 12 and they will agree at the course to pay the severance pay to the workers. There are 20,000 Baht for each worker.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that various groups of workers were asked to resign from their jobs without receiving any severance pay.
remediation_action: After pressure from the Strategic Partners, Issara was able to meet with SFP HR at the Bangkok Headquarters.  HR explained that migrant workers were hired as MOU workers or walk-in workers with different contract end dates. At the end of a migrant worker's contract, the business considered whether the contract can be extended as per Thai government regulations and also whether the worker's performance was satisfactory. If the contract could not be extended because of the government regulations or because of poor performance, the business considered this as separation at the end of a contract and not as a dismissal and was not obligated to provide severance pay.  Subsequently, the labor case was brought by the workers, and the out-of-court settlement was for the business to pay severance to the workers, in the amount of 20,000 Baht for each of the 4 workers.
remediation_validation: The workers confirmed that they received the 20,000 Baht each from the business, in addition to an earlier amount of 10,000 Baht that the business paid to each worker.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case because the business has paid the amount agreed with the workers for the separation.

For the remediation, Issara will calculate based on the survey result and recommend together.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
BHR provided examples from other Thai suppliers that fully cover the time and cost of 90-day reports.
According to K. Seubpon, HR, BFI does not pay any fees without a formal receipt. They also provide transportation for workers who go to immigration on their own.


1) BFI gives the employee 7 business days instead of the usual 3 business days. If they need to do their own business, they have the same 7 business leave days as Thai employees. BFI provides transportation for workers who will complete the 90-day report on their own. This, however, will have an impact on the attendance allowance. Workers can also take annual leave instead of business leave to avoid affecting their attendance allowance.

2) BFI communicated with the workers about the situation. They do, however, have the right to choose from their will.
remediation_notes: A Lao worker reported that the business still collects 100 baht for the 90-day report process. The worker paid 100 baht to HR and interpreter. She paid for the 90-day reporting cost twice already, the first time on Aug 18, 2022 and the second time on Oct 28, 2022. She is part of the 40 MoU workers that arrived in June 2022. There are no receipts for the 100 baht paid each time.
remediation_action: Issara raised this with the business and BFI noted that it was company policy that for 90-day reports, workers can do the report themselves by taking leave (business leave or annual leave). However, the workers have the option to choose an agency to process it for them instead, for which there is a fee and the workers are willing to pay for it.  Issara escalated this issue with BFI senior management and recommended that there should be no cost to the worker, since the 90-day report is necessary for the worker to legally stay and work in Thailand.  Allowing workers to use annual leave or business leave has a cost because either they lose 4 annual leave days over the course of a year if they use annual leave or they will lose their attendance bonus if they use business leave (BFI noted that if a worker takes business leave, this will count against their attendance and they will not get the monthly attendance bonus).  However, the business has not changed its position on this.
remediation_validation: Issara followed up with the workers and they confirmed that they know about the current arrangement. They still prefer to pay the 100 Baht for the 90 day report because they do not want to lose the attendance bonus.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case.  Workers understand that they can use business leave and do the 90-day report themselves rather than paying 100 Baht for it to be done for them; however, they still prefer paying the 100 Baht rather than losing the attendance bonus if they use business leave to do the 90-day report. The business is not willing to change its policy and allow workers to do the 90-day report without having to pay for it or losing out on the attendance bonus.

closed_notes: The business was recommended to have open discussion with the workers on what was allowed for workers to do at the workplace to express themselves regarding the political situation in Myanmar. There was no response from the business regarding the recommendations but the business explained to Issara that the company didn't allow workers to wear any object as a political statement at the workplace to avoid any kind of issues with other workers and to keep a neutral environment at the workplace. Issara explain this policy to workers and we didn't receive any further update from workers on this matter, therefore, this case is being closed.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Contest; The issue with the workers not being allowed to wear NLD clothes or conduct any political activities. 

Since this is a controversial issue; Issara has sent an email to the business as follows. 

Dear Business Partner:
Since the military coup took place last month in Myanmar, the Burmese people are facing an uncertain future but have risen up in large numbers to peacefully protest against the takeover.  In addition to the Covid-19 situation, this political crisis back home is causing even more stress and anxiety for the many Burmese migrant workers here in Thailand.  For businesses that are employing Burmese migrant workers, we understand it is a challenging time to balance workers' right to freedom of expression while allowing such expression to be made in appropriate and safe ways that do not disrupt the work of the business.  

We would like to recommend that the business maintain healthy and open discussions with the workers and come to an agreement with them on what would be allowed as appropriate expressions of their views but at the same time does not impact the workplace.  The business could be supportive in allowing them to express their views, during breaks and outside of work hours, and in a form that is discussed and agreed to between the business and workers.  Any sharing online of such events by workers should not include identification of their workplace, for the safety of the business and the workers alike. Also, we would recommend that the business makes a clear announcement to all workers about what is allowed and what is not, the "do's and don'ts" for the workers, explaining to the workers what their rights are, and what kind of activities are risks for the workers and/or business and therefore is not allowed.

We at Issara Institute hope the political crisis will be resolved peacefully very soon, for the benefit of the people of Myanmar.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that the business was not allowing them to wear any clothing that signified political expressions or conduct any peaceful assemblies demonstrating against the military coup in Myanmar.
remediation_action: The business explained that the company doesn't allow workers to wear any clothing as a political statement at the workplace to avoid any kind of issues with other workers and to keep a neutral environment at the workplace.
remediation_validation: Issara explained the business' position to workers and we didn't receive any further updates from workers on this matter.
remediation_results: Issara didn't receive any further updates from workers on this matter; therefore, this case is being closed.

Context: The issue from workers who are back to work after the explosion nearby factory reported having to breathe unhygienic air pollution, not having proper space for their lunch, and not having purified drinking water in their workplace.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: A group of 11 workers who have submitted resignation a week ago and were preparing to depart are not being allowed to go by the business. The workers reported that their belongings were taken by the business when they were about to leave in a van and that they now do not have a place to stay since they have already given back their rooms. Workers reported the reason for leaving job is as follows:
(1) discrimination against nationalities at the workplace,
(2) the business not keeping the promise of paying double for the working hours during COVID-19 restriction as promised,
(3) translator not being helpful and being biased by just listening to the business and not the workers. 

Recommendations: 
-As it is a worker's right to resign and leave the company, the business shall immediately investigate why this group of workers were not allowed to leave. And then come to an agreement with workers for their departure from the company without restrictions.
-Since the business made the taxi driver leave without the workers, it will be challenging for workers to find a new driver, therefore, the business is suggested to help workers find a new taxi/van for workers safe return. -Since the vaccination is a workers personal health matter, the business should provide vaccination cards or any support documents as proof that workers have received vaccination. If the business does not have such documents, the business should coordinate with the health organization that provided the vaccine to make sure all workers receive the vaccination card. 
-The business should immediately check with all workers and provide their missing daily wages if any. 


Talking Points: 
-What is the reason why this group of workers were stopped by HR? 
-Is business aware of this issue? 
-Workers have reported several workers leaving the job because of several repeated issues in the workplace, what is the business understanding of this? Does the business seek workers' feedback and have done anything to improve the working condition rather than stopping workers from leaving? 
- What was communicated to workers as reasons for not being allowed to leave the company?
-What was the reason for the business calling the police and threatening the workers? 

Added TPs; 
Because workers have resigned and are asking to depart, this situation should be addressed in less than the 3-4 day timeline suggested by SCC.
No resigned worker can be held against their will, or coerced into returning to work
Resigned workers can be provided vaccine certificates and COVID tests to ensure there are no positive cases before departure
Workers can be clearly offered a return to work, with no coercion, and with clear communication on next steps
Because this situation has escalated, Issara can jointly speak with HR and the group of workers if desired, to support communication.
Issara also recommends we provide training to HR reps at SCC, on COVID and other protocols for workforce management.

remediation_action:
Issara reached out to the business immediately.  The business explained that HR had communicated to the workers about the government's travel restrictions to prevent the spread of Covid-19, and that they are not allowed to travel outside Songkhla province because it is currently a Covid-19 red zone.  They said police had come to enforce the travel restrictions and the van driver left without taking the workers after talking to the police.  Regarding vaccination certificates that would be important for when the workers travel back to Myanmar, the business said the document issuance was delayed by the hospital and would be provided to the workers when issued.  For now, the business said the workers are still living in the private dorm and the workers can ask the landlord to stay in the same place. 

The business will get back to Issara with corrective actions within 3-5 days.

The business further updated Issara saying pictures of HR staff with negative comments regarding this incident had been posted on social media and they wanted the workers to remove the posts.

Issara escalated this issue with TU's Sustainability Director, and recommended that no worker that had already resigned should be held against their will or coerced into returning to work. The workers did not want to stay there anymore; they felt pressured and forced to go back to work.  They were even willing to pay any government fines if there were any for crossing province lines.  Since they have resigned, they don't understand why the business is not letting them leave.  They just want to be able to travel back to Myanmar. 

Regarding the social media posts, the workers said they did not take any photos or videos during the incident nor did they post anything on social media or ask their friends to do so.

The workers have confirmed that they have officially resigned from their jobs and are free to leave.

Regarding the wages, workers noted not wanting to wait for the business to conduct an investigation, as they wanted to leave as soon as possible without waiting for any compensation.

remediation_results: Issara had several meetings with the business regarding this issue, however, there has been no resolution and no further actions are being taken. Therefore, this case is being closed with a poor rating.

So workers who do not join that meeting and came late, will not know that.  According to my one informant she know that because she joining that meeting. 

Then O&E asked to talk with that worker who are assigned in case of emergency. He said there are other three workers like him who are assigned by the business in terms of communication with the workers if they Report issue.  Then they have to report to a Thai lady.  They just called her Mom.  He didnt know her name. At first, what ever they report to that lady took an account.  But later, whatever what the workers raised, that lady didn't take any account anymore.

Tomorrow, he will send me the photo of that lady, and the photo of lunch boxes providing to. Thai and Burmese workers.  He said Thai workers received big box with good meal inside such as fry chicken, fiy fish and the Burmese workers received only small box with mixed fish and vegetable curry like that.  As Burmese workers eat a lot of Rice, they are not full with what the business provided to them.  He said how we are going to survive for 21 days like this. call_details.description:
Follow up call with the client about 1. Polluted water issue, Drinking water Issue and 3. No access to ATM Issue.

1. Pollution Water Issue: Not fixed yet. The worker in Zone-C informed me that no technician came. So they just used that water and applied powder ect. The workers went to work all day and just came back. They thought everything was fixed, but not yet. 

2. Drinking water: This issue too. The informant said he didn't see any new water buckets yesterday after we talked with HR. As there are many zones (A,B,C,D,E), sometimes, they don't know if some workers from different zones have taken the bottle as the business just left the water buckets in the entrance of the dorn. Would be great if the business can allocate like 4 or 5 buckets per zone, so that they also can know who has taken and carried it to their room etc. For the water pump, I am checking with my informant in Zone-C and he said, he never saw that.

3. For the ATM issue in hotel quarantine: The informant said, the direct informant hasn't sent him the photo yet, so he cannot send it to me now. I asked the direct informant number and I just finished talking with the informant. He said it's near Siranakhon Hospital (5 min drive from the factory). It's kind of like an apartment. There are around 40 Burmese workers there and there are 4 babies who are under one year olds. While they are in hospital quarantine, the hospital quarantine provides everything, including mile power, baby meal or diapers. But now, when they were being moved to those apartments, they asked the business (P'Kyi Ya, male Burmese representative sitting in HR office), and told him that we will not take any responsibility for our baby. He just asked the workers to give money or give an ATM card to the focal so that he will buy it for the baby. But, I think they still have the responsibility to take care of the worker's baby too since their parents have to follow the business practice. 

4. Male workers have to take care of the babies: And the business managed only the father to take care of those babies and not the mother. The mothers are allocated back to MOU dorm and have to go back to work. The workers do not know why the business did like that. Actually, babies should be with the mother. They talked with P'Kyi Ya and he said the mommy work site required manpower so that they cannot let them taking care of the babies.
