call_details.description:
Follow up call with the client for case update:

1. · Workers not receiving meals on Aug 31 and Sep 1?

Yes, this issue was fixed. The business well prepared the lunch of the workers. For breakfast and dinner, the Two Thai women, who are assigned to distribute the food in the MOU dorm,  are taking care of this. For lunch, it was sent by the hotel. The informant said, the management came and said sorry for the workers who missed the meals on Aug 31 as there are some information gaps between HR and what’s happening on the ground. He (One of the management) regrets and is sorry about that. They will take care of this kind of issue not happening again. 

2. The issue with discrimination in terms of food distribution between Thai workers and Burmese workers: 
This issue has also been resolved. The meal box is now bigger than in the previous. It's enough for the workers. And their current inside also include more ingredients, such as paste, and vegetable (To-Sa-Yar) and fry. So the workers are fine and happy with that now.

3. Limited access to buy goods and basic necessities: TUS said there is a system for workers to order purchases and they are delivered once a week and more zone leaders will be female so female workers can make requests to female zone leaders.  Have the workers confirmed they understand the system, that they can buy what they need, and female workers can make orders through female zone leaders?

Now, the business allows one old Thai woman who used to sell the stuff near the factory. That lady was allowed to come and bring the stuff, such as noodles, cooking ingredients, like fish paste, soy milk, soft drink, etc. She comes to the dorn on Saturday and Sunday. She left her stuff to the dorn and there are four workers who help her sell her products after they come back to work. Workers came and bought the stuff from these four workers. (Informant is one of the four sellers). If they want a special order, they leave these four workers noted down . When the Thai lady comes, the four workers give those special orders to that Thai lady and the Thai lady bought for them.

4· Insufficient drinking water and lack of water dispenser: 
Now, the business came and refilled the water gallon and the workers said it's properly enough. They come with water pumps and they have no problem too. Plus, the business also provides additional ice blocks as well. So they are ok with that.

5· Polluted tap water:  this was fixed and workers have confirmed that the tap water is no longer an issue. 

Yes, there is no issue with that too. Maintenance workers come and  fix that after our escalated call with K'Prad. Now, it's clean.

call_details.description:
Checking with the client how they are being communicated to relocate back to the yellow building based on BHR update on business response 1461. 
(The TUS HR said TUS paid for the Sealight room rental cost in advance for the workers and TUS will arrange free transportation for them to go back and work until the end of B&S. This group of workers said if the business would like them to go back and work the business must allow them to stay close to the factory, if not they won't go back to work because the Sealight hotel and TUS are very far and the worker said they don't want to take long transportation. This part is correct. But the business didn't communicate with them that they had to stay in a yellow building and paid the room cost after one month. They just thought they would be sent back to their own room. 
To solve the problem, workers requested the TUS discussed with the Songkhla Public health care to include the Yellow building in the TUS B&S policy. The Songkhla Public health care agreed to it and allowed 9 rooms under TUS B&S. The TUS already pays for the room rental cost for the workers. The HR said workers will have to pay for the room rental cost next month because the business already arranged for the worker at Sealight Hotel and paid the rental cost in advance already but the worker doesn't want to stay there.  
 
The HR said they have communicated with the worker many times but this group of workers are still saying that they would like to go back to their room. They don't understand B&S policy and are not interested in it. O&E check with the worker how the business communicates to you for relocation back to the yellow housing? 
The client responded that the translator called the focal persons who are assigned in the SEALIGHT Hotel to buy the kid stuff and withdraw cash. The translator called those persons to let the workers know who finished quarantine and had to go back to work. As the workers refused because of the time limitation and there is a problem with the limited bathroom in the hotel, they told those assigned persons to request the business to relocate them back to their room.   
The HR said TUS B&S policy, TUS arranged 4 people in each room during B&S, the worker can choose who they would like to stay with and send the list name of the room member to HR. All local or Burmese workers have to follow the same. 
This 20 workers group is also the same, the workers choose their room members by them self and send the name list to the HR team. The HR said the HR team did not select the people and send them to the same room.)The next day, a van arrived at the hotel and they were asked to board. At that time there was one Thai lady who came and picked them up. When the workers were about to board, she asked please raise your hands if you stay in the Yellow building in front of the building, there were 8 workers there and she asked them to please choose your friends who you think can stay with you in your rooms for only 14 days. As the workers thought only for 14 days, they chose their friends. But, the translator and that Thai lady also involved suggesting or advising the workers too. For example, if there are two couples who stay in that building, they ask them to temporarily stay like only the wifes stay with another two female workers and the two husbands stay with another two male workers. 

On that day, there were also still about 50 workers being sent to other housing near Sunday Market. But, those workers are now relocated back to their own room near near the Yellow Building. That building is called "Rakkhine Housing" and the room are more spacious. The informant who has to stay with her friends in the Yellow housing is also staying there.
Further Update:27 Sep: Yesterday, around 2 PM, the Burmese Translator (Arr Don) and P' Dium (HR) came into Yellow Housing and asked some workers to do a night shift. Since the workers have to share the room with some workers who have babies and some are leaving the job, working the night shift will make them annoyed. So they asked them to relocate them back to their own room. Then they agreed and they asked the workers to sign a paper as an agreement if they are ok to work on night shift. But they have to follow  business policy and they cannot commute except to the building to work. The landlord will strictly manage this. The workers agreed and signed and they started working the night shift. And they told the workers that you cannot go back to your room by yourselves. We have to manage you by transferring you to your room.

28 Sep,  this morning, as no one came up, the workers called the translator and asked them when they could come. The translator and P'Dium came back at 8 AM again. They told the workers that you are not able to relocate now as you have agreed to stay here and we have paid for this room. If you leave now, you have to pay the room fee for this month. The workers said, yes, we will pay. But, they said they still need the approval from management.
The workers said why they did not keep the promise and they manipulated the workers like that. They asked why another 50 workers being sent to Sunday housing and now they can go back to their room "Rakkhine Housing" and not them, the translator didn't translate it back to P'Dium. They are also not happy with the behavior or performance of the translator too.  

O&E asked the following three questions to the workers:
1. Have you been told that you have to pay that room cost after one month? 
Ans: The workers said no.

2. Did you know that you can go back to the SEALIGHT hotel if you don't want to stay here? The workers said no. Even the workers who will finish quarantine in the SEALIGHT hotel will be sent back to their housing (Rakkhine Housing) soon.

3. How long were you being communicated to stay there?
Ans: The translator and P'Dium told them as long as B&S policy.
The workers also added, not only the room cost, but also sharing the room with other workers is not a good practice. Plus, they have to work the night shift, the babies crying, and a lot of distractions.
call_details.next_steps: Have to Update ILM team to check with business why other workers from other housing and the workers in the yellow housing are not being sent back to their room yet.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A group of 40 workers were told that they would need to return to Myanmar for the MOU U-turn process at the end of Dec 2023 but did not provide information about the RA that would facilitate the process and what costs would be covered. They were informed that they would need to wait in Myanmar for 2 months before returning.  
  
This group came with International Focus RA in Jan 2018. They are wondering whether they can work until Apr 2024 according to last year's Thai government cabinet resolution.  Around 10 workers are in conflict area in Myanmar and they don't want to go and wait at Myanmar side for a long time.

They are requesting that their stay in Myanmar is the shortest possible and whether the business can arrange accommodation in Yangon for those who live in conflict areas so they don't have to return to those places.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 15 Dec 2023

According to K. Sirilak, HR director, the MoU U-Turn process typically takes 2-3 months for workers to return and stay in Myanmar. TUS uses two Myanmar recruitment agencies, International Focus and Alpha World Link. This group must investigate how the process works and which recruitment agency should be responsible for carrying it out. They inquired if Issara had any additional information for this group to investigate. We informed them that this group first arrived in Thailand with an international focus in January 2018. So they will look into this group and get back to us within 7 business days.

26 Dec 2023:
TUS got back to us today re TUS issues with corrective actions. They investigated and it was found that there are a total of 40 MoU workers who came to work with TUS in January 2018 with an employment period of 6 years. These workers have a valid visa to stay in the country until 8 January 2024 and are not included in the 4-year MoU workers who are allowed to temporarily stay in the country until 30 April 2024 according to the 3 October 2023 Cabinet Resolution. 

The company has called this group of workers for a meeting twice in December to explain the details of the MoU U Turn. The first meeting was on 4 December 2023 and the second meeting on 22 December 2023 to inform additional details about the MoU U Turn trip. In both meetings, the company had clarified the travel details, steps for document extensions, agency used, and processing time. They also gave a chance to the workers to ask questions, for example, can they bring their children back with them, accommodation in the Myanmar side in case they don’t want to return home, pick-up and drop-off point at the border, etc. The HR officers answered all the questions that the workers have or are concerned about. The workers also signed and gave their consent for voluntary MoU U Turn. 

With regard to the time frame, even though the company has completed the passports for all the workers, it still takes time both in Thailand and in Myanmar side approximately 2 months until the workers can come back to work at the factory. The company has explained all the details to the workers during the meetings.

remediation_action:

These workers have a valid visa to stay in the country until 8 January 2024 and are not included in the 4-year MoU workers who are allowed to temporarily stay in the country until 30 April 2024 according to the Thai government's 3 October 2023 Cabinet Resolution.

The workers also signed and gave their consent to voluntarily return to Myanmar for the MoU U-turn process.

For this case, the workers have to pay 1,500 Kyats per day. So, it will cost them 45,000 Kyats per month not including food. As they have to stay for 60 days, the workers are worried about their monthly expenses, and would like to request that the accommodation cost be reduced.

call_details.description:
Client reported about the difficulties in her quarantine period. She was effective from Covid-19 for more than a week and was not provided any food or water. 

She live in Pai-Apartment. At that apartment, some rooms do not have any windows. There are about 40-Burmese positive workers there and they are not allowed to open their doors and windows. 

The translator reminding them in the group that, don't open doors and windows. But, as they are suffering Covid1-19 attack, they tried to open the door (which do not have windows) or windows, whenever, the neighboring rooms are going to work. But, whenever, the neighboring room workers are back to work, they shout them not to open the door and window. 

The informant guessed it may be the neighboring negative resulted workers or the landlord who must reported this to the translator or business HR. But, the informants said, it is not the right way. Having poor ventilation can increase the spread of the virus and at the time, they have to wait like a week to get the medical care from the hospital. 

They tried to close their door when the negative workers were back from work. But, after they arrive in their room, they can close their door if they are afraid of the positive workers. But, now, having them to shut their door and window along the out of work hour is not fair she said. They reported it to the translator and the translator also just told them to close their window. She would like to request if Issara can help.

The workers requested that if the business can manage this situation, it would be good. Currently, the workers just only depend on outside donors or their friends to bring or help them with water, food or everything. The business bought them only traditional herbs such as Lemon grass, garlic, pepper, and ginger, no medicine.

Workers reported that the business only provides 5 doses of medicine once they start their quarantine which is not enough for some workers who really have the sickness. Workers also added that as they can not travel out for their food, they request if the business can provide some food supplies to them during their quarantine stay.

In addition to that, the communication should focus on the medical assistant whenever workers need it. Workers should be encouraged to contact the focal person if there is anything that they need.

-Are any medical assistance available for those quarantine workers? 
-Have the business introduced the focal point for the workers to contact in case of an emergency?

description: Discrimination – by gender/nationality/ethnicity/other in the work area

call_details.description:
The line supervisor, P’Par, is biased and abusive. She is in Building-3, 2nd floor in Line F21.

1.       Discrimination on Workload and Assignment:

She discriminates in workload assignment and time management between Burmese workers and Thai workers. She assigned three machines/ points to one Burmese worker and if they cannot manage the workload on time, for example, if there are many sewing pieces accumulated in their points, she calls those workers in front of the lines and tells her to hurry. But in case of Thai workers have the sewing piece accumulate in their working lines, she didn’t say that workers anything and ask other Burmese workers to go and help them instead. The workers felt so unfair about this. Mostly most of the Burmese workers are assigned more than one point with difficult tasks and they are being blamed and Thai workers are not.

2.       Issue with Toilet break

When the Burmese workers went to the toilet, she told them to come back quickly and sometimes, she went and followed up to the toilet and called them back. But in terms of Thai workers, she didn’t say anything and she didn’t go and follow up to the toilet although they spent more time than they did.

3.       Issue with Workload

The supervisor asked the workers to amend the QC fails clothes in their lunch times and OT break. She accumulated those clothes and didn’t let the workers do it in the working hour. She asked the workers please eat your lunch quickly and come back to finish those. So, the workers have to eat lunch quickly and finish those. Sometimes she even asked the workers to do it in the times when the workers get a 30 min break before starting OT. She also asks the workers to do trimming the clothes like cutting the thread in that time if there is no QC fails clothes to do.

description: Discrimination – by gender/nationality/ethnicity/other in the work area
closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue.  The worker now understands why some workers are asked to work in different lines while others stay put.  The business has taken action to investigate and instruct supervisors to make this clarification with workers.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that his line supervisor (P Skee, who has since already moved to another different line) was discriminating against Burmese workers by moving them temporarily (for a couple days to a week at a time) to go work in different lines where they are not familiar with the tasks being performed in those lines but the supervisor doesn't ask the Thai workers to do this.  The Burmese workers want to be able to work consistently in the line where they are familiar with the tasks and have become better at those tasks over time.  They don't want to be move around while Thai workers get to stay in the same line.

TPs:
-What is the company's practice in terms of placement of workers in various production lines?  Is there a schedule for moving workers around to different lines intentionally?  If so, what are the reasons for this?
-The practice of moving workers to work temporarily in a different line before returning to his/her usual line seems to be assigned to workers unevenly, with Burmese workers feeling like it is only happening to them while it is not being required of the Thai workers.  What are the reasons for this?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Investigate this matter to establish why workers and only Burmese workers are being moved around to different lines temporarily.  Check records of which lines workers worked in and the dates when workers were moved to different lines.  Interview Burmese workers to get their perspective on why they think this is affecting their work performance and feel as though the company is discriminating against Burmese workers.  Ensure worker safeguards according to TU's non-retaliation policy
-Take disciplinary action against the supervisor according to the investigation results and the company's disciplinary policy
-Communicate with all workers about the company's practice regarding assignment of workers to certain production lines and why workers may be working in different lines and explain clearly how this is NOT a discriminatory practice.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Root Cause:
From the investigation, the following facts were found.

Fried products production line There is a Khun Nui, Dept Manager, Khun Mook, assistant team leader position, and Khun Ski, a senior daily 1. worker position who works as an assistant supervisor for the night shift.
2. Worker allocation for each production line, depends on the daily production plan to meet the needs of customers.
3. The move of work points can occur from 2 situations:
3.1. There is no production plan in that production line. The workers will be moved to work at other lines throughout the job site, considering the suitability of manpower and skills/experience required for each production line.
3.2. There is a partial production plan. Some workers will be transferred to help at other points with the following criteria.
Groups of workers who require expertise or experience in working at that point will not be considered to move the work site, such as workers who are responsible for cleaning the production line area because, at the end of the work, there will be cleaning. This group of workers has the skills to understand the areas that need special care and have the knowledge and ability to use chemicals. And the workers who look at the product code, inspect the quality, and the workers who record the production information (Thai workers) This group of workers has skills in reading and writing, understanding the product code system, checking the quality before entering the frying machine, including being able to calculate the numbers in the production line.
For the other workers besides those groups, If the workers move to help with other work. Supervisors select the workers who have previous work and are able to perform the job so that workers can perform smoothly at the point of departure and earn special rewards. There Khun Ski is a supervisor to help the workers who move to other locations.

Corrective Action:
Supervisors communicate and clarified with the workers in order to gain further understanding of the reasons for moving the production line and various criteria for consideration.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that his line supervisor was discriminating against Burmese workers by moving them temporarily (for a couple days to a week at a time) to go work in different lines where they are not familiar with the tasks being performed in those lines but the supervisor doesn't ask the Thai workers to do this.  The Burmese workers want to be able to work consistently in the line where they are familiar with the tasks and have become better at those tasks over time.  They don't want to be move around while Thai workers get to stay in the same line.
remediation_action: The business investigated the matter and found that the workers were moved to work in different lines depending on the daily production plan to meet the needs of the buyers; a particular line may not be in operation or in partial operation on a given day as per the production plan. Workers that have expertise working in a particular line such as those responsible for cleaning the production line area, those who have Thai reading and writing skills to inspect the quality of the products and make records according to the product coding system will not be moved to other lines, and this more often are Thai workers rather than Burmese workers.  The business has instructed the supervisors to clarify this with the workers so they understand the criteria based on which workers are allocated to work in various production lines.
remediation_validation: Issara followed up the worker and she confirmed she now understands clearly why they get asked to help out at other lines. She also noted that she had been interviewed by the business in its investigation, giving her a chance to provide her perspective on the matter.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue.  The worker now understands why some workers are asked to work in different lines while others stay put.  The business has taken action to investigate and instruct supervisors to make this clarification with workers.

closed_notes: The worker had difficulties finding a new employer after resigning from SEAPAC, because her job cancellation letter had the remark of the worker resigning from work which does not allow the worker to find another employer according to the Thai law. Issara reached out to the business and the business responded that the remark in the letter is as per the worker's request. The business has no control to change the remark from resigning from work to something else. However, the business was open to re-hire the worker if the worker has difficulties finding a new employer. Issara contacted the worker and updated the business response, however, the worker decided not to return to SEAPAC but to continue finding a new employer by her own means.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The issue with a worker who received a home returning letter for resigning from job.

Recommendations; 
-The language used in SEAPAC worker cancellation letters, “resigned, return to Myanmar” is making it essentially impossible for workers who are leaving SEAPAC(for reasons noted below) to be hired by new employers, also making workers more vulnerable during this covid-period. 
-It is ethically recommended for the business to provide departing workers cancellation letters that state the reason for departure which will allow the workers to find new employers.
- The issuing of the cancellation letter should be done within the period of time that workers have to find a new employer.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The business clarified that before the worker left the company, HR had an interpreter explaining to the worker the consequences as follows.
1. The company would like to retain the worker to work at the company and tried to help the worker to change the production line but the worker didn't want to.
2. The company informed the worker if the worker would like to resign the cancellation letter need to be noted that 'resign' and the worker could not change to the new employer according to the MoU practice and Thai law.
3. The company already informed DOE of the worker's resignation. The DOE could not change the reason - mentioned by HR. However, HR was open for the worker to re-ire if the worker has difficulties finding a new employer. The business also added that the worker would be assigned to work for the production wherever she feels more compfortable. 
Issara contacted the worker and updated the business response, however, the worker refused to be back and continue finding a new employer in her own way.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-The business should have clear protocols to issue cancellation letters and these protocols should be followed by all HR staff including interpreters. 
-The issuing of cancellation letters should be done on time to give enough time for workers to find another employer and get all documents and processes done on time. 
-Clear communication with all workers about the process of receiving a job cancellation when they leave the job.
systems_change_business_steps_taken: The business updated having a clear protocol about job cancellation letter, however, workers decided to leave the job.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The issue with the workers at the canteen (J & B restaurant) not getting paid for the national public holidays.  

Recommendations; 

-Cal-Comp to make sure that the workers who serve to Cal-Comp factory's staff receives their basics rights according to the LPA. 
-The business to make sure safeguards are in place for the worker's safety. The business should clearly communicate with the employer about the no retaliation policy towards the workers. 
-Cal-Comp to suggest the business make an announcement regarding the public holidays according to the LPA. Workers should be paid for the public holidays, thus Cal Comp should also recommend the business to remediate workers that have been impacted. 

Talking Points; 
-How does the business make sure that all of the workers in the factory area have access to their basics rights? 
-Is there a person in charge to oversee the working conditions of workers not directly employed by Cal Comp but still working on their compound? 
-And what are the grievance mechanisms channels workers can use in this case? any internal channels to provide support to them?

Timeframe 2 pay periods
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara raised this issue with Cal-Comp not with the business directly, Cal-Comp committed to having meetings with the business and suggested the investigation and the reimbursement. However, the Cal-Comp was only able to push the business  (Restaurant at the Cal-Comp canteen) for the single pay for seven days of reimbursement instead of double pay for working in their public holidays according to the Labor Protection Act to the workers for worked public holidays. Issara checked with the workers and workers have verified receiving seven days of reimbursement.  

32 workers have been paid for 7 days of daily wages. One worker received 2240 THB.
remediation_notes: Canteen workers report not getting properly paid for national holidays
remediation_action: The business mentioned that the J&B workers will get the reimbursement for the 13 public holidays.  The process is ongoing progress. Updated by K Amornrat HR at CC Samut Sakhon.
remediation_validation: Workers confirmed receiving the payment of 7 days of wages.
remediation_results:
J&B agreed to pay 7 days out of 13 days public holidays workers are entitled to receive annually according to the local law, arguing that workers were receiving more than the minimum wage for a normal working day. 

The business responded having done the reimbursement for 32 workers covering for 7 days of annual leaves paid and the total reimbursement is 71,680 THB.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-Cal-Comp to make an announcement to all of the vendors to make sure that all of the workers in the factory compound receive basics rights according to the LPA.
-The announcement should include sick leaves, annual leaves, SSF benefits, public holidays benefits, and other basics rights that are entitled to the workers.
systems_change_business_steps_taken: The Cal-Comp has updated about the communication that taken place with the vendors about the LPA.

call_details.description:
Issue with Annual Leave:
Client reported that two weeks ago, the business has announced to all the workers that the workers can take annual leave on 16th and 17th Apr 2021 as the line will start closing from 10th to 14th Apr during Songkran holiday.  So there are many workers who submitted for annual leave for 16th and 17th Apr 2021. But, on Monday, the business re-announce again that only 5 workers per each line can take annual leave on 16th and 17th Apr 2021 and they will only let the Thai workers take those leave only as they may need to travel from their hometown and meet their family. Apart from the 5 Thai workers, if more workers would like to take annual leave on those dates, they will only allow for leave without pay. There are also some Burmese workers who have submitted the leave request form and have a plan to do Nun and they plan to meet with their relatives during the Songkran holidays. But now the plan was canceled.
The workers are wondering why the business gives the hopes to the workers that they can take annual leave so that they make a plan. But now, that hopes come into discrimination and ruined what they have planned. The business should have a clear explanation for this.

90days report fee (Internal Only):
In the early of Mar 2021, the translator asks 60 baht to each worker who comes to do 90 days reports. He makes a list and the workers have to sign for paying 60 baht as 90days report fee. He asked for the money with the excuse of the budget shortage for a 90 days report and as soon as the budget for that was approved, they will pay back to the workers. After two weeks, he pays back 60 baht to each worker who pays for the 90 days report. Then the workers have to sign too as acknowledgement of they are receiving back their money. So the informant didn't want to report as they are receiving the money back.
call_details.next_steps: Have to escalate the team.

call_details.description:
Issue with Annual leave or sick leave/ Discrimination by nationality in terms of approval the leave:
Client reported that they are being discriminate in term of requesting sick leave or annual leave from the supervisor. They have to show a medical certificate even if they request for one day sick leave. The supervisor makes noise and asks many questions if they request for sick leave. Requesting annual leave also the same. Sometimes, the supervisor doesn't approve and they just take leave without pay if they have urgent matters even if they have the right to take annual leave or business leave. The client mentioned that requesting a leave is much more risky and difficult than holding the tails of three tigers.
For Thai workers, they don't need to show a medical certificate if they took only one day of sick leave. The supervisors also agreed to approve them to use annual leave instead so that they are not losing the monthly incentive.  And she didn't ask any questions and they don't need to talk too much for granting a leave too.In other lines, some supervisors approved annual leave if the worker agreed to use it when they have minor sickness and just need to take a rest in their room. But this supervisor only allows Thai workers and not the Burmese workers. The Burmese workers are just wondering why not the supervisor treats every worker equally. The line supervisor' name is P'Bua, in Line no. 405. She used to be in line 403 before and was reported once before too.

Verbal Abused:
The supervisor used to show the power to the Burmese workers too. She used to shout, hurry up, help each other, in the line. Actually, the Burmese workers are doing their job in a great way too. They try to finish the target as much as they can and they help each other when they have the sewing pieces accumulated in the line. Because of her loud voice, some workers, who do not understand Thai, thought that she was scolding them in front of the public. She can communicate in a soft way and pleasant way as the workers are also trying their job the best. For Thai workers, she used her voice softly and for Burmese workers, her voice tone is so hard. The workers expected her to communicate with every worker's fairy.

call_details.description:
one client from TG1 calls and expresses the poor management of business in terms of Covid-19 measure in TG1.

Not receiving proper quarantine in terms of having Closed contact person with positive cases_
Workers, who have a closed contact person with positive cases, are asked to do a medical check and wait for three days and if there is no severe symptom shown, they are asked to go back to work. But as the hospital does Covid-19 test only to those with severe symptoms, they are not able to take the test and still have to work.

Limitation of medical Check up facility in hospital _
Business does not have any arrangement of medical check up for the workers in the factory. They only asked the workers with severe symptoms to go and have a check at the hospital and bring a medical certificate provided from the doctor so that they can take sick leave. But, when the workers arrive at the hospital, they have to take queue no. and some are rescheduled to do the test in two or three days later. Although they have a high temperature, running nose and sneezing or cough, they are only provided with medicine.
(For those who have close contact with a positive case, before they were able to take the test at hospital. But now as the number of positive cases are increasing day by day, they are not allowed to enter the hospital because they did not meet with the doctor and cannot get a medical certificate. So they still need to continue to work now.)

Discrimination within Nationality _
The client mentioned that Thai workers, who has closed contact with positive cases, are able to take 14 days quarantine. The Burmese workers also would like to get this opportunity too. But now, they still have to work until severe symptoms show up. Even the time the symptom shows, they are not able to get the test right away.

Because of the limitation from hospitals at this time, workers would like to take proper management of quarentine process as guided by Department of Disease Control or they want the business to shut down for a while as they have some difficulties accessing health care. As most of them stay together with family members who work in other factories and some have infants and kids.
call_details.next_steps: Have to alert ILM team

call_details.description:
Client reported that the business did 100% of the tests for all the workers today. Those positive with symptoms will be taken to the government quarantine center while those positive with no symptoms will be quarantined on-site in a separate zone. The business is preparing the room in the factory premise near the Canteen and they ordered the workers to bring the utensil and there are fourteen items. These workers will be the ones with positive results with mild or no symptoms and the business will pick up them by Tuesday.The 14 items they have to bring are
1. Passport
2. Pillow, Blanket, Mat
3. Medicine (That they used to take)
4. Fan
5. Plate, spoon, cup
6. Tooth brush, Tooth paste, Shower Cream, Shampoo
7. Sanitary Pad (For Woman)
8. Detergent
9. Tissue (Enough for 14 days)
10. Mask (Enough for 14 days)
11. Clothes (Enough for 14 days) with clothes hanger
12. Phone, Charger, Power Bank
13. Extension Plug (In case if you need)
14. Mosquito Repellent 

The client also showed a picture of a quarantine site prepared by the business.  There are no facilities there except a far in a room with two layer beds for 12 persons. There is no bed and sheet. Most of the rooms are not well ventilated and the workers are worried it will increase the spread of the virus. There are also some rooms with beds but they think it must be for Thai workers only. They would like to request if the business can provide equal treatment or service to every worker regardless of nationality or if they cannot provide, if they can let them just by home quarantine. They feel a bit bundled to bring all this equipment. They would like to know if the rooms will be discriminately provided to the nationalities or if they can have some workers just by home quarantined if they are not sharing the room with any of their friends or family members.
call_details.next_steps: Have to check the business arrangement and how will they contribute it to the workers

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with annual leaves not being approved for Burmese workers. Workers reported that two weeks ago the business announced to the workers that they can take their annual leave on 16 and 17 after the Songkran holiday but on Monday(5 Apr) the business announced that they only approved Thai workers leaves 5 workers per line. None of the Burmese workers' leaves are approved. 

Please refer to the system improvement section for the recommendations.

Talking Points; 
-Why did the business first communicate to workers saying they could take leave on the 16-17th but now suddenly the business is saying only a limited number of workers can take leave per line (confirm whether it's 5 per line as reported by workers)?  Let the business know many workers have made plans already based on the business' original announcement. 
-Why is the business now limiting the number of workers that can take leave on the 16-17th to five per line?
-What is the business' selection criteria for who gets to take leave and why were only Thai workers approved for leave on the 16-17th? 
-Who made the decision to approve only Thai worker's leave? Is HR aware that only Thai workers' leave requests have been approved?(Closed)

call_details.description:
Issue with Annual leave or sick leave/ Discrimination by nationality in terms of approval the leave:
Client reported that they are being discriminate in term of requesting sick leave or annual leave from the supervisor. They have to show a medical certificate even if they request for one day sick leave. The supervisor makes noise and asks many questions if they request for sick leave. Requesting annual leave also the same. Sometimes, the supervisor doesn't approve and they just take leave without pay if they have urgent matters even if they have the right to take annual leave or business leave.
For Thai workers, they don't need to show a medical certificate if they took only one day of sick leave. The supervisors also agreed to approve them to use annual leave instead so that they are not losing the monthly incentive.  And she didn't ask any questions and they don't need to talk too much for granting a leave too. In other lines, some supervisors approved annual leave if the worker agreed to use it when they have minor sickness and just need to take a rest in their room. But this supervisor only allows Thai workers and not the Burmese workers. The Burmese workers are just wondering why not the supervisor treats every worker equally. Sometimes, the Thai workers are talking on the phone and watching the movies while there is less order and they completed their target. But, when Burmese workers also complete their target and there are not many orders, she asked those workers to go and help other lines. The workers do not feel happy about this too.

Verbal Abuse:
The supervisor used to shout very loudly and her voice was being recorded by workers before. Then she kept quiet. But now, she is back to normal again. Sometimes, the workers are just asking each other about the information with sewing tasks. When she saw that, she would shout loudly what are you talking, keep quiet or work quickly like that. Sometimes, she asks the workers to go and assist other points, while they are completing their target. Those workers go and assist to the other points and the target accumulated again after one or two hours as they have to leave their original points. Then she shouts at those workers by saying that come back quickly your points are getting accumulated. Actually, she can speak in a nice way. She is the one who asked the workers to go and assist and when the target gets accumulated to the workers line, she would like to blame those workers. The workers just would like to know why she behaved like that. As it is the working place and not the nursery school, she shouldn't treat the workers like that. 

The line supervisor' name is P'Lei, in Line no. 110. She has previously been reported by the workers and Issara brings her case with the business once already before.

call_details.description:
Clients reported with the issue of two annual leaves are being deducted while the business prepared on-site quarantine center after the covid-19 test.

The client reported that the business did Covid-19 test on 3 Jul 2021 as ordered by SSO. And then they shared the announcement through the line group that they will deduct three days annual leave from each worker from 5-7 Jul 2021, as they will have to prepare the quarantine site in the factory compound.
1. For those, who still have enough annual leave, will be deducted from the remaining leave balance.
2. The newcomers, who haven't earned the annual leave, will be deducted in advance from the future accursed annual leave.
3. For those, who have already used up annual leave, the business will deduct from the future annual leave. So instead of being entitled to get 6 days annual leave next year, they will get only 4 days.

As the Business received the order from SSO to shut down the factory starting from 7 Jul, the factory started shutting down from that date and  this day was covered by 50% from  SSO. So that the business deducted only two days 5-6 Jul 2021. 

The business didn't declare anything like you can report to HR or Translator if you have any objection or question. They just shared this announcement to the line group. The workers said they used to do like that in the past. But, they are wondering if this is agreed with the law or not. They feel not much happy as the annual leave is so important for them.
call_details.next_steps: Have to alert ILM team

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue# 1. (CLosed) 

Context; The issue with two repeatedly reported supervisors in the respective production lines. Supervisors are reported being verbally abusive, discriminative, and providing preferences towards Thai workers only, complaining to Burmese workers for any request they make. Supervisor name P'Lei, in Line no. 110. and P'Bua, in Line no. 405. 

Previously Provided Recommendations; -The business to conduct an investigation with this specific supervisor. In order to assess the behavior of the supervisors, the business can conduct a survey where workers can rate their supervisors confidentially. Given that workers may not know their supervisors' Thai names, it is recommended that the business arrange an org-chart with all supervisors' names and titles. -There should not be any coercion or retaliation towards workers during the investigation and survey processes. The investigation process must be confidential, workers should not be needing to provide any of their personal information, such as working IDs, their names, etc. 

-The business should create a plan of action based on the results of investigations and surveys. Such actions should include training and disciplinary actions (if necessary). -To communicate to workers the actions the business is taking to respond to workers' grievances, would help the business to strengthen the trust of workers in the business grievance mechanism. Business actions for the previous report; -The business conducted an investigation, then took disciplinary actions towards the line supervisor and provided training on fair and ethical treatment of workers. 


-The business didn't share the details of the investigation with Issara. Recommendations that are missing to follow by the business. NOTE FOR BHR; Please suggest the business follow the following missing recommendations. - Recommend the business to take disciplinary actions towards these supervisors following the company protocol. Since this is the second time these supervisors are reported, please ask the company what would be the appropriate disciplinary actions in this case? Is it a written warning? - Workers reported that the previous actions taken by the business helped improve the situation for a while, but now the supervisors are having abusive behaviors again. For this reason, it is recommended for the business to have a monitoring plan where they can hear from workers directly what the situation is and if further actions are needed. 


-The monitoring plan could be done by creating safe spaces for workers to share their feedback (e.g. morning talks) or the company could also conduct a confidential survey with all workers under these two supervisors. There should not be any coercion or retaliation towards workers during the investigation, open dialogue sessions, and survey processes. The investigation process must be confidential, workers should not be needing to provide any of their personal information, such as working IDs, their names, etc. and workers should receive an explanation of the no retaliation policy that would guarantee safeguards. 


-To work on a plan of actions based on the result of the survey/investigation/dialogue with workers. -To communicate to workers the actions the business is taking to respond to workers' grievances, would help the business to strengthen the trust of workers in the business grievance mechanism. Talking Points. -What is the business action for such repeated issues? -Please propose to the business that Issara is happy to provide training to all supervisors and HR after the business investigation. (CLosed) 

timeframe 1 pay period.

Issue #2 (29-Jul-2021) 

Context: The issue with the workers' annual leave being deducted for the days that the business did not run as it was preparing for a quarantine center in the factory. Workers added that the business deducted their two days of annual leaves (6-7 Jul-2021).

Recommendations. 
-The business should reinstate workers' annual leaves and use the medical leave or COVID-19 special leave instead for those two days. 
- The business is recommended to use any of those leaves (medical or special leave) as both are applicable for COVID -19 since it is a health-related issue. 
- The LPA is a law that protects the rights of workers, including the right to have rest during annual leave days, which means the worker being able to consult with the employer about when the worker would take annual leave, and at a time that is most beneficial to the worker. For this reason, annual leave shall not be allocated by the employers without workers' consent. 
-For this case, workers were not consulted in advance about getting their annual leave days used up for the factory shut down for preparation of setting up the quarantine center. For these reasons, the business shall reinstate workers; annual leave and use sick leave/special leave instead for those two days.  

Talking points. 

-Workers reported not being asked for their consent about the deduction of their annual leaves, is the business aware of this? If yes, what was the understanding of the business about workers' annual leaves?

Within two weeks.

call_details.description:
Worker from this factory called and reported following two issues. 

(1) Lack of supplies during quarantine period; Worker reported that once they are identified as COVID-19 infected or suspected/high risk workers, they have to stay quarantine. 10 days of quarantine for infected workers and 7 days for close contact. However, the business does not provide any foods or even water. If there is a wife being infected, the husband or the family member also has to stay quarantine. It means the whole family members have to stay quarantine and have no access to the foods or water. Workers want the business to provide supplies or assign someone to help them purchase. 

(2) The issue with expense of ATK test kits; If a worker is infected or suspected, have to do ATK test. If a worker feel sick, she has to do the ATK test and also go to the hospital. Once they go to the hospital, the hospital will do the PCR test and confim her to stay 10 days of quarantine. Once they complete the quarantine, on the day 10th they have to do ATK test, on the day 11th another ATK test and on the day 15th follo up test. Total around 4 ATK test for both infected and the suspected workers. The business does not pay for those test kits. Workers find it expensive to pay for the several kits. They want the business to reduce some of the test process and also provde ATK test for free. Once, the worker have approached the HR and requested for the free test, the HR said that even Thai staff have to buy by themselves. 

(3) The issue with the wages for the quarantine period; Follow up on the previous issue where the business used to deduct workers annual leaves for high risks workers quarantine days. The worker said that the business has verbally communicated that they will pay for any kind of qarantine. If a worker is suspected or high risk and have to stay quarantine, the business will pay wages as a special wages. No any leaves will be deducted. For infected workers, the hospital provides MC which can be used for sick leave. Wokrer said that they do not have issue with the wages during their quaratine these days.
Follow up call with the client to check the updates about her relative recruitment process.

A worker reported that his visa was expiring on 27 March 2023 and his passport expired in Feb 2024. On 24 Mar 2023, the business told him that they will not do the extension for him anymore. He is walk-in MOU worker from another factory and he started working with HIT-91 in 2021. Even they cannot extend the visa on the Thai side, he is happy to go back Myanmar and do the U-Turn process. Another worker said his 4-year visa and work permit will expire on 30 May 2023. There are lots of other workers whose documents are expiring in 2023 and they are not sure whether the business will arrange for their contract and document extension. The workers would like to know whether the supplier will extend their documents in Thailand or have them return to Myanmar for the U-turn process. Some workers went to the HR office on 27 March 2023 but HR did not respond to them with a clear answer. Some workers don't want to go back to Myanmar because of the security situation back home. Some are wondering if the business will do the pink card registration for them if the government announces another round.

For MOU workers whose visas and work permits will expire in May 2023, the business will send them back to Myanmar on 3rd May 2023. They need to do the U-Turn from Myanmar side and come back after the process is done. However, the business did not clearly explain the process and timeframe for this. There are a total of 64 workers in total and 13 workers have already done the passport extension. Some workers' visa and work permits will expire on 21 or 21 May 2023. They are wondering if the business can send them back by this time as they still need to inform their landlord one month in advance to leave their room so that they can get a deposit.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that for many MOU workers, their contracts and legal documents (visas, work permits) were expiring, some in March 2023 others in May 2023, but the business had not communicated to them as to whether their contracts and legal documents would be extended, and if so, whether they could have them extended in Thailand or they would need to return to Myanmar for the MOU U-turn process. For a group of 64 MOU workers whose visas and work permits will expire in May 2023, the business said they would need to do the U-turn process but did not clearly explain the process and timeframe for this.
remediation_action: Issara received updates from workers that the business held a communication session with them on 4 May 2023. The business has contracted Smart Thai RA to send the demand list to DOE with name list of 64 workers. The workers will go back to Myanmar on May 21 and stay for three months before returning to Thailand.
remediation_validation: Workers provided an update saying that 50 of 64 workers crossed the border at the Ranong-Kawthaung checkpoint. A Myanmar recruitment agency picked them up at the border and processed the passport renewals at the border. They have all arrived home, needing to stop overnight 3-4 nights in their journey home. The 3,000 Baht they received from the business was not enough for various expenses during this journey. The other 14 workers decided to remain in Thailand and find another job.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case. The business has clarified with the workers about the U-turn process and those workers that chose to do the U-turn have all arrived in Myanmar.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; The issue with lack of communication about the COVID-19 test. Workers raised that they have heard that the business is will not cover medical fees if they get infected. Workers also are concern about how the business handles infected workers. 

Recommendations; 
-The business to provide clear guidance about the assistance for workers that test positive for COVID-19. The guidance shall be provided in written accompany by verbal announcements and it should cover the following information: 
-are there different measures/procedures depending on the severity of the symptoms 
-who will covered the treatment costs (SSF, employer?) 
-quarantine centers and services
-the process that the infected and not infected workers will have to follow (self-quarantine, etc.)
- the wages payment for the days of quarantine whenever needed

Talking points
-How many workers have been tested and found positive so far? How has the business managed infected workers? 
-Which hospital or quarantine centers are the workers being sent to?
-Workers raised that some of the workers from Hi-tech Suksaward are also infected but their spouses are continuing working in Hi-Tech (soi 91). How has the business manage the workers who share the dormitory with the workers from (soi  91)?  
-How have the workers been communicated about the COVID-19 treatment fees?

remediation_notes: Issues: Workers from Roung Thor line reported they were being pressured to agree to work on their day off. The line supervisors threatened the workers saying they would be assigned to difficult jobs such as cleaning the sewers or they would be denied their diligence bonus (Bia Ka Yan) if they did not agree to work on their day off. So, they felt they had to consent to working on their day off even if they didn’t want to do so. Workers also added that the manager switched their day off from Thursday to Tuesday without first consulting them and getting their consent.
remediation_action: Action: Issara has raised this issue with the business, and the business responded that they have the voluntary process for the workers to work on their day-off and to agree to switch their day-off. However, about the workers being assigned to do the cleaning tasks if they do not agree to work on their day-off, the business responded that no workers were pressured to do the cleaning. The business conducted the investigation and found that there was an issue with switching the day-off without workers' consent. HR has clarified with production managers and supervisors that there would be no more switching days-off. If there was a need to do so, workers would need to consent before making such a switch.
remediation_validation: Worker Validation: Issara followed up with the workers, and they have confirmed that this issue is no longer a problem.
remediation_results: Results: Issara is closing this case because the business has made it clear that there will be no switching of workers' days-off, and if such switch is needed in special cases, workers' consent would be needed before proceeding.

call_details.description: The GD ambassador from called Issara and reported that. On 13 May 2021, MMP announced to all Myanmar workers to do Covid 19 Vaccination on 19th May. However, MMP didn't give the comprehensive information about vaccination such as what is the brand of vaccine?  why only Myanmar workers need to ? why not Thai workers? What will be the side-effect of vaccine?. As MMP failed to give comprehensive information, workers are afraid to do vaccination. In this situation, the rumors about the china made vaccine is spreading among Myanmar workers such as: the vaccine is not yet tested, the casualties rate is higher after vaccination. So most of the workers thinking of refusing to do vaccination. But some line-supervisor told the workers that if they refuse, they will have to sign warning letter and may be dismiss from job. So workers would like to get information session about vaccination and they don't want to be dismissed even if they refuse to do vaccination. So they ask help from Issara.

call_details.next_steps: Issara to escalate with the strategic partner.

closed_notes:
Issue #1: Issara reached to the business, the business responded that it was just an announcement and the vaccination will happen to the foreign workers until Thai nationalities are fully vaccinated. Issara suggested the business to communicate with the workers. The business updated having done the communication with the workers via supervisor. Workers updated not being communicated as argued by the business. Since the business is not taking Issara's recommendation, Issara considered closing this case.  

Issue # 2.
Issara had several calls with the business to discuss the issues, the business responded having done the communication with the supervisors from the specific line. However, the business did not commit to doing the investigation, rather argued that the supervisors are not having such behavior but the workers are slandering their supervisor. Issara checked with the workers about the situation, the workers have updated the situation getting worse by being targeted by the supervisor and threatened for reporting to Issara. Issara tried to reach the MD of the factory, however never received any reply. Several weeks later HR of the factory reached to Issara that they have ceased working with Issara, therefore they do not need to take Issara's recommendation into account. Workers keep reporting Issara. Since the business clearly says not taking action as per Issara recommendations, Issara considered closing this case.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue # 1. 

Context; The issue with the announcement that the business made regarding vaccination for Burmese migrant workers only. The issue with the announcement that the business made regarding vaccination for Burmese migrant workers only. Workers reported that the business announced to the Burmese workers that the Burmese workers from MMP will receive vaccines on 16th May 2021 etc. Some supervisors said to the workers that if the workers do not want to get vaccines then they will have to sign documents and the consequences might be dismissal. 


Recommendations:
Given that workers have raised many concerns about the announcements about the vaccination and reporting lack of understanding of how it will be handled, it is recommended that MMP make written and verbal announcements including the following information before the workers are vaccinated: 

When is the process starting?
Who is leading the process?
Is the process the same for Burmese and Thai workers? If not, how is it different and why?
Reassurance that the vaccines that will be used have been approved by the World Health Organization and the Thai Government, therefore, they are safe
Who to contact in case there are any questions about the vaccine? (could be the government hotline)

                       Understanding that this is a topic of concern for all workers, it is recommended that the business is open to dialogue with workers, hear their concerns and be able to reply to their questions so that the process can be smooth and workers feel secure about it. Issara can provide support by reviewing the language of the announcement so the information can be easily understood by all migrant workers. 

In addition to migrant workers’ communication, it is recommended that the business provide similar information to Thai workers. 

Talking points:
Ask the business for information about the vaccination plan: -
When is this happening?
Is this organized by the government?
Is it the same plan for Burmese and Thai workers? If not, how is it different and why?

call_details.description: Issara had canteen outreach with the workers from HiTech Lat yai. One of the workers we met calls and reports this case. She sounds scared when talking on the phone. She doesn't want her husband know that she calls Issara. She's also afraid of retaliation from the business. But she took the courage and made this call. She cried out of emotion while talking on the phone.
The worker was followed up to clarify the case she had raised but she said I was calling the wrong number.

The worker was reached out to get an update on the issue. The worker explained that she was not comfortable talking with Issara in front of her husband. Her husband does not like her to talk to other people.


During the business meeting, the employer informed the workers to come and raise the issue at the HR office because the outsiders could not understand the Maung incentive system of the workplace. She guessed that the employer is trying to know who reported the issue to Issara. She said she will reach out to Issara to update the details on Sunday.

The worker informed the Issara staff that the business had a communication session with workers. The business promised that the workers would be separated into three groups based on how fast and skillfully they can sew. During the next three months, the business will assign targets based on the workers' skills. So, the issue is now resolved.

Worker Voice: During the communication session, the interpreter told the workers that the outsiders could not help the workers if they had these kinds of issues. Why do they contact outsiders? Next time, the workers should come to the office first to clarify.

The worker is unsatisfied with the word the interpreter informed the workers. She thanks Issara for the support.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case.  The workers confirmed that they understand how production targets are set and the incentives tied to meeting those targets.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that workers in her line (B18) didn't understand how the targets were set and how that was awarded as "maung incentive" pay.  Those in line B18 used to receive this incentive under the former line supervisor but has stopped receiving it since the new supervisor (P Nu) took charge.  She noted that this is happening in line B17 as well. Right now, Wanna Yin is in charge of lines B16 and B17, while Wanna Kai is taking care of lines B18 and B29.

TPs:
- What targets need to be met for workers to receive the "Maung incentive"? Is it based on the production of the whole line and incentive awarded to the whole group?
- How often is this incentive provided?
- The worker noted that this incentive ceased after the new line supervisor started.  Why might this be the case? Has the criteria for providing this incentive changed?

Recommendations:
- Investigate to find out how the Maung incentive is set up and what targets need to be reached for the incentive to be paid and why suddenly workers have stopped receiving the incentive with the change of the line supervisor.
- Communicate clearly to the workers the criteria upon which the company determines that a worker will receive this incentive.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Wachirapon, HR manager, stated that she is unsure what the 'Maung Incentive' is 
. Typically, the incentive is determined by the design and product of the order. And the worker would be paid fairly based on the effectiveness and efficiency of the finished product. In terms of supervisors, the line supervisors are sometimes rotated according to company policy because different supervisors have different skills and are rotated for the most effective production.

She will, however, look into it further and get back to us by next week.



BHR followed up and shared about ‘Maung Incentive’ and also case 1,2, and 4.
Case 1. According to the production, every worker at that line must pass the sawing test. If the worker passed, he or she can work and remain on that line. If not, the worker will be transferred to another line.
Case 2. This is not the case; every morning, the production manager will calculate the workforce who will report to work that day. As a result, there is no workload for the workers.
Case 3. HR held a communication session with all workers on the lines. Currently, the company has lower orders and the workers do not have OT. As a result, this occurred and affected every line. There is also no rotation of supervisors on the lines. HR is also available to any workers who have questions but no one is asking. When HR explained the incentive scheme to the workers, they said they understood.
Case 4. HR trained these supervisors on how to communicate with workers. Because these supervisors simply did not communicate with the workers on an ongoing basis. However, these supervisors would improve after the training.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; The issue with the COVID-19 precautions measures and the way of managing COVID-19 test for the workers. Workers reported that some of them have mild fever and cough but not being tested for COVID. 

Recommendations; 

-To make announcements in writing and verbally to explain to workers how the business is handling COVID 19 testing, what the timeframes are, and if this is being done by groups. 
-The business should communicate what is the plan for those who test positive, what would be the quarantine plan, the process of taking sick leave according to the LPA, and any other assistance they would get, such as provision of food and basic needs. 
- The business shall also provide information on who to contact in case of emergency or if workers suspect they have been exposed to COVID or present any symptoms.  The focal contact information (name, contact number,etc.) should be widely communicated to all workers.

Talking Points; 

-How many workers have been tested in both facilities (SMSK and SMPK) and how many workers have been found COVID-19 positive so far?
-What are the processes and plans for those who have been tested positive and for those who are at high risks (close contact with positive cases).  
-Which quarantine centers are the workers have been sent to?
-Are the workers getting paid during their quarantine/sick leave? 

Please share the following information with the business.  

1.       After people tested positive for COVID-19 they need to immediately quarantine for 14 days, which means total isolation from ANYONE else who has tested negative or is untested.  Absolutely nobody who is COVID-negative should be indoors in the same space and air with them.  It does NOT matter if COVID-positive people have symptoms or not – all must quarantine.  Total isolation of all COVID-positive cases is the #1 concern for preventing spread. 

·         Is this quarantine isolation happening or not?  If not, people are being put at risk.  It is worrying that this is one of the main areas that the people do not know about; the people seem to be focusing on symptoms and not isolation, which isn’t correct.

 

2.       For people testing positive for COVID-19, it is normal for severe cases to go to the hospital and mild cases to rest at home in isolation.  And, asymptomatic cases must stay home too.  But are people prepared to live in isolation?

·         Do people in isolation have a way to get food and supplies safely?  For example, getting supplies or food delivered to their door, but nobody being exposed to them? Please be aware to make sure your workers are ready for this so that the spread can be minimized. 

 

3.       For COVID-exposed people: all must be tested starting at 5-7 days from the day when they were exposed.  It’s not just symptomatic who should be tested, but all – 100%, not just “under suspicion” which is unscientific, and unsafe.  They need to know the day they were exposed, and the day that the COVID-positive person got their first positive test.  It does no good to test less than 5 days after being exposed; at that stage, it’s too early to tell.  If the test at 5-7 days is negative and you have no symptoms, you still have to continue quarantine, and normally there is a re-test again at one of two points: (a) if the person starts feeling symptoms, or (b) another 5 days later because sometimes it takes more than 7 days for their infection to be detectable.

·         Is testing happening at the correct timeframes to be effectively detecting infection?  If tests are being done too early, there’s a risk of false negatives and not catching the cases that actually exist.  Are negative tests at Day 5-7 being followed up with a second test around Day 10-14 to confirm that the person is okay to exit quarantine?

 

4.       Being COVID-exposed is a scary thing: there is a lot of anxiety associated with waiting for test results, and even if they are negative, not being sure if they are really negative.  It’s also risky when they see people who are positive or possibly positive mixing around with others, or if they are positive and waiting to see if their family members may have gotten sick from them (and the guilt/helplessness associated with that).  So many sources of anxiety, stress, and fear here. 

·         We (Supplier and Issara) should be ready to provide extra time and attention to the psychosocial aspects of being COVID-exposed and isolation: validating feelings of stress and anxiety, explaining more facts about the infection and quarantine process, helping workers in isolation find productive ways to spend their time while in isolation (maybe even create a group forum on social media!). If workers are in factory dorms then the business could install a wi-fi router so that workers in quarantine have free internet and can communicate with others, learn some Thai language or some crafty things to do at home, etc etc.

call_details.description:
The manager of the shrimp peeling line in building 2 has verbal and physical abuse issues. She can speak Burmese and yell out to the workers, "Don't you have a brain to think? Why don't you understand if I tell you?" While she is yelling out to the workers, she uses her hand to point them out, touching their heads and pushing their shoulders. In July, a female worker got an eye injury because the manager's finger attacked her eye. The worker was told, "If you are not satisfied, go report to the office." The manager did not say sorry for her fault.

The female worker feels insecure about raising the issue and reporting it to the HR office, even though the interpreter came to investigate. However, the other workers called Issara and raised the issue because this line manager's behavior is unacceptable for the whole production line.

This line manager sometimes does not provide lunch on time after working a maximum of five hours. The workers have to work for over five hours before taking an hour's break.

The eight working hours are mostly until 4:00 p.m., but the manager asks the workers to work until 4:30 p.m. and sometimes until 4:45 p.m. The workers do not get overtime for those extra working hours.

In the past, workers could change the needles and knives at any time. Now the workers are asked to inform the supervisor if they would like to change the materials. If three or four workers requested new materials at the same time, the manager would shout and yell.

A few years ago, this manager had an issue with workers from Building 2, and she was moved to Building 3. She has a bad record, and the workers do not want to work with that manager anymore. The workers requested that Issara discuss this issue with the supplier and take serious action against her.  

The manager's name is P'Kyip.

description: Company grievance mechanism not safe/confidential/anonymous
closed_notes: Issara has several meetings including an escalation call with the business and provided recommendations on how to respond to the issue. The business said that they would conduct an internal survey to assess the situation and be able to find out the root cause of the issue and the actions needed to respond to the issue of line supervisors’ behaviour. However, the business later got back to Issara by saying that they were not able to conduct the survey at the moment because of the third wave of COVID-19 issue, but that the company had simplified the process of taking annual leave and the sick leaves by workers getting approval from HR staff instead that getting it from line supervisors. With these changes, workers will not have to deal with the supervisors to request the leaves which will mitigate the issue and reduce the burden of the workers. Since then Issara has not heard any update from the workers. In addition to that, the business is also temporarily closed due to the nearby factory explosion and uncertain opening date. Since there is no clarity on any further steps the company would take given the COVID -19 situation and the current closure of the factory, Issara has decided to close all of the cases related to this report at this point and will update is as needed once the company resumes operations and workers can confirm if the issues have been solved.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
-Workers who are wanting to leave and want to have a proper job cancelation letter when they leave. 

Please see the recommendations for the system change.  

Talking Points;
-Several workers have expressed their challenges with supervisors which lead them to resign from their job, what is the business understanding of these challenges?
remediation_notes: A worker reported having difficulties applying for a new job with the cancellation letter issued by the company. This worker reported that the reasons he had decided to leave the job was due to the poor behaviour from line supervisors and their poor treatment towards workers. Issara has received similar reports from other workers sharing the issues they face with supervisors.
remediation_action: The business said that they would conduct an internal survey to assess the situation and be able to find out the root cause of the issue and the actions needed to respond to the issue of line supervisors’ behaviour. However, the business later got back to Issara by saying that they were not able to conduct the survey at the moment because of the third wave of COVID-19 issue, but that the company had simplified the process of taking annual leave and the sick leaves by workers getting approval from HR staff instead that getting it from line supervisors.
remediation_validation: There is no update from workers, since 1) the business haven't been able to take further actions to address the issues with supervisors and 2) the company has been closed due to the explosion that took place near the company.
remediation_results: Since there is no clarity on any further steps the company would take  and the timeframes for those actions given the new COVID-19 wave and the current closure of the factory, Issara has decided to close all of the cases related to this report at this point and will update it as needed once the company resumes operations and workers can confirm if the issues have been solved.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations; 
-To have open discussion sessions between  HR and workers to understand better what are the challenges being faced by workers and what is driving them to resign. During these discussions, the business is encouraged to share with workers what the business actions are to address these issues.
-The business could also conduct an internal survey to learn why workers want to resign and what can help them remain in Ladybird. Issara can help with the survey questionnaire. Surveys should be conducted in a confidential way where workers feel safe to share the issues that they are facing. 
-The business shall work on a plan to address the issues that are raised in the survey by the workers. 
-The business shall provide training to all supervisors including translators.
-The business shall revise the grievance channels that are meant for workers to raise their issues. The revision should focus on workers' confidentiality and the no retaliation policy. Workers have expressed their concern about raising issues with HR, out of fear of retaliation from their supervisors, therefore it is strongly recommended for the business to reinforce a no retaliation policy and make sure all supervisors are aware of the policy, follow it and face consequences if they commit any actions against such policy.
