call_details.description:
Client updated about the abusive behavior of the line supervisor. 
The client name is Zin Mar Wai, ID:721626. She is currently in PU-4, in line no.67 managed by the line supervisor P'Pa-Yin. 
It's been about a week since the supervisor is finding a mistake on her. She has been working in this line for three years. As she has a problem with her digestive issue, she has to go to the toilet every morning for a week. Sometimes, one time, sometimes two times in the morning. But, she can still handle her points. Although there are two workers in other lines, she handles that task alone. But, she can manage it although she has to go to the toilet because of her health problem. Today, the supervisor called and blamed her for going to the toilet for a long time. Then she told the supervisor that there are many people queuing in front of the toilet this morning and she has to wait. But, the supervisor blamed her for giving the excuse. Then she talked back to the supervisor about why she is telling her like that because she can still handle her points and it's a health problem. Then they argued with each other and finally they asked the translator, Ko Soe Naing, to go and help her to translate for her. She would like the translator to help her translate. Please let the supervisor change the line if she doesn't like her. But, the translator didn't translate all that she said and he told her that she cannot change the line because there is nowhere that needs other workers to support. And he asked her to listen to what the supervisor suggested to her instantly. Actually, she came and joined the business as a sewer and she was asked to do trimming and punch the button hole. Now, it seems like they are asking her to do small tasks and assign her to unimportant roles. Whenever there is not much work, she is asked not to work and gets only 75% of daily wage.
So she became so upset, not only from the supervisor, but also from the translator, and then she decided to leave the job. Then she requests the resignation letter and she signs. The translator reminds her that you will not get a job changeable cancellation letter if you decide to leave by yourself. But, at that time, she cannot make a decision   and change her mind. 
In the evening, she called Issara and explained about this. She is wondering if the business can swift her the line, she will continue to work. She is wondering if we can help her discuss the business although she has submitted the resignation letter. If they don't want her anymore, she requests to provide her job changeable cancellation letter.
call_details.next_steps: Have to alert ILM team in email.

call_details.description:
One client from TG1 reported that the factory started testing Covid-19 positive cases in the working line now starting from Thai workers. And the ambulance comes to pick up the patient in the factory from day to day. The workers don't know how many positive cases were found, but he guessed it would be not less than five. The workers are not sure how the business will manage with the quarantine process. He just knew a few workers who were stationed closely with the positive cases are taking quarantine and others in the same affected lines are working as usual. The workers in the affected line are also afraid to keep working although they are not closely stationed to the positive cases as they share the same entrance, go and go out and interact with each other. On the other hand, the business didn't make any clear communication about the payment if the workers were asked to take quarantine and if they will provide any support during the quarantine period and how is the medical support to those who tested positive.

The client would like to know why the business asked only a closed contact person to take quarantine, how the business will handle the process, including the payment, support during quarantine and medical care.
And another thing is that the business did announce something in the morning between 10 AM to 10:30 AM in Thai language and majority of the Burmese workers do not understand this. They announced it from the HR office and the workers heard this in their working line through the sound box. He also would like to know what did the business announce. It takes about 5 min long.

Issue #1. (CLOSED)

Worker name - Zin Mar Wai, ID:721626. Used to work for line PU-4, no.67 managed by the line supervisor P'Pa-Yin. 

Recommendations (already given):
-The business shall immediately investigate the issues with the worker, supervisor, and translator and make sure that the worker has the opportunity to share what happened and what led her to submit her resignation. 
-It is fundamental that the business takes necessary steps to guarantee there would not be any retaliation towards the worker during or after the investigation. Therefore, the business shall make sure that the supervisor and the translator do not have any negative attitudes towards the worker following the investigation. 
-The worker should be provided with the option of bringing a colleague to support with translation/clarification as needed. 
-The business is suggested to come to an agreement with the worker based on the result of the investigation

Issue # 2. (added on 21-June-2021). 
Context: The issue with lack of communication about the COVID-19 test and the workers who were found positive. Workers raised their questions and concerns about whether they will be paid for their quarantine days, who will pay for the medical treatment costs, and so on. Workers added that the business made announcements in the morning which is about 5 minutes of the announcement but only in the Thai language. 


Recommendations; 
-The business shall provide clear guidance about the assistance for workers that test positive for COVID-19. The guidance shall be provided in writing accompanied by verbal announcements in all workers languages and it should cover the following information: 
-are there different measures/procedures depending on the severity of the symptoms 
-who will cover the treatment costs (SSF, employer?) 
-quarantine centers and services
-the process that the infected and not infected workers will have to follow (self-quarantine, etc.)
-the payment of the wages for the days of quarantine whenever needed

Talking points
-How many workers have been tested and found positive so far? How has the business managed infected workers? 
-Which hospital or quarantine centers are the workers being sent to?
-Workers raised that some of the workers have been tested positive and only a few of the closed stationed workers are being asked for 14 days of quarantine while other workers in the same line are still being asked to come to work. How has the business managed the workers who share the dormitory and production lines?  
-How have the workers been communicated about the COVID-19 treatment fees?

In those lines, the business just asked the workers to take 14 days quarantine who were closely stationed to those positive cases workers. About three or four workers were asked to take quarantine per each closed contact person and other workers in the same lines still have to come to work. The workers in the affected line are also afraid to keep working although they are not closely stationed to the positive cases as they share the same entrance, go and go out and interact with each other. On the other hand, the business didn't make any clear communication about the payment if the workers were asked to take quarantine and if they will provide any support during the quarantine period and how is the medical support to those who tested positive. They would like to know how the business will handle the process, including the payment, support during quarantine and medical care.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with lack of communication about the COVID-19 test and the workers who were found positive. Workers raised their questions and concerns about whether they will be paid for their quarantine days, who will pay for the medical treatment costs, and so on. 

Recommendations; 
-The business shall provide clear guidance about the assistance for workers that test positive for COVID-19. The guidance shall be provided in writing accompanied by verbal announcements in all workers languages and it should cover the following information: 
-are there different measures/procedures depending on the severity of the symptoms 
-who will cover the treatment costs (SSF, employer?) 
-quarantine centers and services
-the process that the infected and not infected workers will have to follow (self-quarantine, etc.)
-the payment of the wages for the days of quarantine whenever needed

Talking points
-How many workers have been tested and found positive so far? How has the business managed infected workers? 
-Which hospital or quarantine centers are the workers being sent to?
-Workers raised that some of the workers have been tested positive and only a few of the closed stationed workers are being asked for 14 days of quarantine while other workers in the same line are still being asked to come to work. How has the business managed the workers who share the dormitory and production lines?  
-How have the workers been communicated about the COVID-19 treatment fees?

timeframe 1 week
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The business informed that the COVID-19 prevention policy has been announced verbally and written since last week. The brief detail is as follows.

1. The infected employees will be paid 100% according to the medical certificate and be recorded as COVID sick leave.
2. The high-risk employees, the workers have two options to select.
    - 100% paid leave, the employees are able to use annual leave or personal/business leave
    - 50% paid leave, the company will pay the employees for using the special COVID quarantine leave


Issara has followed up with the workers, workers have confirmed being clearly communicated about receiving the payment for their quarantine days and not having additional concerns regarding the current situation.
remediation_notes: The issue with a lack of communication about the COVID-19 testing and the workers who were found positive. Workers raised their questions and concerns about whether they will be paid for their quarantine days, and who will pay for the medical treatment costs.
remediation_action: Issara had a meeting with the business, and the business responded that among the Covid-19 positive cases so far, only Thai full-time staff had been infected and no migrant workers. The business added that they were communicating to all workers how the company was handling the COVID outbreak and how they would receive their benefits according to the law and the company policy, such as the payment of their wages while they are at quarantine.
remediation_validation: Issara followed up with the workers and workers confirmed receiving clear information about their inquiries and that they do not have any additional concern.
remediation_results: No further steps are needed for this case.

call_details.description:
Client called and reported that the business announced and asked the workers to take care of themselves as the hospital is full with patients and not accepting patients to do covid-19 test starting from tomorrow anymore. And the number of Covid-19 positive cases are increasing day by day in TG1. The workers are very concerned about this. They would like business to shut down for a while if there is a limitation with medical care in hospitals. 

                  On the other hand, the business didn't have a proper Covid-19 test for the workers. They just asked the workers who have close contact with positive cases to do Covid-19 test and if the result shows negative, they ask those workers to go back and work. So the workers are also concerned about this. (Although the business told us that they follow  DDC guidelines, in practice, they didn't apply it. I have asked the number of those workers who have closed contact with positive cases and been asked to back work. The informant said they will provide me tonight when they come back from work.) 

               Now, the workers, who headed to the hospital to do Covid-19 says that the hospital does not allow them to enter the hospital compound anymore. The workers said, although the hospital would like to do screening in the factory, the business does not allow them to do so and that's why they stop accepting the workers in their hospital.

call_details.description: Client call and express the poor management of business in terms of Covid-19 measure in TG1.

one client from TG1 calls and expresses the poor management of business in terms of Covid-19 measure in TG1.

Not receiving proper quarantine in terms of having Closed contact person with positive cases_
Workers, who have a closed contact person with positive cases, are asked to do a medical check and wait for three days and if there is no severe symptom shown, they are asked to go back to work. But as the hospital does Covid-19 test only to those with severe symptoms, they are not able to take the test and still have to work.

Limitation of medical Check up facility in hospital _
Business does not have any arrangement of medical check up for the workers in the factory. They only asked the workers with severe symptoms to go and have a check at the hospital and bring a medical certificate provided from the doctor so that they can take sick leave. But, when the workers arrive at the hospital, they have to take queue no. and some are rescheduled to do the test in two or three days later. Although they have a high temperature, running nose and sneezing or cough, they are only provided with medicine.
(For those who have close contact with a positive case, before they were able to take the test at hospital. But now as the number of positive cases are increasing day by day, they are not allowed to enter the hospital because they did not meet with the doctor and cannot get a medical certificate. So they still need to continue to work now.)

Discrimination within Nationality _
The client mentioned that Thai workers, who has closed contact with positive cases, are able to take 14 days quarantine. The Burmese workers also would like to get this opportunity too. But now, they still have to work until severe symptoms show up. Even the time the symptom shows, they are not able to get the test right away.

Because of the limitation from hospitals at this time, workers would like to take proper management of quarentine process as guided by Department of Disease Control or they want the business to shut down for a while as they have some difficulties accessing health care. As most of them stay together with family members who work in other factories and some have infants and kids.
call_details.next_steps: Have to alert ILM team

call_details.description:
Client updated that the business yesterday told them that they will do Covid-19 test today. But, when they arrived at the factory today, the business tested only 20 Burmese workers and 65 Thai workers. There are a lot of suspected workers who are sick and didn't receive the medical care as the hospital didn't allow them to come to do  a check anymore. So they are just staying at home. For this, the supervisors told them that you can take a rest or take medicine, but if you cannot provide a medical certificate, you might not get the wage for that.
The business didn't provide any support on how the suspected workers should access medical care.

Not Receiving medical care and screening and proper quarantine_ In TG1, there are a lot of workers who cannot smell, taste, and feel sick. They go to SSO hospital and the hospital reschedules them after 3 or 4 days or some even are not allowed to meet the medical and just go back to their room. Some workers received medical care while some are not as they do not meet the medical staff. In some lines, the supervisor agreed to provide them sick leave while some supervisor told the workers that you will not get paid if you cannot present a medical certificate. So some workers still have to come to work although they used to stay with positive cases. They are not being screened properly and separated for quarantine. They said most Thai workers received quarantine but not 100% too.
 
The business took a Covid-19 test yesterday, but it did not cover 100% of the workers. They tested only 86 workers out of around 18,00 workers. They just tested randomly and where some workers with severe symptoms still left.
For the one with severe symptoms, they took medicine by themselves by asking for the picture of medicine from those who are in hospital and sending them the photo. So try to go and buy themselves.

This morning, one lady called and reported that she felt difficulty breathing and high temperature. But, she hasn't done the test yet and the hospital  rescheduled her to 6 Jul. As she is not quite comfortable sharing her ID, she will try to go and get medical care at an outside clinic first. If it is not resolved, she will call us again.
call_details.next_steps: Have to alert ILM team

call_details.description:
Client reported that the business did 100% of the tests for all the workers today. Those positive with symptoms will be taken to the government quarantine center while those positive with no symptoms will be quarantined on-site in a separate zone. The business is preparing the room in the factory premise near the Canteen and they ordered the workers to bring the utensil and there are fourteen items. These workers will be the ones with positive results with mild or no symptoms and the business will pick up them by Tuesday.The 14 items they have to bring are
1. Passport
2. Pillow, Blanket, Mat
3. Medicine (That they used to take)
4. Fan
5. Plate, spoon, cup
6. Tooth brush, Tooth paste, Shower Cream, Shampoo
7. Sanitary Pad (For Woman)
8. Detergent
9. Tissue (Enough for 14 days)
10. Mask (Enough for 14 days)
11. Clothes (Enough for 14 days) with clothes hanger
12. Phone, Charger, Power Bank
13. Extension Plug (In case if you need)
14. Mosquito Repellent 

The client also showed a picture of a quarantine site prepared by the business.  There are no facilities there except a far in a room with two layer beds for 12 persons. There is no bed and sheet. Most of the rooms are not well ventilated and the workers are worried it will increase the spread of the virus. There are also some rooms with beds but they think it must be for Thai workers only. They would like to request if the business can provide equal treatment or service to every worker regardless of nationality or if they cannot provide, if they can let them just by home quarantine. They feel a bit bundled to bring all this equipment. They would like to know if the rooms will be discriminately provided to the nationalities or if they can have some workers just by home quarantined if they are not sharing the room with any of their friends or family members.
call_details.next_steps: Have to check the business arrangement and how will they contribute it to the workers

call_details.description:
The workers from TG1 reported that they would like to complain about the following. They heard from other factories that most workers just bring their own clothes and they don't need to bring a list of things like that.
1. Fan, mat, extension charger (Most workers share it with their family members and they find it a bit bundled to buy those)
2. The business asked them to buy mosquito repellent and they have to apply it for 14 days. Basically using mosquito repellent for long term like that is not hygienic and not good for the skin. As the rooms they prepared are in a poorly ventilated area where there are a lot of mosquitoes. So they might need to buy a MOSQUITO NET as well. Although it was not listed.
3. The business also asks them to bring the medicine they used to take and the workers assume that the business will not provide any medicine too. For that case, I have explained to them that it must be just in case  the nurse or doctor would like to trace the patient records. But it would be great if we can clarify with the business.
Because of the poor services from the business, the workers would like to ask if it is possible the business can just allow them to have home quarantine in their room as they have the issue? The workers also added that a list of things (14 items) they have to organize is like they are starting a new life.
As we also have the same issue like Cal-Comp, but the workers have no need to bring fans or other things apart from their clothes. And the workers heard the situation from other businesses where workers do not need to bring much about things like that when they have to go to QC, they would like to complain about this. They would like to know if we can have a discussion with business.
call_details.next_steps: Have to report to ILM Management Team

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers have been informed since a month ago that they can no longer bring their own food and curries to the canteen due to the renovation of the lunch box shelves. Workers have to buy food from five vendors in the factory but some have found the curries they bought has gone bad when buying it in the afternoon to eat during the evening break before their OT starts.

TPs:
- Is the business aware that workers are being negatively affected by this ongoing renovation?
- What are the operating hours of the food vendors? Is food available for sale when workers need to buy food?
- How does the business monitor the quality and cleanliness of the food being sold by vendors in the factory canteen?

Recommendations:
- Investigate the quality of the food being sold by the vendors, as workers have noted that some food they have bought was spoiled and couldn't be eaten
- Ensure that the operating hours of the food vendors matches the times when workers would like to buy food, such as in the evening before starting their OT work 
- Communicate to workers how the food being sold by vendors is being monitored to ensure its quality and cleanliness, and the operating hours of the vendors during which time workers will be able to buy food
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 6 Nov 2023

They explained why workers no longer bring their own food and curries to the canteen.
1. There is currently insufficient space for the workers' food containers.
2. The canteen is undergoing renovations.
3. GFPT is a company that produces human food, so they are on the food standard industry to ensure that the outside food that comes to the factory is safe and does not harm the manufacturing process.

So they will investigate the quality of the food being sold by the vendors and ensure that the operating hours of the food vendors match the times when workers would like to buy food they will communicate to workers how the food being sold by vendors is being monitored to ensure its quality and cleanliness. They will send the corrective action by the end of next week.

DATE: 16 Nov 2023

They will have a meeting with the food vendors on November 27th to make sure the food provided for the workers is good quality. They will share with us with the result after the meeting.

DATE: 5 Jan 2024

Root Cause:
Normally, every food vendor must be trained as a restaurant operator, and the factory has food quality regulations such as always warming and heating food. However, it is possible that the employee discovered that the food was not fresh on the day in question. The vendor may not have verified food quality or was unaware of restaurant operator standards.

Corrective Action:
On 10 December 2023, Human Resources investigated the complaint by conducting a survey of the food vendor at the time of the complaint. Informed the vendors of the problem and made improvements. HR inspects the food at least once a week to ensure that it is of high quality. Regularly, HR evaluates the vendors. If it is discovered that it does not meet the requirements. The contract will be canceled by the company.
remediation_notes: Workers have been informed since a month ago that they can no longer bring their own food and curries to the canteen due to renovations. Workers have to buy food from five vendors in the factory but some have found the curries they bought has gone bad when buying it in the afternoon to eat during the evening break before their OT starts.
remediation_action:
HR will have a meeting with the food vendors on November 27, 2023, to make sure the food provided for the workers is good quality. They will share with us with the result after the meeting.

HR investigated on December 10, 2023 by conducting a survey of the food vendors and informed them about the problem. HR now inspects the food at least once a week to ensure that it is of high quality. HR will evaluate the vendors and if it is discovered that it does not meet the quality requirements, the company will discontinue the contract with the vendor.
remediation_validation: Workers updated Issara that the quality of the food served in the canteen has improved, and there are enough food vendors for the workers.
remediation_results: Issara is closing the issue. The workers confirmed that the food quality has improved.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Have a monitoring system in place so that any food provided / sold to workers is of good quality

remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara has shared this issue with the business, the business responded that they have conducted the investigation and assessment, however, the result of the investigation did not identify the issues. 

Issara has checked with the workers, the workers did not agree with the business response. They said that they still have the issue with the insufficient lunch for the last batch of workers.

The Managing Director noted that the business provides rice for free to all workers, and makes sure there is enough for all workers across the three lunch break hours.  For the food that is sold in the canteen, however, she noted that workers are free to buy the food here or with vendors just outside the factory and indeed most workers (90%) buy food from outside or bring their own from home.  She said the food vendors that sell in the canteen also need to make it profitable enough to stay in business and having a lot of leftover food during the last lunch hour will lead to financial losses so the vendors make their own judgments on the quantity of food made available for sale.

For the food that is sold in the canteen, however, she noted that workers are free to buy the food here or with vendors just outside the factory and indeed most workers (90%) buy food from outside or bring their own from home.  She said the food vendors that sell in the canteen also need to make it profitable enough to stay in business and having a lot of leftover food during the last lunch hour will lead to financial losses so the vendors make their own judgments on the quantity of food made available for sale.
remediation_validation:
Issara has checked with the workers, and the workers did not agree with the business response. They said that they still have the issue with the insufficient lunch for the last batch of workers.

Issara followed up with the workers and explained to them that the company has the following arrangement for the food made available in the canteen: 1) The company is ensuring there is sufficient free rice to all workers; 2) the food vendors that are selling food in the canteen are not required to guarantee sufficient food for sale is available for all lunch shifts because the vendors will make a certain quantity so that there isn't a lot of leftover food at the end of the lunch period; 3) there are many food vendors just outside the factory gates which workers can buy food from as additional options. Workers now understand the company arrangement and that there are many options to buy food both inside and outside the canteen.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case because the company has clarified the arrangement of food in the canteen, that the company will ensure there is sufficient free rice for all workers, but food that is sold by the vendors in the canteen may be a fixed quantity based on the discretion of the vendor, and that workers have many options from where they can buy food both inside and outside the canteen.

description: Lack of professional conduct of recruitment agency and/or employer

call_details.description:
One client from Hong Seng called and reported that she was caught by the police because her work permit had expired and was not being extended.

The client work permit and visa has expired since 22 Feb 2021. She passed both her passport and work permit to HR for extension from 29 Dec 2020. In 29 Apr, the HR returned her visa and work permit and told her that only the visa has been extended and the work permit hasn't been extended yet. Once the government allows a work permit extension, they will let her know.

On 22 Mar, the HR told her that the work permit can be extended now so that she can pass the work permit and the fee.  So she passed her work permit on 23 May 2021, together with the fee. On 19 Jun, as the workers had to do Covid-19 test, she went to the HR office and got her work permit book. She thought it was already extended. But, when she came back from the hospital, she checked that the work permit hadn't been extended yet. He planned to give back her passport on 22 Jun, the day she had to go back to work. But, before she was able to return the passport on that day, the police checked in the factory and found her with the invalid work permit. She was taken to the detention center, (she doesn't know the place exactly) followed by one staff from the business and Burmese translator. In the center, she was asked to sign a document (She doesn't know what it is about), and then the staff from the business paid 5,000 THB to the police. Then she was told that she might need to stay there for 3 days and she can go home after that. After three days, she was taken to the Immigration center, where she was told that she will be deported to Myanmar once the government officially opened the border. Then she was sent back to the detention center again.

So she has been detained in the detention center since 22 Jun until now. The business sends three meals per day from Mon-Sat. For Sunday, her sister came and sent her the meal.

She has contacted with the Burmese translator and the translator told her that the only way they can do is to wait until the border officially opens and then she can go back to Myanmar. 

The business did not assure the workers whether they will still rehired her back again or help her to come back with new documents or not. And then what kind of compensation they will give to the workers if they cannot hire her anymore. Or if they will pay anything if she has to go back. 

Besides, she expected the business should coordinate with Immigration as the issue is not caused by her mistake. It's because of the business fault.

call_details.description:
One client from Hong Seng called and reported that she was caught by the police because her work permit had expired and was not being extended.

The client work permit and visa has expired since 22 Feb 2021. She passed both her passport and work permit to HR for extension from 29 Dec 2020. In 29 Apr, the HR returned her visa and work permit and told her that only the visa has been extended and the work permit hasn't been extended yet. Once the government allows a work permit extension, they will let her know.

On 22 Mar, the HR told her that the work permit can be extended now so that she can pass the work permit and the fee.  So she passed her work permit on 23 May 2021, together with the fee. On 19 Jun, as the workers had to do Covid-19 test, she went to the HR office and got her work permit book. She thought it was already extended. But, when she came back from the hospital, she checked that the work permit hadn't been extended yet. He planned to give back her passport on 22 Jun, the day she had to go back to work. But, before she was able to return the passport on that day, the police checked in the factory and found her with the invalid work permit. She was taken to the detention center, (she doesn't know the place exactly) followed by one staff from the business and Burmese translator. In the center, she was asked to sign a document (She doesn't know what it is about), and then the staff from the business paid 5,000 THB to the police. Then she was told that she might need to stay there for 3 days and she can go home after that. After three days, she was taken to the Immigration center, where she was told that she will be deported to Myanmar once the government officially opened the border. Then she was sent back to the detention center again.

So she has been detained in the detention center since 22 Jun until now. The business sends three meals per day from Mon-Sat. For Sunday, her sister came and sent her the meal.

She has contacted with the Burmese translator and the translator told her that the only way they can do is to wait until the border officially opens and then she can go back to Myanmar. 

The business did not assure the workers whether they will still rehired her back again or help her to come back with new documents or not. And then what kind of compensation they will give to the workers if they cannot hire her anymore. Or if they will pay anything if she has to go back. 

Besides, she expected the business should coordinate with Immigration as the issue is not caused by her mistake. It's because of the business fault.

And she would like to be free from the detention center as soon as possible.

-Workers reported to Issara that their visas are not being extended on time and now the workers are working with invalid visas. What is the business understanding on this issue? 
-How many workers are there in this situation?
-What is the process for this group of workers? 
- What is the company’s plan to prevent workers from having issues with the local police for not having valid visas? And what kind of support would they provide in case it actually happened? 

Recommendations

-The business shall have a communication session with the workers and explain in detail how the process is being handled, by whom, timeframes and an explanation of why their documents have not been extended, and how would the company respond in case there are any penalties imposed by the immigration office. 
-The communication should also include information on how the company would protect workers from having any issues with the local police for not having valid documents.
-In ethical recruitment practices, it is the employer's responsibility to make sure all workers' documents are up to date and workers receive clear information about the process.

remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 13 Dec 2023
Sopida, BFI's HR manager, explained that for the payment system working day, all workers who work from the first to the fifteenth of the month will receive their wages, attendant allowance, and incentive on the 25th of the month. According to company policy, workers who have an MoU contract until the 25th of December will receive the bonus proportionately. In this case, the worker's contract expires on December 16, 2023; however, the workers were required to return for an MoU U-Turn on December 13, 2023. So, when the workers return, they are given new contracts, begin a new year of work, and receive a full-year bonus the following year. According to the policy, because the workers returned to Cambodia on December 13th, they must work until December 15th to receive the attendant allowance. However, the worker will still receive the performance incentive on December 15th.  They will then communicate with the workers again about this policy when they return on December 19, 2023.

DATE: 5 Jan 2024

K. Sopida, HR manager confirmed that they communicated the policy on 16 December 2023
remediation_notes: Workers reported that those that needed to return to their home countries to process the MOU U-turn process were scheduled to return before the MOU contract expiry date and before payday and they think the business did this to not have to pay for certain incentives and bonuses that they would have received if they had been allowed to work until the MOU expiry date.
remediation_action: HR explained that all workers who work from the first to the fifteenth of the month will receive their wages and attendance allowance. According to company policy, workers who have an MoU contract until the 25 December 2023 will receive the bonus proportionately. In this case, the worker's contract expired on 16 December 2023 and they were required to return for the MoU U-turn process on 13 December 2023. Therefore, they will not receive the attendance allowance but will still receive the performance incentive. HR communicated this again to the workers.
remediation_validation: The worker confirmed that the manager had clarified this with them, and they now understand that although they will not receive the attendance allowance, they will still receive their performance incentive.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case. The workers confirmed they now understand how the company calculated their allowances and incentives.

description: Issues with regular shift hours or other shift issues: dispute without violation of law or employment contract

call_details.next_steps: BHR to reach out to the business.

closed_notes: Issara had a meeting with the business. The business agreed to conduct the investigation by interviewing several workers for consideration for workers' requests. A few days later, the business informed Issara that they had decided to move the OT hours from before the normal hours to the end of the shift as requested by workers. Issara checked with the workers and workers confirmed the changes made by the business following their request.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Workers who work for the night shift start at 4:30 PM, and they would like to request the business to change the starting time of this shift to 6:30 PM so that the workers can have enough sleep and feel rested, especially during the COVID-19 outbreak. 

Talking Points; 
-Workers would like to request the business to adjust the starting time of the night shift during this period of the COVID outbreak since they would like to be able to have good rest, have time to have proper meals, and be strong. 


-Workers have explained that the starting time of the shift is not good timing for them to have enough sleep as they are starting to work at 4:30 pm which means that they have to wake up around 2 pm to be ready for work and they also can not sleep well in the morning until their roommate (partner) go out for work as they share a small room. 
-Workers also have shared that many workers are being tested positive for COVID-19 which scares them a lot, so they want to be able to have a good rest and be strong. 
-Workers also added that this request is only during the COVID-19 outbreak and that the working hours can return to normal after the COVID-19 cases drop and the situation is controlled. 
-Workers have also added that they could refuse to start working at 4:30 but it impacts their OT working hours (do not get OT if they start to work at 6:30), so they wouldn’t want to lose the chance to work OT hours,  and it is also complicated for the workers to select any shift they want (in case they wanted to change the shift). 
-Given the workers' concern, Issara would suggest the business consider workers’ requests during this (COVID-19) outbreak time and have a dialogue with workers to come to an agreement.
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had a meeting with the business, the business agreed to conduct the investigation by interviewing several workers for consideration of theirs request. A few days later, the business has updated removing OT hours before normal hours start which was the worker's request. Issara checked with the workers, workers confirmed the improved situation which aligns with the business response.
remediation_notes: The issue with workers on the night shift having to start work at 4:30pm, which is too early for them and they would like to request the business to change the starting time of this shift to 6:30pm so that the workers can have enough sleep and feel rested, especially during the COVID-19 outbreak.
remediation_action: The business explained that the night shift was from 6.30 pm - 4.30 am and that the 4:30pm to 6:30pm period was considered OT and so workers could choose to accept or refuse work during this time.  In case of the workers' concerns, HR will survey the workers, consider workers' requests, and come to an agreement. After conducting the survey, the business decided to change the OT schedule as requested by workers.
remediation_validation: Issara checked with the workers and workers confirmed the changes made by the business following their request.
remediation_results: Workers are satisfied with the business actions.

The informant guessed it may be the neighboring negative resulted workers or the landlord who must reported this to the translator or business HR. But, the informants said, it is not the right way. Having poor ventilation can increase the spread of the virus and at the time, they have to wait like a week to get the medical care from the hospital. 

They tried to close their door when the negative workers were back from work. But, after they arrive in their room, they can close their door if they are afraid of the positive workers. The workers requested that if the business can manage this situation, it would be good. Currently, the workers just only depend on outside donors or their friends to bring or help them with water, food or everything. description: Unresponsive grievance mechanism / no action being taken
closed_notes:
Issara raised this issue with the business, the business conducted the investigation and took action. It is reported that the actions taken by the business included a verbal warning and training for the relevant supervisor. After the training, the business conducted an evaluation to assess the improvement of the behavior of supervisors, and it was found that the behaviour had improved. 

Issara checked with the workers, and workers first reported being approached by a supervisor who expressed to workers being emotional about them reporting her behaviour to Issara. Following this event, workers reported to HR feeling uncomfortable with the attitude of the supervisor, so HR reported the incident to the manager. As a consequence, the manager communicated back to the supervisor, who talked with the supervisor. After all the actions taken by the business, workers confirmed that their working environment has improved and they thanked Issara Institute for supporting them.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with three supervisors ( 2 assistant and 1 senior, ลำใย  LB2 and เรณู  LB4 blue cap and เพียงพอ จัยจัย with green cap) being abusive with the workers. A group of workers has reported being constantly and verbally abusive with aggressive behavior and rude words by the supervisors. 

Talking Points. 
-Workers reported to Issara that they have reported the issues they are facing with these two assistant supervisors to the senior supervisor but there has been no improvement in these supervisors’ behavior. What is the role of the senior supervisors if some workers report such issues? Is the senior supervisor responsible to report workers' grievances to HR, or how should they handle such cases?
-For the past few years, workers’ grievances have been well handled by SEAPAC, and Issara noticed the improvement throughout those years, so we would like to know what has been the process in the past and if anything has changed in the grievance mechanisms processes from the company.  
-Does the company have any systems or processes to assess workers' experiences at the workplace, such as surveys or open talks? 
-Are there any activities or any training that the business has not been able to conduct recently which might have led supervisors to behave poorly? 
-Is HR aware of this issue? And if so, how is it being handled? 

Recommendations
-The business shall conduct an immediate investigation about the three reported supervisors. 
-The investigation should make sure safeguards for the workers are in place and that there would be no risk of retaliation. The investigation should be confidential, meaning that workers’ identities should not be exposed in order to mitigate the risks of being targeted. 
-The business shall take disciplinary action based on the business policy and the investigation results. 
-Workers should be treated humanely and this should be followed by all company staff. 


Time Frame - 2 weeks.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; Workers who are requested to quarantine at home due to being in close contact with a Covid-positive person who is not an LB worker will not get paid for those days.


Talking Points; 
Workers have reported not receiving their daily wages if they have to take quarantine for being in close contact with their family members who are not the workers of Ladybird, what is the business policy in this case? 
How many workers are in this situation and what has been the process for them so far? 
How many days of quarantine are required for close contact cases? Who pays for those quarantine days? 
Has the business checked the government regulations on what Covid-related care services are to be covered by SSO and whether and how quarantine days for Covid close contacts are to be paid?  

Recommendations:
-The business should confirm the latest government regulations related to quarantine periods for Covid close contacts and how pay for missed working days due to quarantine is to be handled
We have received the update that the government regulations are as follows:  
-If a worker is found to be positive at the factory, she/he is supposed to be sent to the hospital for the PCR test and if confirmed as positive, receive the medical certificate and recommended to quarantine. The worker should get paid sick leave during those days. 
-If a worker is a close contact, s/he should visit the hospital and report why she/he is at high risk and get the recommendations from the hospital. The regular recommendations for vaccinated people is to take 10 days of quarantine and do another test on the 10th day. -If the result is negative, then the worker can start working. In terms of the wages for the high risk workers who have a medical certificate for their quarantine days, the employer can submit the worker information to the SSF for the 50% of wages. 
-If the worker is not allowed to go to the hospital but the employer orders the worker to take quarantine, it is the responsibility of the employer to pay the worker wages. 
The business should communicate with the workers about how quarantine days for close contacts will be paid.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have a policy where workers have to practice social distancing at any time including in their home. The business added that they assigned the suspected workers to take 5 days of quarantine without pay because they get to close contact which is against the business policy. Issara has provided the recommendations, the business agreed to have an internal meeting with the management and get back to Issara.
After the investigation, the business has revised the policy and created a separate work area for the high risks workers to work for 5 days. They will then be ATK tested again, and if the results remain negative, they will be able to return to the normal production line. This new policy was announced last week and will be implemented this week.
remediation_notes: Workers who were requested to quarantine at home due to being in close contact with a Covid-positive person who is not a LB worker were not paid for those days.
remediation_action:
Issara raised this issue with the business, and the business responded that they have the policy where workers have to practice social distancing at any time including in their homes. The business added that they assigned suspected workers to take 5 days of quarantine without pay because they had not practiced social distancing as per business policy.

After the investigation, the business has revised the policy and created a separate work area for the high risks workers to work for 5 days. They will then be ATK tested again, and if the results remain negative, they will be able to return to the normal production line.

For workers that had already self quarantined and had not been paid for those days, the business checked to see if it could help the workers apply for Social Security compensation at 50% of wages; however, medical certificates couldn't be obtained for these past cases and so couldn't get this compensation for the workers.
remediation_validation: Issara updated the workers that for the quarantine days for Covid high-risk persons, the business had revised the policy to provide a separate work space for such workers.  Issara also updated the workers that Social Security compensation for wages lost could be applied for such quarantine days but because the medical certificate for past cases cannot be issued, they would not be able to apply for compensation at this time.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case because the business made changes to their policy to minimize the need for quarantine and wages lost for Covid high risk workers and tried to help the Covid high risk workers get Social Security compensation for their quarantine days.

closed_notes:

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the worker's concern regarding the lack of medical staff in the quarantine center arranged by the business. Workers reported having asked to do the medical process (COVID test, taking oxygen level, fever, and so on)  by themselves and having asked to show the result with the assigned production staff. 

Recommendations:
-The business shall make sure that all of the staff who are closely working with the infected workers are fully equipped. 
-The business shall clearly communicate with the workers about the process of COVID cases management in the factory QC. The communication should include the following information:  
What the communication has been between the government and the factory regarding the case management and why the production staff is assigned to perform this task. 
How those from productions that are monitoring workers health have been trained to do this task 
Information about the focal person to contact in workers language in case of emergency. 
The business attempt to get medical professionals (If any) 


Talking Points:

-How are the production staff being selected to perform these tasks? Have they received any training? 
-What has been the communication from the government? Has the business tried to find professional medical staff from the government or any hospital (even any online consultation)? 
-Are the production staff who are performing as medical staff fully equipped with the PPE? 
-What is the process for workers to follow in case of an emergency? Has these guidelines and procedures been communicated with the workers? 
-How many workers have been tested Positive for COVID-19 so far? 
- How has the business managed the infected and noninfected workers? Are all workers being quarantined in the business QC? 
Time Frame 1 week.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Business Response ID - 1376
The business responded that the quarantine centers in both Nan Yang Factory 1 & 3 arranged by the company are controlled by the Public Health Province. All the Covid tests are under the supervision of nurses. It is added that the workers have been trained to do all of these tests. However, the business added that all of the workers have been cured and free from the quarantine. There are no workers being quarantining in the business's on-site QC. Therefore, the business did not need to take any action. Issara has checked with the workers and workers have confirmed not having such concerns.
remediation_notes: The issue with the worker's concern regarding the lack of medical staff in the quarantine center arranged by the business. Workers reported having to administer their own COVID-19 tests, measure oxygen levels, measure body temperature, etc.
remediation_action: The business responded that the quarantine centers arranged by the company are managed by the provincial Public Health Office. All the Covid tests are under the supervision of nurses, and even when some workers did the tests themselves, they were first trained by the nurses. Now, all workers that were in the quarantine centers have recovered and left those centers.
remediation_validation: Workers have already recovered so they left the quarantine center. Therefore, they are not experiencing any issues or concerns related to the management of the quarantine center anymore.
remediation_results: No additional issues have been reported since the workers recovered.

call_details.description: The client reported     issues from SCC. According to the client, SCC asked all Myanmar workers ( who is not in quarantine ) to come and work in packaging building from July 5 to August 5th. SCC promised them to paid double for normal working hours and double OT wages for OT working. However on 20th july payroll, most of the workers didn't get the wages what they suppose to get. So the workers ask the pay slip but SCC didn't provide payslip. In this situation, SCC promise the workers they will give remaining balance ( wages ) in 5th August payroll. Once again when the workers get August 5th payroll,  they amount they got was not the amount they should get. SCC provided payslip of August 5th to some workers but  the payslip format has changed ( not written in Burmese). As a result , the workers can't identify if the missing amount of July 20th  has added they were paid correctly as SCC promised. Until now nearly 150-200 workers haven't got payslip for both July 20th & August 5th
call_details.source_recruiter_name: International Focus General Services Co., Ltd

call_details.description: Myint Myint Zar is an active worker of SCC and she is a GD ambassadors as well. She reported that there was an issue with missing payment for July 20th and August 5th pay roll in SCC . The workers haven't got payslip for 20th July payroll and only some people got payslip of 5th August ( payslip in changed format ). As a result the workers only know their wages were not what they really supposed to get but they can't identify what was wrong with this. So the workers want missing payment on time and they would like payslip in clear format with native language. Myint Myint Zar added water in PT housing is not clean enough even to use in cooking. Furthermore the owner of PT is unnecessarily strict workers to get food and water from out-source seller. He open shop in the compound but what he selling is not what workers want.
call_details.source_recruiter_name: International Focus General Services Co., Ltd

call_details.description: This call is to GD ambassador from SCC to know the progress of the issues happening in SCC. Myint Myint Zar reported that there are 45% of Myanmar workers who haven't received the missing payment of July 20th payroll, 5th August payroll until they got August 20th payroll. In terms of payslip, there are only handful of people who got Burmese translated version. Since workers received 20th July payroll, they found missing payment and ask supervisors ( red-cap, green-cap) but no one solved it properly. People approached HR in individual or group and got promise that workers will get missing payment in 5th August payroll. Once again, the workers didn't get the missing payment of July 20th  in their August 5th payroll. So some of the workers gather near the office and claim the missing payment on August 13th. The management regard this act as mini strike and decide all the workers who claim to sign warning letter, to reduce OT working opportunities. Since that time workers start afraid to claim missing payment and they just wait their missing payment in August 20th payroll. Unfortunately, 45% of Myanmar haven't received missing payment even in  August 20th payroll. So they asked helps from Issara.  In this call, Issara informed the ambassador about white card holder who can helps workers in shopping. The ambassador reported that water problem is PT has solved .

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context:  The issue with the payslip. Workers reported not receiving payslips for their recent month's payments. however, some of them who have received the payslip reported that the format of the payslip was changed and it is not in their language so it is difficult to understand their wages correctly. 

Recommendation:

Added Recommendation:
_The business shall provide the payslip to the workers as soon as possible, in a format and language workers can understand easily. The payslip should include clear information about the wages, incentives, and deductions.

-The HR team shall work with the finance team to make sure workers are paid correctly. And the timeframe to proceed with the payment should be communicated to workers.

-Have there been any changes with the payslip recently? 
-Have there been any communication with the workers about the changes to the payslip?

remediation_action:

However, HR was trying its best to print the payslip and distribute it to the workers within a few days.

The business added that they have created a new temporary system to solve this issue, which will allow workers to clock-in and clock-out without requiring face scanning like in the past. The business responded that this system is meant as a temporary solution and workers will be able to receive their pay slips in their language.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue #1. 
Context: The issue with the recruitment fees being charged by the recruitment agency representative who is stationed outside of the Cal-Comp factory area. The person who collects the money is being known as a huanna-sub (sub-supervisor in English). The worker reported that they have contacted a person whose name was included in a job announcement to work at Cal-comp. After contacting the phone number from the announcement, the worker was asked to contact another person, a huanna-sub (sub-supervisor in English) who told the worker that she has to pay 2,500 THB for the job application.  

The worker did not mention the channel through which the announcement about the job vacancy was done nor the name of the huanna-sub who asked her to pay. In addition to that, the worker added that one of her friends was charged 3500 THB to get a job in Cal-Comp in the past. NOTE: So far, Issara knows about 2 workers being impacted however there could be many more. 

Recommendations for remediation: 
-The business to do an immediate investigation to assess the number of impacted workers and identify the people involved in the recruitment process that has been charging workers. Safeguards should be in place throughout the investigation, and workers should not be targeted by the sub-supervisor or recruitment agency representative. 
-The investigation should also cover the staff from the recruitment agencies to identify the root causes of the issue and understand who was involved in the collection of the money.
- Actions should be taken towards those who collected the money, and the business should clarify with the recruitment agency that no fees should be charged to workers and what are the consequences for not following that policy, such as termination of the contract or disciplinary actions if those involved are Cal-Comp employees. 
-As part of the investigation and remediation process, the business shall assess how much money new workers have paid and reimburse them those recruitment fees. 

-The business should set a plan of action with the recruitment agency involved, such as revision of the contract and the penalties for not following the company policy about “zero recruitment fees for workers”, and the actions the agency will take to avoid this from happening again. 

-The business should cross-check through different means with the recruitment agency and workers being recruited, how are the services being provided to job seekers, what is the communication like about the job and the recruitment process, etc. 
-One way of conducting the investigation and a vetting process is for Cal-comp to check all the announcements about job vacancies and verify that there are no fees being charged, that the process is handled legally and ethically, and that all the recruitment agencies are used to work professionally. 

Past history of this case:

Last year (2020) there was a similar case reported and the business conducted investigations for all issues and remediated the impacted workers which is considered a good step made by the company to address issues with recruitment. However, the process took several months and the business did not share with Issara the details of the last investigation conducted regarding walk-in workers being asked to make monetary donations to the Thai RA staff, and only one worker received compensation for that issue. In addition, the company did not follow Issara's recommendation on system change to have communication sessions with all workers and Thai RAs about the company policy of recruitment fees.

Timeframe 1 pay period
remediation_business_steps_taken:
-Issara raised this issue with the business, the business agreed to conduct a vetting process to find out about the announcement that had been made and workers being charged and then get back to Issara.
-The business responded that they have been investigating to find out the person who collected the money from the workers and they have some suspected person for further investigation. It is added that once the business competes for the investigation process, the impacted workers will be reimbursed. 
-The business updated that they have conducted the survey with the newcomer in the past last month but did not find any issue from the survey. The business also reported conducting the survey with the workers who were recruited in August, however, only one worker was found being impacted.

Issara raised this issue with K Narisa (HP focal). She responded that she is aware that the factory is understaffed, however, she will try her best to push the business to work on this issue by the 15th of November.
-The business updated that they have interviewed 171 workers who were recently recruited and found workers being charged 5000-53000 THB by the recruitment agency Number 17. The HP suggested the business conduct interviews with 100% of workers and conduct the reimbursement within December.


Issara had another escalation call with the business, the business responded that they have investigated the original case and repaid the worker.  CC is in the process of interviewing all workers hired since August 2021, 470 total workers of which 210 were hired for production supplying HP.  This is expected to be completed in January 2022 and workers reimbursed.  CC noted there is an issue with hiring of walk-in workers.  Recruitment agencies are using sub-agents.  CC has taken the following actions: they trained the 13 RAs on zero fees, helped them review the job advertisements, and set up the policies/procedures for compliance and RAs not in compliance will be penalized in a 3-step process.  First time, CC will decrease demand of workers from the RA; second time, CC will decrease the demand further, and third time, CC will cancel the service agreement with the RA.

Apart from that, the HP focal, K Narisa suggested Issara to conduct the recruitment fee survey with the worker. Issara will have follow up discussion with the HP and conduct the survey.


K. Piyabutr, CSR, inquired about the completion of the finding report after Issara interviewed the workers.
remediation_notes:
Case #1: 
Two workers reported seeing a job advert for jobs at Cal-Comp and contacted the broker about getting a job as a walk-in worker. The broker told the workers to contact one of the "wanna-said", a representative of the recruitment agency, based in the factory about getting a job. One worker was asked for a payment of 2,500 Baht and the other was asked to pay 3,500 Baht to be able to get a job.

Case #2:
A recruiter was advertising jobs for the business via facebook livestream, offering to take workers from all over Thailand and offering rewards of up to 5,000 Baht to any recruiters that could bring / refer 20 workers to them.
remediation_action:
The business said that they outsource hiring to 7 recruitment agencies, and would investigate this matter. It is noteworthy that last year (2020) there was a similar case reported and the business conducted investigations, eventually partially remediating impacted workers, which was considered a good step made by the company to address issues with recruitment. However, the process took several months and the business did not share/collaborate with Issara regarding addressing root causes, to avoid the same issues from arising in the future (as they are now) - for example addressing corrupt supervisors conducting exploitative recruitment, or conducting communication sessions with all workers and supervisors about the company's ethical recruitment policy and prohibition of informal brokering with recruitment fees.

The business is in the process of investigation and have identified certain suspected persons that may have charged recruitment fees from the workers. 
Once the business competes the investigation, impacted workers will be reimbursed.  The business surveyed new employees that joined in August 2021 but found only 1 worker had paid recruitment fees. 

The Strategic Partner (SP) has requested that Issara conduct a recruitment fee survey on behalf of the business to verify recruitment fees paid.  The SP is in the process of securing agreement on the part of the business to move forward with this.
remediation_validation:
The business is in the process of investigation; there have been no actions or improvements yet that have been verified by workers.  

These issues have been discussed additionally with the Strategic Partner, who has been working with CalComp on escalating issues and CalComp developing a more responsible recruitment process and implementation.  However, issues with current in-country recruitment practices continue to be uncovered, with concerning behavior by Thai recruitment agencies engaged by CalComp and fees being reported by workers.  There is a need to both immediately investigate and repay fees charged to workers in this recruitment, but also develop a more comprehensive plan to address structural issues and resources dedicated to worker recruitment - moving beyond internal company investigations and audits of contracted agencies.  This is particularly pressing given continuing worker reports, continued worker recruitment, and planning for working with Myanmar recruitment agencies for the potential reopening of cross border recruitment.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case.  Issara has conducted the recruitment fee survey to determine the recruitment fees paid by this group of walk-in workers.  The survey results have been shared with the Strategic Partner and with the business.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for system change

-The business is encouraged to use the Golden Dreams Job Marketplace to have a more direct recruitment process and avoid these kinds of risks of fees being charged to job seekers. It is a high risk for the company who will ultimately be responsible for any fees being charged against the company policy and the buyer code of conduct. 
-The business is also encouraged to promote Golden Dreams Marketplace in their social media and other channels to let job seekers know that they can directly apply through the app and no at all will be charged. 

-Effective communication in a wide range should be conducted in the written and verbal post including disciplinary action for those who break the business's recruitment policy or do not follow accordingly.

closed_notes: Issara had a meeting with the business, the business responded that they had conducted the investigation and found the root cause that the immigration had a limited number for document extension because of COVID-19 spread which causes workers documents to get delayed for the extensions. However, the business committed to work with the government to make sure that the worker's documents are extended on time without any delay. In addition, the business confirmed the reimbursement for the impacted workers by the second week of October. Issara checked with the workers that have reported issues, workers confirmed being reimbursed. It is added that 115 workers were announced to do the extension during this period.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers whose visas were not extended on time due the government’s policy which caused the delay of 90 days report, having to pay 500 THB as a fine to the immigration officer. The worker reported that one of the staff from the business collected 500 THB from each worker and asked one worker to do the process. The TUF staff did not do the full process, instead, asking a worker to do his job when they arrive at the immigration. 

Recommendation: 
-The business shall conduct an investigation to find out why the workers are being charged 500 THB and also to find out the root cause of why there were delays in the document extension process that then caused the delay on the 90 days report. 
- In addition, the business should investigate why some specific workers are asked to be involved in the document extension process for other workers, and why this process was not fully handled by the company staff
-The business shall find out the number of impacted workers and reimburse all impacted workers who had to pay for the 90 day report fine. 

Talking Points: 
-Workers reported being asked to pay 500 THB for the fine for delaying the 90 days report. What is the business understanding of this? 
-Who is the person responsible for handling these kinds of processes, why was the process delayed, and why are specific workers being asked to do the process on behalf of other workers?
-How many workers have been delayed for their 90 day report so far? 
-What is the business plan to avoid this happening in the future? 
- What is the reason why workers' documents are being delayed for the extension even though they have informed the HR on time?
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara had a meeting with the business, the business responded that they have conducted the investigation and found the root cause which the immigration had a limited number for document extension because of COVID-19 spread which causes workers documents to get delayed for the extensions. However, the business committed that they will continue working with the government to make sure that the worker's documents are extended on time without any delay. In addition that, the business confirmed to reimburse the impacted workers by the second week of October. Issara checked with the workers that have reported issues, workers confirmed being reimbursed. It is added that 115 workers were being announced to do the extension during this period.
remediation_notes: The issue with some workers whose visas have expired since June 2021 but have not been extended by the business even though workers provided their passports and visa extension fees on time to HR staff.  Workers also had to pay a 500 Baht fine for visa extension past the expiration date.
remediation_action:
Issara raised this issue with the business, and the business noted that this delay was due to the government authorities not being able to process the documents amidst the current Covid-19 situation.  The workers' visas are in the process of being extended, and the business has communicated this update to workers.

The business committed to continue working with the government to make sure that the worker's documents are extended on time without any delay. In addition, the business confirmed it will reimburse the impacted workers for the late payment fine (500 Baht) they had to pay.
remediation_validation: Issara checked with 11 workers and they confirmed receiving the reimbursement for the late payment fine (500 Baht) for the visa extension.
remediation_results:
The time to complete the visa extension process is uncertain due to the current COVID outbreak and the delay from government offices. 

Workers have now received the visa extension and were reimbursed for the late payment fee of the visa extension.

According to workers and based on the announcements based by the business regarding document extension during that period, it is calculated that 115 workers were also impacted by this issue. The business did not provide any details to Issara about the number of impacted workers, however, they said that all impacted workers were compensated.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
System change recommendations:
-The business shall make clear verbal and written announcements about the business policy for the document extension process and also the focal person who is assigned to do this job. The communication should include the roles and responsibilities of the focal and it should be clear that the workers should not be asked to handle the documents and fees of other workers. 
-The business shall also communicate the reimbursement plan to the workers.
systems_change_business_steps_taken: The business agreed to work with the government officials to make sure workers' documents are extended on time. However, it was not clear about the process and the approach.

If the workers request Issara to discuss with the business, the issue will be opened under other KPI related to the missing payment. The workers reported that their belongings were taken by the business when they were about to leave in a van and that they now do not have a place to stay since they have already given back their rooms. Workers reported the reason for leaving job is as follows:
(1) discrimination against nationalities at the workplace,
(2) the business not keeping the promise of paying double for the working hours during COVID-19 restriction as promised,
(3) translator not being helpful and being biased by just listening to the business and not the workers. 

Recommendations: 
-As it is a worker's right to resign and leave the company, the business shall immediately investigate why this group of workers were not allowed to leave. And then come to an agreement with workers for their departure from the company without restrictions.
-Since the business made the taxi driver leave without the workers, it will be challenging for workers to find a new driver, therefore, the business is suggested to help workers find a new taxi/van for workers safe return. -Since the vaccination is a workers personal health matter, the business should provide vaccination cards or any support documents as proof that workers have received vaccination. If the business does not have such documents, the business should coordinate with the health organization that provided the vaccine to make sure all workers receive the vaccination card. 
-The business should immediately check with all workers and provide their missing daily wages if any. 


Talking Points: 
-What is the reason why this group of workers were stopped by HR? 
-Is business aware of this issue? 
-Workers have reported several workers leaving the job because of several repeated issues in the workplace, what is the business understanding of this? Does the business seek workers' feedback and have done anything to improve the working condition rather than stopping workers from leaving? 
- What was communicated to workers as reasons for not being allowed to leave the company?
-What was the reason for the business calling the police and threatening the workers? 

Added TPs; 
Because workers have resigned and are asking to depart, this situation should be addressed in less than the 3-4 day timeline suggested by SCC.
No resigned worker can be held against their will, or coerced into returning to work
Resigned workers can be provided vaccine certificates and COVID tests to ensure there are no positive cases before departure
Workers can be clearly offered a return to work, with no coercion, and with clear communication on next steps
Because this situation has escalated, Issara can jointly speak with HR and the group of workers if desired, to support communication.
Issara also recommends we provide training to HR reps at SCC, on COVID and other protocols for workforce management.

Workers should be free to leave their jobs with reasonable notice.
