remediation_business_steps_remaining: The business to conduct the investigation for the workers missing wages and transfer the money to the worker's bank account.
remediation_notes: A group of 11 workers who had submitted their resignation letters a week prior were preparing to depart by van when they were not being allowed to go by HR staff and the security guard.  They also packed up and left the company dormitory so now have no place to stay. In addition workers noted that they hadn't received their wages for some days.
remediation_action:
Issara reached out to the business immediately.  The business explained that HR had communicated to the workers about the government's travel restrictions to prevent the spread of Covid-19, and that they are not allowed to travel outside Songkhla province because it is currently a Covid-19 red zone.  They said police had come to enforce the travel restrictions and the van driver left without taking the workers after talking to the police.  Regarding vaccination certificates that would be important for when the workers travel back to Myanmar, the business said the document issuance was delayed by the hospital and would be provided to the workers when issued.  For now, the business said the workers are still living in the private dorm and the workers can ask the landlord to stay in the same place. 

The business will get back to Issara with corrective actions within 3-5 days.

The business further updated Issara saying pictures of HR staff with negative comments regarding this incident had been posted on social media and they wanted the workers to remove the posts.

Issara escalated this issue with TU's Sustainability Director, and recommended that no worker that had already resigned should be held against their will or coerced into returning to work.  TU explained that they didn't want the workers leaving the province illegally given the current Covid-19 restrictions.  The Sustainability Director said they would escalate the matter to the factory MD.  The following day, TU completed the process of issuing official separation documents for the workers so that they can leave.

Regarding the wages, the business noted that they could investigate what had happened with workers wages and compensate workers accordingly.
remediation_validation:
Issara followed up with the workers and provided an update, explaining that the business had said they were following government rules of not allowing inter-provincial travel and that the business would get to Issara in 3-5 days about next steps.  

The workers did not want to stay there anymore; they felt pressured and forced to go back to work.  They were even willing to pay any government fines if there were any for crossing province lines.  Since they have resigned, they don't understand why the business is not letting them leave.  They just want to be able to travel back to Myanmar. 

Regarding the social media posts, the workers said they did not take any photos or videos during the incident nor did they post anything on social media or ask their friends to do so.

The workers have confirmed that they have officially resigned from their jobs and are free to leave.

Regarding the wages, workers noted not wanting to wait for the business to conduct an investigation, as they wanted to leave as soon as possible without waiting for any compensation.
remediation_results: The business processed the official resignation of the workers and the workers have been allowed to leave.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
System Change:
-It is the  business responsibility to have good working conditions that allows workers to feel ethically and fairly treated. This will reduce workers turnover rates, as workers would not feel the need to leave the job. In order to assess the level of satisfaction of workers and identify the areas of improvement, the business is recommended to conduct an internal survey or Issara’s worker satisfaction survey to address the root cause of the issue and improve the system. 
-The business to communicate with the HR and the security guard about the business policy on freedom of movement and rights to make decisions. The communication should include the action that will be taken against the offender. 
-The business should communicate with all the workers about their plan to improve the working conditions and maintain the workers. Otherwise, there could be more workers planning to leave the job.
systems_change_business_steps_taken: The business has not taken any action to improve the system. Therefore several workers keep reporting to Issara about their departure from the factory
systems_change_business_steps_remaining: The business to take proper action to improve the system and retain workers as suggested by Issara.

closed_notes:
Issara had meetings with the buyer and they shared that they had checked with the employer about the case and the issue with the immigration was found. The buyer added that the business had submitted worker's documents for the extension on time, however the immigration office could not find the worker information in the system and the worker ended up being arrested and detained. Several months later, the buyer provided an update saying that the business had arranged for the worker to be released from the immigration detention center, and processed her working papers. Issara followed up with the worker who reported feeling mentally and physically healthy. However, the worker added some illegal deductions (100THB for every 1000 THB) from her wages being taken by the immigration officers every time that the business transferred her salary to her through immigration officer. This is an illegal deduction and the police should not have charged the worker such fees. In addition, the worker reported having to pay high prices for food and other basic needs while being at the detention center.

Issara has reported to the buyer the updates from the worker noting the illegal and unethical practices from the police and the business side.

She is currently in a detention center and has been told she will be deported when the borders open.
remediation_action:

The SP provided an update saying that the business had arranged for the worker to be released from the immigration detention center, and processed her working papers.  She will begin work at the business as before.
remediation_validation:
The worker has confirmed that she has received assistance to leave the detention center.  She also received her daily wages during the whole time she had to stay in the detention center.  However, because the business had to send the money to her through the immigration police, the police charged a 100 Baht fee for every 1,000 Baht transferred to the worker.  This is an illegal deduction and the police should not have charged the worker such fees. In addition, the worker reported having to pay high prices for food and other basic needs while being at the detention center. 
 
However, she did not want to request the return of the money the police had taken from her, and was happy to have received wages from the business and to be out of the detention center.
remediation_results: The business worked with relevant government departments to secure her release from the immigration detention center, processed her legal working documents so that she can resume work at the business as before, and paid for her wages during the time she had to stay in the detention center.  The worker has confirmed all this and is happy to be free and back to work.  However, the business had to transfer payments to her through the police at the detention center, and the police made illegal deductions on the money received, so the worker ended up receiving less than what she should have received.

In addition to that, Issara escalated to the TU Sustainability Director and HR at HQ and explained that this issue affected a larger group than just the 6 pregnant workers. After the business conducted another investigation, 68 employees who were infected with COVID-19 and had a history of more than 30 days of sick leave (41 Thai employees and 27 Burmese employees) were identified for payment for those days missed due to Covid-19.  50% of wages were to be paid by the Social Security office and 50% paid by the business (for 2021 only). Furthermore, the business identified another 35 employees who had close contact with COVID-19 patients and ordered by the company to quarantine. They were allowed to take up to 30 sick days and the business has paid wages for quarantine days to all 35 workers. In total 6+ 68 + 35 = 109 workers have been remediated. However, the business did not share the information about the remediation payment. Since it was the issue during the bubble and seal period and it was for 28 quarantine days (24 working days), Issara estimates the remediation payment as follows; 109 x 325 x 24 = 850,200 THB. However, the business took several weeks to identify and address the issues. Issara had to do several follow up with the business based on the worker complaints and update. remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the missing payment of the worker's daily wages during their quarantine period and Bubble and Seal Period. Workers added that there are several workers including pregnant workers who have not received any payment or lower payment than what they used to receive. It is added that there is no clear communication from the business side for their missing payment. In addition to that, some workers who have received some payment have reported not getting a payslip. 


Recommendation:
-The business shall provide the payslip to the workers immediately, in a format and language workers can understand easily. The payslip should include clear information about the wages, incentives, and deductions. 
-The business shall check the payment system to identify the issue with the missing payment and remediate workers according to what they are supposed to be paid. 
-All workers should receive the right payment within the next pay period 
-The business shall communicate with the workers to approach the HR focal person if they have any issue with their wages so that the HR can verify the right amount workers should receive. The focal person should be clear on how to communicate with the workers when workers approach the office. 
-Workers who were quarantined or placed in Bubble and Seal housing and not working should have a clear leave policy that is paid properly. 
- Pregnant workers, in particular, should be fully paid for any days they were in company housing and not working, with a clear policy on what types of leave are applied (cannot be unpaid leave).  
- As workers are unable to afford their current costs, this should be immediately investigated with workers quickly paid properly in the current pay period.

Talking Points:
-What is the business understanding on this issue with the payment? 
-Have there been any changes with the payroll recently? 
-Have there been any communication with the workers about the changes to the payslip? 



Time Frame 2 weeks.

remediation_action:
The business is following up on this matter and requested more information from Issara and also for affected workers to report directly to HR.

The business investigated the matter and found that 6 pregnant workers had not received their daily wages because they requested business leave instead of sick leave for their quarantine days. The business said it made the correction and processed payment on 20th October.

Issara escalated to the TU Sustainability Director and HR at HQ that this is a larger group of workers beyond the 6 workers that TUS investigated and identified as having used personal leave instead of sick leave and TUS had fixed the issue and paid those workers.  The business said it would investigate the missing payments and understands the urgency of the workers.  TUS will also announce to workers to go to HR and report any missing payments to speed up the process.

After the business conducted another investigation, 68 employees who were infected with COVID-19 and had a history of more than 30 days of sick leave (41 Thai employees and 27 Burmese employees) were identified for payment for those days missed due to Covid-19.  50% of wages is to be paid by the Social Security office and 50% will be paid by the business this year only. 

The business communicated to employees regarding the payment of wages for employees who are sick with COVID-19 on Nov 9-11.

The business confirmed paying 50% of wages to 68 employees.  For the other 50% to be compensated by the Social Security Office, they randomly checked with about half of the employees and found that they had received direct transfer payments from SSO.

Workers also reported being discouraged by the business staff from contacting Issara about their issues.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with sick leave. Workers reported being followed by the business when workers take sick leave. If workers take sick leave, the business sends its staff to check workers status. In that situation, the workers feel pressured by the business for taking sick leave. In addition to that, workers also feel pressured when they take sick leave for more than 2 days because the business makes a phone call and puts pressure towards the workers and explains how the business could be impacted if workers take longer leave. Apart from that, the workers also added not being assisted by the business to access their SSF benefits, as the SSF hospital is far from the company and the business does not provide transportation . In that case, workers reported having to pay their own money for their health purpose. This is happening in the lines 21,22,23,24,25,26,27.

Recommendations for the remediation.
-The business shall conduct a wide range of investigations to assess the issue with workers' sick leave and also to assess the number of impacted workers. The investigation should include workers' voices. 
-During the investigation process, the business should make sure that no workers are being targeted by the supervisors. To make sure that no workers are targeted, the business should communicate with the reported supervisor about the business' no retaliation policy and workers rights to have full rest without any corciotion and pressure when they are sick. 
-The business clearly communicates with the workers what their plan will be for this issue.
-The business should look back to their system and make sure that workers are properly paid during their leaves. 
-The business should immediately cease the practice of visiting sick workers without their request. Workers have the right to take 30 days of sick leave annually, and the business may ask for proof of the sickness only if the sick days are more than 3 consecutive days. This is according to the LPA, therefore, the company policy should be aligned with the law, and this should be communicated to all employees, including supervisors. The business should make a clear announcement that visiting a sick person against their will is a violation of the basic human rights, and rights of privacy of a patient. 

-All workers should be introduced to the business grievance mechanism channels and encouraged to use any channel (internal or external as Issara) that they feel comfortable using. . 
-The business shall clearly communicate with the workers about their rights to access their SSF in case they are sick and want to see a doctor. The business should assist the workers with the transportation and the translation if workers want to visit the SSF hospital, or find a closer hospital where the company can register workers through SSF so that they can easily access the service. 
-When communicating business channels with all employees, the business should also explain how workers’ grievances are managed and how safeguards are kept for the workers.

Talking Points:
-What is the process for taking sick leave for workers? 
-Workers reported being visited by the factory staff when they are sick, what is the business understanding of this? 
-Is there any focal person to assist the workers when they are sick and want to visit SSF hospital? If yes, has the business introduced this person to the workers? 
-How many workers are there in each production line?

Description: An Employer shall pay Wages to an Employee for sick leave under Section 32 equivalent to Wages of a Working Day throughout the Leave period, but not exceeding 30 Working Days per year. Whereas an Employee takes Leave for sterilization under Section 33, the Employer shall pay Wages to the Employee for such Leave.

closed_notes:

The business also talked about how some workers were not really sick but asked for sick leave and produced MCs that are very easy to get in Thailand and were abusing the sick leave policy.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the breaks. Workers reported not receiving proper breaks during their lunch time and also before starting OT hours. They said that they take only 15 to 20 minutes of break as they have the pressure to complete the target by the end of the working hours. This is also reported from the production line called (Roung Thor).

Recommendations: 
The business should conduct an investigation across the factory to identify the root cause of the issue. The investigation should be conducted by the HR. All of the workers' information during the investigation process should be kept confidential.
The investigation should include workers' voices and the no retaliation policy to be explained with the line supervisor and manager to avoid the retaliation that can take place during and after the investigation. 


The business shall take action towards the staff that violates the business policy regarding breaks hours. 
All workers should have a rest period of not less than one hour for their lunch and at least 20 mins before starting OT if their OT hours are more than 2 hours according to the LPA section No.27.  
OT working hours should be aligned with the LPA and the buyer's COC.

ETI; Goal: All workers have the right to take lunch breaks, in line with the law, which specifies minimum amount of time allowable. Further, workers should be allowed to take bathroom breaks whenever needed. Limiting use of bathrooms for the purpose of controlling or maximizing productivity can have adverse effects on the health of workers, and should be strictly prohibited. Breaks are required by law as well, in between regular working hours and OT shifts.

Code: ETI Base Code 6.1. Working hours are not excessive; must comply with national laws, collective agreements
Description: Working hours must comply with national laws, collective agreements, and the provisions of 6.2 to 6.6 below, whichever affords the greater protection for workers. Sub-clauses 6.2 to 6.6 are based on international labour standards.
LPA Section 27. On a Working Day, an Employer shall arrange a rest period during work for an Employee of not less than one hour per day after the Employee has been working for not more than fve consecutive hours. An Employer and Employee may agre in advance that each rest period may be less than one hour but the total rest period per day shall not be less than one hour. Whereas an Employer and Employee agree to specify rest periods during work other than paragraph one, the agreement shall be applicable only if it is more favourable to the Employee. A rest period during work shall not be counted as working time except where the total rest period is more than two hours per day, where the amount of time exceeding two hours shall be counted as normal working time. Whereas any Overtime Work after normal working time is more than two hours, the Employer shall arrange for the Employee to take a rest period of not less than twenty minutes before the Employee commences the Overtime Work. The provisions in paragraph one and paragraph four shall not apply where an Employee is required to do work of a continuous nature or character with the consent of the Employee, or in case of emergency work.

call_details.description:
Worker from this factory called and reported following two issues. 

(1) Lack of supplies during quarantine period; Worker reported that once they are identified as COVID-19 infected or suspected/high risk workers, they have to stay quarantine. 10 days of quarantine for infected workers and 7 days for close contact. However, the business does not provide any foods or even water. If there is a wife being infected, the husband or the family member also has to stay quarantine. It means the whole family members have to stay quarantine and have no access to the foods or water. Workers want the business to provide supplies or assign someone to help them purchase. 

(2) The issue with expense of ATK test kits; If a worker is infected or suspected, have to do ATK test. If a worker feel sick, she has to do the ATK test and also go to the hospital. Once they go to the hospital, the hospital will do the PCR test and confim her to stay 10 days of quarantine. Once they complete the quarantine, on the day 10th they have to do ATK test, on the day 11th another ATK test and on the day 15th follo up test. Total around 4 ATK test for both infected and the suspected workers. The business does not pay for those test kits. Workers find it expensive to pay for the several kits. They want the business to reduce some of the test process and also provde ATK test for free. Once, the worker have approached the HR and requested for the free test, the HR said that even Thai staff have to buy by themselves. 

(3) The issue with the wages for the quarantine period; Follow up on the previous issue where the business used to deduct workers annual leaves for high risks workers quarantine days. The worker said that the business has verbally communicated that they will pay for any kind of qarantine. If a worker is suspected or high risk and have to stay quarantine, the business will pay wages as a special wages. No any leaves will be deducted. For infected workers, the hospital provides MC which can be used for sick leave. Wokrer said that they do not have issue with the wages during their quaratine these days.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
There is a delay in the issuing of the work permit, which workers need to access social security benefits such as coverage for delivering babies at the hospital and applying for the child care allowance.

Talking points:
When will the work permits be issued?  
Is the delay on the part of the government?  
How has the company communicated this delay to the workers?

Recommendations for remediation
Investigate and identify workers that were directly affected by this issue, and repay any costs paid out of pocket by the workers for delivery of babies in the hospital or any child care allowance that was forfeited.
Communicate verbally and in writing to all workers when the work permits will be issued and when they can fully access their social security benefits
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Raweeroge HR manager- For the pregnant workers, the HR team is looking after closely with the workers. WP is important for the child support application process. Right now the company has not found the issue yet if the worker reachout to Issara pls suggest the worker to contact the HR directly. And HR will also check with all the pregnant workers as well.


The investigation result:
This case didn't happen. But if it happens, it's probably the case that migrant workers are a walk-in group, applying for a job and being hired as an employee. This group of employees will not be able to use social security rights immediately because they may not have rights in the case that they must have paid contributions for 3 months within 15 months, but the company has purchased health insurance for employees who have not received social security benefits for a period of 4 months. If these employees are sick, they must use health insurance instead.

Action:
In the case of an incident
1. In employee orientation will increase the knowledge of foreign employees who have not received social security rights that if there is an illness, health insurance must be exercised until the SS benefit active.
2. HR makes a copy of the health insurance policy for employees to keep in their passport in case of emergency.
3. If there is an illness, inform HR through an interpreter to help coordinate with the hospital to facilitate
remediation_notes: There is a delay in the issuing of the work permit, which workers need to access social security benefits such as coverage for delivering babies at the hospital and applying for the child care allowance.
remediation_action: The business said the HR team is giving close attention to the pregnant workers but was not aware of any pregnant workers with any specific problems accessing social security benefits for maternity care or benefits for child rearing at this time.  The business wanted such workers to reach out to HR directly. HR will check with all the pregnant workers as well.
remediation_validation: Issara followed up with a worker who reported that he had received his work permit already and was able to get the birth certificate for his newborn. He is now in the process of submitting the application to get child care allowance and reimbursement for child delivery expenses as well.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case, with the couple that had issues with getting social security benefits for their newborn now able to access them because they have their work permits now.

description: Unsafe or hazardous working conditions (OSH issues)

call_details.description: The client Ms. Sandar Win from TUS reported that the Covid positive cases in TUF is multiplying day by day. Although almost all of the workers have been vaccinated in June and July ( two times), there are now nearly 30 Myanmar workers who tested positive. According to the client there are also some Thai workers who tested positive as well. However, the workers still have to go work. In this situation, workers are very afraid to go to work and wearing production uniform ( uniform is to share among workers ). So the workers would like to know when all the workers will be tested or how the the production will keep running safely ?
call_details.source_recruiter_name: International Focus General Services Co., Ltd

call_details.description:
Client reported that her husband is in the MOU dorm too because of having close contact with her. She is a positive patient in 8 days, being isolated separately from a different quarantine site. This morning, as all the suspected workers, who have close contact with positive cases are being asked to go back to work, her husband also has to go back to work too. But, her husband is now feeling sick, having red eyes, running nose, losing the smell, and feeling cold because of the fever. Plus, having to work under a cold room made him worse. So he went and reported to HR. Then HR asked the factory nurse to take the temperature. The nurse told him that it's normal. But, the husband is feeling so cold. They thought the HR had a deal with a nurse.

There is also one couple who has the same symptoms as her husband. But, only the wife is asked to go back and the husband still has to work too. They just said the temperature is normal, but the workers are not fine with the temperature. Plus, not being provided food yesterday, made the workers weaker too.

They expected that it would be great if the business had the Covid-19 test again before asking the workers to go back to work. Plus having more proper measures with the control of disease. It's ok if they are not getting paid. The business shouldn't force the sick workers to keep working.
call_details.next_steps: Have to update ILM team

call_details.description: Contact the client to inquiry whether the business has provided any contact person in case of emergency. She said the business selected one worker who can considerably speak and understand Thai more than other workers. When the workers first arrived at the quarantine center, the MOU dorm, they had a brief meeting and during that time, the business called out that worker and showed the other workers that they could contact him for an emergency. But, when back to the working line, they don't know how to catch up with that worker. She suggested it would be great if they have posted or shared the announcement that includes the information and instruction about how to contact the focal person in case of emergency. So they can easily contact that worker. But, during the operating hours, as they cannot bring their phone, it might not be easy to find that worker too. Now, her husband was sent back to his room now by the business as she requested the supervisor to let him go home.
call_details.next_steps: Have to update ILM team.

call_details.description:
Follow up call with the client about working condition and if there is any emergency contact was given to the worker. The client said it was given but not kind of announced in Public. Some batch may know and some batch may not know that emergency contact worker as they arrived in the dorm in different time.  The business just introduced to the workers once in a meeting.  So workers who do not join that meeting and came late, will not know that.  According to my one informant she know that because she joining that meeting. 

Then O&E asked to talk with that worker who are assigned in case of emergency. He said there are other three workers like him who are assigned by the business in terms of communication with the workers if they Report issue.  Then they have to report to a Thai lady.  They just called her Mom.  He didnt know her name. At first, what ever they report to that lady took an account.  But later, whatever what the workers raised, that lady didn't take any account anymore.

Tomorrow, he will send me the photo of that lady, and the photo of lunch boxes providing to. Thai and Burmese workers.  He said Thai workers received big box with good meal inside such as fry chicken, fiy fish and the Burmese workers received only small box with mixed fish and vegetable curry like that.  As Burmese workers eat a lot of Rice, they are not full with what the business provided to them.  He said how we are going to survive for 21 days like this.  He said, if the business cannot give good equal meal, please give them some time to go back home.  So, they can collect some ration and came back with pots and they can cook and eat more.

call_details.description:
Checking the situation in the Q-center in TUS. The client updated that there are 70 positive workers being sent to another Q-center called "Kun-Yan" in Hat-Yai. They will complete the quarantine by next 4 days according to my informant. At the Q-center, they tried to adapt with the situation, including the Thai food, the noise as they are being provided with beds in a hall with no separate partation. Actually, they lose sleep and nutrition as they try to adapt with Thai food. They are so happy as they will finish the quarantine soon. They thought they would go back to their own room, cook what they would like to eat and sleep in their own room. But, unfortunately, they heard that they will be allocated back to the business compound Q-center (MOU dorn) together with the existing quarantine workers. They worried about the situation. They can bear for 14 days at the current Q-centers, but if they have to take another 14 days, they will die.
So, they also would like to suggest the business to have a grocery shop inside the compound. So that they can buy eggs, fish or some noodles when they are hungry.

call_details.description:
Follow up call with the client about 1. Polluted water issue, Drinking water Issue and 3. No access to ATM Issue.

1. Pollution Water Issue: Not fixed yet. The worker in Zone-C informed me that no technician came. So they just used that water and applied powder ect. The workers went to work all day and just came back. They thought everything was fixed, but not yet. 

2. Drinking water: This issue too. The informant said he didn't see any new water buckets yesterday after we talked with HR. As there are many zones (A,B,C,D,E), sometimes, they don't know if some workers from different zones have taken the bottle as the business just left the water buckets in the entrance of the dorn. Would be great if the business can allocate like 4 or 5 buckets per zone, so that they also can know who has taken and carried it to their room etc. For the water pump, I am checking with my informant in Zone-C and he said, he never saw that.

3. For the ATM issue in hotel quarantine: The informant said, the direct informant hasn't sent him the photo yet, so he cannot send it to me now. I asked the direct informant number and I just finished talking with the informant. He said it's near Siranakhon Hospital (5 min drive from the factory). It's kind of like an apartment. There are around 40 Burmese workers there and there are 4 babies who are under one year olds. While they are in hospital quarantine, the hospital quarantine provides everything, including mile power, baby meal or diapers. But now, when they were being moved to those apartments, they asked the business (P'Kyi Ya, male Burmese representative sitting in HR office), and told him that we will not take any responsibility for our baby. He just asked the workers to give money or give an ATM card to the focal so that he will buy it for the baby. But, I think they still have the responsibility to take care of the worker's baby too since their parents have to follow the business practice. 

4. Male workers have to take care of the babies: And the business managed only the father to take care of those babies and not the mother. The mothers are allocated back to MOU dorm and have to go back to work. The workers do not know why the business did like that. Actually, babies should be with the mother. They talked with P'Kyi Ya and he said the mommy work site required manpower so that they cannot let them taking care of the babies.
call_details.next_steps: Have to escalate to ILM team

call_details.description:
Follow up with the client for Polluted water Issue and Drinking Water Issue.

1. Polluted Water Issue: The client updated that yesterday evening, he came back from work, he said the water is clear and not dusty anymore. He thought the business must come and fix it.

2. Drinking Water:          Yesterday, he heard from the focal assigned person that the business came and explained to them they will refill/ change the new water three times per day. But, they should let the workers relocate the water bucket to the original place after they used it. (Before, they just come and refill new water only one time per day. It's not enough for the worker.) In terms of the water dispenser, the client said he didn't hear anything. But, some workers said, the business told them they will give the workers a water pump by tomorrow.

3&4. Difficult access to withdraw money and Not enough bed in the hotel: I called the client 3 times and he didn't pick up the call. So no update yet.

Issara also update him about the remediation meeting with K'Prad and the business cannot solve with the issue of baby meals and accessary as it was 14 days already. The workers have to take care of their babies by themselves. He said, he is clear now,  because the business used to told them that they will take care of everything during the quarantine, that's why he is hoping for that. But, if they cannot provide any support for the babies, they will try to find their way out for the best.

call_details.description:
Follow up call with the client for case update:

1. · Workers not receiving meals on Aug 31 and Sep 1?

Yes, this issue was fixed. The business well prepared the lunch of the workers. For breakfast and dinner, the Two Thai women, who are assigned to distribute the food in the MOU dorm,  are taking care of this. For lunch, it was sent by the hotel. The informant said, the management came and said sorry for the workers who missed the meals on Aug 31 as there are some information gaps between HR and what’s happening on the ground. He (One of the management) regrets and is sorry about that. They will take care of this kind of issue not happening again. 

2. The issue with discrimination in terms of food distribution between Thai workers and Burmese workers: 
This issue has also been resolved. The meal box is now bigger than in the previous. It's enough for the workers. And their current inside also include more ingredients, such as paste, and vegetable (To-Sa-Yar) and fry. So the workers are fine and happy with that now.

3. Limited access to buy goods and basic necessities: TUS said there is a system for workers to order purchases and they are delivered once a week and more zone leaders will be female so female workers can make requests to female zone leaders.  Have the workers confirmed they understand the system, that they can buy what they need, and female workers can make orders through female zone leaders?

Now, the business allows one old Thai woman who used to sell the stuff near the factory. That lady was allowed to come and bring the stuff, such as noodles, cooking ingredients, like fish paste, soy milk, soft drink, etc. She comes to the dorn on Saturday and Sunday. She left her stuff to the dorn and there are four workers who help her sell her products after they come back to work. Workers came and bought the stuff from these four workers. (Informant is one of the four sellers). If they want a special order, they leave these four workers noted down . When the Thai lady comes, the four workers give those special orders to that Thai lady and the Thai lady bought for them.

4· Insufficient drinking water and lack of water dispenser: 
Now, the business came and refilled the water gallon and the workers said it's properly enough. They come with water pumps and they have no problem too. Plus, the business also provides additional ice blocks as well. So they are ok with that.

5· Polluted tap water:  this was fixed and workers have confirmed that the tap water is no longer an issue. 

Yes, there is no issue with that too. Maintenance workers come and  fix that after our escalated call with K'Prad. Now, it's clean.
call_details.next_steps: Have to update ILM team and close the case.

call_details.description:
Follow up call with the client for the following ATM issue.

1. Mothers in quarantine "hospitals" cannot access cash (ATM machines) to buy essentials for their babies: worker update?

Yes, as business' update, two authorized helpers / workers  from the factory come and check if they would like to order anything. So he can help buy that baby's product. They bring the receipts, together with the withdrawal slip. As the informant was a bit worried, he asked his neighbors to buy these products. (The does not have mobile Apps) 

2. Those in quarantine "hospitals" that did not receive bedsheets and couldn't sleep properly: worker update?

Now they all received the bedsheet. 

3. But, there is an additional issue after some workers finished 24 days quarantine from (14 days Quarantine in hospital + 14 days quarantine in SEALIGHT hotel). There are about 20 workers and they are asked to go back to work. As this quarantine site is very far from the hospital, the workers requested the business to let them go home so that they can go to work. But, the business relocated them to the housing, where there are already existing workers there. So the workers have to share the room with the room owners. There are about 8 rooms, in which workers are being packed to share the space. And one Thai lady from HR, also told those workers to share the room and electric charges with those existing workers (Room owners). The workers said, because of the factory shut down, we are not getting full wages. Plus, we also have to pay for our own room although we do not stay there. They would like to know if we can help them to relocate them back to their own room. As they also bear for 28 days already. There are also some workers who submitted resignation letters too as they cannot continue working there anymore. But, they are now allowed to leave that room because the business has to talk to the landlord. That housing is just in front of the factory gate no.2. The workers said, it's a yellow painted building.
call_details.next_steps: Have to close case no.1&2 and prepare talking points for case number 3.
to monitor the situation.

call_details.description:
Checking with the client how they are being communicated to relocate back to the yellow building based on BHR update on business response 1461. 
(The TUS HR said TUS paid for the Sealight room rental cost in advance for the workers and TUS will arrange free transportation for them to go back and work until the end of B&S. This group of workers said if the business would like them to go back and work the business must allow them to stay close to the factory, if not they won't go back to work because the Sealight hotel and TUS are very far and the worker said they don't want to take long transportation. This part is correct. But the business didn't communicate with them that they had to stay in a yellow building and paid the room cost after one month. They just thought they would be sent back to their own room. 
To solve the problem, workers requested the TUS discussed with the Songkhla Public health care to include the Yellow building in the TUS B&S policy. The Songkhla Public health care agreed to it and allowed 9 rooms under TUS B&S. The TUS already pays for the room rental cost for the workers. The HR said workers will have to pay for the room rental cost next month because the business already arranged for the worker at Sealight Hotel and paid the rental cost in advance already but the worker doesn't want to stay there.  
 
The HR said they have communicated with the worker many times but this group of workers are still saying that they would like to go back to their room. They don't understand B&S policy and are not interested in it. O&E check with the worker how the business communicates to you for relocation back to the yellow housing? 
The client responded that the translator called the focal persons who are assigned in the SEALIGHT Hotel to buy the kid stuff and withdraw cash. The translator called those persons to let the workers know who finished quarantine and had to go back to work. As the workers refused because of the time limitation and there is a problem with the limited bathroom in the hotel, they told those assigned persons to request the business to relocate them back to their room.   
The HR said TUS B&S policy, TUS arranged 4 people in each room during B&S, the worker can choose who they would like to stay with and send the list name of the room member to HR. All local or Burmese workers have to follow the same. 
This 20 workers group is also the same, the workers choose their room members by them self and send the name list to the HR team. The HR said the HR team did not select the people and send them to the same room.)The next day, a van arrived at the hotel and they were asked to board. At that time there was one Thai lady who came and picked them up. When the workers were about to board, she asked please raise your hands if you stay in the Yellow building in front of the building, there were 8 workers there and she asked them to please choose your friends who you think can stay with you in your rooms for only 14 days. As the workers thought only for 14 days, they chose their friends. But, the translator and that Thai lady also involved suggesting or advising the workers too. For example, if there are two couples who stay in that building, they ask them to temporarily stay like only the wifes stay with another two female workers and the two husbands stay with another two male workers. 

On that day, there were also still about 50 workers being sent to other housing near Sunday Market. But, those workers are now relocated back to their own room near near the Yellow Building. That building is called "Rakkhine Housing" and the room are more spacious. The informant who has to stay with her friends in the Yellow housing is also staying there.
Further Update:27 Sep: Yesterday, around 2 PM, the Burmese Translator (Arr Don) and P' Dium (HR) came into Yellow Housing and asked some workers to do a night shift. Since the workers have to share the room with some workers who have babies and some are leaving the job, working the night shift will make them annoyed. So they asked them to relocate them back to their own room. Then they agreed and they asked the workers to sign a paper as an agreement if they are ok to work on night shift. But they have to follow  business policy and they cannot commute except to the building to work. The landlord will strictly manage this. The workers agreed and signed and they started working the night shift. And they told the workers that you cannot go back to your room by yourselves. We have to manage you by transferring you to your room.

28 Sep,  this morning, as no one came up, the workers called the translator and asked them when they could come. The translator and P'Dium came back at 8 AM again. They told the workers that you are not able to relocate now as you have agreed to stay here and we have paid for this room. If you leave now, you have to pay the room fee for this month. The workers said, yes, we will pay. But, they said they still need the approval from management.
The workers said why they did not keep the promise and they manipulated the workers like that. They asked why another 50 workers being sent to Sunday housing and now they can go back to their room "Rakkhine Housing" and not them, the translator didn't translate it back to P'Dium. They are also not happy with the behavior or performance of the translator too.  

O&E asked the following three questions to the workers:
1. Have you been told that you have to pay that room cost after one month? 
Ans: The workers said no.

2. Did you know that you can go back to the SEALIGHT hotel if you don't want to stay here? The workers said no. Even the workers who will finish quarantine in the SEALIGHT hotel will be sent back to their housing (Rakkhine Housing) soon.

3. How long were you being communicated to stay there?
Ans: The translator and P'Dium told them as long as B&S policy.
The workers also added, not only the room cost, but also sharing the room with other workers is not a good practice. Plus, they have to work the night shift, the babies crying, and a lot of distractions.
call_details.next_steps: Have to Update ILM team to check with business why other workers from other housing and the workers in the yellow housing are not being sent back to their room yet.

In terms of checking checking why his friends are being communicated to relocate back to the yellow housing before, he also update the same like the informant "Chaw Chaw Su".

(The TUS HR said TUS paid for the Sealight room rental cost in advance for the workers and TUS will arrange free transportation for them to go back and work until the end of B&S. closed_notes: Issara raised this issue with the business and suggested the investigation. As a response, the business replied by saying that their investigation found one of the cleaning staff using high amount of chlorine to clean the floor which caused other workers in that line to experience various respiratory symptoms such as eye, nose, and throat discomfort and inflammation. remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Unsafe or hazardous working conditions (OSH issues). The worker from Breaded line reported that they suffer sore throat and eyesore from the chemical solution that’s used for cleaning. The workers can hardly work in the line production when the cleaners use the solution to clean the line. They get scolded when they ask line supervisors to tell the cleaner not to use the chemical too much. 

Recommendations; 
The business shall conduct an investigation to find out whether the cleaning agent being used is certified to be safe for use in cleaning this production line and identify why workers are suffering negative symptoms (sore throat and eye sores) when the particular cleaning product is used. 
Investigate why the line supervisors did not respond appropriately to workers that reported getting sick from being exposed to the chemicals in the cleaning product used.  Take disciplinary action as appropriate based on the investigation result. 
Conduct the investigation involving affected workers and those using the cleaning products
Develop a plan of action based on the investigation results to ensure that workers have a safe and a healthy working environment and any cleaning products used are within safety standards. 
The business should communicate to all workers about the business’s plan of action to address this issue and provide transparent information about cleaning products being used and that they are safe for workers.  
Since this is the issue with the chemical, this should be considered a serious issue and the business should take action immediately. 
Remind workers about  the internal grievance channels, how workers can report any issues, noting the focal points that will be handling all issues, timeframe for the issues to be solved, and proper safeguards for those reporting grievances. 


Talking Points;

Has the business received these complaints from the workers? 
Are there any channels for the workers to raise this kind of health related issues?
remediation_business_steps_taken: Issara raised this issue with the business and suggested the investigation. As a response, the business replied by saying that their investigation found one of the cleaning staff using high amount of chlorine to clean the floor which caused other workers in that line get burning nose. However, that cleaning was during the new year only. The business have communicated with that employee and suggested to use standard amount of chemical in cleaning. Since then, the business have monitored and have noticed the improvement. Issara is checking with the workers.
remediation_notes: Workers reported suffering sore throats, burning sensation in their nostrils, and eyesores from the cleaning product being used to clean their working line.  They can hardly work in the line when the cleaners use the chemical cleaning agent to clean the line. When they reported this to their line supervisors, they were scolded rather than having the matter addressed immediately, given the threat to the general health of the workers.
remediation_action: Issara raised this issue with the business, the business agreed to conduct an investigation and get back to Issara.  From the inspection, the business found that there was a big clean-up after the Chinese New Year holiday and 1 cleaning staff had added more liquid detergent than usual because he saw that there were deep stains.  This caused a strong smell and when employees reported the ill effects of the smell, the line supervisor ordered the cleaning staff to reduce the amount of chlorine and remedied the situation immediately that day.  This conflicts with the workers' reports that the line supervisor had scolded them rather than remedying the problem.
remediation_validation: The workers have not raised this issue since the original report
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case because the business has instructed the cleaning staff to use the standard amount of the cleaning detergent, and is monitoring the situation.  Workers have not raised this issue since then.

description: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: dispute without violation of law or employment contract

call_details.source_recruiter_name: International Focus General Services Co., Ltd

closed_notes: Issara raised this issue with the business and suggested recommendations. As a response, the business replied by saying that their investigation did not find the issue with the supervisor not approving workers’ annual leave; however, they did find that supervisors were asking many questions about why workers were requesting leave.  The business reminded the supervisors about the business’ policy on taking leave, and emphasized how they should communicate with workers about leave requests and approvals.  On top of that, the business added that they will provide refresher training to all supervisors by March 2022.  The business did not commit to making a new announcement about the process of requesting annual leave to workers. Issara checked with the workers, and they have not raised this issue since.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context; Issue with workers’ annual leave Workers from the “Breaded” line reported that they can not take annual leave for several consecutive days as they wish.  The business is only allowing them to take one annual leave day every two months, which is not helpful for the workers that may be planning vacation time over several consecutive days. 

Recommendations; 
The business should review its annual leave policy and how it is being practiced.
Workers should be able to determine when he/she will take days off for their personal rest and leisure, and not be restricted to being able to take only one leave day at a time
If the business already has a policy of allowing workers to request and take annual leave days when they would like, disciplinary measures should be  taken against the line supervisor that is restricting workers’ ability to take annual leave for multiple consecutive days


Talking Points
What is the business’s annual leave policy? 
Are workers allowed to take more than 1 day of annual leave per time?
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara raised this issue with the business and suggested for the recommendations. As response, the business replied by saying that their investigation did not find the issue with the supervisor not approving workers annual leaves, however it was found that supervisor asking several questions when workers take leaves. The business added that they have communicated with the supervisor and emphasized the way of communication method with the workers. On top of that, the business added that the HR from the factory has a plan to provide refresher training with all supervisors by March 2022. The business also added that the workers have rights to take their annual leaves consecutively.  However, the business response has not reflected the communication with the workers about the business policy taking leaves. 

Issara is checking with the workers.
remediation_notes: Workers from a production line reported that they are not being allowed to take several consecutive days of annual leave as they wish.  The business is only allowing them to take one annual leave day every two months, which is too restrictive for those that would like to take vacation time over several consecutive days.
remediation_action:
Issara raised this issue with the business.  The business conducted the investigation with employees in the Chup Pang line, and found that supervisors would ask lots of questions when a worker would ask for several consecutive days of annual leave and some would shout at the workers. The HR department has issued warnings to such supervisors. In addition, HR plans to provide refresher training to all supervisors on communication methods in March 2022.

It is concerning that the company holds the position that it has the right to determine when employees take their annual leave and has determined that employees can take 1 annual leave day every 2 months so as to distribute the vacation days throughout the year.  However, the business did allow that if the employee needs to use several leave days consecutively, she must make the request to her supervisor and it will be considered for approval.
remediation_validation: Issara followed up with workers and they have not raised this issue since.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue because the business has instructed the line supervisors on appropriate communication methods when processing annual leave requests from workers.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
The business shall communicate with the workers about the business’s annual leave policy and clarify that workers can use annual leave days without restrictions (such as, only taking one annual leave day at a time).  
Also, take this opportunity to remind workers about the company’s grievance mechanism, the process of how grievances are reported and handled, any specific staff or committee that serves as the focal responsible person to respond to grievances, and encourage workers to report any issues they may have in the future

description: Issues with overtime being involuntary/forced or illegal

call_details.description:
1. Explained to the worker about business’s policy of annual bonus
2. Worker mentioned specifically on Roung Thor line (Textile machines) but other lines seem ok with general conditions. 
- For 8 working hours, there is only a break time around 15-20 minutes for rest and if they do OT there is another break time of 15-20 minutes. 
- A worker needs to monitor 6 lines and for each line there are 13 machines, totally each worker needs to monitor 78 machines. It’s very exhausting, workers need to work non-stop and hardly take a break. 
- There is a day off within a week, but the worker was forced to work on the day off. The manager(Taiwanese) said if they don’t work, their benefit of Beer Ka Yan will be cut off. 
- Communication with the line manager (Ta Noiy) is very difficult, he doesn't explain and communicate well with Cambodian workers. Recently, the line manager moved the worker’s day off to the next 4 days without a clear explanation. Ex. Every Thursday is a day off but the line manager moves the day off to next Tuesday because the Factory will be closed for 2 days for holidays, Monday and Tuesday. Worker said, it’s cheating. Actually, they need to pay double for a day off but as they move, the day off counts as a normal day.

The worker said Yes the business provide the consent form to worker for working on day off. And sometime manager said if they don't work on day off, they may assign worker to do some dirty works like cleaning the canal. So, worker don't want to do that work and willing to sign the consent form. They got double paid for working on day off but they also want some rest when they feel exhausted as well.

Get an update to the worker about business response related to involunteering OT work and replacing holidays. Informed to the worker that next time the business will have a clear communication and ask for prior consent from the workers so, the worker can notice and report back to Issara if the problems is still happening.
call_details.next_steps: Will regularly check with the workers whether the issue still occurs or not.

call_details.description: After I got the business response two weeks ago related to forcing OT and changing the holiday date without proper/prior inform to the workers. O&E follow up and check with the worker that the issue is still occurring or not. The worker confirmed that the situation is improving.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case because the business investigated the matter, identified that there was an issue, and has made it clear that there will be no switching of workers' days-off in the future.  And if such a switch is needed in special cases, workers' consent would be needed before proceeding.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the involuntary work on workers’ day off of the week. Workers from Roung Thor line (Textile machines) reported they were pressured to agree to work on their day off. The business threatened the workers saying they would be assigned to difficult jobs such as cleaning the sewers or they would be denied their diligence bonus (Bia Ka Yan) if they did not agree to work on their day off.  So, they felt they had to consent to working on their day off even if they didn’t want to do so. Workers also added that the manager switched their day off from Thursday to Tuesday without first consulting and getting their consent. 

Recommendations: 

-Regular shift hours and wages should be respected at all times, in line with contractual agreements. Changes in shifts should be made with the consent of workers and with reasonable notice, ensuring that total weekly working hours are in compliance with national law, and extra hours are paid at a premium rate. 
- Workers should not be forced or coerced to agree to the changes or to work on their day off. This includes threats to withhold certain benefits or to punish the worker in any way
- Shifts should not be changed in order to avoid paying premium overtime and holiday rates.
-The business shall conduct an investigation to find out why production demands are leading to workers being overworked, why line supervisors / managers are threatening to punish workers if they don’t agree to work on their days-off, and why the day-off was switched without prior consultation with the workers.  Appropriate disciplinary actions should be taken against the line supervisors / managers that are found to have inappropriately extracted consent from the workers to work on their days-off.  Appropriate training should be provided to supervisors / managers to improve their behavior in this regard.  Remediate the workers for the day-off that was switched to accommodate the factory’s production schedule. 
-The business is recommended to have conversations with the workers and come to an agreement for a fixed day off. 
The business should coordinate with the production and come up with a clear process to get workers consent in order to work on their day off without any coercion. Workers have the right to refuse to work on their day off so that they can make their personal plans for the rest. 
If there is work during the day off of workers, the business shall ask workers if they would like to work on that day, and if so, the business should pay the wages according to the LPA 2x and 3x for OT during day off. 
After the investigation process, the business should conduct communication in written and verbal with all workers who have been impacted by this issue.  

Talking Points: 
-Is HR aware of this issue? If yes, what has been the action plan to solve it? 
Are there any changes on the production which caused workers to change their day off from Thursday to Tuesday?  And if so, how is the business handling the workforce?
-In order to get workers consent to work on their day off, how does the business make sure that the workers fully consent and do so voluntarily?
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara has raised this issue with Nike given that the response from the Everest management was concerning for the previous issues, however, there was no clear respond from the Nike team upon this case. Issara has requested the Nike team to have a try party call to discuss this issue  but Nike has not respond on this request for several weeks. Issara has raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they have the voluntary process for the workers to work on their day off and to agree to switch their day off.However, about the workers being assigned to do the cleaning tasks if they do not agree to work on their day off, the business responded having Five standard policy (cleaning, organizing, cleaning, standardizing, training, and discipline) and no workers to be pressured to do the cleaning. 

After the investigation result, the business responded that they have interviewed some workers and received the issues about switching day-off. For the switching day off, HR discussed and trained with production and supervisors that there would be no more switching days off, and that if they did, they would have to ask the workers and obtain their consent. Production and supervisors have received training and will proceed accordingly.

Issara is checking with the workers.
remediation_notes: Workers from Roung Thor line (Textile machines) reported they were being pressured to agree to work on their day off. The line supervisors threatened the workers saying they would be assigned to difficult jobs such as cleaning the sewers or they would be denied their diligence bonus (Bia Ka Yan) if they did not agree to work on their day off.  So, they felt they had to consent to working on their day off even if they didn’t want to do so. Workers also added that the manager switched their day off from Thursday to Tuesday without first consulting them and getting their consent.
remediation_action: Issara has raised this issue with the business, and the business responded that they have the voluntary process for the workers to work on their day-off and to agree to switch their day-off.  However, about the workers being assigned to do the cleaning tasks if they do not agree to work on their day-off, the business responded that no workers were pressured to do the cleaning. The business conducted the investigation and found that they was an issue with switching the day-off without workers' consent. HR has clarified with production managers and supervisors that there would be no more switching days-off.  If there was a need to do so, workers would need to consent before making such a switch.
remediation_validation: Issara followed up with the workers, and they have confirmed that this issue is no longer a problem.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case because the business has made it clear that there will be no switching of workers' days-off, and if such switch is needed in special cases, workers' consent would be needed before proceeding.

description: Physical and/or other serious abuse by HR/production (illegal)

call_details.next_steps: Issara to have a meeting with the business and raise the issue.

closed_notes: Nan Yang has scheduled a training for supervisors and production manager to improve their communication with their subordinates.  The workers noted that since they have raised the issue, the situation has improved, with the production manager reducing her visits to the production lines and not saying as much during such visits.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the poor treatment by the production manager. Workers who are representing the production line (3 to12 ground floor) reported unpleasant treatment of the production manager (P Mwet) who was promoted last year and managing all production lines. The workers added that the situation is significantly becoming harder since her promotion. Everytime she rounds the production, she points out mistakes and pressures the line supervisors. The line supervisors in turn pressure the workers. Workers said that if she improves the behavior, the line supervisors will also improve how they treat  the workers.  The issues that they have been facing are as follows. (i) When workers take any kind of leave, they will be treated poorly by the line supervisor the next day, because they do not want workers taking leave, (ii) Burmese workers see Thai workers taking sick leave and are paid for those days but for the Burmese workers, it is not the same and they just have to follow whatever the line supervisors say, (iii) Workers are being pressured to complete increased (unstable) targets every day. Workers reported that they had reported this issue to the HR, however, there was no proper action or improvement. 

Recommendation; 

-The business shall conduct an investigation to identify how the production manager’s and the line supervisors’ behaviors are negatively affecting the morale and performance of the Burmese workers.  The investigation should be conducted by HR and any information disclosed by workers should be kept confidential.

-To address the issue with the target setting, the HR should work with the production and revise the target setting to a reasonable and stable amount. 
Recommendations for system change. 

Talking Points: 
-What are the available grievance channels for the workers to report their issues? If any are available, has the business received such issues via available channels? 
- Workers said they went to speak with HR about these issues.  What steps has HR taken so far to address the issues?
-What targets are being set? 
-How does the business make sure or assess the target setting is reasonable and workers are not overworked? 
Time Frame ; 2 weeks.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara has raised this issue with the business, the business agreed to conduct the investigation and share the investigation result with Issara.

The business got back to Issara by saying that they will organize training that is called (individual characteristics) which is for the supervisor's ability to communicate in a way that impresses his/her subordinates. The training will be held at the end of March or early April. Issara will monitor the issues.

The worker updated by saying that since they have raised the issue, the manager has reduced her visit to the production and also does not say so many words while her visit. In general, the situation is improving, the worker said.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that since the new production manager was promoted last year, their line supervisors have been treating them poorly.  The production manager is pointing out mistakes and pressures the line supervisors, and in turn supervisors are pressuring the workers.  If a worker takes leave, the supervisor will treat them poorly the next day and show signs that he is displeased that the worker was off work.  They have found it hard to get approved for sick leave compared to Thai workers who don't seem to have any such problems.  Workers are also being pressured to complete targets that seem to be increasing unpredictably.  Workers reported this issue to the HR but they have not seen any response or improvement.
remediation_action: The business got back to Issara by saying that they will organize training for supervisors to improve their communication with their subordinates, to be held at the end of March or early April.
remediation_validation: The worker updated by saying that since they have raised the issue, the manager has reduced her visits to the production lines and also does not say as much during such visits. The worker noted that in general, the situation was improving.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case because the business has scheduled a training for supervisors & production manager to improve their communication with their subordinates.  The workers noted that since they have raised the issue, the situation has improved, with the production manager reducing her visits to the production lines and not saying as much during such visits.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
-All workers should be introduced to the business grievance channels and encouraged to use any channel (both internal and external, such as Issara) that they feel comfortable using. 
-When communicating grievance channels with all employees, the business should also explain how workers’ grievances are managed and how safeguards are kept for the workers.
-Issara can help review the announcement text that the business will communicate with the workers regarding this issue. 
-Issara will arrange a training event for line supervisors and the HR staff this year, and we will invite the business to participate.

description: Issues with workforce and workloads: no violation of law or employment contract
closed_notes: Issara has checked with the workers, and they said the set targets are very difficult for them to achieve.  They have to work without taking toilet breaks in order to reach the target if they want to get OT work.  Issara tried to reach out to more workers; however, we were not able to talk with the workers from this production line. Since the business did not show any interest to make changes, Issara decided to close this case until further worker reports.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with a heavy workload and the OT hours in the PR production line. Workers reported that the workload increased from 80%-85% to 95% about 20 days ago and it is very stressful for the workers. Workers reported that they do not get OT working hours if they do not reach the set target.  Workers want the business to revise the target to a reasonable workload.  

-The business to conduct the investigation on this working line to assess how targets are being set, and why the target has been increased. The investigation should include production (whoever is responsible for setting targets) and also feedback from workers, to determine between all parties what are realistic targets, and how to manage the workload with the current workforce. 
- Based on the results of the investigation and analysis of the targets, the business should change the target. 
-In addition, the business should make sure workers are not coerced by supervisors or anyone to reach targets through threat of withholding OT working hours. Therefore, it is recommended for the business to clarify to line supervisors from the specific PR  line and to workers that this is not aligned with the company policy and if workers have any issues with this again they are encouraged to use the business grievance mechanism and report it.  

System Change; 

-All line supervisors, production staff and the workers should receive written and verbal communication that reaching production targets must not be forced on the workers by threat of withholding other benefits such as the opportunity to work and get paid OT hours.  The communication should note that any supervisor that tries to force workers to meet production targets in any way will face disciplinary measures. 
-Recommend training to line supervisors and managers on ethics and fair treatment towards workers. 
-Issara can also provide tailored training to full HR teams, and provide systems review and feedback from workers to eliminate labor risks.


Talking Points:
-Who sets the targets and how are targets set?
-How often does the business review and set production targets? Are workers consulted when setting such targets?
-Workers mentioned that they are being threatened in different ways if they don’t reach the increased target.  What is the business understanding of this, has this been reported by workers, and if so, what actions has the business taken so far? 
-How many workers are there in each production line? 

Time Frame 1 week.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara raised this issue with the Director of Quality System from the business, the business responded that it is the business policy to set the target based on the worker's experiences and if the workers do not reach the set target according to the business standard target setting, the business does not provide Over Time work to them. The business also added that they also do not provide Over Time work if a worker takes leave without notifying the business. To solve this issue, the business updated that they have communicated with the workers about the business policy.

Issara has checked with the workers, the workers said that the set target is very heavy for them. They have to work without taking a toilet break in order to reach the target and get Over Time Work. Issara tried to reach out to more workers, however, was not able to talk with the workers from this production line. Since the business did not show interest to make changes, Issara decided to close this case until further report.
remediation_notes: The issue with a heavy workload and the OT hours in the PR production line. Workers reported that the workload increased from 80%-85% to 95% about 20 days ago and it is very stressful for the workers. Workers reported that they do not get OT working hours if they do not reach the set target.  Workers want the business to revise the target to a reasonable workload.
remediation_action: Issara raised this issue with the business, and the business responded that it is the business policy to set the target based on the worker's number of years' experience and if the workers reach the target and perform well, then they will be given overtime work. The business has announced this policy to workers so that they understand the basis on which OT work is offered to workers.
remediation_validation: Issara has checked with the workers, and they said that the set target is very difficult for them to achieve.  They have to work without taking toilet breaks in order to reach the target and get OT work. Issara tried to reach out to more workers, however, was not able to talk with the workers from this production line.

call_details.description:
On April 27, 2023, a worker from Line 29 was sick and took sick leave, but he failed to inform the line supervisor because the supervisor did not pick up his call twice. On the next day, he showed his medical certificate, but it was not accepted and remarked as an absent day by the supervisor. On the payday of May 4, he found out that there was no pay for that day.

He went to the HR office and met P' Dao, who is an HR staff member, and then he was brought upstairs to a meeting room to meet some other HR staff. Finally, the line supervisor arrived at the office and confirmed that he was not entitled to receive the daily wage. He was told that he should call him until he picked up the call. Then he was scolded and told that he would be provided with a warning letter if he raised the issue like this in the future. (That's why he is worried about safeguarding.)

Note: Line 29 has no specific line supervisor. That supervisor is kind of the head or chief of line supervisors, supervising 5–6 lines in total, such as lines 25, 26, 27, 29, 30, and 31. Other workers who requested annual leave in advance also had similar experiences in the past. They were not approved to take annual leave by that supervisor. During the survey as well, some workers raised concerns about this supervisor's behavior of yelling at the workers and not listening to their voices.

Risk: The worker reached out to HR staff for his case on payday (May 4, 2023), and he was well-noticed by the chief supervisor, who threatened him. That's why he does not want to mention his name and get back his daily wage. He just wants the supplier to effectively provide warnings or train all the supervisors as a general rule.

On June 19, the head of supervisors asked him to sew 70–80 pieces of clothing in an hour. He told her that the most he could sew was 40. The supervisor was angry with him and asked him to go work on a different line.

He feels that the supervisor targets him by asking for a higher target workload. He asked whether Issara had already reached out to the employer.
