remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker said he didn't receive his wage for one sick leave day (27 April 2023) because he failed to inform his supervisor. He tried to call both the supervisor and assistant supervisor to inform them but they did not pick up his calls. Even though he had a medical certificate for this sick day, HR still did not agree to pay him for that day.

NOTE: The worker doesn't want to be identified and he doesn't want to get the sick leave pay back. He just wants the supplier to effectively provide warnings or train all the supervisors.

The head of supervisors is female, P' Pyin. She used to be responsible for lines 25, 26, 27, 29, 30, and 31 on the third floor in the past. Now she is working on lines 11 and 12. He said that the HR office would know if he said the production line. Many of the workers do not like her because she always asks them to move from here to there without any reason and always yells at them.

TPs:
- Make sure the business provides safeguards to workers for having reported any issues
- What is the business policy about getting approval for sick leave? If a worker doesn't inform his supervisor about sick leave, will the business withhold payment for that day?

Recommendations:
- Whether a worker informs the business about one's sick leave or not, the worker should still be paid for those days, especially if the worker presents a medical certificate
- The business should allow workers multiple channels to inform the business when they are sick and will be absent from work.  Communicate this clearly to workers, verbally and in writing.
remediation_business_steps_taken: After the remediation call on 20 July 2023, Nan Yang NKPT called for a meeting with the line supervisors in the same month and discussed with them about sick leave and medical certificate. Line supervisors cannot ask the worker for a medical certificate for a one-day sick leave, but 3 days can. BHR called Nan Yang NKPT today and gave them the info of that line supervisor (P Pyin, line no. 12). The business is happy to investigate again in more detail, and will get back to Issara at the end of next week.

remediation_action:
After discussing this issue with Issara, HR called a meeting with the line supervisors and discussed with them about sick leave and medical certificate, that line supervisors cannot ask a worker for a medical certificate for 1-2 days of sick leave. In a follow-up meeting, Issara provided the business with information on the production line number where this issue occurred. The business will investigate, and will get back to Issara.

In the latest update, the business trained line supervisors on the company's policy and procedures for annual and sick leave.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the food supplies during workers' quarantine and the condition of the quarantine center. Workers reported that they are identified as COVID-19 positive and placed to stay quarantined in a facility that used to be a chicken coop. The facility still has a bad smell which workers find difficult to tolerate. In addition to that, the workers said they have to pay for the meals (80 B for meals) and drinking water each day, and the cost is quite high for them

Issara recommendations;
-As an employer, the business is suggested to reconsider reducing the price for the meals or provide it for free if possible.
-Provide a feedback channel so that workers in quarantine can communicate their issues regarding the facilities and services to the business
-Make improvements to the quarantine facility being used, such as sanitizing the structure and surrounding areas to eliminate the strong odor that is making it difficult for workers to stay there
 
Talking points
-How many workers have been tested and found positive so far? How has the business managed infected workers? Have they been tested by government officials? 
-How has the business managed the quarantine center and provided the food and other basic needs for the workers during their quarantine?




Update from the government regarding quarantine rule; 

Infected workers currently have the right to take sick leave and be paid in accordance with the LPA. Workers/employees can receive a free recovery in accordance with their Social Security. The quarantine costs (stay and food) are determined by the symptom and group of Green, Yellow, and Red (UCEP PLUS). If the workers are in the green group, they will have to do the home isolation and there will be no food provided; the workers will only be given medicine. However, the yellow and red workers must be admitted to the hospital, where food and a bed will be provided. However, in the case of providing food, the government encourages employers to provide food and a place for infected workers, according to the Department of Communicable Disease Control, but there is no law requiring employers to do so. According to the Department of Communicable Disease Control, for the factory sandbox, it just happened last year, that the big factories only (over 500 workers) must have a quarantine center and make sure that the employees must be quarantined and no movement to another area to prevent infection.

In addition to that, the workers said they have to pay for the meals (80 Baht for meals) and drinking water each day, and the cost is quite high for them

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client reported that there were 4 workers, including him, who went back to Myanmar on 21 May 2023 with other workers, and they have the issue with getting their passports from Myanmar. There are almost 50 workers who did U-Turn with them and other workers got their passports and they have already signed the contract and are about to come back to Thailand.
When they called and checked with Ko Phyo Min Hlaing, representative of Aung Pyae recruitment agency in Myanmar, he said that their passports got retained by the government as their names are similar to the CDM (Civil Disobedience Movement) staff.  It meant that their passports did not pass the screening process in terms of validating whether the passport' holders are non-involved in anti-government activities. It meant that in order the workers need to get their passport, they will be under interrogation whether they are involved in anti-government activity or not. This kind of interrogation process is a bit scary as they will be tortured. So Ko Phyo Min Hlaing told them if you give 5,000,000 MMK or you will be taking interrogation.
The workers are not afraid to deal with the government if they will be asked some questions. But, they are worried that sometimes, the staff who are involved in the interrogation process are trying to ask the money and they will be tortured even they can give the reason and don't want to pay money.
They have already reported this to the HT-91 line group for "MOU U-Turn". The workers seek help if the business can give them any support regarding this issue. They assured that they are not involved in any kind of anti-government activities. He said both the interpreter and the manager were aware of this.
The manager said that they will only take care of those who got the passports already and will come back soon. They will not take any responsibility to these 4 workers regarding this passport issue. Now, he has already left the line group.
The workers are reaching out to us to see if we can give any support to them or not. The workers add that if the business cannot do anything, they will try to come back to Thailand from illegal channels and try to register for pink cards as the deadline is until 31 Jul 2023.
O&E recommendation:
It would be great if we can check with businesses whether they can give any recommendation letter stating that these workers are working in the factory and not involved in any kind of political activities. Also, it would be good if the business can coordinate with the Myanmar Embassy to approve their recommendation letter too. This would help the workers when the workers have to talk with the government staff on the Myanmar side. From the RA side, I think it's a bit unethical to give the option to the workers like 5,000,000 MMK or you will be interrogated. They should try to coordinate with the government and explain the workers' situation instead.

Here are the workers names and ID cards no. while they worked in HT-91.
1. AUNG THURA (91190603052)
2. THANT ZIN (91190603018)
3. PYONE MOH MOH (91190603119)
4. THIRI SHAN (91190603039)

Recommendations:
- The business to discuss with the RA immediately to ensure that the RA does not collect any fees and helps the workers show they are not involved in anti-government activities and their passports are processed without further delay
- Make every effort to ensure that workers can get their passports
- If providing a letter by the business will help this matter to allow the Myanmar government to issue their passports, the business should provide such a letter to the RA for submission to the government
- Communicate with and update workers what actions the business and RA are taking to help them get their passports
remediation_business_steps_taken: Hi Tech 91 will give the allowance (100 THB per day, excluding Sunday) to the 3 workers starting from 22 May to 2 August 2023.
remediation_notes: The business sent almost 50 workers to Myanmar on May 21, 2023 for the MOU U-turn process but for 4 workers, the government has denied issuing their passports, suspecting them of being involved in anti-government efforts.  The workers have not been involved in such activities, and don't want to pay any money to get their passports but the recruitment agency informed them that they need to pay 5 million kyats or submit to government interrogation.  Since then, 3 or the 4 workers traveled to Thailand using informal channels while one remained in Myanmar.
remediation_action:
The business will investigate with the Myanmar recruitment agency. If there are any fees and costs incurred, they will be responsible for this. First, they will check with the recruitment agency whether the workers are involved with anti-government efforts or not. If not, the business will try to see how they can help the workers get their passports issued. 

Issara escalated this issue with senior management. He noted that he was aware of this case, and suggested that the 3 workers that traveled to Thailand go back to Myanmar to get their passports and come back legally again to Thailand as part of the new MOU batch in early December this year (Hi Tech 91 has a plan to hire 100 new MOU workers). During this time that the workers have to wait, HI Tech 91 offered to give 6,000 Baht allowance every month. But if the workers decided not to go back to Myanmar, they could apply to work at Hi Tech again once they had the proper working documents and cancellation letters from the previous employer.

Issara updated the business that the 3 workers remaining in Thailand requested the 3,000 Baht monthly allowance. The business will pay this allowance to the workers from 22 May 2023 (the day the workers went back to Myanmar to do the MoU U-Turn) until 3 August 2023 (the day the worker start working with the new employers).
remediation_validation:
Issara updated the workers about the options they had after having the escalation call with the business. For the one worker still in Myanmar, she will wait to come back in December in the next MOU batch and is very happy to know about the 6,000 Baht monthly allowance (increased from 3,000 Baht) during the waiting period. 

For the other 3 workers already in Thailand, they said they would not to go back to Myanmar, and will apply to Hi Tech again after they receive the proper working documents and cancellation letters from their current employer. They all confirmed receiving the 3,000 Baht monthly allowance for the two months they were in Myanmar.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case. The business will complete the U-turn process for one worker in Myanmar in the next batch and the other workers received the monthly allowance for the time they were in Myanmar.

call_details.description:
Worker from this factory called and reported following two issues. 

(1) Lack of supplies during quarantine period; Worker reported that once they are identified as COVID-19 infected or suspected/high risk workers, they have to stay quarantine. 10 days of quarantine for infected workers and 7 days for close contact. However, the business does not provide any foods or even water. If there is a wife being infected, the husband or the family member also has to stay quarantine. It means the whole family members have to stay quarantine and have no access to the foods or water. Workers want the business to provide supplies or assign someone to help them purchase. 

(2) The issue with expense of ATK test kits; If a worker is infected or suspected, have to do ATK test. If a worker feel sick, she has to do the ATK test and also go to the hospital. Once they go to the hospital, the hospital will do the PCR test and confim her to stay 10 days of quarantine. Once they complete the quarantine, on the day 10th they have to do ATK test, on the day 11th another ATK test and on the day 15th follo up test. Total around 4 ATK test for both infected and the suspected workers. The business does not pay for those test kits. Workers find it expensive to pay for the several kits. They want the business to reduce some of the test process and also provde ATK test for free. Once, the worker have approached the HR and requested for the free test, the HR said that even Thai staff have to buy by themselves. 

(3) The issue with the wages for the quarantine period; Follow up on the previous issue where the business used to deduct workers annual leaves for high risks workers quarantine days. The worker said that the business has verbally communicated that they will pay for any kind of qarantine. If a worker is suspected or high risk and have to stay quarantine, the business will pay wages as a special wages. No any leaves will be deducted. For infected workers, the hospital provides MC which can be used for sick leave. Wokrer said that they do not have issue with the wages during their quaratine these days.
Follow up call with the client to check the updates about her relative recruitment process.
call_details.next_steps:
Have to close the case with Annual leave and sick leave, expense on ATK test, and quarantine condition
But, have to follow up with business about the other remaining workers of her relatives. Currently, O&E suggest the client to check with HT70 interpreter about job available in HT70 again.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Lack of food and water supplies during quarantine period; Workers who have to stay quarantined for being suspected or being tested positive reported not receiving food and water supplies. They said that if a family member is found to be positive all of the family members have to stay in quarantine but the business does not help the workers for their basic needs including food and water. Workers find it challenging to survive during their quarantine periods.

Recommendation; 
-The business should assign an HR focal point and introduce  him/her with the workers to contact to get the supplies they need during their quarantine. The business should make sure that all workers who are in quarantine have proper meals and medical support as needed. 
-The assigned person should be trained by the business on how to professionally and ethically help quarantined workers if there is a need and the focal person needs to do the purchase with their money. All of the purchases should be recorded by the quarantined workers and cleared between the focal and the workers. 
-Workers to be introduced and encouraged to reach and use internal business grievance channels if they have any issues or concerns. The introduction of the internal channels should explain how the issues will be confidentially managed and ensure the safeguard for the workers.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara has shared this issue with the business, the HR director who joined the meeting with Issara was not aware of this issue. The business will conduct the investigation and get back to Issara.

Workers have confirmed that there are no workers having to do the quarantine at the moment.
remediation_notes: Workers needing to quarantine for Covid-19 were not provided with food and water supplies during the quarantine period.  They are finding it a challenge to get their own food and water during the quarantine period.
remediation_action: The business responded that it made the announcement to workers that high-risk workers can go out to buy food by themselves, but must wear masks at all times, keep social distancing, and don't go to areas with large numbers of people.  The business noted that currently no workers are in quarantine, as they have recovered and returned to work.
remediation_validation: Workers have confirmed that all have completed their quarantine periods and have returned to work.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case because the workers that originally reported lack of access to food and water during quarantine were told they could go out to get their own supplies and have since all completed their quarantine and returned to work.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the sick leave of the workers. Workers reported not receiving paid sick leave when they take sick leave. Workers said that the process for taking sick leave is to report to the supervisor, however it is unpaid. In addition to this, the workers who have to quarantine for being COVID-19 positive reported not receiving paid for those days. 

Recommendations:
-For the issue with the quarantine days, the business should follow the latest government regulations related to quarantine periods for Covid positive and close contact cases and how pay for missed working days due to quarantine is to be handled
We have received the update that the government regulations are as follows:  
-If a worker is found to be positive at the factory, she/he is supposed to be sent to the hospital for the PCR test and if confirmed as positive, receive the medical certificate and recommended to quarantine. The worker should get paid sick leave during those days. 
-If a worker is a close contact, s/he should visit the hospital and report why she/he is at high risk and get the recommendations from the hospital. The regular recommendations for vaccinated people is to take 10 days of quarantine and do another test on the 10th day. 
-If the result is negative, then the worker can start working. In terms of the wages for the high risk workers who have a medical certificate for their quarantine days, the employer can submit the worker information to the SSF for the 62% of wages. 
-If the worker is not allowed to go to the hospital but the employer orders the worker to take quarantine, it is the responsibility of the employer to pay the worker wages. 
-The business should communicate with the workers about how quarantine days will be paid.

-The issue with the unpaid not COVID-19 related issues;  the business should have the policy for paid sick leave. LPA related to the sick leave should be explained with the business. 
-The business should have a clear  process for the workers in order to take sick leave, how it is requested, when, and to whom, including the communication channel.  For sick leave that is less than 3 consecutive days, the Medical Certificate is not required
-For the workers who have already taken sick leave and have not been paid, the business should check the record for the past 6 months and repay the impacted workers. 
-Issara can help with the written and the verbal communications with the workers. In addiiton to that, Issara can also provide training to the HR and supervisors on the management of the foreign workers and the workers rights. 

Time Frame; 2 weeks.
remediation_notes: The issue with the sick leave of the workers. Workers reported not receiving paid sick leave when they take sick leave. Workers said that the process for taking sick leave is to report to the supervisor, however it is unpaid. In addition to this, the workers who have to quarantine for being COVID-19 positive reported not receiving paid for those days.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1: Workers reported that there has not been clear communication from the business about the process for getting their OWIC cards and all this time, their passports and work permits are being retained by the business. It has been months now and workers have been hearing from other people that the Myanmar Embassy has temporarily suspended issuing OWIC cards and they may need to do it in Myanmar.  Now they only have copies of their passports.

Recommendations:
- Workers should have access to their identity documents, and should not be retained by the business for months 
- Communicate clearly to workers about the timeline and when workers can get their identity documents back
- If the OWIC process is suspended, return passports and WPs to workers until this process can be re-started

Case #2: A worker had been working in TUM until 2023 June had returned to Myanmar for U-Turn Process. His wife went back to Myanmar with a TUM arrangement on 1st June 2023 along with other 141 workers. Before the U Turn trip, Ms. Lin ( Myanmar translator) announced that all workers will be called back as U Turn MOU and the business will still pay for the holiday wages while they are staying in Myanmar. However, it has been 6th month TUM hasn't give any information of when they will be  called back and which agency will the workers contact. 

Recommendations:
- Provide clear information to workers currently waiting in Myanmar since June 2023 about the U-turn process, what will happen when, and which RA to contact in Myanmar
- Maintain channels of communication with this group, such as via FB messenger group, and send update announcements on a regular basis.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
# Issue 1: 
Context: Issara received this issue in our housing outreach to Cal-Comp (SMSK) on April 3, 2022.  According to workers that we met at the "pink" dormitory, they heard about other workers having to pay around 5,000 Baht to brokers to get a job at Cal-Comp in Samut Sakhon. And they also heard that workers have to pay 1,000 Baht to brokers to get job cancellation letters.

Recommendations for remediation: 
-The business to do an immediate investigation to assess the number of impacted workers and identify the people involved in the recruitment process that has been charging workers. Worker safeguards should be in place throughout the investigation, and workers should not be retaliated against for having spoken out. 
-The investigation should also cover the staff from the recruitment agencies to identify the root causes of the issue and understand who was involved in the collection of the money.
- Disciplinary actions should be taken towards those who collected the money, and the business should clarify with the recruitment agency involved that no fees should be charged to workers and the consequences for not following that policy, such as termination of the contract or disciplinary actions if those involved are Cal-Comp  employees. 
-As part of the investigation and remediation process, the business shall assess how much money workers have paid and reimburse such amounts. 

-The business should set a plan of action with the recruitment agency involved, such as revision of the contract and the penalties for not following the company policy about “zero recruitment fees for workers”, and the actions the agency will take to avoid this from happening again.
remediation_notes: According to workers that we met at the "pink" dormitory during a housing outreach on April 3, 2022, they heard about other workers having to pay around 5,000 Baht to brokers to get a job at Cal-Comp in Samut Sakhon. And they also heard that workers have to pay 1,000 Baht to brokers to get job cancellation letters.
remediation_action: The business responded that it hasn't recruited any workers in 2022, and therefore there couldn't have been any cases of workers having to pay to get a job at Cal-Comp SMSK.
remediation_validation: Issara followed up with workers at this factory and one confirmed that there had been no hiring of migrant workers in 2022.  He also noted that he wasn't aware of recruitment agents charging money for cancellation letters and didn't know of anyone that faced this problem.  The original report may have been about fees charged by brokers prior to 2022; however, Issara has lost contact with the workers that first reported this issue.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue because we have lost contact with the workers that first spoke about this issue and other workers are not aware of fees being charged to job seekers recently.  However, the business could have done more to investigate this issue more closely, whether there had been such practices by recruiters prior to 2022.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for systems change
- The business should should develop vetting and selection criteria for the recruitment agencies it will work with.  Issara can provide support with the vetting and selection tool
- Do a full review of current recruitment agencies in Thailand and source countries using the vetting and selection criteria, and consider which RAs to continue working with, which it will stop working with, or new RAs to work with in the future
- Review the management service agreements with each RA, update the MSAs to ensure transparency and zero fees for workers.  Develop MSAs with source country RAs directly.  Issara can provide support with the MSA checklist tool
- Check all job vacancy announcements that its RAs are posting, ensure the announcements make the zero fee policy explicit
- Provide full and accurate job description information for all future job vacancies to the RAs

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case.  The business has stated that it is currently not covering the fees for the pink card application and currently is not able to implement the zero fee recruitment of workers.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: A woroker from ISA Value stated that he came to Thailand via the undocumented channel in October 2021 and started working on Oct 2021 and the business collected 2,450 Baht after 15 days of working in ISA Value for pink card application. The client said, in his recruitment journey, he had to pay transportation fees and other expenses from his own pocket.

NOTE* I would suggest generally sharing the issue and also giving some example based on this issue but not sharing the information of the worker. 

TPs:
- What are the company’s current hiring practices, whether through the formal MOU channel or hiring walk-in workers already in Thailand?
- Is it aware of Amazon’s Employer Pays Policy and the company’s obligation to ensure that workers don’t pay for any recruitment-related fees or expenses?

Recommendations for remediation: 
-The business to do an immediate investigation to assess the number of impacted workers and identify the people involved in the recruitment process that has been charging workers. Worker safeguards should be in place throughout the investigation, and workers should not be retaliated against for having spoken out. 
- Disciplinary actions should be taken towards those who collected the money, and the consequences for not following that policy, such as disciplinary actions if those involved are ISA Value staff. 
-As part of the investigation and remediation process, the business shall assess how much money workers have paid and reimburse such amounts. 
-Request to conduct workers recruitment fees survey by Issara.
remediation_business_steps_taken: The ISA Value recruitment policy still requires the worker to pay for the document. They intend to be the employer step by step, such as which fees and costs should be covered by the employer. Work permit 1,450 and health issurance 990 and stamp 10.
remediation_notes: A worker stated that he had migrated to Thailand via the undocumented channel in October 2021 and found work at this business through his sister's introduction who is already working here. He said the business collected 2,450 Baht from him for the pink card application.
remediation_action: The company's recruitment policy still requires the worker to pay for the recruitment-related fees of personal document processing. They intend to gradually implement the Employer Pays Policy in phases.
remediation_validation: Issara has not been able to re-contact the worker.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case.  The business has stated that it is currently not covering the fees for the pink card application and currently is not able to implement the zero fee recruitment of workers.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for systems change
- The business should review its current hiring practices, including how it is hiring workers that are already in Thailand or those that may have migrated to Thailand recently but not through the MOU channel
- Ensure that for all new hires, it is fully compliant with the Employer Pays Policy
- Attend the second ER training for Amazon suppliers, which will be scheduled later this year (tentatively Oct or Nov 2022)

call_details.description:

Shift:                        Night
Line supervisor:        Thai lady (Tom boy, she has a mole on her nose)

She, Shwe Wine Hlaing, reported that she was physically abused again. The incident happened on 11 June at Sushi line while working. At 11pm, the workers were at Sushi line were about to have meal break. SWH was given a large amount of shrimps by the line supervisor who abused her. Some of the shrimp dropped. She was asked to pick them up. She refused to do it as it was not her fault and she wanted to have a meal break. That’s when the line supervisor hit her arm with shrimp basket. It was witnessed by many other workers. When she told the line supervisor that she would report it to HR, the supervisor replied “I don’t care anyone. You can report it to anywhere you want”. 
SWH said, “Although I know that HR would not resolve the issue properly, I still want HR knows about the abuse.” I know that I have been targeted for so many times and no serious action was taken by HR. I have been asked to move across the different lines although I meet the target. I hope that Issara could help me. 
She thinks that it will be good for her to work at Cut Size lines (day shift), to get away from abuse.

call_details.description:
Issue no.1: Forcing the Workers to do OT
The client said that the line supervisor (blue head) named P'Soup asked forcing the workers to do OT. If the workers missed OT for one day, he punished the workers not to do OT for two weeks. 
He is from UC1, in line no.2.

Issue no.2: Discrimination and Verbal Abusive
This line supervisor also talked loudly and scolded the workers if the workers did something wrong in the production line. For a Thai worker, he used a soft voice and reminded them please don't do that again or be careful while he should the Burmese workers, what's wrong with your poor eyes? You cannot check it clearly etc? The workers feel not happy with his bias behavior between Thai and Burmese workers.
call_details.referral_notes: Have to update in SC meeting and close the case

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case with a "poor" rating because the business has not actively sought to investigate the matter and the worker directly affected has already left the factory.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the poor treatment of the supervisor. Workers said that the supervisor from UC1, in line no.2 (blue hat) named P'Soup is abusive toward migrant workers. He treats Burmese workers more poorly than Thai workers. The abusive words that he uses are such as, yelling, saying “what’s wrong with your poor eyes, can’t you check it clearly, And so on. In addition to that workers said that the supervisor also indirectly forces them to do OT. If a worker do not agree or refuse to do OT, the supervisor will not provide OT for the next 15 days. Workers want the supervisors to treat them equally and be fair with the OT hours. 

TPs:
Has the business received any complaint from workers about this supervisor? If yes, what was the action that has been taken? 
What is the OT distribution system? What happens if a worker does not sign up to work OT on any given day?  Does this affect OT hours offered to the worker in the future?
What channels are available for workers to report any issues? How are these channels being communicated to the workers? Are the business channels being used by the workers (if any)? 

Recommendations for remediation:
The business to conduct an investigation about the behavior of this supervisor. The investigation process should include worker voice and safeguards in place so that workers don’t suffer any retaliation as a result.
Disciplinary action should be taken if the supervisor is found guilty of having mistreated and discriminated against the workers. 
The business should also make a clear announcement to the workers about its zero tolerance against discrimination and verbal abuse in the workplace, and the OT distribution policy.


Code: ETI Base Code 6.3. Working hours are not excessive; all OT is voluntary and paid at a premium rate no less than 125% of regular pay
Description: All overtime shall be voluntary. Overtime shall be used responsibly, taking into account all the following: the extent, frequency and hours worked by individual workers and the 
workforce as a whole. It shall not be used to replace regular employment. Overtime shall always be compensated at a premium rate, which is recommended to be not less than 125% of the regular rate of pay.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that their supervisor was abusive toward migrant workers, treating them more harshly than Thai workers. The supervisor would yell at the migrant workers saying "what’s wrong with your poor eyes, can’t you check it clearly?"
remediation_action: HR said if Issara could provide more information for the worker issue, it would be better for the HR team to go and investigate the matter. HR said the business had not received any complaints from the workers about this supervisor.
remediation_validation: Issara followed up with the worker and he noted that he had heard about this supervisor behavior from others but did not work directly under the supervisor. His friend who had told him about this supervisor had already left the factory along with 15 other workers.  Currently, he noted that the supervisor was being quiet and no longer yelling at the workers.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case because the business has not actively sought to investigate the matter and the worker directly affected has already left the factory.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations for systems change:
Provide a refresher to all supervisors about the company’s policies against discrimination and verbal abuse, the fair and voluntary OT system, and how they are to implement them in practice

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that her sister in a group of 34 workers (referred to as "MOU 19 Group") had been sent back to Myanmar on 27 May 2023 for the MOU U-turn process but when they checked with the RA (Arbourfield) on 13 Nov 2023, the RA told them that they would not be employed any longer by SF-2513.

TPs:
- What was communicated to this group of workers regarding the MOU process, such as the procedure and timeline?

Recommendations:
- The business should take responsibility and complete the U-turn process for this group of workers, as originally promised, and that they will return and continue working with SF-2513.
- Communicate clearly with the RA and the group of workers so that all parties are clear about the business decision
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 20 Nov 2023

K Sophon and K Supreeya, HR stated that the MoU Group 19 was the end of the MoU contract. They insist that they did not promise the workers that they would do the MoU U-Turn process, but they did tell the workers that if they wanted to apply for a job at Siam Food 2513 again, they could submit their passport and application to the recruitment agency in advance, and when the company has job vacancies or decides to recruit MoU, they would be prioritized because they are former workers with experience. However, the company has yet to make a decision. The MoU workers will most likely be recruited in April 2024. So, as previously stated, they will communicate clearly with the workers again by next week.

DATE: 23 Nov 2023

According to K. Sophon, HR Director, there is currently no final decision to submit the demand name list for the MoU U-Turn for this group. They are holding internal discussions to determine when the workers will be hired back. They used to collaborate with Golden Gate (Thai RA), who in turn collaborated with Abourfield (Myanmar RA). They are, however, evaluating Golden Gate and Abourfied and looking for other recruitment agencies as options. They will most likely work directly with the source side recruitment agency. They will use the heatmap that Issara shared for their consideration as well.  In terms of the miscommunication caused by the interpreter, they will investigate and communicate clearly to the workers when they will hire the worker back and by which recruitment agency.


DATE: 1 Dec 2023

Issara shared a screenshot of the Line group in which the interpreter communicated with the workers about applying for new passports for the MoU U-Turn. K. Sophon, HR Director, responded that he needs to have an additional investigation with the HR team and the interpreter. If this is the case, he will consult with management. 1. The rationale for moving forward with this MoU U-Turn group 2. Reimburse workers for the passport fee and costs. So we agreed to meet again on December 7 to discuss the corrective action plan.

DATE: 7 Dec 2023

The meeting was attended by K. Sophon, HR Director, K. Supreeya, HR Manager, and an interpreter. They insisted that the company had not yet decided to submit the demand with the name list to initiate the MoU U-Turn process. However, the interpreter only communicated with the workers so they to prepare the documents, which the workers misinterpreted. However, they would like to work with Issara to find a solution. By preparing a budget to present to their management for reimbursement to workers who will return to the company. They would like Issara's assistance in clarifying the passport fee standard through a recruitment agency rather than a broker.  They also stated that they are considering hiring a new recruitment agency and will use our ER toolkit- RA vetting and selection tool to do so. They will most likely submit this list of workers' names in January 2024, and the workers will be able to return by April 2024, but they must wait for the final decision from their management with the budget proposal with the recruitment agency. So we decided on the following steps.
1. Issara can assist SF2513 in determining the legal passport fee (apply through a recruitment agency rather than a broker).
2. Issara assists in communicating with the workers that they currently have the option of applying to another factory; if the workers still want to return to work at Siam Food Factory, they must wait for the company's decision, and the workers will be on the top list for name list and will be reimbursed.
3. After receiving the passport fee information from Issara, they will prepare a budget to present to their management for the MoU U-Turn process with reimbursement.
4. The company will notify Issara in January 2024 with an update on the MoU U-Turn process and confirmation.

DATE: 13 Dec 2023
K. Sophon, HR Director clarified that The company is considering when to bring in these two Myanmar workers. In this case, the company will use the average fee of 3,000 Baht and explain it to the workers so that they understand. Furthermore, the company will reimburse the travel expenses according to company policy.

remediation_action:
The business responded that for this group, their MOU contracts had ended and they did not promise the workers that they would be hired back as MOU U-turn workers. They only told them that they could re-apply and if the company had job vacancies, they would be prioritized for hiring. However, the company has yet to make a decision on hiring more workers and any MOU workers will most likely be recruited only in April 2024 after submitting the name list in January 2024.

HR clarified that the company will consider re-hiring these workers, and reimburse 3,000 Baht for the passport fee and will also cover the travel expenses according to company policy.
remediation_validation:
Workers updated that they have since heard that the business is considering the MOU U-turn process for them and are looking to select a Myanmar recruitment agency to handle this process.

These workers are very disappointed because they paid high passport costs through a broker to expedite the process (there are currently huge delays in processing passports) in anticipation of returning to work with the company. 

Issara provided an update to workers about the company's position in terms of when they may be re-hired and what costs would be reimbursed by the employer, such as the 3,000 Baht for the passport fee and travel expenses. Two workers are going to wait to return to work here while the others are not willing to wait so long.

description: Issues with breaks including lunch/bathroom/OT breaks: minor issue with no violation of law or employment contract

call_details.description:
The client reported that the factory has split two lunch breaks for the workers in the east building and west building. The 1st break starts from 11:30 AM to 12:30 PM and the 2nd break starts from 12:30 to 1:30 PM. The workers in the east building have to hit the 1st break for half  month, and another half month they have to hit the second break as they have to switch the break time with the workers in the west building. It means that every worker has to switch break times every two weeks. The unstable lunch break creates the problem with the workers' stomach habits. For example, workers are just getting used to eating at 12:30 PM and after 15 days, they have to go and eat at 11:30 AM although they are not hungry. As well as while they are getting used to eat at 11:30 AM and when they have to change and eat at 12:30 PM, they are starving at that time. 
So this kind of business management with break times is not convenient for the workers anymore. The business has applied this policy since the Covid-19 outbreak and it's been for almost a year. The workers would like to request if they can go back to normal or if the business can set them stable time for lunch break and not let them change every two weeks.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case because the business has addressed the situation by consulting the workers through the worker welfare committee and settling on the decision to have consistent lunch times for the workers as was the request of many workers.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client reported that the factory has two lunch breaks for the workers in the east and west buildings, with the 1st break from 11:30AM to 12:30PM and the 2nd break from 12:30 to 1:30PM. The workers have lunch during one break for two weeks and then switch to the other break hour every two weeks.  This frequent change in the lunch hour is negatively affecting the workers.  Those used to eating in the earlier hour feel starved when they have to switch to the later hour; when they have to switch back to the earlier hour again, they don’t feel hungry enough.  The business has applied this policy since the Covid-19 outbreak and it's been for almost a year. The workers would like to request that the business allow them to eat at the same time each day rather than having to switch back and forth every two weeks. 

Recommendations for remediation:
The business to survey the workers and respond to the workers’ needs by adjusting the lunch break time so that it doesn’t disrupt their regular eating cycles
remediation_business_steps_taken: The company has decided to fix the lunch break so that workers don't need to change their lunch hour every two weeks.  The business will hold a communication session with the workers to inform them that the lunch break time will be fixed and will not be changed.

remediation_action: The business will consider setting the lunch shift so workers don’t switch back and forth; however, it found that some other workers are not happy with this situation.  The business will consult with the welfare committee and propose a solution.  After further consultation, the business has set the lunch shift so that workers don't have to switch back and forth from one lunch hour to the other every two weeks.
remediation_validation: Issara followed up with the workers and they confirmed that the lunch shift is now set so that workers from the east building get one hour and workers from the west building get another hour.  They are happy with this arrangement.

call_details.description:
This call is to Thinzar Oo from ITC, SCC and she reported that MOU ( 47 former  SCC workers who stuck in Myanmar due to Covid ) arrived SCC on 24th Sep 2022 with the Service of I.F . 20 of them had to stay Quarantine in Mae Sout as they tested positive. So only 27 workers in now SCC private quarantine hostel ( as they are close contact with 20 positive people). The ambassador said these 27 workers will have to stay quarantine for 10 days. P. Kont,  herself brought these 27 workers from Mae Sout. Since these 27 workers  are still in quarantine, it is difficult to get the recruitment information.
Ms. Thinzar Oo said that the brand new MOU group will arrive SCC in mid of Oct with the service of Alpha World Link. They had done contract signing. SCC had already reimbursed the interview cost and contract signing cost. However SCC didn't reimburse the passport cost yet.
Regarding walk in recruitment in August 2022, Thin Zar Oo ( GD ambassador ) confirmed that Ko Zaw Oo ( one of the translators) charged workers 8000 baht for transportation. The other two translators charged 8000- 10000 to walk-in workers.
This info is still second hand info as Thinzar Oo hasn't found direct client to testify this incident.

In our housing outreach, the SCC workers who participated in FGD reported that SCC recruited aroud about 150 walk-in applicants in August 2022. For this recruitment, the translators posted the vacancies announcement on their Facebook and workers who would like to call their friends and relatives to ITC need to follow-up with translators. Sometimes the translators did pre-interview with applicants via video calls and if they think these applicants have high potential to be accepted, the translators help the applicants with transportation arrangements. They charged the applicants from Samut Sakhorn 8500 Baht for transportation and other provinces like Ayutthaya and Pathumthani, the translators charged 10000 for transportation.

The female pink card worker , who started  working on 31 Aug 2022, said that she has to pay 7,500 THB  to the broker named Ko Ko Lwin, who also has the connection with the SIF. Ko Ko Lwin used to connect the workers from different provides across Thailand. Previously, that female worker was being sent to a chicken factory in Nakhon Prathum. Because the business shut down, Ko Ko Lwin made another arrangement for her.

When she first arrived after one month, one of the organizations came and interviewed her. At that time, she felt uncomfortable and did not mention 7,500 THB. 
She has never reimbursed for that amount.

Another male worker, who started working on 26 Aug 2022, said that he hasn't paid anything. He got the job information from one of his aunts, who has a friend working in SCC. Because of his direct connection with the factory, he hasn't paid anything too. 
 He was also being interviewed by the HR team, including the Burmese interpreter, when he first started working. At that time, they interviewed him about what they have to pay in order to get a job, including the document fee and transportation fee. As he only cost 35 THB, he only mentioned that. But never being reimbursed until now too.

The workers mentioned that the business has a wide announcement in terms of the workers having to pay the fee. The business mentioned that if the workers have to pay any fee to those who have connections to SCC, they can let the business know and the business will take action to those and dismiss them from the job. If they came here with others who are not affiliated with SCC, they will take any responsibilities.

description: Issues with regular shift hours or other shift issues: dispute without violation of law or employment contract
closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue because the business reverting back to the day and night shifts again, and overtime work will be provided to workers in June onwards.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Workers reported having to work at odd working hours that they were not aware of when they started their job. The job hours start from 11 PM to 8 AM and so on. Workes want regular working hours as they used to do in the past because they have challenges commuting to the factory during those hours. In addition to that, the workers added not having OT for several months makes them difficult to manage their financial situation. Workers want to know how long non-OT work will continue because they may have to find better income jobs if this will continue for another several months. 


Talking Points
-What are the working hours at the moment? How long does each rotation of shifts last?
-How are working being communicated? 
-What is the workload these days. Workes reported not receiving OT for several months, any changes or updates that the workers should be aware of? 


Recommendation; 

-The business should communicate with the workers about the work shifts and make sure that workers have safe communication channels for their work during odd hours, especially at night. 
-The business should also communicate with the workers about the business workload and OT hours so that workers can make decisions as they wish.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The business response: 
Piyabutr said this night shift was set according to another buyer, not HP. CC and line supervisors already had a discussion meeting and communicated to the workers. This shift started last two months ago and it’s just a temporary shift based on the order of the buyer.

Worker updates are being communicated by the business. The communication said that they will end odd working hours shifts and only have two shifts which are day and night. Workers do not have issues with this anymore. For the OT hours, workers heard from their supervisors that they will start receiving OT starting June. Workers do not have issues anymore.
remediation_notes: Workers reported having to adjust to new working hours at odd times, such as from 11 PM to 8 AM and so on. They are finding it a challenge commuting to the factory during such hours. In addition to that, the workers added not getting OT work for several months, leading to less income than expected. Workers want to know how long this situation will persist because they may need to find jobs with better income if this continues indefinitely.
remediation_action:
The business explained that this night shift was set according to another buyer, not HP. HR and line supervisors already had a meeting to communicate this to the workers. This is just a temporary shift based on the buyer's order. The lack of OT hours for the workers was also related to the buyer's orders and the business wanted all workers to receive the basic salary and not have to lay off workers.

The business has announced to the workers that the business will end the odd working hours shifts and go back to having only the day and night shifts.
remediation_validation: The workers do not have issues with this anymore. For the OT hours, workers heard from their supervisors that they will start receiving OT starting in June.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue because the business reverting back to the day and night shifts again and overtime work will be provided to workers in June onwards.

remediation_results: Issara is closing this case because the business has clarified with workers that they can indeed apply for the Social Security compensation and explained the process for getting it.

remediation_business_steps_taken:
KPI 2070 and 1626: on 16 October 2023, BHR called to follow up with Khun Krit. He has done the investigation in the cutting line and he insisted that there's no such case happened in the cutting line. On 30 September, he did the training on sick leave and leave in general, as well as, employer-employee communication, to all the line supervisors and conducted a special session with line supervisors in the cutting line. None of the supervisors had ever asked the workers to show a medical certificate for sick leave before. Often times when the workers want to take sick leave, the line supervisors give permission to all cases. None of the line supervisors accepted that they shouted at the workers or made the workers felt like they are servants.
He said he knows the worker who reported the issue but he didn't get a chance to talk to that worker. But he just talked to all the line supervisors in the cutting line. There're just a few line supervisors in that line. None of them accepted that such case ever happened. Khun Krit is happy to conduct further investigation and talk to the worker. BHR will follow up with him again at the end of this week.

20 Oct 2023: Khun Krit investigated yesterday by talking to 5 Myanmar workers in the cutting line one by one in his office, including the one he thinks has reported the issue. He asked questions like, "Have any of the supervisors ever made you feel like a servant?", "Do you feel like doing excessive work?", or "Have you ever been asked to show a medical certificate by a supervisor before?".  Everyone said no even when Khun Krit confirmed that they won't be targeted or there won't be any threats or retaliation against them. So I told him that we would have our O&E officer validate with the workers.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1:
The workers reported that the line supervisor, P'New, in Line no.5 and other supervisors discriminated against Burmese workers.  The following examples of discrimination were reported.  
1) She is often verbally abusive, shouting at the Burmese workers if they did something wrong with their sewing task or asked to go to the toilet while she doesn't say anything to the Thai workers.
2) When the Burmese workers asked to change the working line, the supervisor denied their request but she allowed the Thai workers to change lines if requested
3) The supervisor pushed the heavier workload onto the Burmese workers, asking them to work on 2-4 tasks while the Thai workers handle only one.  When pieces accumulated where the Thai workers are working, the supervisor asked the Burmese workers to go and assist, but the reverse wasn't the case.
4) When a worker qualifies to start getting incentive pay is dependent on the supervisor's assessment. The Burmese workers say that they have to wait 1-2 months while Thai workers are entitled to get the incentive within 2-3 weeks.
5) There is a Thai woman who is assigned to replace the needles when they break during operation. This lady spoke loudly and blamed the Burmese workers when they asked for new needles but is nice to the Thai workers. She does not even give the workers pens to note down the stock-in/ stock-out and the workers have to bring the pen by themselves. 

The workers want to have clear policies and that everyone is treated equally.

Recommendations for remediation:
The business to investigate this matter with proper worker safeguards, especially the behavior of the supervisor in line #5 and the supervisor in charge of replacing the needles for the workers
The company’s non-discrimination policy to announced to all workers, and note channels to safely report incidents of discrimination


Case #2:
Burmese pregnant workers feel as though they are being discriminated against in the AAC room where they work.  While Thai female workers eat, chit chat, rest, and lie down during working hours when waiting for the new workload to arrive, the Burmese workers are reported by the Thai workers for doing the same things and were warned by HR not to do this when HR staff came to their room once and found them taking a break.  They feel that this is unfair and now feel like they have to be careful all the time; otherwise, they will be told on by their Thai co-workers and that HR is targeting them to find fault in their behavior.

Talking points:
-What are the expectations for pregnant workers?  Are they allowed to have some breaks where they can lie down and rest?  Is this applied to workers of all nationalities?

Recommendations for remediation:
-The business to investigate this matter with proper worker safeguards
-HR to treat workers fairly and without showing preferential treatment based on nationality
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K.Witsawad, Senior Management- comments on what the workload means by the worker because everyone works at the same time starting from 8 am and finishing 5 pm then continuing OT. The factory also has a clear policy. What is the workload meant by Burmese workers? Do they work more than 8 hours a day? 
He added the verbally abusive - that he and the HR team will go and check in the field and ask all the production line supervisors how they communicate with the workers. If he found the case he would always not allow this kind of issue to pass and let it be. This will take one week and get back to us.

The investigation result:
Reasons to speak loudly Because there are other sounds in the production area, such as the sound of the engine or the wind, it is necessary to speak loudly so that both Thai and Burmese workers can hear, but did not criticize or criticize the workers.

The balance of work has the following criteria;
1.Cycle Time of each step
2. Skills of each worker
3. Balance principle according to Yamazumi, if the sewing process takes less time, Cycle Time must add more jobs or allow sewing in other steps.
As a result, the supervisor's responsibility in line sewing is to maximize efficiency. Workers who can request changes to the sewing process will make the process difficult if there will be no sewing workers.

Action: Timeline, from week 4 of June to week 1 of July
Organize a training for the supervisors of the target group for 1 hour a day to review the legal requirements and other standards. related as follows:
- communication techniques
- Requirements, laws and other relevant standards
- Effects that may occur in case of inconsistent practice

case#1 Discrimination by nationality, Line supervisor

The company's needle-changing procedure is
Employees must prepare for needle changes by doing the following:
- Locate all of the broken needle parts in order to replace the new needle.
- Take notes on the work that sews while the needle is broken, including the PO style, color, machine type, needle type, and when the needle is broken.
- If the broken needle parts cannot be found, employees must bring the sewn item to the warehouse's metal detector. and have the warehouse personnel who inspect the metal sign the inspection certificate; the supervisor must also sign the acknowledgment and approve the needle change.

The needle replacement procedure is a standard procedure that all employees must follow, and cannot discriminate Because any metal parts attached to the customer's product will cause significant damage to the company.



case#2 Burmese pregnant workers feel as though they are being discriminated against in the AAC room where they work

In the case of a pregnant Myanmar worker, a warning was issued because the worker threw a scissor and hit the desk drawer at the quality inspector (QC). Following an investigation, the root cause was discovered to be the worker's dissatisfaction with the fact that quality inspectors frequently glanced at the worker. In this case, if the quality inspector was injured, the worker was threatening his or her colleague, who could be Thai or Myanmar. Pregnant or non-pregnant workers must also be warned.

According to the rules and regulations, workers would be warned, either verbally or in writing, if they violated work regulations. It has nothing to do with discrimination.

The business investigated and found that in the production area, there are loud machinery and engine noises so supervisors needed to speak loudly at times but this was to both Thai and Burmese workers. When workers requested changing lines, the supervisor's responsibility in the sewing line is to maximize efficiency and decisions were based on this rather than the nationality of the worker making the request. The business committed to organize a training for the supervisors on communication techniques, and requirements, laws, and other relevant standards they should apply consistently. For changing needles, the company has a set procedure where the worker must collect all the needle fragments and take the item that was being sewn to the needle changing station to get the needle replaced.  These procedures would be equally followed for all workers, regardless of nationality.

Case #2:
The company did not address the concern that the pregnant migrant workers reported.  Rather, it updated Issara saying a pregnant Myanmar worker had been issued a warning because she threw a scissor and hit the desk drawer at the quality inspector (QC). Following an investigation, the root cause was discovered to be the worker's dissatisfaction with the fact that quality inspectors frequently glanced at the worker. In this case, if the quality inspector was injured, and the worker that was threatening a colleague, whether Thai or Myanmar, would be warned. It has nothing to do with discrimination.
remediation_validation:
Case #1:
Issara followed up with a worker and she said the line supervisor is now quiet in the working line and not shouting the Burmese workers like before. In terms of workload and assignment of tasks, the Burmese workers still need to handle different sewing tasks on a production line rather than one, but there is no monitoring and pushing from the supervisor, so they are happy to work now. In terms of the incentive pay, they received the explanation from the supervisor during the morning talk.

Case #2: 
The pregnant migrant workers provided an update saying there now had a new supervisor and the conditions had improved.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case.  The workers have noted that conditions have improved and they are happy with the current situation.

description: Fees charged by employer: illegal and unethical

call_details.description:
Post Kick-off meeting

We have learned from Everest (Nike's supplier) this morning that they only cover the recruitment fees for the workers who first arrived in Thailand. They do not cover the cost of Visa extension, work permit extension, and medical check up for the workers who need to extend these document. The Everest will advance these fees, but they will be charged to workers. Is this consider to comply with employer pays policy?

call_details.next_steps: IMT will update the SP notes so that we can escalate with Nike.

call_details.description: Follow up about working condition and if they received document fee back from the employer? and worker confirm all Cambodian workers received 13350 baht from employer.

closed_notes: This issue is being closed because Issara has completed the data collection of the recruitment fee survey and is preparing the survey findings report.  The report will be provided to the Strategic Partner and the supplier, for discussion on reimbursement of fees paid by workers beyond what the supplier has already paid back to the workers (13,350 Baht each to the Cambodian workers).
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issara had an ongoing meeting with the business where the business explained that they only cover the recruitment fees for new MOU workers when workers are first recruited. However, other recruitment related fees such as document extension (work permit renewal, ongoing documentation related to employment) are not covered by the business. The business pays the fees in advance but those fees are then deducted from workers paychecks. This practice is against an employer pays policy, as all recruitment fees, including document extension costs, should be covered by the employer.


Talking points:
- We really appreciate our open discussion on current practices, recruitment in general, and how our partnership can work.
- Thanks a lot for raising that currently workers are paying for work permit and visa renewal, or other fees related to ongoing employment such as an updated health check.
- In our ongoing discussions with Nike, we clarified that these fees would fall under their employer pays policy, and should be covered by the employer.  This is also pretty standard for all definitions of employer pays.
- Our recommendation would be to change this practice now, and clarify with workers that these fees will be paid directly by Everest.  You can confirm this shift to us and to Nike.
- Issara and Nike will follow up on the previous practice and include this in our discussions with all Nike suppliers on ways forward in recruitment practice and learning.
- Issara can support the business to fully investigate if all workers are being charged these types of costs, and ensure full documentation of all affected workers, costs paid, and recommendations for repayment of recruitment and employment fees charged.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issara has escalated this issue with the business, the business was not very clearly aware of the Nike policy regarding the Employer Pay Policy. The business responded and said that they will conduct payback to the workers. It was not clear with the process and the timeline. The business added that they will start following the employer pay policy starting from 2022.
The workers confirmed receiving their documents extension fees back from the employer. The amount that they have received was 13,500 THB per worker. 
This issue will remain open until Issara conducts the recruitment fees survey and analyse the amount that the workers have paid so far. After the verification through survey, Issara will consider to close the case with associated rating. At this point, it is hard to say whether the paid amount to the workers is align with what the workers have paid.
remediation_notes: Issara had an ongoing meeting with the business where the business explained that they only cover the recruitment fees for new MOU migrant workers (there are an estimated 28 Cambodian workers affected) when workers are first recruited.
remediation_action:
The business explained that they pay the fees in advance but those fees are then deducted from workers paychecks.

This issue was escalated to the company management and the company responded that they had consulted with the Strategic Partner in Thailand and that the Cambodian workers' recruitment fees would be reimbursed.

Starting in 2022, the company will implement the employer pay policy for extension fees. The company has shared the draft policy announcement with Issara, which will be reviewed and feedback provided.

The business has paid back the workers the amount of 13,350 Baht to the Cambodian workers.  It has also agreed to have Issara conduct the recruitment fee survey with the Cambodian workers, and this is in progress.
remediation_validation: The reported fees charged to workers would violate an employer pays or responsible recruitment policy or commitment, as these types of costs are directly related to recruitment and ongoing employment, such as a work permit renewal.  Issara will be conducting a recruitment fee survey to fully investigate if all workers are being charged these types of costs, and ensure full documentation of all affected workers, costs paid, and recommendations for repayment of recruitment and employment fees charged.
remediation_results: This issue is being closed because Issara has completed the data collection of the recruitment fee survey and is preparing the survey findings report.  The report will be provided to the Strategic Partner and the supplier, for discussion on reimbursement of fees paid by workers beyond what the supplier has already paid back to the workers.

description: Social Security issue (access to health care): minor issue

call_details.description: This is the outreach case collected from housing outreach in HT91.
call_details.next_steps: Have to update in SC meeting.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case.  The workers now understand why sometimes workers are asked to get medical care at a hospital not designated under social security coverage, either for better quality care or because social security coverage has not yet been activated for new workers.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The workers reported that for emergency care or accident cases, the business advised them to get medical care at a hospital not designated under the Social Security coverage.  In such cases, the workers have to pay the cost in advance and they get reimbursement later. This does not happen frequently but the workers would like to know why the business is doing this.

Talking points:
Are there instances when the business will request workers to get treated at hospitals other than the SSO-designated hospitals?  If so, what are the reasons for this?

Recommendations for remediation:
The business to clearly communicate to the workers the company policy on workers’ access to healthcare and relevant coverage under Social Security.  If certain medical care is to be had at hospitals not under Social Security coverage, the reasons are to be clearly stated.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Witsawad - This is all clear that the company would treat the workers more than SSO hospital. Because in some cases, the workers cannot be recovered by SSO hospital. The company would like the workers to be healthy and be recovered as soon as possible to 100% and ready to work. But for symptoms like fever or any non-serious condition, the workers would be treated by the SSO hospital.


The investigation result:
This case didn't happen. But if it happens, it's probably the case that migrant workers are a walk-in group, applying for a job and being hired as an employee. This group of employees will not be able to use social security rights immediately because they may not have rights in the case that they must have paid contributions for 3 months within 15 months, but the company has purchased health insurance for employees who have not received social security benefits for a period of 4 months. If these employees are sick, they must use health insurance instead.

Action:
In the case of an incident
1. In employee orientation will increase the knowledge of foreign employees who have not received social security rights that if there is an illness, health insurance must be exercised until the SS benefit active.
2. HR makes a copy of the health insurance policy for employees to keep in their passport in case of emergency.
3. If there is an illness, inform HR through an interpreter to help coordinate with the hospital to facilitate
remediation_notes: The workers reported that for emergency care or accident cases, the business advised them to get medical care at a hospital not designated under the Social Security coverage.  In such cases, the workers have to pay the cost in advance and they get reimbursement later. This does not happen frequently but the workers would like to know why the business is doing this.
remediation_action:
The business expressed their intention to provide medical care that was even better than what is available in public hospitals covered by Social Security.  In some cases, the workers cannot get adequate care at a public hospital, and so are referred to other hospitals. The company would like the workers to be healthy and recover as soon as possible. But for symptoms like fever or any non-serious conditions, the workers would be treated at the public hospital under Social Security coverage.

The business investigated this matter and found that for the migrant workers that were hired as "walk-in workers" (those already in Thailand), they would not qualify for social security coverage until social security contributions have been made for at least three months and the business has purchased health insurance for these employees. If any of these employees are sick because social security coverage is activated, they would use health insurance instead.

The business will clarify this during worker orientation sessions in the future, that for those who are not yet eligible for social security coverage will be covered under health insurance until the Social Security benefits are activated.
remediation_validation: Issara updated the worker regarding the company policy regarding social security coverage for health care.  The worker now understands why workers sometimes use hospitals not under social security.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case.  The workers now understand why sometimes workers are asked to get medical care at a hospital not designated under social security coverage, either for better quality care or because social security coverage has not yet been activated for new workers.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The workers reported the following issues related to their living and canteen conditions.
1) The canteen area is very small and the business is using some of that space as storage.  It is difficult for the workers to find sufficient space in the canteen to eat their lunch.
2) The drinking water on the ground floor is not cool and has foul smell so the workers have to bring their own water from home or buy water.
3) The factory clinic provides only paracetamol as treatment for all kinds of illnesses experienced by the workers

Recommendations for remediation
Calculate the floor space of the canteen and the number of workers that can be seated during the lunch hour with appropriate distancing according to Covid-19 prevention guidelines.  Make more space available by removing the items being stored in the canteens.  Assign additional space for lunch as necessary if the current canteen area is insufficient for the number of workers.
Test the quality of the water and ensure that the water is drinkable so that workers don’t have to rely on bringing their own water or having to buy it
Investigate the protocols used in the factory clinic, and whether the resident nurse or health practitioner is diagnosing illnesses and dispensing the appropriate medication.  Survey the workers anonymously to assess the quality of the medical service they are receiving at the clinic and receive their suggestions for improvement.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Case#1-K. Yuppadee has been aware of this issue before. Addressing the issue, the company has purchased more tables and put them in the canteen. And of course, there are two lunch times for the workers.

Case#2-This is related to the case one because when the first group of workers have lunch break they get the cold water and the second group of workers might not get the cold water because the cooler might not be cold enough in the short time. However, she will investigate and check this matter.

Case#3 K. Witsawad- according to health care policy the medicine service provided based on First-Aid that might be limited and not much more same as the hospital. If the workers were in a bad condition they should go to hospital. 

K. Yuppadee will investigate this matter and get back to us within one week.


Case #1: Canteen not sufficient space for workers having lunch.
The investigation result:
Because of the covids situation two years ago, the dining room area was set up by keeping distance. To avoid infection, the majority of the employees returned to their rooms for lunch. As a result, there is no shortage of space.
Present circumstances Coronavirus infection has declined. Some employees returned to the restaurant more frequently. resulting in insufficient space to meet needs

Action: Timeline, week 3-4 of June
1. Increasing the size of the dining room and purchasing additional tables and chairs
2. Communicating with workers who live nearby the factory, please go to your room for lunch to reduce your risk of contracting coronavirus.

Case #2: The water dispenser on the ground floor is not cool, has a bad smell, and is undrinkable
The investigation result:
Drinking water is currently not cold and smells. Caused by: 
1. The company has 6 drinking water dispensers and 16 water dispensers, enough for 407 employees.
2. The canteen's drinking water dispensers have two machines and four faucets, one of which does not have cold water due to a faulty compressor.
3. A water dispenser on the first floor. Because the compressor is broken, the drinking water is not cold.
4. Examine each point of drinking water and the result is no unpleasant smell.

Action: Timeline, week 3-4 of June
1. Send the water dispenser to the machine's seller for inspection and repair or replacement of the compressor (waiting for return)
2. Check the results of drinking water for smell through the standard criteria.

Case #3: Issue with medicine: the factory clinic provides only paracetamol as a treatment for all illnesses.
The investigation result:
Rules for dispensing medicines in the factory's medical room.
1. All medicines used in the medical room must be prescription-only drugs. which some workers are unaware
2. When workers experience headaches, toothaches, or other pains, the nurses administer paracetamol.
3. Workers are experiencing muscle aches. The nurse will include it as a topical medication, such as balm or pain reliever.

Action: Timeline, week 3 of June
Additional communication sessions;
1. A meeting of the Welfare Committee and the Safety Supervisors Committee to discuss employee suggestions/complaints.
2. A meeting to communicate to the workers about the rules for dispensing medicines in the medical room when an illness occurs. To take time off work and care for one's health in order to keep one's body healthy and ready to work.
3. Nurse meeting to improve communication about rules when a worker visits the hospital and ask an interpreter to assist the worker in explaining things more clearly. (In case of that worker are unable to comprehend)

remediation_business_steps_taken:
