Issue 
PR Line worker (Processing) night shift reported that the gloves were torn and a worker went to ask to change the new gloves with the supervisor named "Morn". The supervisor did not allow it. Workers use the torn gloves to continue working.
 
Business responses:
The company provides gloves to workers for work. In the case of the worker's gloves are damaged, such as torn gloves, leaked gloves, the worker can bring damaged gloves to request a new gloves at the supervisor or the administrative staff of the department unit before entering the work.

In the case of of worker wants to change gloves during working hours, the worker can request a replacement at the administrative staff. Because the supervisor's working in the production line. However, the worker must bring old gloves to request for replacement. To make sure that there would be no broken gloves mixed with the product.

From the investigation with Khun Morn, he insisted that he never refuses if the worker brings a damaged gloves to replace a new gloves, except when he is in the production line, he would inform workers to request a change at the administrative staff.

From the survey with randomly asking 8 workers, the workers who randomly inquired if the gloves were damaged, could request to change the gloves at the supervisor. However, the most of workers still do not know that in the case of requesting to change during the working hours, they can request a change at the administrative staff.

In this regard, the HR, factory manager, and supervisors have communicated with all workers that how to request changing gloves.

description: Substandard living conditions and privacy in dorm/bathrooms/living space
closed_notes: Due to the time that has elapsed with no progress on engaging with the supplier and addressing this issue, Issara is closing this case as unresolved.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1: 
The business is housing up to 3 married couples in a room and 5-6 single workers in a room without proper partitions so there is a complete lack of privacy. The room is not very big and conflicts between the occupants happen often. In addition, they require the workers to rotate rooms 3-4 times per year. The workers don’t like this kind of management as they have to move all their belongings every time they have to change rooms. And then, when one party fights, all workers have to leave the housing and they are automatically disqualified to get the transportation allowance that the business started providing to the workers who live outside the business housing.

Recommendations for remediation:
- Survey the dorm residents to ask about the overall conditions and receive suggestions for improvements
- Dorm rooms should be assigned so that there is adequate privacy and couples can be housed in separate rooms


Case #2:
There are 12 toilets and bathrooms in the women's dorm where more than 100 female workers are being accommodated. Many toilet doors and locks are broken and cannot be closed properly. Some water taps are not working. Workers have to fight to get to use the toilets and bathrooms. 

Recommendations for remediation:
- Inspect the toilet and shower facilities in the dorms to ensure that all doors, door locks, and water taps are working properly 
- Fix all doors, locks, and water taps that are in disrepair
- Survey the dorm residents to ask about the overall conditions and receive suggestions for improvements

call_details.description:

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case. The business has made arrangements so that the workers can return to work, and the workers have confirmed that they are back at work.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The seven workers whose visa and work permit expired after losing their passports were registered pink cards by Nan Yang, and they were allowed to work until September only. Then, the employer asked them to stop working, stay in their room, and wait for the work permit application. The workers now have to wait without earning money or a job for over a month. Other employers allow their pink card-registered workers to work, but Nan Yang does not. Now the government announces that those workers can do a health check for their work permit applications, but Nan Yang does not contact the workers at all. The worker requested that Issara help with this issue with the supplier.

TPs:
- Why were these workers asked to stop working after Sep 2023?
- Now that the government has made the announcement about migrant workers processing their work permits and visas, what is the business plan for these workers?

Recommendations:
- Allow the workers to start working again, given that they have not had income for over a month
- Communicate with these workers so that they know when they will be able to start work again, and the process and timeline for getting their work permits and visas
- Process the necessary documents for the workers, as per the government announcement
remediation_business_steps_taken:
To sum up the call, Nan Yang cannot take them back to work now. The workers have to wait a bit longer to apply for the work permit. The Nan Yang HR person is in contact with the provincial DoE every week so she will continue to follow up with them. Nan Yang will also communicate with these 7 workers of what's happening and what actions Nan Yang is taking in order to bring them back so the workers are on the same page. I'll also continue to follow up with them again next week. Nan Yang also mentioned that they are paying the workers for any public holidays they have every month.

DATE: 13 Dec 2023
K. Namthip, HR, responded that Nan Yang had already submitted the list of worker names to the DOE. However, DOE stated that the registration system will be fully operational on December 15. So, beginning November 18, Nan Yang will check with DOE again to see if all of the worker names have been entered into the DOE system. They will contact the worker to schedule a health check and return to work.

Date: 19 Dec 2023
The workers were able to go back to work at Nan Yang NKPT since yesterday (18 Dec 2023). Their names are all registered at the DoE NKPT. They have to undergo a health check up early next year which will be arranged by the business.

remediation_action:

HR updated that the workers resumed work on December 18, 2023. They will undergo the required health check early next year which will be arranged by the business.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Many workers' PJ passports and CI passports have already expired. Most of the PJ workers' passports expired in May 2021, and their CI expired in March 2022. The business informed the workers that the documents would be extended, but not yet. Due to the expiry of the document, the ATM cards have expired and the workers cannot withdraw any money. On June 4, the HR office provided a written document in the Thai language to the workers and informed them to withdraw money at the bank. On June 5, the workers went to the bank at Big C, but the bank did not accept the document, and no one could withdraw any cash. Many workers know Issara's hotline number, but they are afraid to contact Issara because they heard rumors that they would be terminated if they contact Issara and raise the issue.

Investigate the incident, with worker safeguards
Take disciplinary action against the personnel that was found to have discouraged workers from using the grievance mechanism

Recommendations for systems change

In this call Issara informed the client the BR that any passport renewal fees or recruitment fees incurred prior to 2023 are not covered by the company policy. This call is to Aye Aye Aung  who reported the KPI ID- 1671 Worker Voice ID- 58849 (Fees Charged by the employer).

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue. The business policy is that fees will be covered as of January 2023 and the workers now understand that passport fees they paid prior to that date will not be reimbursed by the business.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Ma San Nu reported that on 14th Sep at 4 PM all 28 workers (who came to SFP as walk-in MOU in 2017 and started new contract with SFP in 2019) were called to office and HR recruitment manager informed them that the management decided this group to return to Myanmar on 6th Oct as contract ended workers. However, the HR recruitment officer said that calling back these workers as U Turn is not sure and if they need more workers in 2024 these workers will be priority groups.
And HR recruitment manager also asked the workers to sign the consent form. However, almost all 28 workers didn't agree to sign the consent because the business hasn't reimbursed the passport renewal and OWIC cost that they spent in 2022 Jan. The workers asserted that they did the passport renewal by following the business arrangement. In 2022 December, the business announced the list of the workers who must do passport renewal in Chiang Mai. The business provided the necessary documents to all workers and arranged the round trip transportation but the workers had to pay the cost from their pockets. The average amount the workers had to spend for renewing and OWIC is 7400 Baht.  So the workers think that they have the right to get the reimbursement. So the workers ask the Issara to help them to get this reimbursement.

Recommendations:
- If the business had communicated to the workers that their contracts would be extended and they paid for passport extension costs for this purpose, the business should reimburse this cost given that the business has changed its mind about continuing their employment
- Communicate this clearly to workers and provide the reimbursement before they are repatriated to their home country.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 28 SEP 2023
K. Supreraya, HR Operations Manager, explained that SF2513 was writing the Ethical Recruitment policy in November-December 2022, and management approved the EPP to be implemented in 2023. So any passport renewal fees or recruitment fees incurred prior to 2023 are not covered by the company policy. K. Wacharaporn, Production Manager, added that these workers did not follow company procedure and rushed the passport extension process. The company only goes over the company's standard processes and procedures.
remediation_notes: A group of MOU workers whose 4-year contracts are ending were informed by the business that they would be repatriated to their source country on October 6, 2023, as their contracts were not being extended. The workers had paid 7,000 Baht to get their passports renewed in December 2022 with the business arranging this with the assurance that their contracts would be renewed.
remediation_action: HR explained that the business started implementing the Employer Pays Policy in January 2023.  Any passport renewal fees or recruitment fees incurred prior to 2023 are not covered by the company policy.
remediation_validation: Issara informed the workers that any passport renewal fees or recruitment fees incurred prior to 2023 are not covered by the company policy. The workers accepted this.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue. The business policy is that fees will be covered as of January 2023 and the workers now understand that passport fees they paid prior to that date will not be reimbursed by the business.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Communicate well in advance with any worker or group of workers whose contracts are coming to an end whether their contracts will be renewed or not. Once communication has been made to renew their contracts, the business should take responsibility for what they have promised its workers.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Robert from Royal Gate International, Myanmar RA, reached out to Issara as he was informed by MD of Htay RA that someone from TUM contacted them on 22nd May (Sunday) and asked to cancel the job interview that they are planning to have on 23rd May (Monday). Almost all the job seekers were either on the way to Yangon or already arrived. According to Htay RA, the interview was cancelled as Andy Hall asked why TUM had selected a new RA instead of working with current RAs and if they continued with the recruitment, he would let TU's customers know about this. Htay RA was confused and wondered why TUM has to cancel everything based on one person's comment while this might cause a big problem to Myanmar RA if job seekers report the case to MOLIP that the job interview was canceled without having any good reason. RA had to inform and apologize to the job seekers about the cancellation and they feel unfair that job seekers had to cover the costs based on this unexpected short-notice cancellation. Robert also checked with Andy but Andy said that he is no longer with MWRN and denied having anything to do with the situation.  

TUM demand of 800 workers (200 workers x 4 batches) was approved by Thai DOE in December 2021 and approved by Myanmar MOLIP in March 2022. TUM selected Htay RA and had a business deal since early 2022; however, TU never shared this information with Issara as part of recruitment updates and planning. 

Robert updated Chaw to update that Htay RA has been informed by TUM that TUM will have an auditor working for TUM who is based in Yangon conduct an assessment with Htay sometime soon.  Chaw asked who from TUM contacted Htay but Robert does not have the information and it seems like Htay does not want to provide that information to Robert/Issara. 

Chaw followed up with Robert to get update on the job interviews for TUM.  Robert confirmed that the interview had been canceled and TUM said that they will have to conduct an audit of Htay and only after that, will they be able to resume the recruitment. 

Htay RA mentioned to TUM that they are planning and willing to engage with Issara but the contact person from TUM replied that they do not work with Issara. This has led to Htay not contacting Issara directly but providing updates to Robert.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The TU has already consulted with that RA, and they are working with the RA to reimburse the job seekers who returned home. The TU will soon hold a meeting and training for the Myanmar RA. And the TUM is still recruiting these job seekers in accordance with the plan.


TUM plans to reimburse workers directly once the workers cross the border and start working with TUM. Under the current timeline, the workers are scheduled to move to Thailand in early Jan.

For workers whose interviews were previously canceled and who chose not to pursue work at TUM (and therefore will not cross the border this Jan 2023 to work for TUM), the TUM HR team will work with Htay to contact and identify those people. In those cases, the reimbursement will come from the agent.
remediation_notes: A recruitment agency contracted by the business to hire MOU workers from Myanmar had scheduled interviews with many job applicants but was asked by the business just a day before the day of the scheduled interviews to cancel the interviews and put the recruitment process on hold.  This has led to many applicants traveling to Yangon from various parts of the country spending considerable time and money for the transport, meals, and accommodation only to be informed at the last minute that their interviews have been cancelled.
remediation_action: The business has consulted with the recruitment agency, and they are working with the recruitment agency to reimburse the job seekers who had returned home because of the interview cancellation. TU will soon hold a meeting and training for the Myanmar recruitment agency. TUM has communicated with the recruitment agency to alert the group of workers whose interviews had been canceled that their costs would be reimbursed
remediation_validation: The RA has already announced on their Facebook page letting workers know to reach out to them for the reimbursement.  Two workers have reached out to the recruitment agency while others may or may not choose to do so.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case.  The recruitment agency has made efforts to contact the affected persons to offer reimbursement for the costs incurred, and a few have been contacted while many others have not and presumably may have traveled to Thailand for work.

call_details.description:
The drinking water provided by the factory smells (like a fresh river-smell), and the workers cannot drink it well. So, the workers have to buy the water bottles, but the issue is that the business does not allow them to keep the water, even in the locker. At the lunch break, the workers buy a water bottle, but if they cannot finish it, they have to throw it away. 

The workers want the business to get the water without any smell.
call_details.next_steps: To refer the case to Ko Brendan

closed_notes: This issue is closed.  The business has replaced the water dispenser and filter to improve the quality of the drinking water and has provided a temporary fix for the toilet water supply for flushing and is also fixing the water pump.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1:
The drinking water provided by the factory smells like river water, and the workers cannot drink it. So, the workers have to buy their own bottled water during the lunch break but they are not allowed to take it out of the canteen area and so they have to throw it away if they cannot drink all of it.

Talking points:
What is the company policy regarding drinking water and where workers are allowed to take their water bottles and drink water?

Recommendations for remediation:
Inspect the quality of the drinking water provided to workers, identify and fix the problem to ensure workers have access to clean hygienic drinking water
Get feedback from workers about their experiences regarding the drinking water situation and recommendations on improving the drinking water provided by the business and also where workers are allowed to take and keep water bottles
Communicate to workers how the business has improved the quality of the drinking water and workers’ access to drinking water


Case #2:
The toilet near the factory clinic (behind the canteen) has a water supply issue. It’s been 2-3 weeks. The workers cannot flush the toilet so the toilets get clogged. Workers have to wait in a long queue, and they get scolded by line supervisors when unable to return on time from their toilet break.

Talking points:
- How can workers inform the business management about facilities that are not functioning properly so that fixes can be made in a timely manner?
- Is the business aware that the toilets near the clinic are not flushing and has been an issue for 3 weeks? 

Recommendations for remediation:
- Inspect the water pressure and conduct maintenance service on the toilets; check and ensure all toilets are flushing and enough water pressure.
- Communicate to workers the actions that the business has taken after the toilets have been fixed; suggest ways for workers to report such problems in the future so that fixes can be made sooner
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Case #1:
The businesses responded that it is not allowing workers to have water bottles on the production line because the workers do not throw the bottles into the trash bins.  Therefore, the company restricts the water bottles to the canteen only. The company is aware of the drinking water issue. Previously, the drinking water filter was changed twice a year; now, it is changed every quarter, and the quality and smell are checked every week. As a result, the business insists that the workers get to drink high-quality water. The business will announce to the workers how it is monitoring the drinking water quality and send us the action plan by next week.

Case #1:
K. Wachiraporn, HR manager shared the action plan that they have already changed the new water dispenser for workers. So the problem should be resolved.


Case #2:
The HR mentioned that now they are fixing the pump and will communicate this on the board.

remediation_action:

Previously, the drinking water filter was changed twice a year; now, it is changed every quarter, and the quality and smell are checked every week. The water dispenser has also been replaced.  The business will announce to the workers how it is monitoring the drinking water quality.

Case #2: 
HR has noted that they are fixing the water pump and will communicate this to workers on the board.
remediation_validation:
Case #1: 
The worker updated Issara saying that the drinking water was not smelly anymore.

The worker updated that the toilet water supply issue is in the process of being fixed.  In the meantime, the business has provided, as a temporary fix, clean water in big buckets so the workers can use and flush the toilets.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Nyi Nyi reported that he was attacked by the gangsters on the way back home from work on 16th August 2023 at 4:30 am after his night shift. He and his two friends were attacked with a metal rod by the gangsters on a motorbike. On the same day, another gangster attack happened at 68 Sub-agent owned compounds and another incident happened at the place near Factory 11 Gate. In these attacks, the gangster used a metal chain and metal rod as well. The workers assume that the gangsters attacked them to get money or valuable things. It is apparent that the gangsters often attack more on the paydays like the 16th & 30th of the months. For this latest incident, the workers reported to the fore-men of their respective production lines but the workers haven't known yet how the business will take action on this.

- Investigate this matter immediately; police report should also be filed
- Develop a corrective action plan with immediate safety measures for workers commuting to the workplace, especially in the late night / early morning times
- Communicate to the workers what actions the business is taking to make the commute safer for workers and update them on police investigation and actions as well

Workers reported that regular OT hours of 2 hours per day is recorded in their pay slips but any OT beyond 2 hours is not properly recorded.  Since the extra payment for the "extra OT" is not stated in their pay slips, workers are not sure if they are receiving the right amount either.

Talking points:
What is the current OT policy and the maximum number of OT hours per week?
How is a worker’s work time recorded?

Recommendations for remediation:
Investigate the practice of having workers work more than 2 hours of OT per day and not recording the excess OT hours in the workers’ pay slips
Investigate the delayed payments of these excess OT hours worked, which is delayed for 4-5 weeks and is not reflected in the workers’ pay slips
Workers should be paid on time, and the correct pay according to the hours worked should be stated in the workers’ pay slips

The worker mentioned that he got the pressure day to day from the line supervisor related to setting the target to the worker. Worker said they were told to finish 100 kg/person before 1 hour break within 5 hours. So, that means in 1 hour workers need to slice 20-21 kg chicken meat that normally a worker could do at 10-15 kg only. If the worker does not complete the target, the line supervisor stares and says to the workers that they are lazy, and always go to the toilet. Workers feel that this is such a piece work (paid by the amount of completed tasks), and feel pressure and irritated by line supervisor behavior. 
The detail info:
- There are around 60 workers on the production line
- Production line: Prer Roub - Kirami S3
- Line supervisor: Female; Monyrat

Moreover, worker also raised that there is no response on proposing the materials from the line supervisor. Workers lack of carry cart (need 3-4 more) and Knives sharper (3-4 more), it is very difficult for the workers as the materials are not sufficient and that used to be a dispute between the workers because they seize for the materials. Workers used to request the materials from the line supervisor but she doesn't seem to care at all.

The worker said, there is no improvement at Kirami line F3. The line supervisor Ms. Monyrath still shouts to the workers about the target that workers should be complete if workers are not complete she will blame the workers. And the line supervisor doesn't care at all about the worker lacking the materials (only 15 knives sharper for 40 workers, it is not enough to them) and the meat carry cart, didn't work well when report to the line supervisor she not response. 

But the workers mentioned the sick leave and toilet issues, and the worker said it has improved.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue with deductions for bathroom breaks during OT when workers return from the toilet later than the 15-minute break. And if workers are late to work about 1-5 minutes, they are forced to deduct half of that day’s OT wage. And they will receive a lower year-end bonus based on the numbers of these deductions.

Talking points:
-Are workers able to take toilet breaks if needed during their OT hours?
-How is the OT hours of workers recorded and how is the payment calculated?  Does the business deduct any pay for penalties such as being late from a toilet break?
-How is the year-end bonus calculated?

Recommendations:
-Workers should be allowed to use the toilet when needed, and payment for OT hours worked should be paid in full
-Communicate to all workers, verbally and in writing, the policy for payment of OT hours and clarify that there are no deductions for the OT hours worked
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The business HR responded that workers are allowed to take toilet breaks if needed during their OT hours. According to company policy, no pay is deducted for penalties such as being late for a toilet break. The year-end bonus for workers is based on the company's profit, and not on the worker's performance during overtime. HR will investigate and get back to us.


The process of investigation will be finished by Sep 13th.


K. Sarayuth, HR shared that as previously mentioned, according to the policy, no pay is deducted for penalties such as being late for a toilet break. The bonus is based on the company's profit, not on overtime or breaks. HR trained the supervisors regarding the policy to address the issue and emphasize the freedom to go to the toilet. He noted that the supervisors sometimes might ask the workers who go to the toilet so long because of caring for the worker. Mr. Tun Tun Win: Worker ID #91190603131.  The client joined HIT91 as an MOU worker in 2019 but was being assigned to the Hi-Tech warehouse in Suksawat Soi 64. This location was known as HIT64 and there are about 7-8 workers there. In HIT64, the business stocks rolls of different garments and the workers in that site have to work with stock-in/out and deliver the garments to-from HIT91 and HIT70. The workers have to carry the heavy garment rolls. After working there for two years, he is suffering from a stomach problem and so he cannot manage to work there anymore. He has to be hospitalized for a week and then after he is  discharged from the hospital, the doctor recommends that the job is not suitable for him anymore. So on 16 Apr 2022, he asked to move and work at HIT91 as a sewing worker.

But now, he is in a probation period and the production manager, P'Man, told him that his performance is not satisfactory as a sewing worker. They had him try and work in the ironing section too but because he injured his foot in an accident while he was working in HIT64 and he cannot manage to stand for very long. If a worker with 3 years sewing experience can sew 40 pieces per hour, he can manage to sew like 30 pieces.  And he has been asked to sew many different patterns and designs, with each taking time to get better at.  He would like the business to give him more chances to try as a sewing worker or if they are not happy with his performance, to consider having him work in the cutting or printing lines because he cannot manage to carry heavy loads in HIT64 and he cannot stand for long to do ironing work.

Talking points:
-Is the business aware that this worker was hired as an MOU worker at HIT91 but was assigned to work in another HIT facility for two years?
Recommendations:
-Workers should be provided with comprehensive job information before signing the employment contract, and the business should assign the worker to the location and provide the working conditions as promised originally
remediation_business_steps_taken:
The following are the rules for transferring workers:
- The transferee line must have a vacancy rate in order to receive the transfer.
- The transferee line that will receive the transfer must have a need to hire more workers.
- Workers applying for transfer must have the necessary qualifications or skills.

This worker previously worked at DC64 and requested to be transferred to branch factory 91 as a sewing apprentice despite not being a probationary employee but is a sewing apprenticeship based on the worker's preferences, it has nothing to do with the probation. Approximately one month into sewing training, the worker informed the trainer that I do not want to practice sewing and would like to move on to another job. The trainer had spoken with HR and suggested that the ironing position be filled. Asked if the worker is interested in becoming an ironing worker, which the worker refused. Currently, the worker works as a sewing worker for Line Sewing 15. The worker has not been transferred to another position, and HR has communicated and explained with the employee to gain a better understanding.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that he had joined HIT91 as an MOU worker in 2019 but was assigned to the Hi-Tech warehouse in Suksawat Soi 64 known as HIT64. As this warehouse stocks rolls of different garments and the workers have to lift these heavy rolls and deliver the garments to-from HIT91 and HIT70, he ended up suffering from a stomach problem and a foot injury, with the doctor recommending that this job was not suitable for him anymore. description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies

call_details.description: The job-seeker was advised to stay connected with the Issara and asked him to provide information about whether the company has insurance policies for workers at the factory. Because the job-seeker told me on the phone that the worker died on 4 July had an accident on the speed breaker (bump) at the premises of the hostel when he was returning to the hostel. He fell down from his motorbike and when some workers saw that they informed the security guards. Then he was taken to a hospital and he was admitted to the hospital for seven days at ICU then on the 7th day he was declared dead. The incident suggested that the worker was died when not on duty and on motorbike accident.

Having 450 workers engaged at work for the last 14 months, how it seems that Ramatex is not going and willing to extend their visas. It seems to be unfair and unaccountable behavior from Ramatex side following the workers' rights.

closed_notes: It is hard to assess the quality of remediation as Issara has not received concrete updates on action taken by business.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue #1.
Death of Nepalese wokers;  Frequent death of Nepalese workers due to different reasons, death from accidents outside the workplace, some suicide in their housing, and some from sickness. Workers wanted to know if they have the right to get any compensation from the company. The latest death happened on 4 July 2022. When the death happens the company normally pays around 2,000 Ringgit only. Workers think that they are supposed to get more than that. 

Issue #2. Lack of information about workers' rights; Several workers reported not knowing their rights, they said that they want to know the benefits that they have such as annual leaves, sick leaves, life insurance, and the procedures to take leaves. They added that they do not have a workers' manual that they can refer to if they want to know something. 

Talking Points; 
How does the business communicate with workers about their rights, and other policies that are related to them - what language and how often, etc? Who from HR is responsible to make sure that workers are updated with all of the information they need? 
What are the business understanding and awareness of the frequent death of Nepalese workers? 
How does the insurance policy work for foreign workers and local workers? 
Do workers have life insurance in case of death? 
Is there a worker's manual that workers can refer to when they need it? If not, any plan to have it? How can Issara support the business in the development of the manual and dissemination? To share that general information on the rights of migrant workers is on Golden Dreams that Burmese workers can read and we are in the process of having that for Nepalese workers but not for all the workers.  

Recommendations;
The business to clearly communicate with all workers under Ramatex group about the insurance policy in case of work-related and non-work-related death. The communication should also cover the process of reporting to different departments, the time frame, and benefits for the family of death worker. 

Reference; Work accidents and deaths for foreign workers are regulated under the Workmen Compensation Act 1952. However, death under this Law is related to work
According to this Law, if the injury related to work caused death, the compensation is 60 months' earnings or 18 thousand ringgit, whichever is less.


Issue #2. 

Context: About 450 workers were recruited by the business under the amnesty period which is called the "Recalibration Program" which means that the business was allowed to recruit walk-in undocumented workers during the COVID-19 period and apply for the legalization process. Workers added that the business recruited about 450 workers from different factories and promised to legalize them, however, it has passed 14 months now that the workers are not invited for any legalization process such as medical tests or fingerprints. Workers recently heard some rumors about workers' documents not being able to be legalized. Workers are concerned about their uncertain status in the future. 



Talking Points; 

-Which nationalities, and how many workers were recruited under RP and What is their status of them? 


Recommendations; 

The business should clearly communicate with all workers about the status of their documentation process including why it is taking longer than expected and what is the plan for them.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issue #1. 

If a worker is dead inside the workplace, the business will consider case by case for compensation, however, if a worker is dead outside of the factory, they are not entitled to get compensation. SOCSO and SKIPA cover up to 20,000 MYR for medical expenses. For death cases outside of the workplace, the business provides 2000 MYR as solidarity support. The business does not buy life insurance because there were some cases workers would suicide to get compensation for their family members. The business has stops the practice of buying life insurance 10 years ago. However, there are some workers who have insurance in Nepal, if they died they will get compensation from Nepal. The factory is working with the recruitment agency to get the recommended insurance company in Nepal so that workers can be benefited when needed.

The company agreed to clarify the company policy with the workers. 


It has passed several weeks now the business has not come with the update. Issara is facing challenges to get updates or responses from Ramatex HR. Since it has been several months, Issara has decided to close the case. 


Issue#2. 

Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that for the workers who were recruited under the "Re-calibration Program", we just got the confirmed result from Immigration last week and currently arranging the FOMEMA health check. For some workers with failed results, we are appealing to Immigration. We will communicate with the workers once we get the update from immigration. 

Issara suggested doing the communication before the result came out from the immigration to avoid workers having to decide about their future at the very last minute as Issara has learned from other factory workers. 

The business has not replied to these suggestions. Since it has been over several months, Issara is closing these issues with poor remarks.
remediation_notes:
Issue #1. Workers wanted to know that in case of death, whether they have the right to get any compensation from the company because when business gave 2,000 ringgit for the death happened back in July 2022, they felt that the deceased worker's family should get more than that. 

Issue #2. Lack of information about workers' rights. Several workers reported not knowing their rights and wanted to know the benefits such as annual leaves, sick leaves, life insurance, and the procedures to take leaves. 

Issue #3. About 450 workers were recruited under the amnesty period which is called the "Recalibration Program". Some received their documents and work permit but some still have not.
remediation_action:
Business shared with Issara that if the dead happened inside the workplace, the business will consider compensation, however, if the dead happened outside the factory, the business provides 2,000 MYR as solidarity support.

Re. workers to be informed about their rights, business noted the gaps and said that they would improved the communication with the workers.

With regards to the updates on documentation process, it was hard for business to give the timeline but business shared with Issara that they received the confirmed result from Immigration last week and currently arranging the FOMEMA health check. For some workers with failed results, the business submit the appeal to the Immigration and will communicate with the workers once they get the update from immigration.
remediation_results: No concreat updates from business but no report from workers either hence, the case will be closed.

description: Fees charged by upstream/village-level broker: legal but not ethical

call_details.description: Brendan made a follow-up call to A Kyee Lay to continue discussing walk-in recruitment issue.
Brendan made a follow-up call to A Kyee Lay to continue discussing walk-in recruitment issue.

closed_notes: Issara raised this issue with the business, the business responded that they do not hire any workers through brokers; however, the business did not take any proactive actions as suggested to mitigate the risks in the future.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
In June 2022, TUS announced, via translator, that they will be recruiting workers when the government opens registration for undocumented workers. The translator posted the announcement on his personal Facebook. Several workers from TUS invited their relatives and friends from Myanmar. Many of them came to Thailand using the informal channel. It’s heard that they had to pay 25,000 baht to brokers (it might be the broker couple) who arrange the transportation from Myanmar to Thailand because they also announced the job vacancy on their Facebook saying that they can help the job seekers to come to Thailand and there are no job application fees. 

When the job seekers arrived in Thailand, the broker couple (Kyang Sayar and Ma Mee), who are not TUS employees, told them that they should register pink card with other different employers first. So that it will be easy for the workers to move to TUS when TUS accepts the workers. The couple charged 13,000 per job seeker for pink card registration.

When TUS interviewed applicants for recruitment, none of these workers were invited to be interviewed. We don’t know exactly what’s the reason behind it. Maybe the workers didn’t have the document required by TUS. Maybe TUS heard about the brokers charging money from the workers. It’s unclear. There are about 70 workers using the service of the broker couple. TUS accepted other workers coming that are not tied with the broker couple. 

Getting rejected by TUS, the brokers took the workers to SCC to apply for jobs. The workers were rejected by SCC as well. Again, it’s not known why. However, some of them got accepted when they mentioned the name of TUS interpreter, who reports this information. 

The TUS interpreter, our ambassador, wants Issara and TUS to know about how the brokers are exploiting job seekers and migrant workers at TUS factory. He said he will send us the photo of the broker couple. He stresses that Issara keeps him confidential.

Talking points:
- Update TUS about this risk of brokers taking advantage of a company hiring announcement and charging fees to job seekers
- Is TUS aware that based on the company announcement, existing workers invited their friends and family back home to come to Thailand for this job opportunity?
- Is TUS aware of this broker activity?
- How did TUS determine which applicants to invite for the job interviews?  The job seekers that came with the broker were denied the opportunity to interview for the job.

Recommendations for remediation:
- Investigate this matter regarding the broker activity, and the TUS process for selection of workers to be hired as pink card workers.
- Communicate clearly to workers for all hiring announcements what kinds of job seekers should apply.  For this recent hiring of pink card workers, this was meant for undocumented workers already in Thailand and not for job seekers in Myanmar.

All workers should be able to take sick leave based on the business policy when they are sick and also should have access to their annual leaves anytime they wish. However, the business should make it clear to the workers about the procedure of taking leaves.

Issara to provide training to line supervisors, leaders, and managers.

The normal policy for the workers is if they are sick, they have to report to line leaders, and leaders to report to HR. remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context;  A group of workers who were recruited under the recalibration program by a local agent to work for Mapa glove reported not receiving their documents as of yet. They said that there are 8 of them in total (Seven Indonesian and one Nepalese). According to the workers, they are working under the management of the agent and receive their wages through the agent. They have reported not having a passport or a permit. In addition to that, workers also reported not having employment contracts with MAPA Gloves. When they have issues at the workplace, they are told to report to the agent which means they do not have access to the business grievances like other workers. Workers reported that they are happy with the working conditions, however, they wanted to have proper documentation in their hands of their safety. 

Talking Points; 
Issara team to focus on the worker's confidentiality and the safeguard for the workers and explain the business until they understand the importance of the worker's safety. 
What is the business understanding of this group of workers? How many workers were recruited during the recalibration period? 
How are the documents of these workers being managed? What is the reason why these workers have not gotten their documents even after 8 months of their work in the factory?  Who pays the monthly salary of these workers? The business or the agent? 
According to Malaysian Law, since 1 April 2019, an agency is not allowed to be the principal employer; they can only act as a recruiter. What are the business understanding and interpretations of this law?
If the business is aware that these workers are being employed under the agent, what are the challenges for the business to hire them directly under Mapa company? Has Mapa ever thought about the risks of having an agent managing the workers this way?

Recommendations for remediation and system change. 

If there are no major challenges, the business is suggested to process recruiting these workers under the company name. Before processing any steps for these workers, the business should make sure that the agent does no harm to the workers. Workers should not be asked or pressured for making calls to Issara. 
Workers and the agent should be clearly communicated about the business plan of action. 
The business should find out why these workers' documents are not being issued so far and communicate the status with the workers.
Workers should have a proper contract including information about their rights, grievances, and benefits like other workers, and they should be informed and treated like they are Mapa’s employees
Workers should receive their official documents to be able to work legally under the law of Malaysia. And for any good reason that Mapa cannot provide the documents, workers should be informed about this with a timeframe of when they can get their documents.
Workers should receive their wages through Mapa Glove not through the agent to avoid timely and accurate payment, and Mapa should have a mechanism to check and confirm this with workers and should ensure that there will be no reprisal for reporting or sharing information with Mapa and Issara. 
Workers should have access to the grievances of Mapa Glove and be remediated accordingly. Mapa may also share Issara worker voice channels should workers want to communicate in their own language and if they wish to do so for different reasons.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
This group of workers were recruited under the "Recalibration Program" through an outsourcing agent. Outsourcing through an agent during the COVID-19 outbreak is legal. These workers are under the process of legalization by the agent. Only after the legalization process is completed, the workers will become official workers of Mapa and will get the contract as well. The process is taking longer than expected by the government side and it has announced it to complete the process at the end of 2022. The business expects to finalize the process by then. 

Next steps; there are no clear next steps from the business side since the business has no leverage to do anything. It depends on the government. However, Issara communicated with the workers about the business response.
remediation_notes: A group of workers who were recruited under the recalibration program by a local agent to work for Mapa glove reported not receiving their documents.
remediation_action: After going through the process of legalization run by the agent, the workers will become official workers of Mapa and will get their contract as well. The process is taking longer than expected by the government side and it is expected to take until the end of 2022.
remediation_validation: Mapa will inform the process to the workers and Issara will also inform the workers.
remediation_results: Issara has considered closing this case as the recalibration program is beyond the control of the business and almost all the businesses are having the same issues as the government process is slow. Issara will re-open the case if workers report any concerns in the future.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Issue with electric bills and punishment for using over-limited bills. Workers reported that the business allows them to use only 20 kWh per month for each person and if any workers' bills exceed 20 kWh, the business asks workers to do gardening for 2-3 hours as a punishment on their day off. In addition to that, if workers' EC bills cross set the limit for more than two months, the business will ask workers to leave the housing and charge for that extra bill from workers. Room number of the workers who are being asked to leave the housing are 13/4 and 13/14. Workers said that there is a new housing manager who just joined three months ago to BFI and he is the one asking workers to leave the housing. In addition to that, workers also reported that they only have rice cooker, curry cooker and a fan, they do not even have fridge like other workers, however, they are the one being told of exceeding the limit. Workers also have no idea why their bills are over than others even though they do not have many EC devices. 

TPs; 

What is the business policy related to worker housing?  Does it set a monthly limit on electricity usage for the workers?  If so, how did you determine this limit?  What happens if a worker exceeds the limit?
Is the business aware that workers are only allowed to use 20 KWH per head (which is about 75B per month)?
If a worker exceeds the limit in any given month, s/he has to perform ‘gardening tasks’ for free on his/her day off?
If a worker exceeds the limit for two consecutive months, s/he is asked to leave the company housing and to find a rented room outside? 
Who is the focal person who manages the company housing?

Recommendations, 
Conduct an investigation about this issue to find out about workers having to do gardening on their day off and having to leave the housing if they exceed the electricity consumption limit. 
Review the conditions of the free housing that’s being provided to workers as a company benefit.  The limit set for free electricity should be realistic, and there should be a fair policy for charging workers for any excess use rather than setting punishments such as having to do gardening work or having to leave the dorm altogether.  
Communicate this housing and utilities benefit and its conditions clearly to all workers so they understand what is being provided to them by the business
remediation_business_steps_taken:
According to K. Onanong, HR office in charge of the dorm, all workers who live in the dorm are allowed to use a limit of electricity of 20 kWh/person if three workers live in the same room, which equals 60 kWh. The reason for the limit is that the workers are not required to pay anything, and the company calculates the cost of electricity as 20 kWh/person is sufficient and based on the company cost. If a worker used more than 20 kWh, the workers would request a maximum of three hours of clean service (sweep things, collect tree leaves, etc.)around the dorm, no gardening (cutting the trees), this isn't punishment but ask for collaboration, and also insists that no extra bill for the workers ever more than 20kWh in accordance with the dorm policy. However, if the worker is unavailable on a particular weekend, the worker may postpone to another week.

Furthermore, the company has no policy requiring workers to leave the dorm if they have used more than 20 kWh for more than two months. On the other hand, the company would assist the workers in investigating and determining why the electric bill was so high, as well as checking and repairing the electric devices for the workers.

Next step, K. Panida mentioned that the company will make verbal and written announcements to remind workers of the policy. The corrective action plan will be sent to us by next Wednesday.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that in their factory dorms, the business allows them to use only 20 kWh of electricity per month for each person and if any workers' bills exceed 20 kWh, the business asks workers to do gardening for 2-3 hours as a punishment on their day-off. In addition to that, if any workers' electricity bill exceeds this limit for more than two months, the business will ask the worker to leave the housing and find a rental outside the factory.
remediation_action:
HR explained that in the factory dormitory, each resident worker is allowed a maximum of 20 kWh of electricity. The business has this limit because this is provided free to workers and 20 kWh/person is sufficient. If a worker uses more than 20 kWh, the worker will be requested a maximum of three hours to  clean the dorm area (sweeping the floors, collecting tree leaves, etc.). This isn't punishment but the business is asking the worker to volunteer and insists that workers don't pay any money for exceeding the 20kWh limit.

Furthermore, the company has no policy requiring workers to leave the dorm if they have used more than 20 kWh for more than two months. On the other hand, the company would assist the workers in investigating and determining why the electric bill was so high, as well as checking and repairing any electric devices for the workers.

The company will make a verbal and written announcements to remind workers of the policy.  It will clarify that workers will not be asked to leave the dorm for exceeding the 20 kWh ceiling for two consecutive months. Also, when workers are asked to help out with some cleaning for having exceeded the limit, it is clear that this is to be voluntary.  In the long run, the company will come up with a transparent method to charge workers for the excess electricity use rather than asking them to "volunteer" to do cleaning work.
remediation_validation: Issara explained the business' position to the workers and they thanked us for the update.  They were not using many devices during this time and for cooking, they were using charcoal instead of an electric cooker. And in terms of the forcing workers to leave the dorm for two months of excess electricity usage, they also agreed that this may have been a rumor. A worker provided a further update saying although he didn't hear an announcement related to this issue, the situation had improved. The dorm manager didn't tell any workers to leave the dorm even if their electricity usage exceeded the limit and only required workers to pick up leaves around the compound for about 30 minutes and provided food to such workers.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case because workers are happy with the current situation that no one is being required to leave the dorms if they exceed the electricity use and the cleaning around the compound is minimal and not such a concern for them.

Issara assumed that she may have found a job which is why she may not want to carry this issue forward as she does not belong to SKP anymore. For the bigger group of workers who were repatriated without prior notice, even though it was not the mismanagement from the factory but an unclear process from the Malaysian government,  Issara suggested the business have transparency by communicating with them about their status so that workers can have their own plan in the case where their permit could not be granted by the government.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A group of workers which includes 28 of them reported being dismissed unfairly by the business without prior notice. They added that in that group, they have workers in different document types, some of them have been there as a regular MoU, and others were recruited under the “Recalibration program”. The business informed workers about their dismissal on the 21st of September and asked them to stop working starting from 22 September and be ready to be repatriated on the 30th. Workers found it very challenging to be repatriated as they were not prepared to do so and they had no idea about their documents. Workers who were recruited under the MoU process reported their documents not being provided by SKP for a year or more for some workers, and other workers who were recruited under the recalibration program reported having to provide their documents to the SKP since they arrived till now. 

Specific case about Thandar Linn. 
Worker name - Thandar Linn (ID 505554)
HR name - Ms. Fienaz
There is a specific worker who approached Issaara for a specific investigation of her case as follows. She was recruited under the recalibration program in November 2021, 11 months from now. Since her arrival to the SKP, she was given an employment contract and told that her document will be processed for legalization. Since then, she was never asked to do neither medical checkups or fingerprints. She was suspected to the business not having done anything to her document for the extension. When she arrived to the factory, she had a valid passport, visa, and 5 months of WP. If she was dismissed before her work permit expired, she would had returned back to her previous employer. When she was informed about her dismissal by the SKP HR (Ms. Fienaz), she asked what was the reason for her dismissal, Ms. Fienas replied that it was because of the delay from the business side to submit her documents for the legalization process. Because of this poor management of the HR, worker feel very upset and is not completely ready to return back as her place in Myanmar is not a safe zone given the political situaiton. Worker added there are many more workers in the same situation which she wants the business to stop doing this. She has decided to continue staying in Malaysia regardless of her document status. HR provided her passport yesterday and she is waiting for her salary. After that, she will leave SKP’s housing. 



Talking Points; 

-Given SKP’s previous reasons that there are 28 workers who were dismissed and in a plan to repatriate, can we get the detail of the workers who are being repatriated? 

-Which nationalities, how many workers were recruited under RP, and how many under the MoU process? What were the reasons specifically? If blacklisted, for what reasons? 

-What is the business understanding of the Thandar Linn case? She was told by Ms. Feinas that it was the delay from the HR side. If that is the reason, it is unfair for her as it was not a mistake from her side but from the business. In Issara’s opinion, this worker deserves compensation according to Malaysian law. What is the business understanding? 

As it was previously mentioned there are 138 workers who were in the process of appealing, what is the status and possible outcome for them?

Recommendations; 

-Individual workers are to be clearly communicated about their dismissal with written proof. 
-Those who were dismissed because of poor management from the business side should be considered for compensation equal to one month's salary according to contract clause No. 19 C.
-The remaining who are under the appealing process should be clearly communicated about their document status and the expected date for them to receive their document in their hand.
-The business to make sure all workers have proper documentation in their hands. 


Reference: Severance payments

EA Employees who have been employed for 12 months or more are entitled to the following minimum statutory severance payments pursuant to the Employment (Termination and Lay-Off Benefits) Regulations 1980:
10 days’ wages for every year of employment under a continuous contract of service with the employer if he has been employed by that employer for a period of less than 2 years.
15 days’ wages for every year of employment under a continuous contract of service with the employer if he has been employed by that employer for 2 years or more but less than 5 years.
20 days’ wages for every year of employment under a continuous contract of service with the employer if he has been employed by that employer for 5 years or more.
For non-EA Employees, the entitlement to severance payments depends on the employment contract. If the contract is silent, there is a general expectation that a financially-able employer should pay reasonable severance compensation.
10:19
The Employment Act sets out minimum statutory benefits and entitlements. However, most of the Employment Act only applies to employees who fall within the scope of the Act (referred to here as “EA Employees”). 
EA Employees are generally — (1) those whose wages do not exceed RM2,000/month; or (2) those who, irrespective of wages, are engaged in manual labor, engaged in the operation/maintenance of vehicles, supervising/overseeing other employees engaged in manual labour, are engaged in any vessel, or are engaged as a domestic servant.
This distinction between EA Employees and non-EA Employees is important, and the employment terms and conditions of non-EA Employees are usually freely negotiable between employer and employee and would be whatever is set out in the employment contract and other employment documents. Having said that, as general market practice, most non-EA Employees would be contractually-entitled to benefits as good as or better than those provided in the Employment Act (with obvious exceptions such as entitlement to overtime payments).
Reference; Remedies for Unlawful or Unfair Dismissal


Filling a complaint with the Director General of Industrial Relation:

In the event an employee feels that their dismissal is unlawful or unfair, the employee must file a complaint with the Director General of Industrial Relation within 60 days of their dismissal[9].

Thereafter, the department will attempt to settle the matter between the employer and employee[10]. If it fails, the department will then notify the Minister in charge of human resources[11] and the Minister may refer the matter to the industrial court[12].

If the court favours the employee’s case, the court can either order that the employee be reinstated or be compensated, based on the factors laid down in the act[13]. Either party can still appeal to the high court if they are not satisfied with the outcome.

Inherent Power of Minister Responsible for Human Resources:

The minister may also compel the employer to provide benefits to the employee[14].

Filling a Civil Claim:

Alternatively, an employee can claim for damages for breach of contract in the civil court.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue # (1) 

Food served at the factory canteen: workers reported not having options to choose the vendors for them to eat for their meals. They said that the meals provided in the canteen have poor hygiene and the taste is unsatisfactory. They see worms,bullet fragments and insects, hair or stone in the meals they buy from the inside canteen. Notably in the curry and rice dishes. Attempts to eat outside are thwarted by security guards who report such behavior to management, leading to warning letters. 

Issue # (2) 

Toilet issues: Workers reported there are around 30 toilets for them and it is not enough especially in the morning when everyone needs to use it. The business has previously argued having the standard of one toilet for 6 workers according to the buyer policy. However, approximately 10 toilets in the facility are either broken or not functioning properly, reported by workers. In addition to that, hostel residents also rely on these toilets, as the bathroom and toilets are in the same space and result in long morning queues. 

Issue # (3) 

Daily Water Shortages: The water scarcity issue primarily occurs at night, when a large number of workers return from their shifts and require water. It takes 20 to 30 minutes for the water supply to resume, causing considerable inconvenience for workers after their long day of work. It's possible that some senior employees have addressed this, but many of others are apprehensive about approaching HR due to concerns about potential repercussions.


Issue # (4). **Internal NOTE*: The business said that they follow the standard of the Dyson and they did not agree with this issue in our first meeting. 

Cooling fans in the housings: Workers reported that they are provided with two ceiling fans for 10 of them and it is not enough especially for the day time when the weather is too hot for day shift workers.

Thein Lwin Oo (Ko Fatee) reported that 380 Burmese MOU workers arrived to Cal-Comp on 28th September with the service of Aye Lin Leh Htut ALLH (Myanmar recruitment agency) but haven't started working yet. -How is CC working with ALLH? with the Thai recruiter?  What are their responsibilities?

Worker's info:
Name: Ms. SREY BEN
Employee code: 791299

King Pac's recruitment information: who, how many paid to which RA, when, how much for what and why, and how 

In 2022, an electronic factory named JCY from Saraburi province dismissed around 1,000 workers who had completed a 4-year MoU contract. That factory contacted 'The First' Thai RA, and most of the workers were directly recruited by King Pac. The workers were divided into two to three groups, and those who raised the issue with Issara arrived on February 16, 2022, mostly. It affects over 600 workers, at least, according to the worker.

When the workers arrived at King Pac, those who needed to renew their passports were collected 4000 to apply for a new passport on March 2, 2022, by Ma Phyu, who is the focal interpreter from 'The First'.

There is another Thai RA and its interpreter's name is known as 'Kayin Ma' (means Karen lady). That Thai RA mainly recruited walk-in workers, not the workers from the JCY factory. (Note: Before Issara visited the factory for kick-off and canteen outreach, Kayin Ma, the interpreter, and Thai RA had a communication session with workers at the housing and informed them not to inform Issara of any costs related to documents. Oct 26th: The client is the husband of HT91 interpreter Mrs. Kyu Kyu Hlaing. He is also working in HT91 in the packing line. He would like to report this case but, as his wife is the interpreter, he is worried that they will both be in Target. He will wait and make a decision and let O&E know when to raise the case.

Update on 31 Oct 2022: He has agreed that we can report this case without mentioning his name. He said, other Thai workers are not bad like A-Tart. A-Tart used to also shout at other Thai workers too. So he requested to submit the case by referring to A-Tart only. It would be great if the supervisor is aware of this and monitors A-Tart's behaviour.

He said he reported this to HR 2 months ago, using the LINE messaging app and his wife interpreted the message to the Thai HR staff. But, he didn't receive any feedback from HR and nothing has changed with A-Tart.

Nov 3rd update: He said, it's ok even if HR knows that he is the one reporting this issue. Because he cannot bear to be treated in the current condition anymore. So he requests us to talk with business about this.

Talking Points:
-How does the business deal with conflicts arising between Thai and Burmese workers?
-Is HR aware that this issue of a Burmese worker being mistreated by a Thai worker was reported in the past but HR did not take any concrete action?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Investigate this matter, and identify the cause of the mistreatment of the Burmese worker by Thai workers. Conduct the investigation without naming who reported this issue to safeguard the worker that reported it.
-Clearly communicate with all workers regarding the expected behaviors between co-workers.  Monitor the workers for improved performance.  Ensure that the workers understand that the business will not tolerate any retaliatory behavior, to ensure the safety of the worker that reported this issue.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Raweeroge, the HR manager, was aware of the situation and had already investigated and issued a verbal warning to the Thai worker.


K. Raweeroge, the HR manager responded as follows.

HR has invited both the supervisor and the worker to clarify. What is the root cause? Both of them currently understand each other and please see the results in the following conclusions:

1. The worker mistakenly assumes that the supervisor is dissatisfied with the complaint because supervisors frequently inquire about time off work, but the language barrier made communication difficult.

2. The supervisor is pleased that the worker is willing to voice their opinions in terms of what is incorrect.

3. The supervisor complimented the worker on a job well done but frequently took leave and requested that the worker improve.

4. HR has given the supervisor communication training. If you want to speak with workers who engage in lengthy discussions, it is preferable to communicate through an interpreter to avoid misunderstandings. Because migrant workers may not understand.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that in his line there is only one Burmese worker (himself) and the other Thai workers are treating him very poorly. Although they are all at the same position, this Thai worker and the others ask him to do more work than them. He reported this to HR 2 months ago, using the LINE messaging app and his wife (she is the factory interpreter) interpreted the message to the Thai HR staff. But, he didn't receive any feedback from HR and the Thai worker's behavior has not changed.
remediation_action:
HR was aware of the situation, had already investigated the matter, and issued a verbal warning to the Thai worker.  After receiving the worker update saying that the situation had not improved, HR will further investigate the situation. 

HR invited both the supervisor and the worker to discuss the issue. The worker mistakenly assumed that the supervisor is dissatisfied with the complaint he made because the supervisor frequently inquired about time off work.  The supervisor and HR clarified with the worker that the supervisor was not targeting him because of his report to Issara but was concerned about his frequent absence from work.
remediation_validation:

Issara followed up with the worker after the business investigated the matter further after the worker update. He confirmed that he had met with HR and his supervisor and they discussed the issue about his requesting sick leave and annual leave. Currently, he thinks the relationship between the workers and the supervisor is good and his co-workers are not bossy anymore. He is happy at work now.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue.  The worker confirmed that his co-worker is no longer treating him poorly and the business has taken action to address the matter and clear up the worker's perception that he was being targeted for reporting his grievance.

The workers reported that the business has increased the production targets and offering OT work only to those workers that meet the target.  Sometimes, the workers will be allowed OT work if they reach 70-80% of the target and even then, the line supervisors might increase that threshold to 90% of the target.  And even when the workers meet the varying targets, they might still not be offered to do OT work because the business does not have more garments to be sewed that day. 

TPs:
-How is OT work offered to workers?  Is OT work offered to all workers or only to those workers that meet a certain daily target during normal working hours?
-How are the daily production targets set and have the targets been increased recently?

Recommendations for remediation:
-If it is the company's policy that OT hours are offered to all workers and not tied to performance during their normal working hours, investigate how line supervisors are acting against the said policy
-Train line supervisors on how to communicate clearly about the production targets to workers and the way OT work is offered to workers
-Communicate to all workers, verbally and in writing, the company's system for OT work, that it is offered to workers without discrimination.  If it is offered based on performance, this should be clearly explained as to how this is done objectively
-Communicate to all workers, verbally and in writing, how the daily production targets are set.  If the targets change or fluctuate, there should be an explanation as to how these targets are calculated and why there might be changes in the set targets

call_details.description:
Checking with the client how they are being communicated to relocate back to the yellow building based on BHR update on business response 1461. 
(The TUS HR said TUS paid for the Sealight room rental cost in advance for the workers and TUS will arrange free transportation for them to go back and work until the end of B&S. This group of workers said if the business would like them to go back and work the business must allow them to stay close to the factory, if not they won't go back to work because the Sealight hotel and TUS are very far and the worker said they don't want to take long transportation. This part is correct. But the business didn't communicate with them that they had to stay in a yellow building and paid the room cost after one month. They just thought they would be sent back to their own room. 
To solve the problem, workers requested the TUS discussed with the Songkhla Public health care to include the Yellow building in the TUS B&S policy. The Songkhla Public health care agreed to it and allowed 9 rooms under TUS B&S. The TUS already pays for the room rental cost for the workers. The HR said workers will have to pay for the room rental cost next month because the business already arranged for the worker at Sealight Hotel and paid the rental cost in advance already but the worker doesn't want to stay there.  
 
The HR said they have communicated with the worker many times but this group of workers are still saying that they would like to go back to their room. They don't understand B&S policy and are not interested in it. O&E check with the worker how the business communicates to you for relocation back to the yellow housing? 
The client responded that the translator called the focal persons who are assigned in the SEALIGHT Hotel to buy the kid stuff and withdraw cash. The translator called those persons to let the workers know who finished quarantine and had to go back to work. As the workers refused because of the time limitation and there is a problem with the limited bathroom in the hotel, they told those assigned persons to request the business to relocate them back to their room.   
The HR said TUS B&S policy, TUS arranged 4 people in each room during B&S, the worker can choose who they would like to stay with and send the list name of the room member to HR. All local or Burmese workers have to follow the same. 
This 20 workers group is also the same, the workers choose their room members by them self and send the name list to the HR team. The HR said the HR team did not select the people and send them to the same room.)The next day, a van arrived at the hotel and they were asked to board. At that time there was one Thai lady who came and picked them up. When the workers were about to board, she asked please raise your hands if you stay in the Yellow building in front of the building, there were 8 workers there and she asked them to please choose your friends who you think can stay with you in your rooms for only 14 days. As the workers thought only for 14 days, they chose their friends. But, the translator and that Thai lady also involved suggesting or advising the workers too. For example, if there are two couples who stay in that building, they ask them to temporarily stay like only the wifes stay with another two female workers and the two husbands stay with another two male workers. 

On that day, there were also still about 50 workers being sent to other housing near Sunday Market. But, those workers are now relocated back to their own room near near the Yellow Building. That building is called "Rakkhine Housing" and the room are more spacious. The informant who has to stay with her friends in the Yellow housing is also staying there.
Further Update:27 Sep: Yesterday, around 2 PM, the Burmese Translator (Arr Don) and P' Dium (HR) came into Yellow Housing and asked some workers to do a night shift. Since the workers have to share the room with some workers who have babies and some are leaving the job, working the night shift will make them annoyed. So they asked them to relocate them back to their own room. Then they agreed and they asked the workers to sign a paper as an agreement if they are ok to work on night shift. But they have to follow  business policy and they cannot commute except to the building to work. The landlord will strictly manage this. The workers agreed and signed and they started working the night shift. And they told the workers that you cannot go back to your room by yourselves. We have to manage you by transferring you to your room.

28 Sep,  this morning, as no one came up, the workers called the translator and asked them when they could come. The translator and P'Dium came back at 8 AM again. They told the workers that you are not able to relocate now as you have agreed to stay here and we have paid for this room. If you leave now, you have to pay the room fee for this month. The workers said, yes, we will pay. But, they said they still need the approval from management.
The workers said why they did not keep the promise and they manipulated the workers like that. They asked why another 50 workers being sent to Sunday housing and now they can go back to their room "Rakkhine Housing" and not them, the translator didn't translate it back to P'Dium. They are also not happy with the behavior or performance of the translator too.  

O&E asked the following three questions to the workers:
1. Have you been told that you have to pay that room cost after one month? 
Ans: The workers said no.

2. Did you know that you can go back to the SEALIGHT hotel if you don't want to stay here? The workers said no. Even the workers who will finish quarantine in the SEALIGHT hotel will be sent back to their housing (Rakkhine Housing) soon.

3. How long were you being communicated to stay there?
Ans: The translator and P'Dium told them as long as B&S policy.
The workers also added, not only the room cost, but also sharing the room with other workers is not a good practice. Plus, they have to work the night shift, the babies crying, and a lot of distractions.
