remediation_issara_recommendation:
A group of 8 MOU workers called our hotline to report about crowded accommodation arranged by TUS. TUS arranged for three couples (6 workers) to stay in a single room. They paid 3,000 baht as a deposit to the TUS’s interpreter. The workers said that the room is too crowded and unethical for 3 couples to share the same room. These workers arrived at TUS in Oct 2022 as MOU workers. There were around 100 MOU workers in this particular batch. The Myanmar recruitment agency was Alpha World Link. They didn’t know they will be asked to stay like this. On the Myanmar side, U Hlwan Moe from AWL asked the workers how they would like to share the room. The workers said “A room with two workers (a couple)”. U Hlwan Moe noted down their name and the workers thought that they would be arranged to stay as they requested. UHM didn’t confirm to the workers that their request will be fulfilled. To make it worse, some couples were arranged to stay separately in different rooms. Out of frustration, these 8 workers tried to find a new housing near TUS factory and they found one. The housing is not ready yet to stay as it is still under construction. But the landlord told them they can stay at the housing once ready. The 8 workers paid 3,000 baht to the landlord as a deposit for two rooms. The workers are planning to share the room with 4 workers each which is a lot better than the housing arrangement done by TUS. However, the landlord returned the deposit yesterday after making the payment for the deposit 10 days ago. The landlord said that TUS made him return the deposit. The landlord didn’t give any further reasons why the deposit was returned to the workers. The workers would like to ask Issara to help with the housing issues. It’s too crowded at the housing arranged by TUS. But when they tried to find a better place by themselves, TUS prevents them. The workers do not know what agreement TUS and the landlord have.

TPs:
-What is the company's policy regarding worker housing and the number of persons per room?
-How does the company consider privacy for married couples that are being housed in the company dorms?

Recommendations for remediation:
-Company housing should ensure that housing arrangements for workers in company dorms should adequately accommodate the privacy requests of the occupants, especially married couples.
-Investigate the incident where workers that had paid a deposit to rent a room outside were denied, with the landlord saying that TUS had convinced him to reject accepting these workers as tenants
-Workers should be able to choose where they live, whether in the factory dorm or outside in private rented housing
remediation_business_steps_taken: According to K. Siliruk, HR, the company's policy regarding worker housing is that there are usually 3-4 workers per room. And some workers (couple) request private rooms, for which they must pay extra. Furthermore, workers have the option of living in the factory dorm or outside in private rented housing. So they will investigate why these workers stay in the same room with six other people, as well as the incident in which workers who had paid a deposit to rent a room outside were denied, with the landlord claiming that TUS had convinced him not to accept these workers as tenants.
remediation_notes: A group of 8 MOU workers reported that three couples were arranged to stay in a single room in the company dormitory, with limited privacy. The workers said that the room is too crowded and unethical for 3 couples to share the same room. They arrived as MOU workers in October 2022.  When asked by the recruitment agency in Myanmar about the housing, one worker had stated his desire to be in one room with his wife and had assumed that this request would be met.  Out of frustration, these 8 workers tried to find a new housing near the factory but the landlord who had initially taken a deposit from them returned the money and told them that the company had made him return their deposit.
remediation_action: Issara raised this with TUS and it replied that the company's policy is to house 3-4 workers per room. And some workers such as couples will request private rooms, for which they must pay extra. Furthermore, workers have the option of living in the factory dorm or outside in private rented housing. HR will investigate why these workers are staying in the same room with six other people, as well as the incident in which workers who had paid a deposit to rent a room outside were denied, with the landlord claiming that TUS had convinced him not to accept these workers as tenants. TUS conducted a survey of room demand from all workers again on Nov. 21, and found that there was a total increase in demand for 15 rooms.  TUS is in the process of finding additional rooms and will notify workers that wish to move their accommodation.
remediation_validation: The couples that were looking for private rented rooms were able to do so. Other workers still in the company dorms updated the situation saying that there were no issues with accommodation at this time.
remediation_results: This case is closed, as the workers now don't have accommodation issues with some finding housing outside the company dorms and those in the dorms noting they don't have issues with the accommodation anymore.

call_details.description:
On January 31, 2024, the worker from Xian-Ning called Issara and informed her about the business coaching session near the HR office around 3:00 p.m.

The business said that they did not know who reported the issues to Issara, but the Issara team would come to the factory on February 1. All the workers should cover up the issues. "The business looks after you to get a job, and you all should look after the employer too. If Issara asks, answer that you get a daily wage and OT, six days of annual leave, double wages for working on holidays, and the employer pays for the document extension cost and provides the PPE at no cost at all."

In the past, the workers had the experience of covering up the issues in front of the visitors (not sure about the audit or DOE), and then the business provided them with 300 THB for not telling the truth.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that workers are paid by piece rate, around 200-250 Baht per 8 hour shift but they should have received the minimum daily wage of 344 Baht per day. When they worked on public holidays, they were not paid at the double rate. In 2023, the business didn't fully give 13 public holidays as required by law. The business also does not cover the cost of document processing costs. Finally, workers have to pay out of pocket to buy tools needed for work and they have to pay 100 Baht to rent lockers at the factory. The business asked them to lie about all this during a recent factory audit.

Recommendations:
- Workers should be paid according to the minimum daily wage per 8-hour shift and paid appropriate wages for work on public holidays.  Work should not be paid on a piece-rate basis.
- Make this change, pay slips should reflect this new wage structure, and clear announcements should be made to all workers about the company's payment system.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 1 Feb 2024

K. Orawan HR explained that XianNing just recruited the walk-in migrant workers in October 2023. They insist and confirm that all employees get the minimum wage according to the law. 
they will investigate what is happening on the ground and get back to us next week.

They now are required to scan their faces at entry and exit, much like Thai workers. To verify and confirm working hours on the payment system and avoid mistakes in paying wages.

BHR called to clarify how they paid workers before they had their bank account numbers and entered them into the business system. She responded that she will find out and get back to us by next Tuesday.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case #1: 2 workers at Pataya Food, (Bang Par Site), ROAT Station (loading & unloading work) were unfairly dismissed on 28th Sept 2023. The client reported that the chief line-supervisor P.Yon was very verbally abusive, put so much workload on the workers and he always threatened workers saying "I can dismiss you anytime". So the 9 workers reported his abusive behavior to the office in the 2nd week of August 2023. As a consequence of this, P. Yon retaliated against the 9 workers. He assigned one staff to keep eyes on these 9 workers and find fault and take the photos of these workers actions and the movement. On 28th September, the two workers out of nine workers Mr.Ko Ko Naing (Worker ID - 16220872) and Mr. Khin Zaw (ID-16320532) were called to the office and accused of smoking in a non-smoking area and were immediately dismissed. The manager showed them a photo of them smoking and forced them to sign on the dismissal letter. Actually the area where they smoked is not a non-smoking area but it is an official public smoking area where office staff, truck drivers and other production workers come to smoke. On that day they were caught smoking, there were another six or seven workers smoking in that smoking area but only this two of them were caught in the photo. According to the client, there used to be signboards written in Thai and English as  " Smoking Area" but the manager put it down in the next few days of their dismissal.

Recommendations:
- Investigate this matter immediately.  Workers should not be targeted for dismissal as retaliation for reporting a grievance against their supervisor.  Ensure worker safeguards in place.
- Reinstate the workers, given that they were smoking in an approved smoking area, which was only changed to a non-smoking area after the workers' dismissal.
- Take disciplinary action against the supervisor, as he deliberately sought to find fault that led to the dismissal of workers that he targeted

Deadline: 1 week

Chonticha, HR manager, explained that HR was aware of the situation; they investigated and discovered that this worker was in charge of detecting anyone who entered the production line using the detector rollers. Case #1: Issara received a report that workers were dismissed for smoking in an area that was designated as a smoking area, with the smoking area sign being taken down only after the workers' dismissal.

Case #2: Workers were recently dismissed for wearing a brooch pin and without prior warning and others for not changing into flip flops to use the toilets.
remediation_action:
Case #1: The business responded that the policy of no smoking on factory grounds was enforced since December 2022, and announcements were made in the languages of the workers during the three-month period of December 2022 to February 2023. As smoking in the factory area is a serious violation, the policy states this will result in immediate dismissal. Issara escalated this to the MD given that the smoking allowed signs were still up in the area where the workers had been smoking. The MD noted that the announcement has been clear and these workers acknowledged understanding the policy. The business has now taken down the sign.

Case #2: The business stated that it has strict procedures where workers cannot wear metal items into the production area and workers understand this requirement. The worker was therefore dismissed for having worn the metal brooch into the production area. For workers dismissed for not wearing flip flops into the toilet, the business noted that this would not be grounds for immediate dismissal. The business will investigate this matter and get back to Issara.
remediation_validation:
Case #1: Workers noted that the smoking area still had the sign up on the day they were accused of smoking there although the business is saying that they enforced the policy since December 2022. Issara updated the worker saying that the business position was the policy was announced for many months and he was aware of the policy, regardless whether the sign was still there or not. The worker had nothing to say about the decision but he said he already got a new job. 

Case #2: Issara explained the reason the business dismissed her, and although she didn't agree with the decision, she accepted that the business wouldn't change its position.

Context: Cambodian workers who completed 4 years of MoU reported saying that they were charged by the recruitment agency (SMS) for the U-turn process. They had to pay a total of 25,000 THB over two payments. This includes the Travel Document (Black Passport), visa and work permit extension. For workers that needed to get the renewal without going back to their home country first, the cost was around 50,000 THB.

TPs:
-Is BFI covering the costs of document extensions for workers, such passport, visa, and work permit as part of the Employer Pays Policy? 

Recommendations for remediation:
-The business immediately communicates with SMS and other HR focals who are responsible to do the extension of workers documents and stop charging workers for the extension fees. 
-Clarify the company's policy with all workers, HR and SMS regarding recruitment fees, including extensions of legal documents for all MoU and non MoU workers, and what fees will be covered by the business. 


Note; 

For the remediation, Issara will calculate based on the survey result and recommend together.


The business owed 143,000 to workers.

remediation_action: Issara raised this with the business and BFI responded that it covers the costs of document extensions for workers except for the passport fee. Investigate Case:
19 Cambodian workers whose visas expire on 30/4/2022, a group of workers who have completed 4 years, who have received a waiver to stay in Thailand for another 6 months after applying for a second visa after completing 4 years according to the cabinet resolution 15/3. The workers asked for the latest document to be photocopied in order to apply for a visa with immigration. Coordinating at the beginning of December, there was a queue to stamp the visa on 25/12, where the workers brought the passport to the staff but had not yet received it back, which the interpreter had communicated to get it back because the company do not have the policy to keep labor passports.

Solution:
Ensure that workers are aware of their status and have a common understanding of the process for processing the documentation for this resolution. In addition to communicating by having an interpreter to coordinate, HR has arranged a meeting with workers to communicate and understand. Because the immigration requested to check the worker's documents before informing the queue in order for the company to take workers to extend the 6-month visa period by getting a queue on 25/12 because immigration was busy with a mission, applying for a visa, doing CI and checking the appearance of the entire province to be completed. All workers who submit passports to the staff every time have reiterated that they must request a return passport within a period of not more than 3 days through the interpreter if it exceeds the period or has not been returned. They can inform Khun Kung Ratchada directly. As for workers who want to apply for leave to go back to the country, they can leave as necessary but must ask the HR staff first in every case because each group of workers is allowed to stay in the country differently. In addition, every time documents from workers are collected for processing, the staff will arrange a series of meetings to clarify the workers in order to understand.

They have followed up with HR through the interpreter but have not received a clear response.  They want to make sure they get their passports back because they have a wedding event that they plan to attend in Cambodia in February 2023.
remediation_action: HR mentioned that they arranged a meeting with the workers and informed the workers of the situation. At the moment, all Cambodian workers' passports have been renewed but they need to be stamped with the visa extension. All workers have been reminded that they should get their passports back within three days and if it exceeds this period, they should report to HR directly. Workers who want to apply for leave to go back to the country, they must request it and get approval first in every case.
remediation_validation: The worker provided an update saying that the HR interpreter showed him his new passport (5-year validity) and told him the passport would be handed to him soon after it was photocopied for the visa application process.  HR also told him that he would be able to go back home with this passport in Feb 2023 as he had earlier planned.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case.  The workers know that they will get their passports with extended visas soon and will be able to take leave and travel back to Cambodia.

remediation_business_steps_taken:
According to K. Wichai, HR manager, according to company policy, no lockers for workers are opened and checked by TUM officers without their permission. And the workers have either purchased or have their own master key. As a result, the company does not have the key to unlock it. They will, however, investigate this issue and respond to us within 7 working days.


Investigation/Explanation

Mr. Kanyakorn, Assistant HR Manager, investigated and checked with the production department on 28/1/2023. The production manager 2 informed that on that day, a customer went to randomly inspect the locker without notice, resulting in the workers who own the lockers not being present.

Corrective/Responsible

Khun Kanyakorn, Assistant Manager of HR Department, discussed with Production Manager 2 and Production Manager 2 to prevent recurrence as follows:
1. There is a communication sign for randomly inspecting the Locker in order to communicate with the male/female Locker Room worker.
2. If the inspection locker is opened for GMP purposes, the owner of the locker must be present at all times for inspection.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that their lockers had been opened and checked by TUM officers without their permission.  Since workers keep important and valuable items in their lockers, such as passport, phone, purse/wallet, etc., they need to give permission before the business opens their lockers for inspection.
remediation_action: Issara raised this with the business. description: Unfair dismissal

call_details.description:
Nan Yang (SMSK) is terminating the workers in these months. The factory provided wages for a month to pink-carded workers as a form of compensation or severance pay before they were terminated.

However, the factory terminates the MOU (4, 5, and 6-year) workers very frequently without severance pay or compensation.

Yesterday, on 29 January, the interpreter Zin Ko Ko informed 6 MoU workers who completed 6 years that they will be terminated on 2nd Feb. Since last month, the worker has asked the interpreter whether she would be terminated. She also requested to be informed at least one month in advance if she would be terminated so that she could prepare. At that time, the interpreter told her that the factory had no plan to terminate the workers.

Now, it is only THREE days in advance informing the workers about the termination. The interpreter told them that there would be no severance pay for them even if they reported the issues to DLPW or DOE. During their conversation, there was two HR staff as well. The interpreter translated for them.

She said the factory does not terminate the workers in a large group because the employer does not want the workers to get together in a group to report the case. That's why the workers are terminated in a small groups separately. 

She seems so sad and cried during the call and requested Issara to help her. She received Issara's number from the ambassadors who joined the training on this weekend (29-Jan).
call_details.next_steps: to discuss the issue with BHR and ILM

call_details.description:
Good news from the worker from Nan Yang (SMSK)!

Yesterday, the interpreter contacted the worker to come to the office this morning. When the workers arrived at the office, the HR gave three different answers. 

1) They were thinking of providing severance pay. 

2) They were planning to send the workers back to Myanmar to renew the MoU. 

Finally, HR informed the worker to continue working as usual and that there was no need to worry about the document's extension because they would plan to do it. 

The interpreter told the worker that the HR staff was curious about who contacted Issara and raised the issue. They said they are now busy arranging for the extension of the document because of the worker's voice coming from Issara. 

The worker is very happy and in tears, and she updated me on her experiences calling the Issara hotline and meeting some ambassadors who joined the training on Sunday. She said, "It is the very first time I bravely contacted an organization and received precious support. Now I can continue working because of Issara. I am thankful to Issara and the ambassadors who share the Hotline number with me. I asked for a Hotline banner from them to post nearby my apartment so that many Burmese workers would see it. I will definitely share my experience with other workers too."

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case.  The worker that reported this issue is exceedingly happy that she is able to continue to work at Nan Yang and has not been let go as she had initially been told.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Nan Yang (SMSK) is terminating many workers' contracts in recent months. The factory provided wages for a month to pink-carded workers as a form of compensation before letting them go. The factory is also terminating MOU (4, 5, and 6-year) workers' contracts very frequently without severance pay.

On 29 January 2023, the interpreter Zin Ko Ko informed 6 MoU workers who completed 6 years that they will be terminated on 2nd Feb 2023. Since last month, the worker had asked the interpreter whether she would be terminated or not and had requested to be informed at least one month in advance so that she would have time to prepare. At that time, the interpreter told her that the factory had no plans to terminate the workers. Now, however, they were told of their termination only THREE days in advance, with no severance pay even if they reported the case to DLPW or DOE. During their conversation, two HR staff communicated this and the interpreter translated for them.

The worker observed that the factory does not terminate the workers in one large group to avoid collective action on the part of the workers. That's why the workers are terminated in a small groups separately. 

She was very sad and cried during the call and requested Issara to help her. She received Issara's number from the ambassadors who joined the training this weekend (29-Jan).

description: Physical and/or other serious abuse by interpreter (illegal)

call_details.description:
The issues related to workload, line supervisors and interpreter behavior: 

The day shift from production calls Yakik where the worker slices chicken meat and makes the skewer. There are 6 lines and each line has around 50-60 workers which are supervised by 2 line supervisors. The new workers were set to work in a line and they will be moved out to another line when they could do work better so, the new coming workers are easy to be target and closely monitor by the line supervisors. 

The worker raised that all the workers in Yakik generally were oppressed by the line supervisors to complete the target as they called "Yort", in an hour workers need to finish 100-150 kg meats (depend on which part of the chicken they do the skewer) and if workers can't complete the task the line supervisor will shout and scold to them by calling their ID number and sometimes even threat to the workers "If you can't do the job well just go back to your home country, please resign". Additionally, to make the skewer there is a rule to weigh the meat properly not to be over or less than the determined standard but to follow the rule workers can not complete the target as they want. 

Here are the consequences and difficulties workers face:
1. To complete the target, workers (mostly new workers because they have not gotten used to with the job yet) do the skewers without the proper weight as it takes time and when it were caught by the line supervisor, the line supervisor asked workers to sign on warning letter. 
2. When workers can't complete the target, the line supervisor shouts out their ID, scolds the workers by saying "If you can't do the job well just go back to your home country, please resign" and sometimes insult workers on the microphone. Moreover, workers were also asked to sign on the warning letter.  
3. By receiving the warning letter, workers'annual bonuses will be cut off and workers could be terminated if they received many warning letters.
4. Workers feel depressed and frightened from the managing of the line supervisors in oppressing the workers to complete the target. And some workers even skip the toilet break even if they need to because they are afraid the target will not be completed. 
5. Most workers dare not to raise issues because they are concerned about being targeted by the line supervisors. Only when the workers decide to go back home, they dare to raise the case. 

Due to #5, some workers used to raise the issue to the interpreter for her to reach out to the HR but it seems less effective and worker thought the interpreter don't deliver their complaint to the HR. The interpreter's behavior is rude and careless. The interpreter said everyone can do why you can't, and blame the worker. The worker feels disappointed and never wants to raise the interpreter again. The interpreter name Chiva. 

What the worker wants: No oppression to the workers to complete the target, treat the workers fairly with respect; no shouting, scolding and don't ask workers to resign. And the interpreter should change her behavior by treating the worker nicely and be helpful.

The worker called to inform o&e to withdraw the case as she had already moved to another line. 
The worker said, she had told the line supervisor that she couldn't work to complete the target as the line supervisor want so now they moved her to another line that she can work without the oppression of the target but there is no OT available. The worker mentioned that she is no longer at the reported line, worker request not to raise the issue to the business.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case because the worker has requested we not raise this issue with the business.

When they cannot meet the target, the line supervisor will shout and scold them, telling them to resign if they can't do their jobs.  Workers asked the factory interpreter to report this issue to HR on their behalf but the interpreter (Chiva) didn't do so and blamed the workers instead.

Rated poor due to the long delay in receiving the business response.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: The issue with the workers unapproved documents. A group of workers who were recruited under the "Recalibration Program" in 2022 reported not getting their documents since they have started working for this factory. They said that it is not clear if their documents are being processed or not. 


Talking Points: 

-What is the status of these workers? 
-What has the business done so far? 


Recommendations: 

The business to clearly communicate with the workers if the issue is with the government site.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Business responded that there are about 450 workers in this situation, the business has been trying so hard, visiting the immigration once a week to follow up. However, the government process is extra slow which caused all the delays. The good news is that the business was able to pay the registration fee to the immigration for half of the workers which means their documents are to be approved and distributed soon. For the remaining workers, it is not sure if they will be rejected or accepted, if they are rejected, the business will do the appeal as they need more workers. 

Issara suggested the business to communicate with all of the workers about these updates. 

Business responded that it is impossible for them to do so as there are so many  workers and are in different shifts. 


Issara suggested the business to issue such an update in writing so that Issara can help communicate with the workers. The business agreed to do that, however the business failed to do so. 

Several months later, the business updated that they were able to register half of the workers out of 450 and distributed their documents in their hands. However for the remaining workers who did not pass to be registered and officially work in Malaysia, the business has been trying to register under another round of "Recalibration 2.0" which is less strict than the previous one. The business is hoping to complete the application by the middle of June,2020. However, the business is not sure when the work permit will be distributed to the workers. 

Issara has updated the business response to the workers.

Workers have been following up with the Issara, however Issara is not able to get the clear update from the business yet.
remediation_notes: A group of workers who were recruited under the "Recalibration Program" in 2022 reported not getting their documents since they have started working for this factory. They said that it is not clear if their documents are being processed or not.
remediation_action:
It has been a challenge for all the business in getting approval from Immigration. Recently, the business updated that they were able to register half of the workers out of 450 and distributed the documents. However for the remaining workers who did not pass to be registered and officially work in Malaysia, the business is in the process of registration them under the second round of "Recalibration 2.0" which is less strict than the previous one. The business is hoping to complete the application by the middle of June,2023. However, the business is not sure when can they distribute the work permit to the workers.

In the latest update, the business has processed the workers as part of Recalibration 2.0 so they can work legally but they are still in the process of getting the thumbprint, health check, and getting the work permit. Among this, they have found two issues: fake passports among Myanmar workers and registered with another employer in 2023 and so cancelled in the government system.  For the passports, the business is reporting the lost passport to apply for new passports for them. For those registered with another employer, the business will do the cancellation of the former employment for these workers and then go through the government verification process. The workers know about this process and will seek updates from time to time.
remediation_validation: Issara has lost contact with the workers.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue, as the business has confirmed that the workers have been informed that they are registered as part of Recalibration 2.0 so the workers can work legally but the process to get the actual work permit is based on the government processing timeline. Rated poor due to the long delay in receiving the business response.

remediation_issara_recommendation: A worker reported that the business assigned workers to work 3 shifts since December 2022. In the current situation, there are approximately 3000 workers who are working 3 shifts. The working hours in 3 shifts are: 8 am to 4:40 pm (first shift), 4 pm to 12:40 am (2nd shift) and 12 to 8:40 am (3rd shift). Since the business started 3 shifts, the workers have been facing different kinds of challenges such as sleeplessness, lack of appetite, attacks from gangsters during the commute (especially 4 pm to 12:40 am shift workers). The business tried to extend the 3-shift system until June 2023 so the workers went on strike on 24th March 2023. In order to stop the uprising of the workers, the manager of Cal-Comp called the Line Leader meeting and propose 2 options. The first option is the business will change from 3 shifts to 2 shifts but many workers will have to be dismissed with cancellation letters and one month severance pay. And the second option is the business will keep practicing the 3 shifts but the business will take more care of workers' security and may consider to provide 1,000 Baht to workers as a shift bonus. After calling line leader meetings, the business distributed the voting forms to all workers to choose 3 shifts or 2 shifts to work. Unfortunately the voting system was not anonymous. The workers had to mention their ID and names in the voting form.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that the business assigned workers to work 3 shifts since December 2022. Since the business started 3 shifts, the workers have been facing different kinds of challenges such as sleeplessness, lack of appetite, attacks from gangsters during the commute. The business tried to extend the 3-shift system until June 2023 so the workers went on strike on 24th March 2023. In order to stop the uprising of the workers, the business allowed the workers to vote whether they wanted to go back to the 2-shift system, which would have to involve lay-offs, or to stay with the 3-shift system without lay-offs and a 1,000 Baht shift bonus.  The voting was not anonymous, and the workers had to mention their names and worker ID # in the voting form.
remediation_action: The business called Issara with a request to help explain the situation to the workers and that they should agree to keep on with the 3-shift system.  Issara declined and noted that we are not here to side with the business and communicate this message that the business requested.
remediation_validation: The workers voted to move back to the 2-shift system and this ended with the business laying off more than 1,000 workers.  The workers that had reported the issue about the business trying to pressure them to keep to the 3-shift system have been let go.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case with a poor rating. The business has resorted to laying off workers when workers expressed their request to work on a 2-shift system.

call_details.description:
Toe Wai aung - SKP အလုပ်ထုတ်ခံရ
+60 13-713 8620

closed_notes: Business communicated the process and progress of the work permit under the recalibration program to the workers and also took immediate action to inform the worker about the mis-information.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue #1 

Context: Several workers reported being dismissed from work without pre- notice. They said that they were recruited under the re-calibration program as a walk-in worker. Since then, the business has taken their passport for the registration, however workers were informed of being dismissed. 

Talking Points: 

- What caused these workers to be dismissed? 

Recommendations: 

- The business should clarify the reason for dismissal and reconsider to hire them if possible. 


Issue #2
Context: Unfair dismissal- A worker who has been working for the SKP for about 9 months called and reported that he has been asked to sign a document to be sent back with the reason of being absent from work frequently. The worker said that he has not been missing from work for more than 3 days in 9 months and it has not been two years according to his contract. He does not want to go back to Myanmar yet.



Talking Points: 

- What caused this worker to be dismissed? 

Recommendations: 

- The business shall look into his attendance to learn the number of days he has been missing from work. 
- If the workers have not been missing from work for more than 3 days as reported by the worker, the business should reconsider his dismissal. 
- If the worker is found out to be having several days of absent, the business should consider to provide compensation based on the Myanmar and Malaysian contract.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Issue #1. 

The businesses responded that the reason for workers' laid-off is not because of the business but because of the government process. The business has submitted all required documents to immigration to apply for the work permit for all workers who are in need, and after several months, the immigration replied back to SKP with the list of workers whose work permits could not be granted. The business tried appealing but only some were granted but 28 still got rejected.

Issara suggested the business to do the communication with the workers about their appealing process so that they can be prepared. Workers who were laid-off have reported Issara saying that they were not prepared to go home or find another job as they were not given any prior notice. However, the business has agreed to communicate.



Issue #2.

The business responded that they have never informed the workers being dismissed, it was a misunderstanding. The business has communicated with the worker. 

The worker confirmed being communicated about misunderstanding and now it is confirmed that the worker will not be dismissed.
remediation_notes:
Several workers recruited under recalibration program reported being dismissed from work without any pre-noticed and their passport were taken for the registration proccess. 

A worker reported that he has been asked to sign a document to be sent back to Myanmar with the reason of being absent from work frequently.
remediation_action:
The businesses submitted all required documents to immigration for the work permit which took several months, and then the immigration replied back to SKP with the list of workers whose work permits could not be granted. The business tried appealing but only some were granted but 28 still got rejected hence, business had to send them back to their home countries. 

The business confirmed that there was a misunderstanding about the dismisal of the worker so they communicated to the worker that he would not be sent back home.
remediation_validation: The worker confirmed being communicated about misunderstanding and not being dismissed. And business communicated with the workers about the appeal process and updates.
remediation_results: Workers reported improved communications from the business, and management met with the workers to explain the document process.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The business distributes only a pair of gloves a day to the workers (especially in Pae Lu, RP line). From experience, workers know only one pair a day is not sufficient for the fish peeling task. Although workers have the right to ask for new gloves when one is dirty or damaged, it is very hard for workers to ask for new gloves from the line supervisors. Therefore, the workers want to get two pairs of gloves per day.

TPs:
- Does the business replace gloves when they are damaged?
- Does the business put a limit on the number of gloves that workers can request per day?

Recommendations:
- If it is the business policy that basic personal protective equipment is provided to workers and replaced when they are damaged, workers should be able to request new gloves when their current gloves are damaged, even if it's more than one pair per day.
- Investigate why the line supervisors are not willingly replacing gloves for the workers and making it difficult for workers to even ask for them.  Also, the business should listen to the workers' experience and opinions saying that they need two pairs of gloves per day
remediation_business_steps_taken: According to the policy about the glove change, normally, a pair of gloves can be usable all day. However, if the glove is broken, the worker can ask to change new gloves with the supervisors. After investigation, the supervisor change the gloves for the workers every time. However, HR trained and communicated this policy and procedures with the supervisors and workers on 7 Jun 2023.
remediation_notes: The business distributes only a pair of gloves a day to the workers; however, workers know only one pair a day is not sufficient for the fish peeling task. Although workers have the right to ask for new gloves when one is dirty or damaged, it is very hard for them to ask for new gloves from the line supervisors. Therefore, the workers want to get two pairs of gloves per day.
remediation_action: The business responded that according to company policy about the glove change, a pair of gloves can be usable all day but workers can request for a new pair from their supervisors if it gets broken or damaged. After investigation, the business noted that the supervisors change the gloves for the workers every time. However, HR trained and communicated this policy and procedures with the supervisors and workers on 7 Jun 2023.
remediation_validation: A worker updated Issara saying that in terms of insufficient gloves, now the business practices giving workers an extra glove after lunch time. However, they also announced that the workers can also ask another one in case they need a replacement.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case, as the worker confirmed that they are getting gloves replaced and can ask for new ones as needed.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations:
Conduct regular training to line supervisors. Train line supervisors to ensure that damaged personal protective equipment (PPE) are replaced without question so that workers can carry out their functions effectively without concern for their safety.

call_details.description:
The worker said, around 20 Cambodian workers including him that come at the same batch the visa almost ended in mid June 2023. The workers hold the 10 years Passport and end 4 years MOU contract plus 2 more years visa extension, and now another 2 more years visa almost ends but their Passport validity still has 4 more years. The worker raised some concerns related to their document processing such as:
1. As the visa almost ends in mid June 2023, when the workers check with the business there is no clear response about the plan. Workers are curious what the business arranges for their document renewal (MOU u-turn) because there is no announcement to the workers yet. 
2. Some workers are concerned that when their document is renewed, their role will change or not. As the business is going to renew the contract with the workers when the workers go back to work; are they back to their role and position? 
3. Is there a way that workers can process the new document without leaving the country because their passport is still valid but they just need the new visa?

The business response has been informed to the worker:

As around 20 workers their visa will expire in mid-June 2023, the business responded that they will communicate with the workers to clarify and explain for the MOU u-turn process on 26/05/2023. And also confirmed that even all workers' documents will be renewed but their title and position still remain, there is no change or replacement. 

The validation from the worker:

The worker said the business already called and communicated with them about the document process. As workers still have a valid passport, the process would be easier. The business mentioned to the workers that maybe workers just need to go to the border for a day to do a 2 year visa. For any updates, the worker will get back to the o&e.
call_details.next_steps: To close the case

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case.  The business has clarified with the workers that it will facilitate and pay for the U-turn process, and the workers have confirmed that they understand what will happen now.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The worker said he and around 20 Cambodian workers came to work in the same batch and their visas will expire in mid-June 2023. The workers hold 10-year validity passports and have completed their 4-year MOU contracts during Covid which was extended during that time for 2 more years but this is now going to expire. When the workers checked with the business about whether their legal work documents will be extended, there was no clear response. If they were to go back home for the MOU U-turn process, the workers also have questions about whether they will get their current jobs back when they return. 

TPs:
- How does the business communicate with workers when their visas, WPs, MOU contracts are going to expire?  Do they alert them about next steps, whether they will be extended or not?  How soon in advance before the expiration date does the company communicate with each worker or batch of workers?

Recommendations:
- Hold a communication session with this batch of 20 Cambodian workers, to help them understand what the process will be given that their visas are going to expire in mid June.  
- If their contracts will be extended, inform them about the MOU U-turn process, the steps involved, the parties involved (like the RA), cost and who will pay, and the timeframe. Be clear on the nature of their jobs, roles and responsibilities when they return to start a fresh MOU cycle.
remediation_business_steps_taken: K. Anchan, HR will communicate with the Cambodian workers on May 26. They intend to continue hiring Cambodian workers and will proceed with the MoU Uturn. When the workers return, they will all be given the same role and responsibilities.
remediation_notes: A batch of 20 Cambodian workers came to work together and their visas will expire in mid-June 2023. The workers hold 10-year validity passports and completed their 4-year MOU contracts during Covid which was extended during that time for 2 more years but this is now going to expire. When the workers checked with the business about whether their legal work documents will be extended, there was no clear response. If they were to go back home for the MOU U-turn process, the workers also have questions about whether they will get their current jobs back when they return.
remediation_action: The business will communicate with the Cambodian workers on May 26. They intend to continue hiring Cambodian workers and will proceed with the MoU U-turn process. When the workers return, they will all be given the same roles and responsibilities.
remediation_validation: The worker said the business already called and communicated with them about the document process. As workers still have a valid passport, the process would be easier. The business mentioned to the workers that maybe workers just need to go to the border for a day to do a 2-year visa.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case.  The business has clarified with the workers that it will facilitate and pay for the U-turn process, and the workers have confirmed that they understand what will happen now.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations:
- As there are many batches of workers whose legal documents will be expiring at different times, the company should set a protocol so that xx days in advance of a contract/visa/WP expiration date, workers will be informed about the next steps.
- HR to conduct these communication sessions with each batch of workers according to the protocol

description: Unfair dismissal

call_details.description:
Female worker who went back to Myanmar from YRC called Yan Naing this afternoon. She arrived safely at her home last night 8 pm. The total reimbursement amount she received is 58,053 THB. It is included:
1) Stipend 31,770 THB
2) Accommodation 500 THB
3) Transportation 8,900 THB
4) Overstay visa fine 13,000 THB
5) Jobless Paid 3,883 THB

In the meeting with seven workers, the employer informed them that transportation to Mae Sot will be arranged and that 3000 THB will be provided for transportation in Myanmar to go back to their village.
Here are the risks and relevant information for workers:
No Myanmar RA name is clearly provided by the employer. The workers were told that the employer would contact Thai and Myanmar RAs recommended by Golden Dreams.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
There are four MoU workers whose visas and work permits will expire in August 2023. The HR staff informed them that they would be let go after the documents expired. The HR department said each worker would be provided with 10,000 THB upon separation. The workers would like to get severance pay according to the number of working years at YRC. They would also like to get proper cancellation letters to change employers because they would like to try to change the employer before they leave the country.

Myo Kyaw Zin's Visa/WP expires on August 15, 2023. Last working day on August 10, 2023. 
Aung Ye Naing's visa/WP expires on August 6, 2023. Last working day on August 3, 2023.

Talking points:
- Why has the business chosen to not extend these workers' employment?  Is it due to performance or is it due to government regulations?
- Is the business aware that the Thai DOE considers that migrant workers should receive severance pay when the business ends the employment, just like Thai workers?

Recommendations: 
- Provide severance pay to worker according to their years of service
- Provide cancellation letters so that they can find new employers here in Thailand, given that the situation in Myanmar is unstable and potentially unsafe for them to return
- Consider offering the workers the option of doing the U-turn process so that they can return to work on a new MOU cycle
remediation_notes: There are four MoU workers whose visas and work permits will expire in August 2023. The HR staff informed them that they would be let go after the documents expired. The HR department said each worker would be provided with 10,000 THB upon separation. The workers would like to get severance pay according to the number of working years at YRC. They would also like to get proper cancellation letters to change employers because they would like to try to find a new employer in Thailand.
remediation_action: Issara reached out to the business, and HR responded that they had consulted with the Thai Department of Employment and DOE had advised that the business doesn't have to pay for severance since the contract is ending and it's not the business dismissing the workers. Therefore, YRC will only provide 10,000 THB each to the 4 workers. YRC also doesn't have plans to do the MoU U-turn for these workers because the business orders have decreased and they are more keen to hire Thai workers because hiring migrant workers is difficult given the inconsistent government policies on migrant worker management. Finally, the business said it will cover the costs for the repatriation of these workers back to Myanmar.
remediation_validation:
Among the four workers, two had to pay for recruitment fees and document extension fees themselves. They should be reimbursed for this according to the business' Employer Pays Policy. The workers did not mention this truthfully in the recent recruitment survey conducted by Issara because they were afraid of retaliation by the interpreter or HR staff. They added many workers had to pay the interpreter to extend their visas and WP, but they kept quiet during the survey. As the husband of the interpreter is working at the factory, and they are worried that he is hostile to the workers.

All four workers confirmed that they received the lump sum payment from the business, around 16,700 Baht each.

Regarding the recruitment fee reimbursement of two workers, Issara will share the survey results with the business soon, based on which reimbursement will be recommended.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case. The workers understand that the business is not obligated to extend their contracts and have confirmed that they have received lump sum payments upon separation.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: Have a clear policy on worker separation and how this will be dealt with, whether it will be to pay severance just like the company would do for Thai workers.

call_details.description: This is a call from a pilot knit worker reporting abusive line supervisor

Ko Thu reported that Phee Wah and Phee Lit not keep identifying for the workers who reported the case to Issara anymore and they managed the line as if nothing had happened. In terms of the behavior Phee Lit is not complaining and shouting as before and none of the supervisors used the words like " you can go back to your country anytime".

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case, with workers noting the improvements in how their supervisors are treating them. However, the business did not take concrete action regarding this poor treatment by line supervisors.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client reported that the chief line supervisor from E-Zone (P' Watt), often comes to the E-Zone line workers (especially to Walk-in workers in E-Zone) and accuses them of working slowly because they haven't been getting OT work since the Songkran Festival. But workers are trying to reach the target of 200 shirts within the 8-hour shift, regardless of whether they get OT or not.  They feel the chief supervisor is complaining for the sake of complaining and when she says, "if you don't want to work here, you can resign anytime and go back to Myanmar and we have many more to come", it hurts their feelings because of the unstable political and economic situation back home in Myanmar.

Recommendations:
- Supervisors should be verbally encouraging and affirming, rather than disparaging to the workers under their supervision
- To suggest migrant workers go back home is a xenophobic remark that is unprofessional and should not be spoken by supervisors in any circumstance
- Any criticism of low performance should be based on actual productivity numbers, and accompanied with advice on how to improve performance not verbal threats to leave the country.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that the chief line supervisor often comes to the E-Zone line workers (especially to walk-in workers) and accuses them of working slowly because they haven't been getting OT work since the Songkran Festival. But workers are trying to reach the target of 200 shirts within the 8-hour shift, regardless of whether they get OT or not.  When she says, "if you don't want to work here, you can resign anytime and go back to Myanmar and we have many more to come", it hurts their feelings because of the unstable political and economic situation back home in Myanmar.
remediation_action: Issara raised this issue with the business. The business is not sure who this supervisor is; the business will investigate and get back to Issara in two weeks.  The business usually organizes training for their line supervisors twice a year, typically in June and December and will train them on effective communication with workers.
remediation_validation:
Issara followed up with workers and they said the verbal abuse and pressure to reach the target is still happening. Other line supervisors under the chief supervisor also are acting in a similar way, telling workers to "go back Myanmar if you don't focus on this work".

In a more recent update, a worker updated Issara saying that the line supervisors are no longer complaining and shouting at them as before.  They are also acting as if nothing happened even though before they were accusing workers for having reported this issue of their poor treatment of workers to Issara.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case, with workers noting the improvements in how their supervisors are treating them. However, the business did not take concrete action regarding this poor treatment by line supervisors.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
Recommendations:
- Conduct line supervisor training which includes content related to cultural and racial sensitivity, so that employees don't feel verbally abused based on race, nationality, culture, etc.

description: Issues with workforce and workloads: no violation of law or employment contract

call_details.description:
The worker who drives the forklift in the factory raised that the factory has reduced manpower to work so that there are not enough workers to work and it takes time-consuming. 
Before, two workers had to work together to carry the load with a forklift, and now there is only one. 
The worker had raised the issue at the HR office, but no action was taken. 
The workers would like to have enough manpower like before.

This is the follow-up call with the forklift driver from Seapac SMSK on June 8, 2023.

The driver said he had already resigned from his job and it was okay not to raise his issue with the employer because he was not working more for Seapac. However, the driver provided more information about his workload. The forklift driver does not have to carry the load by hand. The driver just needs to carry the load and boxes on the forklift and drive from one building to another. In the past, the line supervisor gave frequent breaks, and no driver had to drive all the time. And sometimes, when a driver gets too tired, another driver can help him drive. Now no one can help each other, and the drivers feel very tired. When he requested it from the supervisor, the supervisor did not allow it. Many forklift drivers have left their jobs, and now he feels like the manpower is not enough to help drive each other.

And what he understands is that the forklift driver from other factories receives around 40 THB for the extra fees. That 40 THB is provided by the external company that operates these forklifts. In Seapac, the forklift drivers receive only 10 or 20 THB. The drivers are not happy about it as well.

The driver was asked whether Issara needed to raise the issue with the supplier; he said it would be difficult to provide more updated information after raising the issue. So, he said it was fine not to escalate the issue with the employer.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case.  The worker has already left the business because he couldn't handle the workload.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that there used to be two forklift drivers but now there is only one.  They would carry heavy loads from the production line to the place for packaging and then moved around with the forklift machine. The worker raised this issue to HR already but no action has been taken. They would like to have enough manpower like before.

TPs:
- What is the job description of the forklift driver? Does the driver also need to carry heavy loads in addition driving the forklift machine?
- Has there been a manpower reduction among workers carrying loads for packaging and transporting using the forklift machine?
- What was HR's response to the worker's request for additional manpower?

Recommendations:
- Communicate in a timely manner to the worker that raised the concern to HR what the business plan and response will be

call_details.description:
This is the follow-up call from a worker from King Pack regarding passport renewal announced by the interpreter, Ma Phyu, from The First Good Man (Thai RA).

On the payday of January 5th, Ma Phyu announced that the workers had to pay for passport renewal: 5000 THB by January 6th. Many workers requested that she wait until the next payday on January 20, and she accepted the request.

Some workers called Issara and informed her about the interpreter's announcement for collecting passport fees. (Jonah received the call.)

On January 20, the workers went to meet the interpreter and informed her to wait for a while until the payment came into their bank account. At that time, the interpreter told the workers that she would not accept the money from the workers and would not extend their passports because she heard that some workers reported her to Issara. The workers said it was not to report her passport fee collection, and it was just a call to cross-check. The interpreter said that just a call to cross-check is the same as reporting her to Issara.

She said, "I would not accept your money and not renew your passport anymore. If you can wait until the employer renews for you, just wait. If the employer does not renew, it is up to the employer. If you are not hired anymore, just accept that situation and quit your job."

Now the workers feel very upset about it. The interpreter, Ma Phyu, does not seem to extend the workers' passports anymore because she knew that the workers had contacted Issara.

Some of the workers' passports will expire in February, and some of the workers' passports will expire on March 13.

The workers are worried about their passports now and have concerns about the interpreter retaliating against them for contacting Issara.
call_details.next_steps:
John - to prepare talking points to raise the issue with the supplier ASAP. 

Note: The safeguard of the workers is very crucial since the interpreter knew who called Issara and they are concerned about their safeguard now. 

In the past, the suppliers promised that the interpreters from Thai RAs would not be used anymore. Why are they still involved in the document process and trying to charge the cost from workers? Is the supplier aware of it?

call_details.description:
This is the follow-up call from a worker from King Pack regarding passport renewal.

On January 31, five HR staff and the interpreter from the production line met the workers and checked the workers' passport expiration dates.

The HR said, "I'm not sure we can renew your passport on time, but we will renew the passports for all the workers without charging the cost. Does someone collect the money from you now? If yes, come to inform the HR office directly."

However, the HR did not provide the exact date or the process for renewing the passport. The workers are still worried that the supplier will not renew their passports. 

The workers requested that Issara reach out to the supplier and ask for details of the process of renewing passports and the date to renew their passports.

The worker updated that the last meeting with the business was on January 31, and there was no other meeting or updates from HR about the passport renewal. 

Now it is half of February, and the workers are worried about how to renew their passports on time. The workers would like to know what they should do.
call_details.next_steps: Issara BHR: to reach out to the business

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A walk-in MOU worker moved to King Pac from Saraburi with the service of The First Good Man RA. He reported that the business asked 13-14 workers whose passport will expire in Feb 2024 to give 5,000 Baht the next day for the passport renewal process. As it is the very last minute notification, the workers are facing difficulties to give 5,000 baht.

TPs:
- Are passport renewal fees not covered by the employer as part of its EPP?
- Why were the workers informed about needing to cover this cost on such short notice?

Recommendations:
- Communicate well in advance with workers regarding all document processes, such as passport/visa/WP renewals, so that any preparations needed on the part of the workers can be made without having to rush because of the short notice given by the business
- Communicate clearly with migrant workers about all the fees and costs involved in recruitment and all document renewals/extensions, and a breakdown of what is covered by the employer and what is to be covered by the worker, if any.

call_details.description:
Sick leave: the requirement of a medical certificate

The King Pac factory has a total of six working zones, such as A, B, C, D, E, and F. Some production zones are separated into two parts: inside and outside, but some production zones are not separated. Each zone has 3–4 supervisors, so the workers cannot say the name exactly.

Many workers from different zones are facing the same issues regarding the requirement of medical certificates for taking one or two sick days.

The supervisors from Zone B asked the workers to request sick leave three days in advance. Who would know whether they would be sick the next day? If the worker has no MC, the day is marked as absent and not paid.

The supervisors from the storeroom also asked the workers to submit MC, even if they took one day of sick leave. If the worker has no MC, the day is marked as absent and not paid.

The workers in Zone C also face the same issue.

One worker did not mention the zone, but what he said is that the supervisor suspends those who take sick leave from work for a few days as a punishment called 'Phet Ngan'. (If a worker takes sick leave frequently or does not submit MC, the worker is suspended to work 7 days during the low season, or something like that.)

That's why it is difficult for workers to mention the names of their supervisors exactly, and many workers are facing the same issues in different production zones with different line supervisors.

Inquiring with the supervisor It was discovered that the majority of supervisors Obtain a medical certificate from a current employee. The following are the reasons given by the supervisor for the request.
1. To prevent the spread of COVID-19, employees who become ill should seek medical attention. to detect COVID-19 and obtain a medical certificate to confirm the absence of COVID-19
2. To prevent frequent sick leave behavior that may be false on the part of some employees. not seriously ill
3. To protect employees' interests when it comes to annual worker evaluations. Absence/absence / (Time Attendance) is a criterion for evaluating employees' annual performance. Sick leave with medical certification It's preferable to taking sick leave without a medical certificate.

Immediately Action:
- On 9 June 2023, Organize a meeting and training to clarify complaints and remind supervisors of their legal right to sick leave if they want to protect the employee's benefits. must explain the reason Allow the staff to acknowledge rather than force or request a medical certificate. In the case of employees taking 1-2 days of sick leave as required by law, Providing a medical certification is the employees' right to decide whether or not to retain their rights
- On 14 June 2023 communicate with workers by holding a meeting to clarify the workers' rights again


BHR recommended that King Pac communicate with the impacted workers who did not receive proper sick leave, and that the workers contact HR directly for remediation. They agreed and will make the verbal and written announcement this week.
remediation_notes: Workers in some production lines reported needing a medical certificate even for being sick for 1 day. Another worker said the supervisor suspends those who take sick leave frequently for 7 days as punishment.
remediation_action:
The business responded that workers are always paid for sick days even if they do not have a medical certificate. HR had a meeting with line supervisors on June 9th and with workers during the morning talk on June 14th, the business has communicated about the sick leave policy in all languages of the workers. Based on the worker update, the business will also announce to workers that those affected by this should contact HR directly for remediation.

In the country escalation, HR met with supervisors and workers, and explained that workers have the right to take sick leave, no MC needed for 1-2 days. If they were not approved for sick leave, they should go to HR directly and they will check case by case. HR (verbal and written) announced this on Aug 29, 2023.
remediation_validation:
The workers provided an update saying they have not heard any announcements from HR about the sick leave policy yet. Workers provided further information saying many supervisors marked them as absent with no pay for being sick even for one day if they cannot show a medical certificate.

In the latest update, the workers said there was no announcement about the sick leave policy or remediation. The workers still have to submit the medical certificate for taking 1-2 days of sick leave.

Some workers saw the written announcement about the sick leave policy in one building and also near the scanner. If they have issues, they will go to the HR office.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue. Workers confirmed that the sick leave policy is clear about not needing medical certificates for less than three consecutive days.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:

Conduct regular training of line supervisors, including how to implement key company policies such as the sick leave policy

call_details.description:
King Pac's recruitment information: who, how many paid to which RA, when, how much for what and why, and how 

In 2022, an electronic factory named JCY from Saraburi province dismissed around 1,000 workers who had completed a 4-year MoU contract. That factory contacted 'The First' Thai RA, and most of the workers were directly recruited by King Pac. The workers were divided into two to three groups, and those who raised the issue with Issara arrived on February 16, 2022, mostly. It affects over 600 workers, at least, according to the worker.

When the workers arrived at King Pac, those who needed to renew their passports were collected 4000 to apply for a new passport on March 2, 2022, by Ma Phyu, who is the focal interpreter from 'The First'. 

On November 22, 2022, the interpreter announced the cost of a visa and work permit extension on their internal Facebook closed group. The post said the worker had to pay a total of 23,700 THB three times: the first payment was 10,000 THB, the second payment was 8,100 THB, and the third payment was 5,600 THB, which was confirmed by the HR office. No workers were informed of the clear cost breakdown.

The workers are not aware of what kind of visa and work-permit status they are entitled to now. Their passports and work permits have been retained as reasons for the document extension. When the workers asked for the documents, the interpreter said they were in the process of being extended.

There is another Thai RA and its interpreter's name is known as 'Kayin Ma' (means Karen lady). That Thai RA mainly recruited walk-in workers, not the workers from the JCY factory. (Note: Before Issara visited the factory for kick-off and canteen outreach, Kayin Ma, the interpreter, and Thai RA had a communication session with workers at the housing and informed them not to inform Issara of any costs related to documents. That's why many workers keep quiet about the fees.)
call_details.next_steps: To update in supply chain meeting and ILM team.

The worker and his wife who had to pay 27000 THB to the interpreter for the pink card registration went to the HR office and met K. Ping Pong. Now the interpreter contacted him and returned 25,000 THB. 
His friend also got back 6,500 THB. 
So a total of 31,500 THB was returned to the workers by the interpreter.

description: Discrimination on workloads and assignments

call_details.description:
The production line named 'sin-tike' is the line where workers have to set up the bobbin in the machines. There are around 30 workers, including Thai and Burmese. The workers have regular OT from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. almost every day. But the issue is that the supervisor provides extra OT hours from 8:00 to 10:00 p.m. to only 7-8 workers.

Only those 7-8 workers are provided a job on Sunday with double pay.

So, the other workers feel the behavior of the line supervisor, who provides OT and works on Sunday, is unfair. It has been happening for over a year already.

The workers would like to know why the line supervisors treated them unfairly regarding OT and Sunday work because all the workers have to work equally as assigned.

The workers want the line supervisor to provide the same OT hours to everyone or rotate for the extra OT and Sunday work.

The workers' production line is 'Sin-Tike', 2121.

On June 6, 2023, around 8:30 a.m., a director (the worker said 'Phaw-aww") and the translator had already visited the production line and met the workers, asking about the overtime. Some workers raised the issue with that director. After that, the director asked the supervisor to provide OT fairly to all the workers equally from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. only.

The workers would like to say thanks to the director for coming and listening to their voices, and they are happy and satisfied. The workers also confirmed their production line number with Issara as above.
call_details.next_steps: To inform the production line number with the supplier and get the date they will train and the supervisors

call_details.description:
On 5.6.2023, the director and the manager of the department came and met with the workers and listened to what the workers raised.

On 6.6.2023, the manager of Department 2121 had a communication session with all workers from production and announced the overtime.

On 7.6.2023, the supplier (managers from the HR office) had another communication with workers and made the announcement.

All the workers will get OT from 6:00 - 8:00 p.m fairly. No more workers get extra overtime.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case.  The business has clarified to the workers that all workers will now be offered 2 OT hours per days, 6 days per week, rather than giving some workers 2 OT hours and giving others an additional 2 more OT hours.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
There are around 30 Thai and Burmese workers in the "sin-tike" production line where workers have to set up the bobbin in the machines. They get regular OT from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. almost every day but the supervisor provides extra OT hours on top of that from 8:00 to 10:00 p.m. and work on Sundays for double pay to only 7-8 workers. This has been happening for over a year, and the workers want the supervisor to distribute the OT hours and double-pay work broadly to the whole group rather than just to the 7-8 workers.

NOTE: Several workers called Issara about this same issue

TPs:
- What is the business' OT policy and maximum working hour cap per week?  Ask for the written policy regarding OT.
- How is OT work offered to workers, based on what criteria?

Recommendations:
- OT hours should be offered to workers fairly, without discrimination or on a preferential basis
- Investigate the matter, with worker safeguards. The business to make it clear to the supervisor not to target the workers after this investigation. Check HR records of OT hours worked, by worker.
- If the supervisor has been offering OT hours preferentially and unfairly, discipline the supervisor according to the company's disciplinary policy.
- Communicate to workers, verbally and in writing, the business' method of offering OT hours to workers and explain the fairness of the method
remediation_notes: There are around 30 Thai and Burmese workers in a production line where workers have to set up the bobbin in the machines. They get two OT hours almost every day but the supervisor provides two extra OT hours on top of that and work on Sundays for double pay to only 7-8 workers. This has been happening for over a year, and the workers want the supervisor to distribute the OT hours and double-pay work broadly to the whole group rather than just to the 7-8 workers.
remediation_action: Issara raised this issue with the business, and HR wanted to get more specific information from Issara about in which line this was taking place to be able to investigate the matter. HR said the OT policy is maximum of 12 OT hours per week and maximum of 3 days per week, meaning this would be 4 OT hours for 3 days per week.
remediation_validation: A worker updated Issara saying that on June 6, 2023, around 8:30 a.m., a director and the interpreter had already visited the production line and met with the workers, asking about the overtime. After that, the director asked the supervisor to provide OT fairly to all the workers equally from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. only. The workers would like to say thanks to the director for coming and listening to their voices, and they are happy and satisfied.  In the latest update from the worker, the business announced to workers for three days (June 5-7, 2023) that OT will be 6-8pm only each day, and will be offered to all workers
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case.  The business has clarified to the workers that all workers will now be offered 2 OT hours per days, 6 days per week, rather than giving some workers 2 OT hours and giving others an additional 2 more OT hours.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
- Ensure that the business has a clear policy on OT work, which provides a fair system for offering OT hours to workers without discrimination or preferential treatment.
- Ensure that the business trains supervisors on proper implementation of the OT policy so that they do not abuse their position of authority

Context: An abusive senior worker: Several workers from the mixing department reported his abusive behavior towards his fellow colleagues. As he has been working for Mapa for more than 10 years, he has good relationship with line supervisors and the HR even though he is not yet neither a line leader or supervisor to do monitoring of others work. However, he threatens his fellow colleagues with their visas being canceled if they do not follow what he asks, constantly interferes in their matters, acting like a detective and exaggerating issues. He reports everything to their supervisor making issues to non issues. In addition to that, he also threatens workers with physical harm as well as putting pressure on if any workers do not borrow money when he needs it. 


Talking Points: 

-Has the business ever received issues from workers about him? If, yes, what have been the actions so far? 


Recommendations: 

-The business to conduct immediate investigation based on the several workers' reports against him. 
-The business to make sure the safeguard of other workers as the issue came from a small production where only 17 workers work and it could be easy for him to identify the whistle-blower. 
-The business should communicate with all workers about the business policy that against abusive working conditions.
remediation_business_steps_taken:

The business will conduct an investigation and get back to Issara. 

Workers updated that the offender was trying to find out who the reporter was saying that he will cancel their visa and send them back to Nepal because the line supervisor supports him. 


Issara updated the business about this update from workers, the business responded that they had communicated with the production manager, line supervisor about this abusive worker behavior since last week. In addition to that, the business had communicated with the offender just yesterday which was after the offender had threatened whistle blowers. The business added that they are confident that he will not be threatening again because HR has already communicated with him yesterday and he seemed to understand the business's no retaliation policy. 

Issara has communicated back to the worker and has not received additional concerns from them, therefore, this case is decided to be closed.

remediation_results: Workers receive no further threats from the abusive workers and expressed no concern therefore, this case is closed.
