remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Issue with the sexual harassment: Several workers reported sexual harassment being practiced by the production manager in different ways as following: 

Worker A;
It has been reported that he tends to offer Overtime and extra bonuses in exchange for date nights and  intimate relations and those women who decline his offer are being treated poorly. It has been reported that there was an Indonesian female worker who suspected of going out for a date with him but later left the job. It is also reported by the aunt who worked in Mapa that her niece has gone out for night dating a couple of times with that manager (note: this information was shared by the aunt of the girl who went out with this manager, however this aunt has recently left and is currently in Nepal). 

Worker B; 
There was also an incident where this manager pulled the stripe of a female worker's bra at the workplace and he used very rude and unpleasant words with the workers whenever he is not happy with the particular workers. He used bad words such as comparing female workers' appearance and their private parts and saying that your private part looks like this and that based on your appearance. Workers reported that there were a couple of Nepalese and Indonesian female workers going out with his manager (second hand information). 

Worker C; 
The manager usually approaches naive workers and newly recruited workers who are vulnerable and cannot speak Malay and/or English languates. For those who do not speak Malay language, he asks someone as a mediator who communicates with the targeted female worker and arranges grab car to pick the workers at the housing.  For those who speak the language, he firstly asks for the phone number and starts the conversation.


Issara recommended the followings: 

- The business shall conduct careful and thorough investigation to identify the impacted   workers since there could be many impacted workers. After the investigation, the business to make sure expectations of the victims are addressed. 
- The business shall make sure there is no retaliation and unintended negative consequences against workers during and after the investigation, and to also ensure that reported workers and affected workers will be fully protected. 
- The business shall check CCTV around the area where the offender works as part of investigation, and to keep the footages as the evidences. 
- Issara to provide psycho social support to the workers if needed, and also support the investigation process as needed.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
30 April, 2023: The business responded saying that they are aware of the issue however it was 2022 that they have given warning to this manager, however the business wanted to know if this is happening after 2022 or not. 

And after Issara confirmed that the abuses happened after 2022 April, after the warning, and happening till now, the business has seriously considered and discussed with Issara on the steps they would take and started the investigation process.  

18 May, 2023: The business requested to Issara to communicate with the workers and seek their consent to talk with the business in a confidential investigation. In addition, the business also asked Issara whether there were any complaints from Indonesian workers. When Issara confirmed that, according to Nepalese informants, Indonesia workers are also affected, the business said they would try to contact former Indonesian workers who have returned to Indonesia and current workers who might be willing to provide information.   

22 May, 2023: Three workers updated Issara that they had already spoken with the business at the coffee shop and had the conversation about their experiences on the behavior of the manager. A former Nepalese worker also talked to the business and provided all the information. Workers reported that they were happy about the investigation but a few still skeptical and doubtful that effective action would be taken to the manager.
remediation_business_steps_remaining: The business have gathered good evidence and in the process of getting legal advice. After that they will inform and engage the HQ.
remediation_notes:

remediation_action:

remediation_validation: Issara staff reached out to workers who involved in the investigation process to validate the outcomes.

call_details.description:
King Pac's recruitment information: who, how many paid to which RA, when, how much for what and why, and how 

In 2022, an electronic factory named JCY from Saraburi province dismissed around 1,000 workers who had completed a 4-year MoU contract. That factory contacted 'The First' Thai RA, and most of the workers were directly recruited by King Pac. The workers were divided into two to three groups, and those who raised the issue with Issara arrived on February 16, 2022, mostly. It affects over 600 workers, at least, according to the worker.

When the workers arrived at King Pac, those who needed to renew their passports were collected 4000 to apply for a new passport on March 2, 2022, by Ma Phyu, who is the focal interpreter from 'The First'. 

On November 22, 2022, the interpreter announced the cost of a visa and work permit extension on their internal Facebook closed group. The post said the worker had to pay a total of 23,700 THB three times: the first payment was 10,000 THB, the second payment was 8,100 THB, and the third payment was 5,600 THB, which was confirmed by the HR office. No workers were informed of the clear cost breakdown.

The workers are not aware of what kind of visa and work-permit status they are entitled to now. Their passports and work permits have been retained as reasons for the document extension. When the workers asked for the documents, the interpreter said they were in the process of being extended.

There is another Thai RA and its interpreter's name is known as 'Kayin Ma' (means Karen lady). That Thai RA mainly recruited walk-in workers, not the workers from the JCY factory. (Note: Before Issara visited the factory for kick-off and canteen outreach, Kayin Ma, the interpreter, and Thai RA had a communication session with workers at the housing and informed them not to inform Issara of any costs related to documents. That's why many workers keep quiet about the fees.)
call_details.next_steps: To update in supply chain meeting and ILM team.

call_details.description: As the supplier confirmed, Issara Burmese staff reached out to the workers and informed them that King Pac was going to use 10 news translators who got promoted. call_details.description:
This is the follow-up call from a worker from King Pack regarding passport renewal announced by the interpreter, Ma Phyu, from The First Good Man (Thai RA).

On the payday of January 5th, Ma Phyu announced that the workers had to pay for passport renewal: 5000 THB by January 6th. Many workers requested that she wait until the next payday on January 20, and she accepted the request.

Some workers called Issara and informed her about the interpreter's announcement for collecting passport fees. (Jonah received the call.)

On January 20, the workers went to meet the interpreter and informed her to wait for a while until the payment came into their bank account. At that time, the interpreter told the workers that she would not accept the money from the workers and would not extend their passports because she heard that some workers reported her to Issara. The workers said it was not to report her passport fee collection, and it was just a call to cross-check. The interpreter said that just a call to cross-check is the same as reporting her to Issara.

She said, "I would not accept your money and not renew your passport anymore. If you can wait until the employer renews for you, just wait. If the employer does not renew, it is up to the employer. If you are not hired anymore, just accept that situation and quit your job."

Now the workers feel very upset about it. The interpreter, Ma Phyu, does not seem to extend the workers' passports anymore because she knew that the workers had contacted Issara.

Some of the workers' passports will expire in February, and some of the workers' passports will expire on March 13.

The workers are worried about their passports now and have concerns about the interpreter retaliating against them for contacting Issara.
call_details.next_steps:
John - to prepare talking points to raise the issue with the supplier ASAP. 

Note: The safeguard of the workers is very crucial since the interpreter knew who called Issara and they are concerned about their safeguard now. 

In the past, the suppliers promised that the interpreters from Thai RAs would not be used anymore. Why are they still involved in the document process and trying to charge the cost from workers? Is the supplier aware of it?

call_details.description:
This is the follow-up call from a worker from King Pack regarding passport renewal.

On January 31, five HR staff and the interpreter from the production line met the workers and checked the workers' passport expiration dates.

The HR said, "I'm not sure we can renew your passport on time, but we will renew the passports for all the workers without charging the cost. Does someone collect the money from you now? If yes, come to inform the HR office directly."

However, the HR did not provide the exact date or the process for renewing the passport. The workers are still worried that the supplier will not renew their passports. 

The workers requested that Issara reach out to the supplier and ask for details of the process of renewing passports and the date to renew their passports.

The worker updated that the last meeting with the business was on January 31, and there was no other meeting or updates from HR about the passport renewal. 

Now it is half of February, and the workers are worried about how to renew their passports on time. The workers would like to know what they should do.
call_details.next_steps: Issara BHR: to reach out to the business

Workers had reported to Issara about how they were being asked by the interpreter to pay 5,000 Baht for passport renewals but it was on such short notice (asked on Jan 5, 2024 to pay the next day), they had difficulty coming up with the money. They negotiated with her to wait until the next payday on Jan 20, 2024, which she accepted at the time. On January 20, the workers went to meet the interpreter and informed her to wait for a while until the payment came into their bank account. At that time, the interpreter told the workers that she would not accept the money from the workers and would not extend their passports because she heard that some workers reported her to Issara. Some of the workers' passports will expire in February 2024, and some of the workers' passports will expire on March 13, 2024.

TPs:
- What is the current arrangement of the HR interpreters? King Pac had made the decision to hire its own interpreters and discontinue use of the FGM interpreters but it seems Ma Phyu is still involved in collecting money from workers about the passport renewal.

Recommendations:
- Investigate the matter and what role the FGM interpreter is currently playing. If this interpreter has been acting independently without the knowledge of HR, this has to be discussed with FGM management directly to stop this outside interference immediately

supplier_name: Nan Yang Garment Co., Ltd. (Nakhon Pathom)
description: Unresponsive grievance mechanism / no action being taken

call_details.description:
On April 27, 2023, a worker from Line 29 was sick and took sick leave, but he failed to inform the line supervisor because the supervisor did not pick up his call twice. On the next day, he showed his medical certificate, but it was not accepted and remarked as an absent day by the supervisor. On the payday of May 4, he found out that there was no pay for that day.

He went to the HR office and met P' Dao, who is an HR staff member, and then he was brought upstairs to a meeting room to meet some other HR staff. Finally, the line supervisor arrived at the office and confirmed that he was not entitled to receive the daily wage. He was told that he should call him until he picked up the call. Then he was scolded and told that he would be provided with a warning letter if he raised the issue like this in the future. (That's why he is worried about safeguarding.)

Note: Line 29 has no specific line supervisor. That supervisor is kind of the head or chief of line supervisors, supervising 5–6 lines in total, such as lines 25, 26, 27, 29, 30, and 31. Other workers who requested annual leave in advance also had similar experiences in the past. They were not approved to take annual leave by that supervisor. During the survey as well, some workers raised concerns about this supervisor's behavior of yelling at the workers and not listening to their voices.

Risk: The worker reached out to HR staff for his case on payday (May 4, 2023), and he was well-noticed by the chief supervisor, who threatened him. That's why he does not want to mention his name and get back his daily wage. He just wants the supplier to effectively provide warnings or train all the supervisors as a general rule.

22 May 2023

Line supervisor: P' Mway Lid

Worker: Thae Su

The workers were sewing white clothes, and there were no clear instructions from the line supervisors. When the supervisor checked the cloth, she saw the pencil marking was not covered by the seam. The supervisor started shouting and talking to the worker. The worker did not understand what the supervisor said since there was no interpreter in the production line. What she understood was that she was asking to remove the yarn from the cloth. The worker asked, "Why has there been no clear instruction since before? When we used to sew the black shirt, it happened like that a lot." The supervisor was angry with her and took the cloth and threw it on another table. She kept sewing the rest of the clothes. The supervisors kept yelling and shouting at her. The worker brought the shirt back to her table. The supervisor raised the issue at the HR office, saying that the worker did not listen to her and threw clothes at her.

The HR staff asked about the issue in detail at the office. The worker explained to them that she did not throw clothes at the line supervisor. She just brought her clothes back to her table. This case happened because of a lack of clear instructions from the line supervisors.

The HR staff told the worker, "Don't you know that the line supervisor has the rights to tell the workers if the workers are wrong? You should know that the supervisors have their rights. You are wrong in this case, so you will be provided a warning."

She asked, "What about the supervisor? The supervisor was also wrong in this case." 

All the HR staff started laughing at her. She could not say anything more. After a day, she was sent to work with quality control (QC) responsibilities. She has to stay very close to the seats of line supervisors and check the products from lines 21 and 22, where there are two QCs for each line. She has to work as a helper for quality controllers.  


June 16, 2023 

The production lines are very hot in Nan Yang, especially on the third floor. The workers, including supervisors from the 1st and 2nd floors, brought their own table fans to get cool.

The QA supervisor is the head of QCs from lines 17–24, and the worker saw that she was using a table fan. So she went to ask the QA supervisor whether she could also bring a small fan to use. When she asked like that, the QA supervisor quickly plugged out her fan, hid it, and started talking and yelling. She did not understand what the QA supervisor was saying.

The worker went to the HR office and explained the issue to the HR staff. P' Dao, the HR staff asked her to wait for a while and then, brought her to the meeting room, where there was another HR staff. HR asked the QA assistant supervisor to translate for her.

After talking about the case, she was informed that it was just the QA supervisor's behavior and asked to forget about it. She was asked whether she is currently happy with her new responsibilities as a QC. She said she was recruited as a sewer, and she would like to go back to the sewing line. She was informed that there is no other place if she does not want to work as a quality controller (QC). "You have to work anywhere we assign you, even though you were recruited for sewing," HR said. She asked about using a table fan, and she was informed that using a table fan is also not allowed.

The worker informed Issara that there are chairs for all quality controllers (QC), but when they sit, the supervisors come and hit the workers' hands and backs to get them to stand up. She said she really wants to go back to the production line as a sewer, but the supervisor from her previous line also does not like her. When she raised the issues at the office, no HR staff responded to her request to go back to sewing duties. They just follow what the supervisors say. "If HR does not solve the issues and listen to the workers, how will the workers have their rights?" said the worker.
call_details.next_steps: Escalate to discuss with management

call_details.description: On June 19, the worker was asked to move to the second floor, where she has to work as a quality controller for the cutting line. She has to check the logo on the clothes.

On June 19, the head of supervisors asked him to sew 70–80 pieces of clothing in an hour. He told her that the most he could sew was 40. The supervisor was angry with him and asked him to go work on a different line.

He feels that the supervisor targets him by asking for a higher target workload. He asked whether Issara had already reached out to the employer.
call_details.next_steps: Develop TPs/recs and reach out to management

call_details.description:
This is the follow-up call with the worker who did not get paid for sick leave on 27 April 2023. 

After MoU workers were terminated at the end of July 2023, the production lines were changed and moved. The affected worker is currently working at line No. 12 on the ground floor, where the same head of line supervisors is responsible. The worker is still insecure about providing his ID number. Since the employer is terminating workers batch by batch, he is worried if that supervisor targets and terminate him.

The head of supervisors is female, P' Pyin. She used to be responsible for lines 25, 26, 27, 29, 30, and 31 on the third floor in the past.

Now she is working on lines 11 and 12.

He said that the HR office would know if he said the production line. Many of the workers do not like her because she always asks them to move from here to there without any reason and always yells at them.

This is the follow-up call with the worker.

According to the worker, the head supervisor is currently working on lines 7 to 17. The name of the child is P'Pyin. The supplier should know that supervisor well, said the worker.

He added that so many workers at Nan Yang have issues requesting leaves. Many line supervisors do not want to provide leave properly.
call_details.referral_notes: BHR to get back to the business
call_details.next_steps: In this case, the supplier should provide clear internal training about the sick leave policy to all the supervisors.

call_details.description:
The affected worker had a meeting with the manager from the HR office, and he was well explained about the situation, and the sick leave matter would also be responsible, said the manager.

The affected worker and several workers confirmed that the behaviours of line supervisor P' Pin are improving. She does not yell at the workers these days. 
The worker thanked Issara and employer for taking care of confidentiality and safeguarding. 

The case can be closed.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case. The workers confirmed that the HR manager had met with them to explain the sick leave policy and how it is to be practiced.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker said he didn't receive his wage for one sick leave day because he failed to inform his supervisor. He tried to call both the supervisor and assistant supervisor to inform them but they did not pick up his calls. Even though he went to HR and explained his situation and presented the medical certificate for the sick day, HR still did not agree to pay him for that day. Instead, he was scolded by the supervisor (who was also at his meeting with HR) that he would be given a warning letter if he raised the issue like this in the future.

NOTE: The worker doesn't want to be identified. He just wants the supplier to effectively provide warnings or train all the supervisors.

TPs:
- Make sure the business provides safeguards to workers for having reported any issues
- When a worker has an issue or grievance, what channels are there for that worker to report it to the business (HR, grievance box, etc.)?

Recommendations:
- When there is a worker grievance, there should be clear protocols for response and timeline within which the business takes action
remediation_business_steps_taken: After the remediation call on 20 July 2023, Nan Yang NKPT called for a meeting with the line supervisors in the same month and discussed with them about sick leave and medical certificate. Line supervisors cannot ask the worker for a medical certificate for a one-day sick leave, but 3 days can. BHR called Nan Yang NKPT today and gave them the info of that line supervisor (P Pyin, line no. 12). The business is happy to investigate again in more detail, and will get back to Issara at the end of next week.
remediation_notes: Issara received a report that workers didn't receive wages for sick leave even when they had medical certificates. When workers went to HR to report this, still no action was taken.
remediation_action:
After discussing this issue with Issara, HR called a meeting with the line supervisors and discussed with them about sick leave and medical certificate, that line supervisors cannot ask a worker for a medical certificate for 1-2 days of sick leave. In a follow-up meeting, Issara provided the business with information on the production line number where this issue occurred. The business will investigate, and will get back to Issara.

In the latest update, the business trained line supervisors on the company's policy and procedures for annual and sick leave.

In the country escalation meeting, the business noted that the training included how grievances should be handled, that workers should be safeguarded and there should be no retaliation against those reporting such grievances.  The business will also make an announcement to all workers about the grievance and non-retaliation policy to help workers feel safer to report grievances to the business.
remediation_validation:
The worker updated Issara that after many MoU workers were let go at the end of July 2023, the production lines were changed and moved. The affected worker is currently working in a line where the same head of line supervisors is responsible. The worker is still insecure about providing his ID number but provided the production line number which could trigger the business investigation.

The HR manager met with the workers to explain the sick leave policy and the workers clearly understand how sick leave will be processed.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case. The workers confirmed that the HR manager had met with them to explain the sick leave policy and how it is to be practiced.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Train HR staff and line supervisors on how to appropriately respond to worker grievances, as per the business' grievance mechanism policy

description: Threats aiming to discourage lodging grievances

call_details.description: This call is from Ko Pai Thu, Pilot Knit and in this call, Ko Pai Thu reported that the business had called a meeting to blame the workers for reporting the case to Issara and the business has been doing the investigating to find out the workers who reported Issara the abusive line-supervisors case.
This call is from Ko Nay, Pilot Knit to give us the case update of Level-2 abusive line-supervisor case.

Ko Thu reported that Phee Wah and Phee Lit not keep identifying for the workers who reported the case to Issara anymore and they managed the line as if nothing had happened. In terms of the behavior Phee Lit is not complaining and shouting as before and none of the supervisors used the words like " you can go back to your country anytime".

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case, as the worker has confirmed they are not being asked about who reported to Issara any longer.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
After workers reported the issue of poor line supervisor behavior, a worker reported that the business had called a meeting to line E-Zone Line-4 workers on 30th May 2023 to blame the workers for having reported the case to Issara and the business has been investigating to find out which workers had made the report. The business threatened the workers that they might close or reform the line.

Recommendations:
- Investigate what meeting took place on May 30th and why workers were made to feel as though they were wrong to report the poor supervisor behavior issue to Issara with a threat of punishment
- Communicate clearly to all workers, verbally and in writing, that the company has a grievance mechanism policy that promotes worker's right to use any grievance channel they choose, including Issara's independent channel, and that they can do so without fear of retaliation.
remediation_notes: After workers reported the issue of poor line supervisor behavior, a worker reported that the business had called a meeting with workers from certain production lines on 30th May 2023 to blame the workers for having reported the case to Issara.
remediation_action: HR said the business organized a meeting with workers and trained the line supervisors regarding various company policies such as the non-discrimination policy, non-retaliation policy, and grievance mechanism policy.
remediation_validation: A worker updated Issara saying the business doesn't keep asking who reported the issue to Issara anymore, and the line supervisor behavior has improved.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case, as the worker has confirmed they are not being asked about who reported to Issara any longer.
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
- Review the grievance mechanism policy, and the procedures for responding to worker reports
- Train the responsible persons so they have the capacity to respond appropriately to worker reports and ensure there is no suppression of worker voice

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue. The workers have confirmed that the supervisors' practice has changed and they are now able to take toilet breaks when needed.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
She said that there are 13 workers working in Pine Apple Line C, and they usually start work at 7:30 and finish work at 4:30 in the evening. For the last two months, the line-supervisor has not allowed the workers to take a toilet break after 11:00 am and after 4:00 pm, saying in half an hour it will be the lunch break or the end of the work shift. Furthermore she allows the workers to go to the toilet one by one. 

TPs:
- What is the company policy regarding toilet breaks? Can workers go when and as needed?
- Is there a practice that only one worker from a line can go to the toilet at a time? Is that because a certain number of workers are needed for the line to operate normally? If so, how has this been communicated to the workers?

Recommendations:
- Workers should be able to use the toilet when needed, without having to wait for the lunch break or the end of the shift
- Communicate this clearly to all workers; train line supervisors so that they implement this properly and not limit toilet access at certain times
- Communicate clearly to workers production line requirements, such as a certain number of workers needed to be in a given line and how the company makes appropriate adjustments when workers take toilet breaks
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 20 Nov 2023

According to company policy, workers can use toilets at any time, according to K. Sophon and K Sopreeya, HR. The supervisor has to ensure that the production line runs smoothly so that workers can go to the toilet as needed, but not all workers in the line can go at the same time. They will, however, investigate this production line and communicate clearly to the supervisor and workers that the workers can use toilets as needed. They will get back to us by next week with the corrective action.

DATE: 27 Nov 2023

K. Sophon, HR Director shared the corrective action that last week, The HR team trained the supervisor/line leader to explain and emphasize that there is no set time for workers to use toilets. So every worker has access to the toilet at any time.
remediation_notes: Workers reported for the last two months, the line supervisor has not allowed the workers to take toilet breaks after 11:00 am and after 4:00 pm, saying in half an hour it will be the lunch break or the end of the work shift (they start work at 7:30am and finish work at 4:30pm).
remediation_action: HR investigated and trained the supervisors, emphasizing that there is no set time for workers to use toilets and they should be allowed to access the toilet when needed.
remediation_validation: Workers confirmed that they are now able to take toilet breaks when needed.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue. The workers have confirmed that the supervisors' practice has changed and they are now able to take toilet breaks when needed.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Have a system in place so that workers can take toilet breaks when needed but this doesn't affect the production in any given line

A client reported that she is an MOU worker who came with Golden Royal Mandalay in 30 Jan 2023. When Cal-Comp dismissed the workers in Samut Sakhon site, his brother was also in the group. So, she talked with the Thai recruitment agency no.45 staff "Mr. Wai Yan Soe" if she can also get the cancellation letter to find another job like her brother since she doesn't want to keep working there alone. "Mr. Wai Yan Soe" told her that she can. So she resigned and her last working day was Apr 3, 2023. After that, she contacted Wai Yan Soe many times and he told her that he will get the cancellation letter for her. She hasn't received the cancellation letter but she cannot contact Wai Yan Soe anymore. She is wondering if we can help her to get the cancellation letter. She said she still needs to get paid 10 days of wages from Cal-Comp. 

O&E called and checked what is the reason why she hasn't received the latest wage for 10 days. She said, this 10 days wage was kept as a deposit while the workers start working. The worker also adds that it is a tradition that Cal-Comp used to do this practice. So the workers should the employer knows in advance before they leave so that they can get back the wage for these 10 days.

However, she said that she doesn't have the pay slip anymore. She just wants the cancellation and it's ok even she didn't get back the wage for 10 days.

His name is Pan Sandar.
ID: C-375620
Starting Date:30 Jan 2023
Last working day: 3 Apr 2023
Thai Recruitment agency no.45

TPs:
- Is it company practice that 10 days of wages are held from workers as a deposit? Is this something the business is doing or the Thai RA?
- What is the deposit for? And how is it returned to workers when they leave?
- The only deduction the employer is able to make is as compensation to the Employer for damage caused by the Employee either wilfully or with gross negligence, with the prior consent of the Employee, and it should not exceed 10% of the payment.

Recommendations:
- The business should not withhold any wages from workers, and should return this money to the worker that has resigned immediately
- The business to communicate clearly and transparently to all workers, verbally and in writing, its policy that it doesn't withhold any wages from workers except for a few restricted instances and what deductions are to be made from their pay (such as social security contributions)
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Anchan, HR sent us an email to clarify as follows. 
Normally, our company will release salary twice as follows

~ 1st time, the release due date will be set for every 1st by calculating the working day during 5th – 19th

~ 2nd time, the release due date will be set for every 16th by calculating the working day during 20th – 4th

For this case;

Employee had worked on January 30th to February 4th. Therefore, the employee will receive the salary on February 16th.


K. Anchan, HR CC (SMSK) shared with us the worker's payroll record, that the work was paid on March 20th-3rd, 2023. 

https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-jsaq2k_XWWoqZKzvPR7dvcsEdEUZmiG/edit#gid=1754267130
remediation_notes: An MOU worker that resigned and is waiting for the cancellation letter from the business also noted that she didn't receive wages for 10 days, which is something the business has withheld as a deposit when a worker starts working.
remediation_action:
The business responded saying that salaries are paid as follows: the first payment is made on the 1st of every month for the worker's time worked during the 5-19th of the previous month and the second payment is paid on the 16th of every month for the time worked during the 20th-4th. The business stated that this worker worked from January 30 to Feb 4, 2023 and should have received the salary on Feb 16, 2023. 

After the worker noted that she resigned on 3 Apr 2023, the business checked and confirmed in the payroll records that this worker had been paid fully up to 3 Apr 2023
remediation_validation:
Issara followed up with the worker and she said she did not resign on 4 Feb 2023, as claimed by the business. She didn't receive payment for the working days between 20th Mar to 3rd Apr 2023 since she resigned on 3 Apr 2023 and the 2nd payroll for that period  was paid on 16 Apr 2023.

In the latest update, the worker called back and updated that she found out that the salary had been transferred on 16 Apr 2023 when she went and checked with the bank.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case. The worker confirmed getting the full wages she is entitled to.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case.  The business took actions to plan for a safe U-turn process before taking the alternative to renew worker documents in Thailand based on the new government policy.  Workers confirmed that they are very happy about this.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that there was a sudden announcement from the business saying more than 200 workers completing their 4-year MOU contracts would need to return to Myanmar to complete the U-Turn process. The business explained this to the workers in batches and told them they needed to wait in Myanmar until the demand was approved by the government. The business would not be responsible for the expenses that workers would incur during this unspecified waiting period. Additionally, the workers would have to pay for the costs of the U-turn process themselves.

The workers are concerned about the following:
1. Some workers (currently 7) cannot go back home during the waiting period because their villages are in the conflict zone and are worried about their safety.
2. Workers don't know why they have to pay for U-turn process costs, how long this process will take, or which recruitment agency will facilitate the process.
3. The business said workers would need to decide and inform the business on the very day this was announced. If a worker chooses not to do the U-turn process, the business will let them go without providing any severance pay. 

Talking points:
- Does the business know some workers are from conflict zones and they could be at risk of bodily harm if they had to go there during the waiting period?

Recommendations:
- The business should cover the costs of the U-turn process as a responsible and ethical recruiter, aligning with customer EPP expectations
- The business should make arrangements with the Myanmar recruitment agency to ensure that workers can be safe during the waiting period and don't need to return to their home villages during this time
- The business should communicate clearly the steps of the U-turn process, the timeline from start to finish, and the recruitment agency that will facilitate the process.
- If workers still choose not to do the U-turn process, provide them with severance pay as per the number of years of service
remediation_business_steps_taken:
According to K. Narisra, HR manager, the company is aware that some workers are afraid to return to Myanmar. Currently, CPH has submitted the demand and given the name list to SHWE HPAAN SERVICE RA in order to obtain approval from MOLIP, and the RA has said that the workers do not need to return to their home village but will instead stay and wait in Myalawadee. The RA will specify how long workers must wait and provide accommodations. 

She added that there are 2 options.
1. Mou U-Turn - CHP covers all the recruitment fee
2. As a result of the government announcement, HR is now considering registering MoU workers who have completed four years in Thailand. HR will, however, discuss this with top management next week. They will then communicate clearly with workers.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that there was a sudden announcement from the business saying more than 200 workers completing their 4-year MOU contracts would need to return to Myanmar to complete the U-Turn process. The business explained this to the workers in batches and told them they needed to wait in Myanmar until the demand was approved by the government. The business would not be responsible for the expenses that workers would incur during this unspecified waiting period. Additionally, the workers would have to pay for the costs of the U-turn process themselves.
remediation_action: Issara reached out to the business, and the HR manager noted that the company is aware that some workers are afraid to return to Myanmar. Currently, the business has submitted the demand list to the Thai government and given the name list to SHWE HPAAN SERVICE (the Myanmar Recruitment Agency) in order to obtain approval from the Myanmar government. The Myanmar recruitment agency will make arrangements so that workers do not need to return to their home village but will instead stay and wait in Myawaddy, where accommodations will be provided for them and the RA will provide more information on how long workers must wait. For this MOU U-turn process, the business will cover all fees.  Alternatively, given the very recent Thai government announcement that there will be another round of registrations for undocumented workers in Thailand, the business has decided to register the workers here in Thailand.
remediation_validation: The worker updated that the business has announced that they will apply for the pink card for all workers and the workers do not need to go back Myanmar and do U-Turn anymore. All the workers are so happy about this.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case.  The business took actions to plan for a safe U-turn process before taking the alternative to renew worker documents in Thailand based on the new government policy.  Workers confirmed that they are very happy about this.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: The business should have an annual schedule for visa, WP, and contract extensions so that workers have their documents extended in a timely manner; ensure that workers are informed well in advance of the extensions and how the process will be handled so that they are not left wondering and stressed about what will happen to them; ensure the business covers the costs of the U-turn process as per EPP and customer requirements.

call_details.description:
The worker raised a problem with the lack of safety equipment. Three years ago, the business used to provide safety sneakers to the workers to protect their toes from heavy metal falling on them. But since then, the business has never provided it again, and some workers need to buy it themselves. And there used to be an accident with a worker; the metal bar fell off and hit the worker's leg; the worker's leg got broken. The worker requests that the business provide the safety equipment to the workers as before, as they used to provide it annually to the workers.

And the worker also raised the same issue that used to be discussed with the business before about unfair treatment in providing a bonus to migrant workers. The Cambodian worker received a very small bonus of 2000 baht per year if they had a good record of working without taking any leave, but the Thai worker received much more; they received the full amount of their monthly wage as a bonus. This practice has been going on for five years.
call_details.next_steps: BHR will reach out to the business.

call_details.description:
O&E explained to the worker these responses from the business:
1. Discrimination about equal annual bonus pay between foreign employees and Thai employees Now the HR team was raising the case with our top management about the process and evaluation system for proper annual bonus pay for foreign employees.

Validation with the worker: The worker thanks for raising this with the business. 

2. Discrimination about protection equipment between foreign employees and Thai employees Everest equally provides PPE (personal protective equipment) for both foreign and Thai employees. A foreman in every department always checks with workers about PPE needs and provides replacements when needed

Validation with the worker: Actually, the PPE is provided equally. But what he had raised before, he expected to have more, as the business used to provide. However,that is ok, even with current materials that are enough.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue. The workers have confirmed that they understand the new policy and the PPE items that will be provided to them when and as needed.

call_details.description:

Again, HR said they would be provided on July 19th. Since the HR department kept postponing and did not pay the workers, the workers requested Issara to help them get paid.

Workers' names: Ye Min Tun, Khaing Loon Zaw, Chan Aye

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case. The business has provided pay slip evidence that the workers were paid during those pay periods, and Issara has not been able to contact the workers since then to verify this payment.

call_details.description:

The worker shared that, regarding the missing OT payment, work was added whenever he swiped the card for clock-in and clock-out; he always ensured that his ID number appeared on the screen, but when he received the payment, it was a missing OT payment as compared with the hours they had worked.Some workers used to follow up with the line supervisor, but there was no result.Additionally, the worker mentioned the abusive behaviors; they are from P-Leang/team leader (line supervisor assistant).They shout at the workers in order to ask them to do something.The way they communicate and talk with the Cambodian workers is not respectful.
Beyond the two issues raised above, the worker shared two new issues: one is about the high recruitment fee for MOU workers. The workers need to pay around 485 USD to the recruitment agency for MOU work with CP-RAM, and when they arrived in the destination country, they mentioned that they were supposed to get 2000 baht reimbursement from the business, but the Agency also collected it. Another issue is that there is no interpreter at the HR office; it is very difficult to raise issues or find support from HR.If there are interpreters, it is helpful for the workers to seek support and assistance whenever they face difficulties.
call_details.next_steps: Discuss the case with CP-RAM

call_details.description:
Get back to the worker to update them on the discussion with the business and their responses. 
Please see BR 2444.
Will validate with the worker again when the business shares the investigation findings with Issara.

After sharing with the worker the business responses and validating them with the worker:
1. The issue with missing OT payments:the business told workers if they were missing OT payments, they could go and check with OT logger staff. The workers can get back their missing payment after checking with the OT logger. But the point is that the missing payment always happened, even after the business investigated and found no system and/or machine error. On this recent payday, some workers are still missing payment, and even though they can check with the OT logger and get back the payment, some workers decide not to do so. The workers want a clear and accurate system for recording timesheets and payments.

2. The behavior of skilled staff (Pi-leang) is much better and improved.

3. Lack of interpreter: the worker acknowledged that there is a Khmer-Surin (Thai) who can speak Khmer at the HR office.But he didn't see any posters about the interpreter service yet; he will check at the canteen or entrance if there are any, which he will capture and share with Issara. However, the business should hire a native interpreter that could communicate smoothly with the workers and support them whenever they need help, such as going to the hospital, because right now workers need to go by themselves if they get sick without the support of the interpreter.

4. High cost of MOU: The worker acknowledged what the business has mentioned, but now RA has even increased it from 485 USD to 530 USD. The workers understand that this is the policy of the business: they need to be responsible for the recruitment fee in the source country, but it is burdensome to them; they don't earn much, but they need to pay a lot for the recruitment fee. The workers hope that the business and the buyer could consider supporting the workers with the recruitment fee.

Update the business response to the worker: 
K. Chanchai from the technical support team explains that CP Ram is aware of the human error that caused the OT approval to be delayed by the supervisor. They are looking into the problem. However, if some workers do not receive their OT payment during the payment period, they will receive it automatically in the next payment. HR informed all employees about the situation on September 6, 2023.

The worker said there is a verbal announcement at the production line explaining to the workers about the OT record that if there is OT work, the workers don't get out of the line and someone will note them down and make sure their OT work will be recorded properly, and if there is no OT work, workers just normally swap the card and leave. The worker understood but requested to wait and see on Payday 25 first whether the action from the business is effective or not.

K. Supranee, Human Resources She confirmed that CP Ram hires interpreters on the production lines. Workers who do not work the night shift can also contact their supervisor/manager and request that an interpreter be placed in the production line to assist the workers with interpreting the hospital. By September 11, 2023, they will also have a written announcement for the interpreter to help on the night shift to communicate with the workers. They will share the corrective action.

He will check if there are some announcements and take the picture share with Issara.

The worker shared that he saw the announcement of the interpreter from the HR office already, but he didn't see further announcements from the business about the availability of the interpreter 24/7 to support the workers at any time. O&E explained to the worker from the business response that the worker can contact the interpreter at any time.

However, related to missing OT payments, the worker shared that still many workers are missing their payments. O&E explained again about the business response related to OT payments; the business said some OT payments could be late because the line supervisor submitted workers's time sheets late, but those payments will be included in the next payroll, so O&E suggests to the worker to check and get the payslips from the workers who shared that missing payment by providing the previous payslip and the current payslip, whether the missing payment is included in the next payroll or not. The worker will try to check with those who are missing their payment and get back to Issara.

The worker said he received the full payment during the payday on September 25th,and from what he had mentioned, other workers were still missing their payment. When he asked the payslips to compare between the previous payment and the next payment that they received, they didn't provide it to him, so as the business said, some workers will receive a late OT payment because their line supervisor shared the OT timesheet late, but the payment will be included in the next payment. As there is no clear information or evidence that shows that the issue is still happening, the worker confirmed that Issara can close this case as he already received the full payment.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue. The workers understand that there may be missing OT wages in one pay period if there are delays on processing the OT work approvals and one worker confirmed that he has received missing pay in the most recent pay period.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker raised concerns about the difficulties working at CP-Ram. Cambodian workers were treated poorly by their line supervisors related to how they talk and manage the Cambodian workers. The worker reported that there is a miscount of the OT hours by their line supervisor as they don't record it on the timesheet, and the worker dare not talk to or raise concerns with the line supervisor or HR. The worker requested whether Issara could engage with the business and communicate with the workers at CP-Ram as well as support workers in remediation.

TPs:
- How does the company recorded the minutes/hours worked by workers?  How are OT hours recorded?  Is this a manual system, fingerprint or employee card scan system, etc?

Recommendations:
- Investigate what may have led to concerns from workers that their actual OT hours worked are not being properly recorded into the company's HR system
- If there has been an under-reporting and under-paying of OT hours to workers, this should be paid back immediately
- Communicate to workers how the company records hours worked so that workers understand that it is a fair and reliable system and they will not be at risk of being underpaid
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K.Nutasit presented that they investigated and verified that all workers received their OT hours correctly in the OT system. Issara provided more information about the case in which the OT calculated with the ID machine card did not work properly. K.Nutasit stated that if workers clocked out incorrectly and did not receive the OT wage. They can check with CCTV to reimburse for the worker. However, they will investigate and double-check with the machine, as well as announce the worker who is affected by the OT wage, so that the worker can go directly to HR and receive the OT wage.


Root cause:
The company conducted a sampling of the timesheets of 2,500 employees to check their time records, OT in July 2023 whether OT
payments were correct at various work points of CPRAM, as a result, no problem was found. Moreover, from the verification of the
time record machine system in June - July 2023, no abnormalities were found. It will be a check from the Time in-out information
of employees at various card swipe points in the HR system.

Preventive Action:
1. The Human Resources Department will collect a record of complaints related to human rights issues (via Complaint box,
internal hotline, and VOS (Voice of Stakeholders)) and reports to the top management of CPRAM every 2 weeks.
(Date to be started and completed: 29.08.2023)
2. Add more communication channels to complain about various problems by adding Line OA of the Labor Relations
Department (Date to be started and completed: 01.09.2023).
3. Promote the company's existing communication channels, such as complaint boxes, internal hotlines, and VOS. Engage
employees at all levels by adding additional communication signs where most employees visit
(Date to be completed: 21.08.2023).

However, if some workers do not receive their OT payment during the payment period, they will receive it automatically in the next payment. HR informed all employees about the situation on September 6, 2023.


DATE 12 Sep 2023
K. Korakot, Technical Manager shared the corrective action. Please see more details in the link as follows;
https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1JYsOgtg02BUlyF_Rn4uZ8z5-CWv0kspc


Root Cause:
Following our investigated, it is found that it may be due to a overdue payment in employee salaries cycle causing the company
to not be able to pay in time for the actual pay period but the company (HR) collects the number of employees who are overdue
payment each month in the HR database to make payments in the next round instead. There may be some groups of employees
who are not yet aware of this. Even though the factory regularly has morning talks on this matter.


Preventive Action:
Short Term: CPRAM will conduct a morning talk in 3 languages: Thai, Cambodian, and Burmese for all employees and all
nations to understand and acknowledge in the matter of receiving a refund payment in the next payment period. If there is a
problem of overdue payment. (Date to be completed: 11.09.2023)
Long Term: The Human Resources Department will separate the detailed information on overtime pay in the employee's
payment form, if there is overtime payment added from overdue payment in the previous actual payment cycle in order to
notify the employees that the overdue payment has been paid in the next payment period. (Date to be completed: within 2024)

remediation_action:
HR stated that if workers clocked out incorrectly and did not receive their OT wage, they can check with CCTV to reimburse for the worker. The business announced during the morning talk in 3 languages on September 6, 2023, that affected workers can go directly to HR to check, and also explained that there were some late payments due to late approval of OT work by the line supervisors, which would be included automatically in the next pay period. HR has identified the number of employees who are owed overdue payment.

In the future, HR will provide any overdue payment that is paid in the next pay period as a separate line item in the pay slip in order to notify the employees that the overdue payment has been paid in the next payment period.
remediation_validation:
Workers noted that the business announced to workers that if they were missing OT payments, they could go and check with HR staff logging work hours of staff and can get back their missing payment. But the workers want to point out that this is happening often, even after the recent business investigation. On the recent payday, some workers found they didn't get paid fully for their work.

A worker confirmed he received the full payment during the payday on September 25th, 2023. For others, missing pay from the previous pay period will be paid in the next pay period.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue. The workers understand that there may be missing OT wages in one pay period if there are delays on processing the OT work approvals and one worker confirmed that he has received missing pay in the most recent pay period.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client worked at a Korean BBQ restaurant located in KL Kepong Jalan Metro Perdana, which is one of fifteen branches of the restaurant chain. Out of the fifteen branches, this particular one was problematic. The restaurant has six Nepali and thirteen Burmese workers. The owner's son is abusive towards the Nepali workers, creating a hostile work environment. Issara is able to speak with two workers. They have been working for this employer for 10 months. They are all MoU workers. They are reporting as a group of 5 Nepali workers, but the client is quietly reporting. The client and the workers want to either be transferred to another branch under the same company or find employment in another company. The client has debts to pay and doesn't want to return to Nepal. The workers have a contract they made in Nepal, but the company made another contract which the client doesn't have and is unaware of its contents.
Following are the major issues reported by workers.

1) Document retention: Workers passports are held by the employer since they started their employment. The company also kept their passports and didn't provide them with worker ID cards (Jalan cards) or necessary documents. 

2) Restriction of Movement: The workers were not allowed to leave the premises, and this restriction also made it difficult for their friends to visit them.

3) Unfair suspension: Workers were frequently suspended for minor mistakes or even without any reason. During these suspensions, the company did not provide any food, and the workers were not allowed to go out and get their own. They were also denied access to basic amenities, like cooling fans, during these periods. One incident occurred when a friend of the client was suspended for simply asking a Burmese worker to clean a stain. The owner verbally abused him and kept him in detention (suspension) for 28 days. Throughout this time, the company did not provide any food or salary, leaving the workers in a dire situation. His friends attempted to provide food secretly, but they had to be cautious as the company would punish them if they were caught bringing in more substantial amounts of food or any food. 

Recently, the victim was suspended by the company for two months. During this period, he received no salary or food from the company. The suspension was a result of the employer demanding the victim to memorize the restaurant menu quickly.

If workers demand to change the employer, they are asked to work 4 months without pay and there are some workers who have accepted this situation as they could not bear the harsh working environment. 

4)Physical abuse: Physical assault includes being kicked, slapped on the face and belly, and having ears pulled. The employer even physically assaulted the client's genitals. Such harassment occurred almost daily and targeted everyone except.

5) Long working hours and incorrect payment: Workers have to work 14-15 hours a day. In return, they received a basic salary of 1500 RM and a 300 RM overtime allowance each month. 

6) Lack of Sick Leave: Even when the workers fell ill, they were forced to work, as the owner wouldn't allow them to stay in the hostel. 



Moreover, during salary payment time, the owner would abuse the workers and suspend them for minor mistakes. The owner often used the workers as a target for his frustrations, taking out his stress related to the business on them. Whenever the business is slow he will start abusing the worker for no reason.

description: Timesheets/payslips/other basic pay-related documents not provided to worker

call_details.description: The worker reported that he works from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. (sometimes until 7:15 p.m.) for the day shift; the line supervisor asked workers to scan the card at 6:30 p.m. but asked them to go back to work until they finished the target at 7 p.m. or 7:15 p.m. So, it seems like the worker has been working for OT for around 3–3:15 hours, but the worker received only 2:30 hours of OT. The worker also used to check with the line supervisor, but there was no result. Due to many workers complaining about the missing OT payment, the business has stopped providing the pay slip to the workers anymore. Additionally, the worker said that during long public holidays such as Songkran workers were asked to work, but he didn't come to work because it was a public holiday that had been announced in the factory. But when he came back to work, the line supervisor gave him a warning letter.
call_details.next_steps: Start engaging with the business

call_details.description:
The issue with payslips not being provided

Business response: The business responded that the paper pay slips have been prepared for all the workers, and it has regularly been communicated to the workers that they can collect them at the HR Office at their convenience. Also, the Smartphone app “E-Pay Slip” has been launched and is operational, so that all workers, both local and migrants, can check the accuracy and correctness of each and every wage payment.

Worker validation: The worker didn't know that about getting the payslip at the HR office or the smart phone app, and even some workers used to ask for payslips, but HR didn't provide them. However, after raising this with Issara, the worker saw the corrective action from the business, and now the payslips are provided directly to the workers at this latest payday. The worker confirmed to close the case, and if this happens again in the future, he will visit the HR office to get the payslip, as the business mentioned.

The issue with OT

Business response: The business conducted an investigation of the entire operation and found that it was related to the employee’s weekly working hours exceeding 72 hours. The Supervisor had workers clean the production lines; an extra half-hour extended beyond the actual clock-out time. The incident involved four Cambodian workers, and this happened three times, which is in violation of the Company’s Rules and Regulations.  Therefore, a written warning was issued to the Supervisor in question, and it was communicated to all parties concerned that resorting to such a practice was decidedly prohibited. The business will reimburse the missing wage payment to the four workers as of the payment round of August 25, 2023.

Worker validation: The worker acknowledged the business investigation and confirmed that it does not happen anymore.

The issue with line supervisor behavior

Business response: The business conducted an investigation that showed that any written warnings issued during the period following the Songkran Holidays, i.e., between the 15th and 17th of April 2023, did not involve any cases of absence from work during the Songkran public holidays on the 13th and 14th of April 2023.
The written warnings issued were, in fact, relevant to such cases of absence on the workdays following the Songkran, either on the 15th or the 16th of April 2023.

Worker validation: The worker said this should be the unclear communication from the line supervisor to the worker because during those Songkran holidays, the worker consented to work on April 13–14, and the line supervisor announced that the holidays are from April 13–15, and that's why the worker didn't come to work on April 15th. Next time, the business or line supervisor should have communication with the workers, and the worker himself will check properly to avoid such an incident. The worker will wait and see about the next holiday. Issara can close this case at the moment, as he understands from what the business shared.
call_details.next_steps: To close the cases

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case.  The worker confirmed that workers are now receiving their pay slips.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client is reporting about the abusive line supervisor in her working line. The line supervisor's name is Siriwat, and the workers call her “Wa-Na-Yai”. She is managing line no.1,2,3,4, wearing “Yellow Cap” in Fish Peeling Line in Building-1. The workers have to arrive at work by 6:30 AM and sometimes they have to work until 4:30 PM without getting OT payment although the working hour is between “7:00AM-4:00 PM”. If the workers have not arrived at the working line by 6:30 to 6:40 PM, she shouts at the workers and she treats them poorly. Sometimes, she also asks the workers to stay until 4:20PM or 4:30PM when they are not finished with their workload. The workers do not get the OT payment for the extra 20-30 min working hours. The line supervisor is punishing the workers to take leave without pay when she finds out that there is some fish bone and blood in the fish flesh/meant they have peeled. Before this kind inspection of fish bone and blood were allowed until 4-5 trays per day. But now, when the bone and blood are found in the fish meat by 2 trays, the line supervisor gives a punishment to those workers not to do OT and not to come to work by having them taking leave without pay. Sometimes, the workers thought that the supervisor would deliberately get some fish blood and bone and she just put this to the fish meat/flesh so that QC found this when they were checking. Because the workers said they tried their best not to include the fish blood and meat in the fish they have peeled. So the workers said, it would be good if the business can have an investigation about this.

TPs:
- Does the company have a practice where workers are required to report to work earlier than their work shift hours?  If so, how is the clock-in / clock-out system recording the hours worked and are they paid for all the time on the job?

Recommendations:
- Investigate this matter where workers are saying they are not being fully paid for the time they are working and if they peel fish in a way that doesn't meet the company standards they are penalized for it by being asked to leave and not being paid for it
- Ensure safeguards for workers and that supervisors understand the company's non-retaliation policy
- According to the investigation results, discipline the supervisors that did not follow company policy in regards to paying workers fully and not penalizing them for mistakes that may be made accidentally by workers
- Communicate with all workers that they will be paid fairly for all the hours they work and clarify how their hours worked are logged properly so that they are paid fully. Also, clarify that no workers would be penalized unreasonably for mistakes that may be made by workers on the job.
remediation_notes: A worker reported that a line supervisor managing several lines would force workers to arrive at work by 6:30AM and sometimes they have to work until 4:30 PM without getting OT payment for the additional time worked (the working shift is between 7AM-4PM). The line supervisor is also punishing the workers to take leave without pay when she finds out that there is some fish bone and blood in the fish meat they have peeled. Sometimes, the workers suspect that the supervisor would deliberately put some fish blood and bone into the fish meat to get them in trouble because the workers tried their best to prepare the fish meat according to the required standards.
remediation_action: HR will investigate this matter with the safeguards for workers and get back to Issara within 7 working days.
remediation_validation: Workers updated Issara that they do not have to arrive early and leave later than their shift anymore.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case. Even though we have not heard back from the business about its corrective actions, the workers have already confirmed the improvement and they don't have arrive early or leave later than their shifts.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: Ensure supervisors are trained to properly implement company policies related to logging the time worked by workers and paying them fully for those hours

description: Issues with breaks including lunch/bathroom/OT breaks: violation of law or employment contract

call_details.description:
The worker followed up on the issue related to OT and missed payments, as it is still happening.
Additionally,the workers raised another issue about sick leave. It is very difficult to request sick leave. Even the factory creates a line group channel to communicate between workers and line supervisors, and workers can request leave online. But when the worker got sick, he requested a leave via line group, but the line supervisor asked the worker to come and bring a medical certificate to request sick leave directly at the factory; otherwise, the line supervisor would not approve the request for sick leave, even for a day's sick leave.
One more thing: whenever workers went to the toilet, their name was noted down, and they were permitted to go no longer than 15 minutes.The toilets are a bit far away, and sometimes the workers return a bit late; their name was reported, and as a consequence, the worker was not allowed to work OT or double-pay on Day-off.

O&E checked with the worker about the status of the issues and explained to the worker about Issara's ability to engage with the business to resolve the cases. As we discussed with the buyer, the business (CPF) does not allow Issara to work with them, so our ability to get engaged with the business directly in terms of resolving the problem is not possible. However, O&E shared that there is an NGO that has engaged with the business (LPN). If the worker is okay, we will try to reach out to LPN to support the worker. 

The worker confirmed that the remaining issues are quite better if Issara has difficulties reaching out to the business; the issues could be closed. However, it is great to know that there is an NGO that is available at the factory, and the worker could reach out. The worker asked to share the contact information of LPN (Facebook Page) with him, and he will reach out to them if there are any issues. 

O&E shared the Facebook page of LPN with the worker via Messenger and let the worker know that we would try to reach out to LPN, and if we got another contact number that worker could contact easier, Issara would share it with the worker.

- The business to make sure the workers have valid visas to travel back. Workers should not be sent back with a temporary pass as they could be blacklisted by the immigration from entering back to Malaysia. 
- The business should compensate workers for not informing one month in advance about their dismissal. 
- The business to make it clear to all workers about their status departing process.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Business: The reason for dismissal is because of the low order from the clients and the business is shrinking. Therefore, the company decided not to have many foreign workers. Business promised to have a proper valid visa for them to legally return back and also communicate with all workers about their status at the moment. The business added that they have informed workers one month in advance which is why the workers are not entitled to compensation. 


Workers confirmed receiving valid visas and back to their home country. 
This case is considered to be closed.

description: Lack of access to safe and credible grievance mechanism

call_details.description:
For a visa, WP extension, or any document process, the employer asked for over 4000 THB, saying that the worker had to pay for half and the employer pays half.
After providing a social security card, the employer collected 300 THB, saying it was for the police fees.
If a worker resigns from a job, the employer asks to pay over 6,000 to 8,000 THB, saying the worker has to return all the costs. If the worker does not pay for it, that worker cannot apply for any other job. Other employers cannot change the employer for that worker. The workers do not understand how the employer remarks on the cancellation letter. In that way, workers cannot change jobs or resign from their current jobs freely.
In the last canteen outreach, the workers were informed to go back into the production line right after finishing lunch, and they were asked not to stay outside of the production lines. And the manager, line supervisors, and interpreters are watching who were talking with Issara's staff. So, no one dared share any information during the visit.
The worker said that it would be difficult for workers to inform each other about the survey because some workers might whisper about who has a connection with Issara to the supervisors and interpreter.

The worker said that after talking with Issara staff during the canteen outreach, the manager from the production asked the workers what Issara staff talked to them, what Issara staff are communicating with them using phones, etc. 

The worker said that she does not feel safe.

The worker updated that the business posted a black-and-white A4 paper that included Issara WV channels, which is the last page of the business announcement for the ER-WSS survey. And the business displayed a written announcement that said workers could answer and communicate with Issara freely. 

However, there is no Issara Hotline poster. So, more posters would be sent out to NR Instant, and BHR would ask the supplier to display them so that the workers could see them.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue. The workers have received the business announcement with Issara's worker voice channels, along with a message that workers can freely communicate with Issara without fearing retaliation. However, the business response was very delayed.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
During the most recent canteen outreach, the workers were informed to go back into the production line right after finishing lunch, and they were asked not to stay outside. The manager, line supervisors, and interpreters were watching who was talking with Issara's staff. So, no one dared share any information during the visit. The worker also reported that after the canteen outreach, the production manager asked the workers what Issara staff had talked to them about, and who was currently communicating with Issara staff. 

Recommendations:
- The business to publicly endorse workers using all available grievance channels, including both internal and external ones like Issara's, and should not in any way discourage workers from reaching out and reporting issues.
- Management and supervisors shouldn't exhibit behaviors that can be perceived by workers to be efforts at suppressing workers' freedom to express their grievances and report issues
remediation_business_steps_taken:
John, Ana, and Pick discussed with K. Tithipol, Senior Human Rights Specialist from Tesco first. Because NR Instant does not want to talk with Issara directly. So the Issara team discussed with K. Tithipol how to address the issues. He suggested that he would set the tri-party call for Tesco, NR Instant, and the Issara team to have a remediation call.

15 Sep 2023 tri party call
The business will make an announcement to all workers that they are encouraged to use any worker voice channel, including Issara's independent channel. Supervisors will be instructed not to be seen as asking intrusive questions about workers' interactions with Issara which has been perceived as threatening by workers.


DATE: 6 Nov 2023

K. Thitipol, Senior Human Rights Specialist shared the NRF corrective action. Please see the photos and details in the link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CCS_Am-bUSUOQ8QtNU_FnK6bA877e437

On 24 November 2023, They communicated with the workers at the canteen for 4 times at 11:00 am, 11:30 am, 12:00 pm, and 12:30 pm as follow contents as:
- Introduce Issara worker voice channels that are open for every worker.
- The worker can ask/answer and give information to Issara freely and with no retaliation.
- Posted the announcement on the bulletin board
remediation_notes: Workers reported that when Issara staff visited, the business informed them to go back to their production lines right after finishing lunch, to limit their interaction with Issara. The manager, line supervisors, and interpreters were watching who was talking with Issara staff and the production manager asked the workers what Issara staff had talked to them about.
remediation_action: On 24 November 2023, HR communicated with the workers at the canteen 4 times at 11:00 am, 11:30 am, 12:00 pm, and 12:30 pm to announce that Issara's worker voice channels are open to all workers, that workers can report to Issara freely with no retaliation. This was also posted on the bulletin board.
remediation_validation: A worker updated Issara that the business posted an A4-size paper announcement that included Issara's worker voice channels, and the message that workers can communicate with Issara freely.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue. The workers have received the business announcement with Issara's worker voice channels, along with a message that workers can freely communicate with Issara without fearing retaliation. However, the business response was very delayed.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: Review the grievance mechanism policy and the evaluate how effective the grievance channels are.  Revise the policy and/or protocols as appropriate to ensure both internal and external channels are active, responsive, and safe for workers to use
