description: Fees charged by recruitment agency: legal but not ethical

call_details.description:
As we have a meeting with CP-Ram on Friday afternoon, O&E reached out to the worker to get more detailed information or any additional concerns, if there are any.
The worker shared that, regarding the missing OT payment, work was added whenever he swiped the card for clock-in and clock-out; he always ensured that his ID number appeared on the screen, but when he received the payment, it was a missing OT payment as compared with the hours they had worked.Some workers used to follow up with the line supervisor, but there was no result.Additionally, the worker mentioned the abusive behaviors; they are from P-Leang/team leader (line supervisor assistant).They shout at the workers in order to ask them to do something.The way they communicate and talk with the Cambodian workers is not respectful.
Beyond the two issues raised above, the worker shared two new issues: one is about the high recruitment fee for MOU workers. The workers need to pay around 485 USD to the recruitment agency for MOU work with CP-RAM, and when they arrived in the destination country, they mentioned that they were supposed to get 2000 baht reimbursement from the business, but the Agency also collected it. Another issue is that there is no interpreter at the HR office; it is very difficult to raise issues or find support from HR.If there are interpreters, it is helpful for the workers to seek support and assistance whenever they face difficulties.
call_details.next_steps: Discuss the case with CP-RAM

call_details.description:
Get back to the worker to update them on the discussion with the business and their responses. 
Please see BR 2444.
Will validate with the worker again when the business shares the investigation findings with Issara.

After sharing with the worker the business responses and validating them with the worker:
1. The issue with missing OT payments:the business told workers if they were missing OT payments, they could go and check with OT logger staff. The workers can get back their missing payment after checking with the OT logger. But the point is that the missing payment always happened, even after the business investigated and found no system and/or machine error. On this recent payday, some workers are still missing payment, and even though they can check with the OT logger and get back the payment, some workers decide not to do so. The workers want a clear and accurate system for recording timesheets and payments.

2. The behavior of skilled staff (Pi-leang) is much better and improved.

3. Lack of interpreter: the worker acknowledged that there is a Khmer-Surin (Thai) who can speak Khmer at the HR office.But he didn't see any posters about the interpreter service yet; he will check at the canteen or entrance if there are any, which he will capture and share with Issara. However, the business should hire a native interpreter that could communicate smoothly with the workers and support them whenever they need help, such as going to the hospital, because right now workers need to go by themselves if they get sick without the support of the interpreter.

4. High cost of MOU: The worker acknowledged what the business has mentioned, but now RA has even increased it from 485 USD to 530 USD. The workers understand that this is the policy of the business: they need to be responsible for the recruitment fee in the source country, but it is burdensome to them; they don't earn much, but they need to pay a lot for the recruitment fee. The workers hope that the business and the buyer could consider supporting the workers with the recruitment fee.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case. The worker acknowledged that they understood that they needed to pay for these recruitment fees and consented to this prior to coming to Thailand, and currently the business will not change its policy to cover the workers' recruitment fees even though its customer requires the Employer Pays recruitment.
remediation_issara_recommendation: A worker reported that workers needed to pay around 485 USD to the recruitment agency for MOU work with CP-RAM, and when they arrived in the destination country, they mentioned that they were supposed to get 2,000 baht reimbursement from the business, but the recruitment agency collected even this amount.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Root cause:
1 After an investigation, it was found that the Recruitment agency had sent the cost of payment for Cambodian MOU
Worker to the employee for the cost that the employee had to pay by themselves (485 USD or 17,000 baht), which the
employee acknowledged and accepted the cost before proceeding to the next step.
2 From the investigation, it was found that there would be employees who borrowed money from the agency and the
employee already clearly understand this term of paying the balance that they borrow following the rental document
that they sign in the document with agency.

Preventive Action: -
remediation_notes: A worker reported that workers needed to pay around 485 USD to a recruitment agency to be hired as MOU workers, and when they arrived in the destination country, they were supposed to get 2,000 baht reimbursement from the business, but the recruitment agency collected even this amount.
remediation_action: The business investigated and updated Issara that it has a policy where the worker pays for the recruitment fees and the recruitment agency indeed charges 485 USD, which the worker will consent to before traveling to Thailand. Regarding the 2,000 Baht which the recruitment agency had taken, the business said some workers were indebted to the recruitment agency and this amount was to repay the debt, which is also acknowledged in writing by the workers. Although the business is not complying to the Strategic Partner's EPP, the business has communicated to the Strategic Partner that it will not change its own policy where workers pay, and will not reimburse these workers.
remediation_validation: Issara followed up with a worker and he acknowledged what the business has mentioned, but now RA has increased the recruitment fee from 485 USD to 530 USD. The workers understand that this is the policy of the business: they need to be responsible for the recruitment fee in the source country, but it is burdensome for them to cover because they don't earn much.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case. The worker acknowledged that they understood that they needed to pay for these recruitment fees and consented to this prior to coming to Thailand, and currently the business will not change its policy to cover the workers' recruitment fees.

call_details.referral_notes:
The group of 32 U-Turn migrant workers called to Issara Yangon hotline to ask for help for their problems. They are the U turn workers from Pataya food Industry from Mahachai. Although they arrived back Myanmar since March 2023 and have been waiting for 5 months already. But there is no response from employer yet and they could not go back to factory in U-Turn process yet. That is why, they called to Issara to report the problem.
Ma Kay Thi Soe who called to Issara hotline said that the employer "Pataya Food Industry" told them that the factory will call the workers back within one month. But it is over 5 months already and there is no contacts and response from the employer side yet. So, they would like to get the update information from Pattaya Food industry. At first, they heard the news that Myanmar RAs Ngwe Sin Kabar agency will send them back to factory by U-Turn. But there is no response from the agency too. When they contacted to the agency, the agency said that they cannot do anythings as the employer did not provide any info to them and did not contact to agency at all. The agency said employer did not give any workers information to the agecny and no guidance from the employers side. So, they cannot tell anything to workers about that. 
So, the workers asked for help from issara to contact with the employer from Thailand. Do we have any connection from that Pataya foods?
The workers said that they all have the valid passports and all the passports are being updated and ready to go.
But as they did not hear any information from the employer for 5 months, and being in trouble as they do not have any income for long time. 
The workers provided employer info and agency info.
Ngwe Sin Kabar agency is in Official list but it is new agecny and we never had any contact with them before. So, Wint told the workers that I will report it to BKK team and ask whether how we can help for them.
The workers also sent the hand-written letter to ask for help from Issara too.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue. The workers are very happy that they will be returning to the business as U-turn workers and will receive a monthly allowance while waiting for their return.
remediation_issara_recommendation: The group of 32 U-Turn migrant workers called to Issara Yangon hotline to ask for help. Although they returned to Myanmar since March 2023, there is no response from the employer yet and they could not go back to the factory. The business had told them they should return to work in one month but now it's over 5 months. At first, they heard the news that Myanmar RA Ngwe Sin Kabar will send them back to factory by U-Turn but there is no response from this agency either. When they contacted to the agency, the agency said that they cannot do anything as the employer did not provide any info to them. The workers said that they all have the valid passports and all the passports are being updated and ready to go.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
K. Chonticha, HR manager, responded that HR is aware of the situation. She explained that Pattaya Food currently has lower orders and does not require additional workers. She will, however, consult with top management in order to have clear solutions for this case and workers as soon as possible. It might be in the following weeks.


K. Chonticha, HR manager, defined that there is currently no clear policy on this case from top management.
remediation_notes: A group of MOU U-turn workers called to Issara Yangon hotline to ask for help, saying although they had returned to Myanmar since March 2023, there has been no response from the employer for five months as to when they can return to work at the factory.
remediation_action:

remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client worked at a Korean BBQ restaurant located in KL Kepong Jalan Metro Perdana, which is one of fifteen branches of the restaurant chain. Out of the fifteen branches, this particular one was problematic. The restaurant has six Nepali and thirteen Burmese workers. The owner's son is abusive towards the Nepali workers, creating a hostile work environment. Issara is able to speak with two workers. They have been working for this employer for 10 months. They are all MoU workers. They are reporting as a group of 5 Nepali workers, but the client is quietly reporting. The client and the workers want to either be transferred to another branch under the same company or find employment in another company. The client has debts to pay and doesn't want to return to Nepal. The workers have a contract they made in Nepal, but the company made another contract which the client doesn't have and is unaware of its contents.
Following are the major issues reported by workers.

1) Document retention: Workers passports are held by the employer since they started their employment. The company also kept their passports and didn't provide them with worker ID cards (Jalan cards) or necessary documents. 

2) Restriction of Movement: The workers were not allowed to leave the premises, and this restriction also made it difficult for their friends to visit them.

3) Unfair suspension: Workers were frequently suspended for minor mistakes or even without any reason. During these suspensions, the company did not provide any food, and the workers were not allowed to go out and get their own. They were also denied access to basic amenities, like cooling fans, during these periods. One incident occurred when a friend of the client was suspended for simply asking a Burmese worker to clean a stain. The owner verbally abused him and kept him in detention (suspension) for 28 days. Throughout this time, the company did not provide any food or salary, leaving the workers in a dire situation. His friends attempted to provide food secretly, but they had to be cautious as the company would punish them if they were caught bringing in more substantial amounts of food or any food. 

Recently, the victim was suspended by the company for two months. During this period, he received no salary or food from the company. The suspension was a result of the employer demanding the victim to memorize the restaurant menu quickly.

If workers demand to change the employer, they are asked to work 4 months without pay and there are some workers who have accepted this situation as they could not bear the harsh working environment. 

4)Physical abuse: Physical assault includes being kicked, slapped on the face and belly, and having ears pulled. The employer even physically assaulted the client's genitals. Such harassment occurred almost daily and targeted everyone except.

5) Long working hours and incorrect payment: Workers have to work 14-15 hours a day. In return, they received a basic salary of 1500 RM and a 300 RM overtime allowance each month. 

6) Lack of Sick Leave: Even when the workers fell ill, they were forced to work, as the owner wouldn't allow them to stay in the hostel. 



Moreover, during salary payment time, the owner would abuse the workers and suspend them for minor mistakes. The owner often used the workers as a target for his frustrations, taking out his stress related to the business on them. Whenever the business is slow he will start abusing the worker for no reason.

remediation_business_steps_taken:
Business: There were workers drunk and using foul language toward another worker. In response, he slapped him. alcohol content by their breath to define whether workers have consumed alcohol for
investigation especially during working hour, company related activity and accident /
fighting case happened.

beverages before work” and take this opportunity to provide briefing to all workers

Three workers who were involved shared the medical expenses 666MYR each and 877MYR was shared by the business. All parties agreed and singed the document. The document was also in the language of workers.

On 18 November, business also updated the preventive actions to be taken by company:
1. HR planning to purchase an alcohol test device. Purpose is to examine worker's alcohol content by their breath to define whether workers have consumed alcohol for investigation especially during working hour, company related activity and when accident/
a fight occurred.
2. Update existing hostel rules and regulations, adding “Do not drink alcoholic beverages before work” and take this opportunity to provide briefing to all workers with sharing this case as an example (worker’s name and face will be hidden).
3. Company will invite Police Batu Pahat to conduct the “Crime prevention programs and criminal offenses talks” at hostel for all workers to further understand the law of Malaysia to avoid going against the law.
4. To review the company hostel rules and regulations in order to tighten workers discipline especially on alcohol consumption.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Issue #1. 
Unapproved sick leave and poor policy: The company has the policy of workers having to request leaves three days in advance which is not reasonable for sick leave. This policy has led to situations where employees hesitate to take sudden sick leave because it results in salary deductions. Consequently, many workers end up working even when they are sick. 

Issue #2. 
The worker voiced dissatisfaction with the behavior of their supervisors. Requests for leave are consistently denied, and there's evidence of favoritism among workers, where some can easily secure leave while others struggle, even during emergencies.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Oct 16 2023, Sick leave MC; If workers go to the private clinic, which has to be approved by the company so that workers can get paid. Workers pay advance and claim with MC. 400 MYR. No mc, no money. If they are sick and did not have MC can request for annual leave when they are back to work but has to call the supervisor to inform them why they are not in the production. 
Workers can get the mc sick leave signed by their supervisors and be approved for their sick leave. 
Workers can check their remaining annual leaves that are shown in their payslip. In case the supervisor does not approve their request, workers can go to the HR office to see the HR. The HR will have a meeting with the translator to find out why their leaves are not approved. If they do not inform the supervisor in time, the supervisor will not be happy. If workers inform the supervisors after their leaves, then the supervisors will reject. Workers can call supervisors if they feel unwell when they wake up.


Update on 18th Nov, 2023. 

Issara has not received additional complaints from workers, therefore, this case is considered to be closed at this point.
remediation_notes: The business has the policy of workers having to request leaves three days in advance. This policy has led to situations where workers ended up working even if they are not well because taking leave may result in salary deductions. And workers also reported  dissatisfaction with the behavior and bias of the supervisors in approving leaves.
remediation_action:
Business shared that if workers go to the private clinic and get MC, they can get sick leave and they can claim the costs up to 400 RM per annum. And in case of not having MC, workers can still request annual leave when they are back to work however, it is advised that they call their supervisor informing them in advance (prior the working hours) so the production team can make necessary arrangements for the production. 

Workers can check their remaining annual leaves that are shown in their payslip.  If workers do not inform in advance, the supervisors may reject their leave in which case workers can go to the HR office, and HR office will investigate and take necessary action.
remediation_validation: Issara has not received additional complaints from workers.
remediation_results: Issara has not received additional complaints from workers, therefore, this case is considered to be closed at this point.

description: Unfair dismissal

call_details.description:
A worker who had raised concerns about the cost of paying the interpreter for the service to accompany him out of office hours was terminated last week. He did not inform Issara about his unfair dismissal and retaliation, but his friend sent out a message, and it said, "Issara! It is okay if you don't help us, but do not disturb us. Now my friend who informed you about the cost of the interpreter has been dismissed. Please stay away from us."

That's why many issues are serious, and the interpreter definitely knows who paid her for what. And when the issues reached the supplier, the workers got targeted and retaliated.

The O&E officer reached out to the worker's friend and explained that the business record said he was absent for three days without informing. According to the law, a worker who is absent for three days can be terminated by the employer. He saw the message.

The case can be closed.
call_details.referral_notes: To close the case

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue, as the worker acknowledged the reason for the dismissal.

- Based on the investigation, reinstate the worker if he has been dismissed without sufficient grounds

description: Issues with wages: in violation of law

call_details.description:
A worker called to report a recurring issue of suppression from the line supervisors.
The worker raised that in these few months, 1-2 times the line supervisor asked workers to complete the target first before they could leave during their two hours of OT work. Each time that line supervisor asks workers to complete the target of two hours of OT, the workers need to do 5–10 minutes extra, but they receive only two hours paid for OT.The workers don't appreciate this practice, even though it doesn't happen all the time, because they need to catch the bus on time; otherwise, the bus will leave them.
The worker suggests that the line supervisors should be trained and not suppress the worker's efforts to complete the target. On the other hand, the OT hours should be counted or summed up of all the minutes or hours that worker worked.
Details information:
- Plant: Processing Plant (Brae Roub)
- Department: Kirami
- Line: S3
- There are 6 lines, and each line has 70–80 workers.

Aside from the issue raised above, the worker has two follow-up questions for the business:
1. Will I be targeted if I urge or raise an issue against supervisors or an issue that happened at the workplace? The worker's concern that the business will not do visa extensions or renew the documents for him when he completes the 2/4 MOU contract.
2. Any disciplinary action that leads to not renewing or terminating the workers' contracts? The decision made by the line supervisor or HR?

1. Will I be targeted if I urge or raise an issue against supervisors or an issue that happened at the workplace? The worker's concern that the business will not do visa extensions or renew the documents for him when he completes the 2/4 MOU contract. 
2. Any disciplinary action that leads to not renewing or terminating the workers' contracts? The decision made by the line supervisor or HR?

The documents or contract renewal do not depend on the line supervisor; it is an arrangement from HR, and normally it depends on the worker's choice whether he or she would like to renew the contract or not because GFPT always wants workers to continue working with them as long as the workers do not break the rules and regulations of the factory that are all about causing damage to the factory.

description: Issues with security in living/dorm conditions

call_details.description:
The worker reports that during his day off on Thursday, he went out to buy some food around 200 meters from his rental room. As it was raining, he didn't bring the passport along with him. The police caught the worker by accusing him of not having the documents. The worker asked the police for 2 minutes to get the documents for them, but they didn't listen. The police brought the worker to the police station; the worker was allowed only to contact the relative to get the documents and bail him out.The worker was transferred from the local police station (Keha) to the immigration office at Ban Sao Thong. In the end, the worker could contact his brother, who brought the worker's documents to the immigration office and got the worker out, but the worker needed to pay the police 3,000 baht for the transportation of the worker to the immigration office. The worker said the business should take care of this coincidence and make sure this will not happen to their foreign employees again because the worker felt insecure and afraid whenever he went out, even though he is a documented worker. 


Only if the business asks for the worker's identity; the worker consents to sharing it with the business, as below: 
Line: Roung Cheurt 
Name: Vann De El
Sex: M 
Shift: Day
call_details.next_steps: BHR reach out to the business

call_details.description:
Share with the worker about the discussion with the business. Actually, the business also received a call from the worker and was waiting to support them in providing the document as needed from the police, but when the business called to check with the caller again, he said he had already brought the worker's document and got him out of the police station. However, the business will make a poster announcement to raise awareness with the workers and ensure their understanding of keeping the important document along with them all the time to avoid such a coincidence. 

The worker understands that it is not what business can do more of, and he needs to be careful next time. And he hopes that other workers will take it as a lesson learned and well understood.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue. The worker understands the incident that happened was due to the Thai government regulations and he will be more careful to always carry his personal identity documents.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that during his day off on Thursday, he went out to buy some food around 200 meters from his rental room. As it was raining, he didn't bring the passport along with him. The police caught the worker by accusing him of not having the documents. The worker asked the police for 2 minutes to get the documents for them, but they didn't listen. The police brought the worker to the police station; the worker was allowed only to contact the relative to get the documents and bail him out.The worker was transferred from the local police station (Keha) to the immigration office at Ban Sao Thong. In the end, the worker could contact his brother, who brought the worker's documents to the immigration office and got the worker out, but the worker needed to pay the police 3,000 baht for the transportation of the worker to the immigration office. The worker said the business should take care of this coincidence and make sure this will not happen to their foreign employees again because the worker felt insecure and afraid whenever he went out, even though he is a documented worker. 

Only if the business asks for the worker's identity; the worker consents to sharing it with the business, as below: 
Line: Roung Cheurt 
Name: Vann De El
Sex: M 
Shift: Day
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 19 Sep 2023

K Rungnapa HR explained that HR was aware of the situation and attempted to assist the workers by bringing a copy of the document to the police. However, according to the foreigners' working management emergency decree, the workers were charged a fee of 3,000 Baht. To avoid this situation, the company will issue a reminder to migrant workers to keep their passport and work permit with them at all times, even when on holiday or going to the market. They plan to make a verbal and written announcement by September 29, 2023.
remediation_notes: A worker went just about 200 meters from his home to buy some food but did not take his passport with him as it was raining. The police stopped him, checked for his legal documents, and took him to the immigration office, disregarding his request to walk back home and present his passport. He ended up needing to pay 3,000 Baht to the police.
remediation_action: HR explained that they were aware of the situation and attempted to assist the worker by bringing a copy of his legal papers to the police. However, foreigners are required to carry their legal identification with them at all times as per the Thai law. To prevent this in the future, the company will issue a reminder announcement to migrant workers to keep their passports and work permits with them at all times, even when on holiday or going to the market.
remediation_validation: The worker understands that the business couldn't have done much more than what the HR team did and he will be more careful next time. He hopes that other workers will take it as a lesson learned and also take precautions.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue. The worker understands the incident that happened was due to the Thai government regulations and he will be more careful to always carry his personal identity documents.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue. The workers have confirmed that the break issue has been solved.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that there is a written announcement that states that if workers take a toilet break longer than 13 minutes four times in a month, they won't get overtime hours for a month. If it happens five times in a month, they could be fired. Despite the employer saying the toilet break issue is not connected to overtime, this written announcement is connecting toilet breaks to OT. The worker suggested that MRG should really improve communication by making both verbal and WRITTEN announcements.

NOTE: This issue was only recently closed.

Recommendations:
- Retract the current written announcement.  Issue new written and verbal announcements to clearly state that there will be no punishment for taking long toilet breaks. 
- Managers and supervisors should be trained on this so that they can communicate this clearly to workers and implement the policy correctly
- Disciplinary measures to change the behavior of a few workers that may be seen to manipulate the toilet break policy should not be withholding overtime work or a threat of dismissal.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 25 Jan 2024

K. Alisa, the Director responded by assigning the production manager to investigate who violated the policy. The investigation is currently ongoing. If they discovered someone who was violating the policy after the investigation, they would be issued a warning following the disciplinary measures. Then they will make a written and verbal announcement emphasizing that there will be no punishment for taking long toilet breaks and will train the staff. She'll send us the corrective action next week.

DATE: 9 Feb 2024

K. Juthamas, HR, shared the corrective action taken after discovering that the production line violated company policy by using this announcement. On 5 Feb 2024, the line leader and manager received a verbal warning and were trained by HR. Next, if the line leader or manager does it again, they will receive a written warning as part of the discipline procedure. HR communicated clearly to the workers that they have the right to use the toilet at any time without any punishment for OT.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that there was a written announcement stating that if workers take a toilet break longer than 13 minutes four times in a month, a worker will not be allowed to work OT for a month and if it happens five times in a month, a worker could be fired.
remediation_action: The business responded that it will investigate who violated the company policy, which does not punish workers for taking long toilet breaks. The staff that made this announcement threatening punishment will be issued a warning. The business will make a written and verbal announcement to correct the message, and emphasize that there will be no punishment for taking long toilet breaks.
remediation_validation: Workers updated Issara saying their toilet breaks are now 15-minutes long and they don't have to punch-in and punch-out for these breaks. And they are not penalized anymore for taking longer toilet breaks.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue. The workers have confirmed that the break issue has been solved.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Reconsider how the company will implement a policy where workers can take toilet breaks as needed but are not taking excessively long breaks that affect production. The current policy of a 13-minute time limit should be changed, as such a time limit is arbitrary and may not be sufficient time for workers that may have stomach and digestive issues.

description: Denial of benefits to pregnant workers

call_details.description: Call from Nilar Naing  from TUM Factory-2 ( Worker ID- FH 2399 ) from fish trimming line reporting issues with pregnancy benefits.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case.  The worker has confirmed receiving the needed signatures from the employer
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker from TUM Factory-2 (Worker ID- FH 2399) from fish trimming line reported that she gave birth to a baby on 7th September 2023, and she had to stay in the hospital for like 10 days since her baby is not well. As she thinks she needs a birth certificate and hospital card for her baby as fast as possible, she took birth certificate application and hospital card application from hospital and submitted to TUM office on 11th Sep with the help of her cousin sister to get employer's signature. However she hasn't got the form back with the employer's signature. Until 25th Sep, she went to the office in person 4 times to get it. In last time, the office interpreter angrily told her that "you don't need to come very often, we are not working only for you, we will call you when the form is ready". When she asked around other friends who had experience in this matter, her friends told her that you need to go to the office very often to remind them otherwise they would forgot and even your form would lost. Underneath it all the client asked Issara to help her to get employer's signature as fast as possible and suggest TUM office regarding improvement in issuing the necessary document for mothers and babies.

Recommendations:
- Since the worker needs the employer's signature for these applications for the birth certificate and the baby's hospital card, this should be signed off without delay.
- HR office staff and employer to be re-trained on responsiveness to worker requests and to have set timelines for responses, given that delays such as in this case will have direct negative impact on the worker
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE 26 Sep 2023
K. Prad, Director of Sustainability, will notify TUM to check and speed up this case with information that the worker needs the employer's signature for the birth certificate and hospital card applications.



DATE 27 Sep 2023
K Prad emails to explain this case as follows.

On September 12, 20236 (night shift), the worker made contact and submitted the documents to the HR interpreter, and the HR received the documents to make a company recommendation letter. The worker was informed by the HR interpreter who received the documents that the process would take approximately two weeks. The interpreter will contact the worker using the phone number provided to come pick up the documents.

On September 13, 2023, around 11:00 a.m. Normally, the steps for processing documents include a company recommendation, a copy of the director's ID card and signature, a copy of the house registration/ID card of the power of attorney, and an offer to sign every single document.

The delay is due to the fact that the HR team involved is on an emergency mission and must contact government agencies. So this worker's documents are processing slower than usual. Furthermore, the power of attorney who must sign these documents is on an emergency leave of absence. Therefore, the document is being delayed even more.

On September 27, 2023, officials will proceed quickly and contact the worker to come pick them up. If the process is still not completed, the HR interpreter will explain it to the worker again.
remediation_notes: A worker who recently gave birth needed to apply for her child's birth certificate and hospital card but these application forms require the employer's signature. The HR office has delayed signing off on the application forms for several weeks, even after the worker repeatedly went to the HR office to follow up on her request.
remediation_action:
The business will check and speed up this case given that the worker needs the employer's signature for the birth certificate and hospital card applications.

The business since September 12, 2023, when the worker submitted the documents to the HR interpreter, there have been delays due to the fact that the HR team was on an emergency mission. On September 27, 2023, HR will proceed quickly and contact the worker to come pick up the documents. If the process is still not completed, the HR interpreter will explain what the delays are and when the worker can expect to get the documents.
remediation_validation: The worker confirmed that she got the employer's signatures for birth certificate and  hospital card applications
remediation_results: Issara is closing this case.  The worker has confirmed receiving the needed signatures from the employer
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Develop protocols for the timeline within which worker requests are responded to. Otherwise, the power differential between the HR office and the worker means HR / interpreter can use his position of authority to delaying response to requests, which will have negative impact on the workers.

closed_notes: Workers requested Issara not to raise this with the business, as they feared being targeted for retaliation given that there are only a small number of migrant workers working here.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported they were being deducted wages for paper wasted during the production process. At the same time, it seems as though the business is selling the waster paper to recyclers but is not sharing this money with the workers.

description: Discrimination – by gender/nationality/ethnicity/other in the work area

call_details.description:
Client reported that the business is discriminating about treating the pregnant workers between Myanmar and Thai. For Thai workers, the business let them work in Air-conditional room and do the light job likes attaching the sticker or something. But, for Burmese Pregnant workers, they have to work in the regular lines like other workers. If the costumers (Buyer/ or audit) come, the business asked those Burmese pregnant workers to go and work in the air-conditional room for a while. After they left, they asked those pregnant workers, to go back and work to the normal line again. The Burmese pregnant workers feel unfair about this. And they wish why the business can treat them fairly. 
Yesterday, they went and report to HR and HR just said why you are so complaining. The pregnant workers before they are working and like that and not complaining. 
The client supposed that the clients/ customers (buyers) might not want them to work in the line as it is so distracting and noisy in the production line, they said actually, it's not quite comfortable for them to work. But, it would be great if they can be treated equally. The business doesn't communicate with the workers too.
call_details.next_steps: Have to update ILM Team and send email

call_details.description:
Follow up call with the client for the case of discriminating pregnant woman of Thai and Burmese workers. The client mentioned that apart from the embroidery room and the heat transfer room, there is another air-conditional rooms called ACC. Yes, as business mentioned, both of these two rooms are not allowed the pregnant workers to work there because of there is smelling about chemical fume such as glue or other spray.
But, in ACC room, it is a kind of sewing stock are placed and where they allowed only Thai pregnant workers and not the Burmese pregnant workers. The business said both pregnant workers of nationality are working, but actually not. 
The workers mentioned that even if they are not allowed to go and work there, the business should have the Thai pregnant workers to work like them in the working line. They used to work one month before when the buyers or audit come as recommended by HR. But, the Thai pregnant workers find problem with them and they reported to the supervisors that Burmese workers are not working well. Without taking proper investigation, the Burmese workers are called back to the original working place. The client said it's not kind of professional to do like that. Every pregnant workers  should be treated the same must not being asked to work in the normal working line where it is noisy and uncomfortable. They got the training from the audit/ buys who have visited them before.
call_details.next_steps: Have to update in SC meeting

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
closed_notes: Worker was communicated about the process and paid 865RM as a compensation. And business has agreed to add to their policy and put in EC to give one month advance notice in case of no renewal of the contract.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: A worker reported his contract not being extended by the business. He was informed only 13 days in advance before he was asked to stop working. He was asked to sing a document about the renewal of the contract about two weeks ago, however, suddenly was informed of not being extended his contract anymore. 



Recommendation: 
- It is the best practice to inform workers one month in advance before they are asked to stop working. Otherwise, it would be best to compensate for the days that the business failed to inform the worker. In this case, the worker was informed 13 days in advance which means he should be compensated for 17 days of his wages. 




Internal Note; 

The business screen shared the worker contract, the contract only mentioned the procedures about dismissal. This issue is not dismissal, therefore the business argued saying that the reason they did not inform one month in advance to the worker is because there is no written policy for not renewing contract. Since they did not have written policy, Issara highlighted the best practice about recruitment which include workers to be informed about their status so that he/she can be financially and mentally ready for the next steps if the business decide not to renew the contract. The business agreed with that and they said that they will propose to the management and get back to us.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
Business; we will propose the management based on the recommendations from Issara if this worker can get the compensation as he was not informed one month in advance. If the management agrees with the proposal, the HR team will communicate with the worker and get back to Issara. The HR team added that they will notify one month in advance if there are any workers that they decide not to extend their contract.

Worker update: 
The worker have updated that he have received 865 MYR for the days that the business missed to inform him in advance. The worker thanked Issara for the intervention.
remediation_notes: A worker reported his contract not being extended by the business and he was informed 13 days in advance and asked to stop working. He signed on a document that he would like to renew the contract about two weeks ago hence, he was surprised and sad to leave the company as he is the main breadwinner of the family.
remediation_action:
Business inform him that signing the document does not mean that the contract will be renewed because the respective official and HR will review his past record of displinary action and performance for renewal. In his case, he has warnings and issues with performance. 

However, management agreed with Issara's recommendation to consider the compensation as he was not informed one month in advance. The business also noted that they will give one month notice in case of not extending the contract.
remediation_validation: The worker have updated that he have received 865RM and understood the decision.
remediation_results: Worker was communicated about the process and paid 865RM as a compensation.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: To inform workers at least a month in advance in case of contract not being extended,and to also communicate the process of contract renewal to all workers.
systems_change_business_steps_taken: They have agreed and will include this in their policy.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
PSM Line-3 (night shift/Pet meal processing); The workers know this line supervisor name as "Wanna-Ni", wearing green cap. 

The supervisor did not set the exact or consistent break time for the workers. She gives breaks based on the raw material availability. Sometimes at 8 AM, sometimes at 9 AM, sometimes at 10 am or sometimes at 11 AM. The workers start work at 5:30 AM. Sometimes the workers are so hungry and sometimes, the workers have to eat without getting hungry.

Recommendations:
- Workers should be given a consistent break time for lunch so that they can eat at an appropriate and predictable time
- Investigate this matter, with worker safeguards.
- Announce the appropriate changes and the appropriate time for the lunch break

Deadline: 7 working days
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 4 Oct 2023

K. Kung, HR, asked for the date on which the supervisor threw the tray to the workers. They will examine the CCTV footage. However, according to the information provided by Issara, they will investigate this case with many issues, including worker safeguards, and get back to us within seven working days.


DATE: 20 Oct 2023

Investigate Case:
This is due to PF3 line employees being assigned to replace other line employees that there is insufficient manpower. Each day, Line PF 3 replaces workers in another area and the arrangement is flexible dispatch to another line. It rotates based on the request from other departments. As a result, PF3 Line workers dispatched to another production line, would have break times the same as workers in that area. The workers will have uncertain break times if there is circulation to many areas. Each day is determined by the break time of the area being dispatched to assist.

Solution:
HR met with line PF3 workers via interpreter to discuss the break time arrangement for dispatching workers to help work in other departments. Workers are now organized as regular workers and have a fixed line, so they can take a break at the same time every day or not change frequently if necessary. It is organized as follows: 1. Take breaks when workers are aware of the situation of going to help in different departments at specific times and dispatching to help another line.  2. In the case of not going to help with work in another department, there will be two breaks: the first set at 10:30 a.m. or the second set at 11:00 a.m.


DATE: 14 Nov 2023

They are aware of the situation, according to the Issara update. They will speak with the supervisor to be trained on not forcing any workers to work after their shift has ended. They will communicate to all workers that no more than extra time is required for workers to work and that no one will be forced to work after the work time is completed by the end of November 2023.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that their supervisor does not set a consistent break time for the workers but rather gives breaks based on the raw material availability. Sometimes the workers are so hungry but have to wait and other times they have to eat without feeling hungry.
remediation_action: HR investigated, and found that workers were being assigned to other lines with insufficient manpower and so would need to take breaks according to the schedule of that line. Workers are now organized as regular workers in a fixed line with regular break times but when they do need to be assigned to another line as per production demand, they should be aware that they will need to follow the break times of that line.
remediation_validation: Workers updated that they can now go to the toilet freely now without needing to wait for a long time to get one worker to come and replace their function.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue. Workers confirmed that they can take breaks when needed.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Have a monitoring system in place so that supervisors are also provided some oversight and policies such as regular lunch breaks are practiced consistently across the factory

Moreover,he got sick after that and asked for a day of sick leave from the line supervisor; they required him to present them the medical certificate, but as he just rested in his room, he couldn't provide them the medical certificate. As a result, he received a warning letter.

The other issue was that the worker mentioned that the factory cooperated with True Company, and they asked workers to subscribe to the True Sim card. The subscription is 200 baht per month, and it will be deducted directly from workers' accounts. Most workers want to refuse, but HR puts a lot of pressure on the workers to subscribe to the True Sim card by asking the interpreter to tell the workers that if they don't subscribe to the sim card, HR will consider eliminating them.

O&E shared back to the worker about an CSO (LPN) who is working directly with the business, but the worker said he didn't know anything about that CSO and he never saw any poster or announcement of the COS.

1.  KPI #2087: Issue with annual leave or sick leave: violation of law

The worker mentioned that the sick leave issue is still happening; the line supervisors still require the medical certificate even for 1-day sick leave; otherwise, they do not approve sick leave.

2. KPI #2086: Verbal abuse and/or other poor treatment by HR or production (not illegal) 

The worker said even though there is not much support or care from HR, his injury has already healed, and they moved him to work at another line that's safer to avoid such an incident.

And O&E followed up about the pressure of the monthly SIM card subscription; the worker said it's become normal now as every month the SIM card agent comes to the factory and does the topping up for the worker. If the worker doesn't want to continue, just stop topping up. And the news of the pressure from HR is just a roamer, but workers assume that and are afraid to reject the monthly SIM card subscription.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue.  Workers confirmed the business is still providing transportation services when needed to receive medical services off-site
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that the business announced in September 2nd week that they will no longer arrange transportation service for going to the medical center (clinic or hospital) and the workers have to arrange this by themselves. Workers are not being reimbursed for the transportation fees they have to pay out of pocket.

TPs:
- What are the reasons for discontinuing the transportation support for workers needing to go to the hospital? Are they expected to pay for the transportation cost themselves?

Recommendations:
- Resume transportation support so that workers can get this support without having to pay for this out of pocket
- Reimburse workers for transportation fees they have paid during the time that the business discontinued the transportation support
- Communicate clearly with workers about the support the business provides, and the procedures workers should follow to request and receive this support
remediation_business_steps_taken:
KPI 2090: Khun Da was checking with the interpreter at Vertex and Hear Tong also confirmed that there was no such announcement that the transportation service was cancelled. The interpreter reported that there's 1 case that 1 pregnant worker took an annual leave and she came to the factory asking for an interpreter and transportation to the hospital because she had a doctor appointment on that day thinking that the factory would provide transportation for her. Khun Da said usually the factory will provide transportation for every worker to the hospital if they are sick when at the factory, but not when the worker is at home or is taking leave. However, for this case, the worker took leave so the factory didn't provide her transportation. She has to go on her own because she took leave basically. I was trying to ask if the worker could be reimbursed for the transportation she spent out of her pocket, however, Vertex refused on the ground that she was on leave. Hia Tong said he'll emphasize with the Vertex team that they should have compassion and provide transportation to a pregnant lady even when she was on leave, or at least help her to call a taxi if the factory van is not there.

KPI 2107 and 2090: BHR informed Vertex that the cases happened in Factory 3 in the Line 8 - 13. Khun Da will coordinate with Vertex Ubon and further investigate and will get back to Issara.

On 21 October 2023, Vertex called the workers for a meeting/comms session to clarify about the heath care services. Please see attached the participant list and photos of the meeting shared by Vertex. The interpreter who made the announcement about the 10,000 THB reward was also given a warning by Vertex.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that the business announced recently that transportation service to get to the hospital or outside clinic was being discontinued. Workers have to arrange for their own transport and are not being reimbursed for the transportation fees they have to pay out of pocket.
remediation_action:
The business noted that there was no such announcement about discontinuing the transportation service to the hospital. The business provides transportation for every worker if they are sick when at the factory but not when the worker is at home or is on leave. For this case, the worker was on leave so the factory didn't provide her with transportation.

On 21 October 2023, Vertex called the workers for a communication session to clarify that transportation to off-site heath care facilities were still being provided. The interpreter who made the announcement about the 10,000 THB reward was given a warning by Vertex.
remediation_validation:
A worker noted that the interpreter had announced that transportation service would not be provided. Recently, the interpreter was walking around trying to identify the workers who called Issara and she said she will give 10,000 Baht to whoever would point out the reporter.
 
In the latest update, workers confirmed that there was a communication session where the business announced that transportation service to health centers were still being provided to workers.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue.  Workers confirmed the business is still providing transportation services when needed to receive medical services off-site
