description: Threats aiming to discourage lodging grievances

call_details.description: This call is to Mr.Kyaw Htet from Vertex who reported the Level 2 case from Vertex and this call is to get worker Validation regarding the case.
call_details.next_steps: To prepare talking points for additional issues

call_details.description: This call is to Nay Lin Oo from Vertex to get the workers' validation about the level-2 case.
call_details.next_steps: Talking points for additional issues

call_details.description: This is from Vertex worker Mr. Lay Gyi to give us validation regarding the transportation issues. He reported that on 21 October the business called them and made an information session and announced that the transportation for going to the health centre is still available.
call_details.next_steps: john to close the case

call_details.description: Ko Zaw Htike sent us a message from messenger to give us validation regarding the transportation issues and blocking workers voices. He reported that in the third or fourth week of October the business called them and made an information session and announced that the business will still be providing transportation for health service and they will book taxi for workers when office Van is not available. And make the workers aware that the 10000 reward for identifying the reporter to Issara is not the business policy and action.
call_details.next_steps: John to close the case

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue. The workers have confirmed that the business announced they don't have to be afraid of reaching out to Issara to report any issues or concerns they may have
remediation_issara_recommendation:
In a follow up to another issue, Issara told a worker that the business didn't announce that they will not arrange transportation for workers to get medical service. He noted that the interpreter had indeed announced that transportation service would not be provided and that he did this himself to lighten his workload. Recently, the interpreter was walking around trying to identify the workers who called Issara and she said she will give 10,000 Baht to whoever would point out the reporter.

TPs:
- What are the roles and responsibilities of this interpreter?
- Is he able to make announcements on his own or does he always interpret for HR staff or supervisors when they need to communicate with workers?

Recommendations:
- Investigate this matter, with safeguards to workers because they are being directly targeted for having reported a grievance.
- Take disciplinary action against the interpreter as per the investigation results and the company's disciplinary policy
- Workers should feel safe to report grievances at any time.
- Communicate to all workers, verbally and in writing, the company's non-retaliation policy
remediation_business_steps_taken: On 21 October 2023, Vertex called the workers for a meeting/comms session to clarify about the heath care services. Please see attached the participant list and photos of the meeting shared by Vertex. The interpreter who made the announcement about the 10,000 THB reward was also given a warning by Vertex.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that after they reported a grievance to Issara about the interpreter, this person found out and was trying to identify the workers who called Issara, saying she will give 10,000 Baht to whoever would point out the reporter.
remediation_action:
Issara updated that business saying this happened in Factory 3 in Line 8 - 13. HR will investigate and will get back to Issara.

The interpreter who made the announcement about the 10,000 THB reward was given a warning by Vertex.
remediation_validation: Workers confirmed that the business called them for a communication session and announced that the business did not have a policy to give 10,000 Baht rewards to identify those who reported any grievance to Issara.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue. The workers have confirmed that the business announced they don't have to be afraid of reaching out to Issara to report any issues or concerns they may have
systems_change_issara_recommendation:
- Review the grievance mechanism policy and non-retaliation policy
- Conduct regular training to ensure all staff and workers know about the grievance mechanism (both internal and external such as Issara's) and be clear about disciplinary actions to be taken against any that retaliate against those who report grievances.

description: Issue with time card scanners/manual recording/systems to register working hours

call_details.description: The client is reporting the case regarding the scanning in her working place.
call_details.referral_notes: Have to alert John to draft for talking points.
call_details.next_steps: NA

call_details.description:
Checking with the client and updating her about the business response. In terms of with the issue with which scanner has the issue, the client said that if one scanner has the issue, every scanner in the Building-2 happens at the same time as the system has connected each others.

And O&E suggested her to reach out to HR as a short turn solution and as she mentioned earlier that she has the issue with interpreter. So O&E is clarified with her which interpreter. She said, there are a lot of interpreter in TUM and she mentioned that the interpreter in "Bi-Phat" room, at TUM-2 HR office is so bad. She is originally Mon ethnic. She died her haired as kind of blonde or yellow like this. Her face looks slim and small. She is also working as a interpreter in Mahachai-2 hospital too. So the business should aware of her appearance. 
She used to heard that this interpreter is so bad in turn of communication to the workers. Whenever the workers approach HR, she shout like "What are you coming again" or "Will you bring us the problem again etc". So She said, it would be great if the business' take any action regarding to this interpreter too.
call_details.next_steps: NA

call_details.description: Calling the client and checking with her to validate the business responses.
call_details.next_steps: We can close the case since the workers reported that they do not have the issue anymore.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue, as the workers confirmed that they are not facing any issues with the scanners anymore
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that the facial recognition scanner is often malfunctioning and workers coming in at 6am often have to go back and re-scan at 6:30am after work has started or the line supervisor needs to make a manual note. There is a technician that can help fix the issue with the scanner but he often blames the workers for the malfunction and refuses to help them sort out the issue. If their working hours are incorrectly recorded because of this, then they have to go to HR to get it sorted.

Recommendations:
- Investigate this matter and identify the problem with the scanner so that workers don't have to ask for the technician to fix the issue or for the line supervisor to have to make a manual note of the workers' starting times
- Have clear procedures for what workers need to do if the scanner doesn't work in the future so that it doesn't disrupt with their work and those responsible for responding with the fix do so in a timely manner
- Communicate to the workers the business actions to fix this technical issue, when it will be fixed, and what workers should do if the scanner doesn't work in the future.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 1 Nov 2023

K. Wichai, HR Manager, would like to know if this is from the TUM or ITC buildings. We confirmed that this is a TUM structure. He explained that if the worker was wearing a hat or if anything changed on his or her face, the system might not scan properly. They will, however, investigate this matter and identify the problem with the scanner, as well as communicate with the workers who are having issues with the face scanner to contact HR directly to rescan the worker's face again and add to the system to ensure that the worker can have face scanner easily, timely, and properly. And Issara can help to communicate to the workers to contact HR directly. They will send us the corrective action next week.

DATE: 30 Nov 2023

Investigation Result:
The Human Resources Department verified with workers who were still unable to scan their faces into the system and spoke to the supervisor. It was discovered that each worker can now properly scan their faces.

Corrective Action:
HR announced that if any worker is unable to scan the face, they should contact the HR office directly. (Leave the application room) in accordance with the factory building in which the worker works, or notify the supervisor. The completion date is December 1st, 2023.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that the facial recognition scanner that records their clock-in times often malfunctions
remediation_action: HR explained that if the worker was wearing a hat or if anything changed on his or her face, the system might not scan properly. The business investigated, and verified that all workers were now able to scan their faces into the system. HR also announced that if any worker is unable to scan his/her face, they should contact the HR office directly.
remediation_validation:
Workers provided additional information saying that when one scanner didn't work, all the other scanners would also not work.

In the latest update, workers said they didn't face the scanner problem these days. The business also made an announcement about how to report this issue if it were to happen again in the future.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue, as the workers confirmed that they are not facing any issues with the scanners anymore
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Conduct annual reviews of the systems in place for recording workers' clock-in and clock-out times so that workers are paid fairly according to the actual times worked.

description: Verbal abuse and/or other poor treatment by HR or production (not illegal)

supplier_name: Food and Drinks Public Co., Ltd.
description: Unfair dismissal

call_details.description:
A mobilizer from Food & Drinks shared that all migrant workers at Food & Drinks will be terminated on November 1st. The mobilizer said the factory is being restructured, and they only accept Thai workers. Sadly, 90 Burmese and Cambodian workers will lose their jobs at Food & Drinks. They are very frustrated with finding a job now, and some workers need to renew their documents before they can change employers.

O&E cross-checked with other workers:the workers said the factory terminated only workers who were hired under sub-agency, and the workers hired under factory work as usual. And the termination was informed a few weeks ago; the sub agency promised to find a new job for the workers if they could wait until the new year.
It was a validation call with a worker from Food and Drink who encountered a terminated contract who was hired under a sub-agency.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue. Many workers have moved elsewhere and are not seeking to apply for jobs at F&D. Some that tried still got responses from HR that they were only employing Thai workers.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that those working at F&D but hired by a sub-agency will be let go on Nov 1, 2023. These workers are concerned about finding a new job now, and some workers need to renew their documents before they can change employers. The business made this announcement only a few weeks ago and the sub-agency promised to find them new jobs if they could wait until the new year. Now some workers are looking for new jobs, and some workers are trying to get documents that could be used to change employers. 

TPs:
- How long has F&D had workers that were hired by a sub-agency and not directly by F&D?
- Why are these workers being discontinued?  Is it because there is not enough production?  Or is F&D trying to discontinue the practice of workers being hired by a sub-agent?

Recommendations:
- The business to consider hiring the current workers directly rather than through a sub-agency; to transfer those workers from the sub-agency to be officially employed by F&D
- If the business is unable to continue hiring these workers, take responsibility and ensure these workers have all the proper documents that will allow them to find another employer
- Communicate to these workers clearly what actions F&D will take: whether to hire them back officially as F&D workers or to provide them with the right documents to change employers
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 7 Dec 2023

Issara sent an email requesting a remediation call but received no response from Food and Drinks. Issara attempted to contact them by phone but was unsuccessful.

DATE: 14 Dec 2023
Able to contact by phone

K Suchart, Plant Manager, explained that he knew the issue. The subcontractor chose to leave the job with F&D. The company intends to keep the workers. These workers are the subcontractors' employees. He attempted to contact the subcontractor many times but was unsuccessful. He did, however, confirm that F&D no longer uses any subcontractors. F&D will hire and recruit workers through legal channels. (MoU and walk-in). In this case, if Issara can assist in communicating to the workers that if they want to work at F&D, they can apply directly to F&D, but please ensure that the workers have legal documents.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that those working at F&D but hired by a sub-contractor will be let go on Nov 1, 2023. These workers are concerned about finding a new job now, and some workers need to renew their documents before they can change employers. The business made this announcement only a few weeks ago and the sub-agency promised to find them new jobs if they could wait until the new year.
remediation_action: The factory manager responded that company will continue to employ these workers but will be employing them directly rather than through a sub-contractor. These workers should apply for work directly with the company. In the future, the business will hire workers directly.
remediation_validation: Issara updated the workers and encouraged them to apply for work at this factory as walk-in workers.  They responded that the business said it will only recruit Thai workers, which conflicts what the business informed Issara. Many have moved to other provinces or have returned to Cambodia.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue. Many workers have moved elsewhere and are not seeking to apply for jobs at F&D. Some that tried still got responses from HR that they were only employing Thai workers.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Ensure the business is legally compliant and only have workers that are legally hired directly by F&D
next_description:
communicate and inform the workers to apply for work directly with F&D
follow up with more workers to see if there are some that are still wanting to continue working at F&D
close

description: Unresponsive grievance mechanism / no action being taken

call_details.description: This is the call from the mobilizer in HT-70 who reported about the issue of 3 workers being arrested why doing MOU U-Turn in Myanmar.
call_details.next_steps: have to alert John to draft for talking point.

call_details.description: The client is following-up about the process of our discussion with business and RA.
call_details.next_steps: Have to alert K'Tong to have a call with business.

call_details.description: Follow-up call with the client for case update.
call_details.next_steps: Have to follow-up with business if they can give up the interpreter name and close the case.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue. The business is taking action to respond to worker concerns about possible risk of arrest when they return to Myanmar for the MOU U-turn process.  Workers have confirmed they can reach out directly to the company interpreters to express any concerns they may have.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client reported that 3 MOU workers from HT-70 got arrested during the U-Turn process in Myanmar. They were sent back to Myanmar on 27 Oct 2023 thru the Myawaddy-Maesot border. They signed the contract at Pin-Lone hall on 29 Oct 2023 with Aung Pyae Recruitment Agency. During the contract signing ceremony, the police official from the military came and arrested them. These three workers include Mrs.Yamin with her husband "Mr.Kyaw Win" and "Mrs.Su". (Mrs.Yamin is now pregnant).  Workers are being sent for the U-turn process batch by batch and they have come to know that 13 workers' names are on the government list to be arrested. At the factory, there is a pro-military group of workers and a pro-democracy group that have voiced their differences.  The pro-military group may have reported the workers from the opposing side to the Myanmar military regime to be arrested. As HT-70 started the MOU U-turn by batch by batch. The next earliest batch is 3 Nov 2023. Some workers discussed with business that they do not want to go back for U-Turn are they are under high risk. But the business said, if they do not want to do a u-turn, they can resign. So, some workers are planning to resign, while some workers expect that they still want to work if we can help them negotiate with business.

What the workers' request: If we can negotiate with the business for the sake of  the rest of 12-13 workers who are at high risk, not to come back to do U-Turn currently. So the mobilizer will let those workers not leave the factory. Or if the business or RA can cooperate together to help those workers from being arrested or not. For the 3 workers who were arrested, only one worker is visible in terms of anti-government in social media and not the other two workers. They are wondering if we can also check with RA and business to help the couple too because the wife is now pregnant.

TPs:
- Is the business aware of the three workers that were arrested in Myanmar for suspected anti-military actions?
- Is the business aware that workers fearing they will be arrested in Myanmar came to voice their concerns to HR but their request was ignored?

Recommendations:
- Coordinate with the RA to negotiate the release of the three workers that have been taken into custody
- Delay the return of workers for the U-turn process until April 2024, especially those 13 workers whose names are on the Myanmar military list and have a high risk of being arrested.
- Monitor the situation and update the risk assessment until it is clear that it is safe for the workers to return for the U-turn process
- Respond to worker requests appropriately, given the current situation where three workers have known to have been arrested by the Myanmar military for suspicion of involvement in anti-junta actions
remediation_business_steps_taken:
HIT 70 knew the case already before I called. They were informed by a worker that the 3 workers got arrested on the Myanmar side. They are well aware of the 13 workers who are in the list but they haven’t seen the list so they don’t know who these 13 workers are.  Actually no one has seen the list, neither HIT 70 nor the workers. They said they have heard about that list from 2 years ago from the workers. The information about the list spreads widely by word of mouth. Yesterday they had a meeting with a group of workers who are going back for U-Turn next Friday and asked if they have any concerns about going back. They said no, so this is how HIT 70 is making sure that there’s no workers who are in that list going back for the U Turn. They are also aware of the 3 October 2023 cabinet resolution but the cabinet resolution cannot apply because the cabinet resolution refers to migrant workers who finished MoU 4 or 6 years (from 1 July 2020 - 31 December 2023 only), but they have workers whose MoU will finish in Jan 2024 too. But it’s good to know that they are communicating with the workers before they send them back for the U Turn, making sure that the workers’ concerns will be addressed.

6 Nov 2023 - Hear Tong acknowledged the case and is trying his best to help the 3 workers who got arrested on the Myanmar side. There was 1 pregnant worker who managed to get out of the prison but she decided to stay further to take care of her husband who is still in jail. There's another female worker who is still in jail but HIT 70 doesn't know where she's located and her cousins are working out where she's imprisoned. For the MoU U Turn process, HIT 70 is already communicating with every batch of workers who are going back for the U Turn, which is a good thing, and Issara encourages them to keep doing that. For the workers who will finish 4 or 6 years MoU in January next year, the 3 October 2023 cabinet resolution cannot apply. Issara recommends HIT 70 that they ask the workers' consent if they want to go back for the U Turn or not, and it's up to the workers' decision. Issara also recommended that they communicate with the group of workers who came back from doing the U Turn, so they'll get a better sense of what's happening during the process. Hear Tong also emphasized that our O&E officer should encourage the workers to use the internal grievance mechanism first before going to Issara. So HIT 70 will give us the contact details of the 3 worker representatives and 2 interpreters.

13 Nov 2023 - Regarding the MoU U turn, HIT 70 has been continuously communicating with groups of workers who are going back to Myanmar for MoU U Turn. In the first week of November, HIT 70 communicated with a group of 25 workers who will be going back to Myanmar. Within this group, only 1-2 workers have raised concerns about going back, however, they decided to go back anyway. This group of workers have returned to Thailand on 8 Nov and nothing bad happened. 

Another group of 35 workers will be going back to Myanmar on 11 November. HIT 70 communicated with them on 8 November to see if they have any concerns or fear about going back. No one has raised concerns.
remediation_notes: Issara received reports that workers have been arrested in Myanmar under suspicion of anti-junta actions while they were in the process of doing the MOU U-turn process.  Another 13 current workers that are soon to return to Myanmar for the U-turn process are feared to be on the military list of persons to be arrested.  Workers went to HR to request they not return to Myanmar yet but HR simply noted they can resign if they didn't want to do the MOU U-turn process.
remediation_action: Issara raised this with the business, and HR responded that they are aware of this issue. Regarding three workers that were arrested in Myanmar, one has been released while the business is working get the others released as well. HR is communicating with every worker batch that is returning to Myanmar for the U-turn process. In the first week of November, a group of 25 workers returned to Myanmar, and within this group, only 1-2 workers raised concerns about going back to Myanmar but they decided to go back anyway. Another group of 35 workers will be returning on November 11, 2023 and none of them had fears about going back.
remediation_validation: Issara updated the workers about the situation of those that had been arrested in Myanmar and that the business is making sure that if any worker is concerned about returning to Myanmar, HR will work on a solution and workers are encouraged to reach out to the interpreter or HR. The direct phone numbers of the interpreters were provided to the workers.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue. The business is taking action to respond to worker concerns about possible risk of arrest when they return to Myanmar for the MOU U-turn process.  Workers have confirmed they can reach out directly to the company interpreters to express any concerns they may have.

description: Discrimination on workloads and assignments

call_details.description: Ms.Mae Nu and Ma Hnin from GFPT called to report the issues happening in GFPT Pae Lu Session Myanmar cleaning workers.
call_details.next_steps: prepare talking points
call_details.source_recruiter_name: Moe Moe Family General Services Co., Ltd

call_details.description: This call is a outgoing call to Mae Nu from GFPT who reported the discrimination on workload issues. This call is to let her know that  business response.
call_details.next_steps: to close the case
call_details.source_recruiter_name: Moe Moe Family General Services Co., Ltd

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue. Workers confirmed that cleaning duties are being assigned across all nationalities without discrimination.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Ms.Mae Nu and Ms. Hnin from GFPT called to report the issues happening in GFPT Pae Lu Section Myanmar cleaning workers. She reported that Pae Lu section are located on two different floors, it is 2nd and 4th Floor of GFPT main building. There are altogether 80 Myanmar cleaning workers out of 130 cleaning workers for these Pae Lu Sessions (for day/ night shifts). When it comes to the workload and assignments, the chief line-supervisor of Pae Lu Session usually assign Myanmar workers to work the difficult and tiring jobs but not to Cambodian and Thai workers. For example, Myanmar workers are assigned to work toilet cleaning tasks, drain cleaning tasks while other nationals are assigned to clean the production floor. When Myanmar workers can't take the assigned tasks anymore, they approached the chief line-supervisors and asked to assigned other tasks, the chief line-supervisor asked the Myanmar workers " Would you like to take my role of giving tasks to workers?  then wear my caps and write down your name in the assignment tracker by yourself for what tasks you are willing to do". The workers regard this as power abuse and humiliating the workers According to these two workers, there are 3-4 Myanmar workers in 2023 who had to sign the warning for negotiation over the assigned tasks.

TPs:
- What are the cleaning tasks in the Pae Lu section? Are they tasked to do "cleaning" for the whole shift or is this something they do for a certain portion of their work shift? Of the 130 workers tasked with "cleaning duties", how are the tasks assigned to workers and by whom?
- Is HR aware that Myanmar workers are given the more difficult tasks while the Cambodian and Thai workers get the easier tasks?

Recommendations:
- Investigate this mater; identify how tasks are allocated and assigned among the workers assigned cleaning duties. 
- Communicate to workers clearly about how cleaning tasks are allocated to workers, and demonstrate that the assignments are done "fairly" without discrimination by nationality of the worker
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 6 Nov 2023

K. Sarayuth, Human Resources focal, and K Rungnapa, Employee Relations Dept. They explained that the GFPT 'Hygiene Department' handles all cleaning tasks. They were unaware of the situation, so they must investigate the workers' assignment to this department. They will also communicate clearly to the workers about how cleaning tasks are assigned fairly. They will send the corrective action by the end of next week.

DATE: 16 Nov 2023

K. Sarayuth shared the statement from the investigation as follows.
The Health Department follows the Business Ethics Code Guidelines. It is carried out with integrity and sincerity. Do not discriminate against workers because of their race, religion, gender, marital status, or physical disability. Cleaning and keeping the bathroom clean workers of Thai and Cambodian nationality are also performing such work. There are no green books or other documents at the health department. which requires work to be signed at each work point. The Health Department arranges for work to be allocated and assigned to workers based on worker knowledge, ability, and suitability.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that workers from one nationality are assigned the difficult cleaning duties while the workers from other nationalities get the easier cleaning tasks. They feel the supervisor is discriminating against them in terms of the tasks assigned to them.
remediation_action: The business responded that it follows the Business Ethics Code Guidelines, which includes the statement that there will be no discrimination against workers based on their race, religion, gender, marital status, or physical disability. Cleaning and keeping the bathroom clean is assigned to workers of all nationalities based on worker knowledge, ability, and suitability.
remediation_validation: Workers updated that since the second week of November, the cleaning duties had workers from all nationalities.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue. Workers confirmed that cleaning duties are being assigned across all nationalities without discrimination.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Have a clear non-discrimination policy and train all supervisors and workers on how this is implemented in practice

supplier_name: Nan Yang Garment Co., Ltd. (Nakhon Pathom)
description: Lack of professional conduct of recruitment agency and/or employer

call_details.description: The seven workers whose visa and work permit expired after losing their passports were registered pink cards by Nan Yang, and they were allowed to work until September only. Then, the employer asked them to stop working, stay in their room, and wait for the work permit application. The workers now have to wait without earning money or a job for over a month. Other employers allow their pink card-registered workers to work, but Nan Yang does not. Now the government announces that those workers can do a health check for their work permit applications, but Nan Yang does not contact the workers at all. The worker requested that Issara help with this issue with the supplier.
call_details.next_steps: To reach out to the supplier and discuss

call_details.description:
HR did not contact the workers until December 5. So, the seven workers went to the HR office and asked how the business planned for their work permit and providing jobs. The HR officer did not come out and meet the worker. The interpreter came out and informed the workers that the business would contact them after December 15 for the health check-up. The business has not provided jobs to the workers yet.

The worker would like to know how the MD of Nan Yang communicated with the HR team and what the clear plan was to get back to the workplace. It is very difficult to struggle with the daily expenses and room rent without having a job.
call_details.next_steps: To follow up with the supplier.

call_details.description:
The worker from Nan Yang was called out and updated on how the supplier responded to their issue. According to the business responses, DOE stated that the registration system will be fully operational on December 15. So, beginning November 18, Nan Yang will check with DOE again to see if all of the worker names have been entered into the DOE system. They will contact the worker to schedule a health check and return to work.

The workers were encouraged to reach out to the HR office on December 18 and get an update on when the supplier will set up a date for a health check for the work permit and a date to get back to the workplace.

The workers confirmed that they started working back at Nan Yang on December 18, and the employer is in the process of applying for a medical checkup and work permit for all 7 workers. The workers will have to do health check-up on 4 January. The case can be closed.
call_details.next_steps: To close the case

closed_notes: Issara is closing this case. The business has made arrangements so that the workers can return to work, and the workers have confirmed that they are back at work.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The seven workers whose visa and work permit expired after losing their passports were registered as pink card workers by Nan Yang, and they were allowed to work until September 2023 only. Then, the employer asked them to stop working, stay in their rooms, and wait for the work permit application. The workers now have to wait with no job or income for over a month. Now, the government has announced that those workers can do a health check for their work permit applications, but Nan Yang has not contacted the workers at all. 

TPs:
- Why were these workers asked to stop working after Sep 2023?
- Now that the government has made the announcement about migrant workers processing their work permits and visas, what is the business plan for these workers?

Recommendations:
- Allow the workers to start working again, given that they have not had income for over a month
- Communicate with these workers so that they know when they will be able to start work again, and the process and timeline for getting their work permits and visas
- Process the necessary documents for the workers, as per the government announcement
remediation_business_steps_taken:
To sum up the call, Nan Yang cannot take them back to work now. The workers have to wait a bit longer to apply for the work permit. The Nan Yang HR person is in contact with the provincial DoE every week so she will continue to follow up with them. Nan Yang will also communicate with these 7 workers of what's happening and what actions Nan Yang is taking in order to bring them back so the workers are on the same page. I'll also continue to follow up with them again next week. Nan Yang also mentioned that they are paying the workers for any public holidays they have every month.

DATE: 13 Dec 2023
K. Namthip, HR, responded that Nan Yang had already submitted the list of worker names to the DOE. However, DOE stated that the registration system will be fully operational on December 15. description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies

call_details.description: Trafficking case

closed_notes: The client is out of contact. Issara decided to close this case.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client worked at a Korean BBQ restaurant located in KL Kepong Jalan Metro Perdana, which is one of fifteen branches of the restaurant chain. Out of the fifteen branches, this particular one was problematic. The restaurant has six Nepali and thirteen Burmese workers. The owner's son is abusive towards the Nepali workers, creating a hostile work environment. Issara is able to speak with two workers. They have been working for this employer for 10 months. They are all MoU workers. They are reporting as a group of 5 Nepali workers, but the client is quietly reporting. The client and the workers want to either be transferred to another branch under the same company or find employment in another company. The client has debts to pay and doesn't want to return to Nepal. The workers have a contract they made in Nepal, but the company made another contract which the client doesn't have and is unaware of its contents.
Following are the major issues reported by workers.

1) Document retention: Workers passports are held by the employer since they started their employment. The company also kept their passports and didn't provide them with worker ID cards (Jalan cards) or necessary documents. 

2) Restriction of Movement: The workers were not allowed to leave the premises, and this restriction also made it difficult for their friends to visit them.

3) Unfair suspension: Workers were frequently suspended for minor mistakes or even without any reason. During these suspensions, the company did not provide any food, and the workers were not allowed to go out and get their own. They were also denied access to basic amenities, like cooling fans, during these periods. One incident occurred when a friend of the client was suspended for simply asking a Burmese worker to clean a stain. The owner verbally abused him and kept him in detention (suspension) for 28 days. Throughout this time, the company did not provide any food or salary, leaving the workers in a dire situation. His friends attempted to provide food secretly, but they had to be cautious as the company would punish them if they were caught bringing in more substantial amounts of food or any food. 

Recently, the victim was suspended by the company for two months. During this period, he received no salary or food from the company. The suspension was a result of the employer demanding the victim to memorize the restaurant menu quickly.

If workers demand to change the employer, they are asked to work 4 months without pay and there are some workers who have accepted this situation as they could not bear the harsh working environment. 

4)Physical abuse: Physical assault includes being kicked, slapped on the face and belly, and having ears pulled. The employer even physically assaulted the client's genitals. Such harassment occurred almost daily and targeted everyone except.

5) Long working hours and incorrect payment: Workers have to work 14-15 hours a day. In return, they received a basic salary of 1500 RM and a 300 RM overtime allowance each month. 

6) Lack of Sick Leave: Even when the workers fell ill, they were forced to work, as the owner wouldn't allow them to stay in the hostel. 



Moreover, during salary payment time, the owner would abuse the workers and suspend them for minor mistakes. The owner often used the workers as a target for his frustrations, taking out his stress related to the business on them. Whenever the business is slow he will start abusing the worker for no reason.

remediation_issara_recommendation: Workers in the "MOU 19 Group" noted that the business told them in the 3rd week of April 2023 that they had to stay in Myanmar at most 7-8 months and then they will be called back as MOU U-Turn workers. They stayed in touch with the company interpreter via a Facebook group and FB messenger. The business also took copies of their Household Registrations and National IDs to arrange for the U-Turn process. On 17th Nov 2023, the business sent a message via FB messenger group that if they would like to come back to SF-2513, they must go to Arbourfield agency by 20 Nov 2023 and submit their passports to arrange U-Turn and the business also said that the workers don't need to pay any money to agency as the business had already paid to agency. Believing this information from the business, the 13 workers from MOU 19 group went to Yangon and arrived at Yangon on 20th Nov. But the agency told them that their names are not in the U-Turn list of SF-2513. They spent 50,000-80,000 MMK each to go to Yangon (she traveled there from Ayeyarwaddy) but they have lost their money, time and effort. They would like to request the business to consider hiring them back as originally promised.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 20 Nov 2023

K Sophon and K Supreeya, HR stated that the MoU Group 19 was the end of the MoU contract. They insist that they did not promise the workers that they would do the MoU U-Turn process, but they did tell the workers that if they wanted to apply for a job at Siam Food 2513 again, they could submit their passport and application to the recruitment agency in advance, and when the company has job vacancies or decides to recruit MoU, they would be prioritized because they are former workers with experience. However, the company has yet to make a decision. The MoU workers will most likely be recruited in April 2024. So, as previously stated, they will communicate clearly with the workers again by next week.

DATE: 23 Nov 2023

According to K. Sophon, HR Director, there is currently no final decision to submit the demand name list to for the MoU U-Turn for this group. They are holding internal discussions to determine when the workers will be hired back. They used to collaborate with Golden Gate (Thai RA), who in turn collaborated with Abourfield (Myanmar RA). They are, however, evaluating Golden Gate and Abourfied and looking for other recruitment agencies as options. They will most likely work directly with the source side recruitment agency. They will use the heatmap that Issara shared for their consideration as well.  In terms of the miscommunication caused by the interpreter, they will investigate and communicate clearly to the workers when they will hire the worker back and by which recruitment agency.


DATE: 1 Dec 2023

Issara shared a screenshot of the Line group in which the interpreter communicated with the workers about applying for new passports for the MoU U-Turn. K. Sophon, HR Director, responded that he needs to have an additional investigation with the HR team and the interpreter. If this is the case, he will consult with management. 1. The rationale for moving forward with this MoU U-Turn group 2. Reimburse workers for the passport fee and costs. So we agreed to meet again on December 7 to discuss the corrective action plan.

DATE: 7 Dec 2023

The meeting was attended by K. Sophon, HR Director, K. Supreeya, HR Manager, and an interpreter. They insisted that the company had not yet decided to submit the demand with the name list to initiate the MoU U-Turn process. However, the interpreter only communicated with the workers so they to prepare the documents, which the workers misinterpreted. However, they would like to work with Issara to find a solution. By preparing a budget to present to their management for reimbursement to workers who will return to the company. They would like Issara's assistance in clarifying the passport fee standard through a recruitment agency rather than a broker.  They also stated that they are considering hiring a new recruitment agency and will use our ER toolkit- RA vetting and selection tool to do so. They will most likely submit this list of workers' names in January 2024, and the workers will be able to return by April 2024, but they must wait for the final decision from their management with the budget proposal with the recruitment agency. So we decided on the following steps.
1. Issara can assist SF2513 in determining the legal passport fee (apply through a recruitment agency rather than a broker).
2. Issara assists in communicating with the workers that they currently have the option of applying to another factory; if the workers still want to return to work at Siam Food Factory, they must wait for the company's decision, and the workers will be on the top list for name list and will be reimbursed.
3. After receiving the passport fee information from Issara, they will prepare a budget to present to their management for the MoU U-Turn process with reimbursement.
4. The company will notify Issara in January 2024 with an update on the MoU U-Turn process and confirmation.

DATE: 13 Dec 2023
K. Sophon, HR Director clarified that The company is considering when to bring in these two Myanmar workers. In this case, the company will use the average fee of 3,000 Baht and explain it to the workers so that they understand. Furthermore, the company will reimburse the travel expenses according to company policy.
remediation_notes: A worker in a group of 34 workers had been sent back to Myanmar on 27 May 2023 for the MOU U-turn process and was informed on 17 Nov 2023 that they should travel to Yangon and contact the recruitment agency by 20 Nov 2023 to get ready to return to Thailand.  However, when 13 workers arrived, the recruitment agency informed them that they were not on the MOU U-turn worker list.
remediation_action:
The business responded that for this group, their MOU contracts had ended and they did not promise the workers that they would be hired back as MOU U-turn workers. They only told them that they could re-apply and if the company had job vacancies, they would be prioritized for hiring. However, the company has yet to make a decision on hiring more workers and any MOU workers will most likely be recruited only in April 2024 after submitting the name list in January 2024.

HR clarified that the company will consider re-hiring these workers, and reimburse 3,000 Baht for the passport fee and will also cover the travel expenses according to company policy.
remediation_validation:
Workers updated that they have since heard that the business is considering the MOU U-turn process for them and are looking to select a Myanmar recruitment agency to handle this process.

These workers are very disappointed because they paid high passport costs through a broker to expedite the process (there are currently huge delays in processing passports) in anticipation of returning to work with the company. 

Issara provided an update to workers about the company's position in terms of when they may be re-hired and what costs would be reimbursed by the employer, such as the 3,000 Baht for the passport fee and travel expenses. Two workers are going to wait to return to work here while the others are not willing to wait so long.
next_description:
- O&E communicates and validates with the workers.
- get update in Jan 2024 about the inclusion of these workers in the name list and also the reimbursement of expenses to workers

description: Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies
closed_notes: The client later decided to leave the current employer and find another employer. Issara is closing the case as the client has decided to leave the contracted employer.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: 

-One of the clients shared that his nephew came to KL, Malaysia on October 4th, 2023 through AGA International, RL: 530, a recruitment agency in Bangladesh. he paid a total fee of 420,000tk to the agency for visa and everything. an addition of 10,000tk was spent for medical check up on their own. Total 3905 USD. 

- a total of 400 workers came in separate groups along with him through the same agency. the clients nephew signed a contract for Orionplus Construction (M) SDN BHD, for the contract he paid 2,000tk in Bangladesh (which is a common practice for signing and getting contract in hand, according to the client). 

- since their arrival in Malaysia they have not been provided with any job yet. they are kept together in groups in a facility on factory site. the agency and Orionplus promised them that between 15th-17th November they will provide them with CIDB card and only after then they can start working. 

- in the beginning they were told that if someone finds work and wishes to leave the place they could, by paying RM1,000-RM1,500 they can take their passport and leave. soon after, they announced and stopped the practice. 

- from 4th October they were given RM50 weekly for food, which is to be deducted from their salary once they start working. 

the client provided a contact number of a representative of Orionplus, (03-4131 9961) and upon request of Issara staff shared the contract of his nephew and one of his friend, who were contacted directly to double check the issues. they shared the same concern, that they have not started working yet and they are worried that they can not start earning money after leaving their country. 

according to the management of the business, since the workers got their training classes to acquire the CIDB card on 4th November 2023, they should be receiving their CIDB card within the next 15 days since the test. but until now they have not received the card nor any work. 

the current updates are the followings:

- the workers has done the CIDB training, but they have not received the physical card yet. 
- online tracking of the card says its in the process of delivery (find it in the issue link along with the contract).
- the Bangladeshi broker who was the focal to bring them here is not answering their calls anymore.

the client is requesting Issara to if possible contact the management and ask when can they start working, because when the victims ask these questions to the management they are not given any answer and are often ignored.

Issara is trying to get the consent from the clients to refer their case to another local organization in Malaysia.

description: Treated poorly and/or threatened by RA or broker: serious violation
closed_notes: This case was referred to Our Journey as they have the expertise to handle such issues. Issara went through the consent process and workers agreed to share their contact with Our Journey for them to directly connect. Issara have shared the contact number of the person that had reached out to Issara and his name upon request from Our Journey.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Context: Including this client 210 other Bangladeshi workers were brought to Malaysia with calling visa promising a job here. it has been 4 months since then and they are not provided with any work. moreover, following are the issues that the client shared: 

- they are kept somewhere in JB and are not allowed to go out of the confinement.
- there was a Bangladeshi (contact given in issue link) broker through whom they came who is believed to be retaining their passport. when they kept asking for the passport, allegedly he said, "if you guys continue to ask for your passport, we will burn them" and now he is not reachable anymore.   
- they are not given food regularly, don't have access to fresh water to drink, and the electricity is irregular. 
- they are not allowed to go the embassy. 
- there is a Tamil, Malaysian who is kept to look after them, who allegedly physically abuse them. 
- the client and the workers have reasons to believe the normal police are taking bribe to overlook this issue. so they have no where to go. 
- they are kept and forced to stay there against their will. 
- both from the origin and the destination side they have not received any support.
- the client even requested if Issara can, they should send the immigration police. 

the client was requested to share contacts of other victims to connect and get more details by Issara staff.

remediation_issara_recommendation: The worker reported that her MOU-U turn has to expire on 19th December but HR asked to go to re new MOU-Uturn on 14th December. And payday will be on the 15th. remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 13 Dec 2023
Sopida, BFI's HR manager, explained that for the payment system working day, all workers who work from the first to the fifteenth of the month will receive their wages, attendant allowance, and incentive on the 25th of the month. According to company policy, workers who have an MoU contract until the 25th of December will receive the bonus proportionately. In this case, the worker's contract expires on December 16, 2023; however, the workers were required to return for an MoU U-Turn on December 13, 2023. So, when the workers return, they are given new contracts, begin a new year of work, and receive a full-year bonus the following year. According to the policy, because the workers returned to Cambodia on December 13th, they must work until December 15th to receive the attendant allowance. However, the worker will still receive the performance incentive on December 15th.  They will then communicate with the workers again about this policy when they return on December 19, 2023.

supplier_name: Daorae (Desa Sri Hartamas) Sdn Bhd, a Korean BBQ restaurant
description: Verbal abuse and/or other poor treatment by line supervisor/management (not illegal)
closed_notes: The client is out of contact. Issara decided to close this case.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
The client worked at a Korean BBQ restaurant located in KL Kepong Jalan Metro Perdana, which is one of fifteen branches of the restaurant chain. Out of the fifteen branches, this particular one was problematic. The restaurant has six Nepali and thirteen Burmese workers. The owner's son is abusive towards the Nepali workers, creating a hostile work environment. Issara is able to speak with two workers. They have been working for this employer for 10 months. They are all MoU workers. They are reporting as a group of 5 Nepali workers, but the client is quietly reporting. The client and the workers want to either be transferred to another branch under the same company or find employment in another company. The client has debts to pay and doesn't want to return to Nepal. The workers have a contract they made in Nepal, but the company made another contract which the client doesn't have and is unaware of its contents.
Following are the major issues reported by workers.

1) Document retention: Workers passports are held by the employer since they started their employment. The company also kept their passports and didn't provide them with worker ID cards (Jalan cards) or necessary documents. 

2) Restriction of Movement: The workers were not allowed to leave the premises, and this restriction also made it difficult for their friends to visit them.

3) Unfair suspension: Workers were frequently suspended for minor mistakes or even without any reason. During these suspensions, the company did not provide any food, and the workers were not allowed to go out and get their own. They were also denied access to basic amenities, like cooling fans, during these periods. One incident occurred when a friend of the client was suspended for simply asking a Burmese worker to clean a stain. The owner verbally abused him and kept him in detention (suspension) for 28 days. Throughout this time, the company did not provide any food or salary, leaving the workers in a dire situation. His friends attempted to provide food secretly, but they had to be cautious as the company would punish them if they were caught bringing in more substantial amounts of food or any food. 

Recently, the victim was suspended by the company for two months. During this period, he received no salary or food from the company. The suspension was a result of the employer demanding the victim to memorize the restaurant menu quickly.

If workers demand to change the employer, they are asked to work 4 months without pay and there are some workers who have accepted this situation as they could not bear the harsh working environment. 

4)Physical abuse: Physical assault includes being kicked, slapped on the face and belly, and having ears pulled. The employer even physically assaulted the client's genitals. Such harassment occurred almost daily and targeted everyone except.

5) Long working hours and incorrect payment: Workers have to work 14-15 hours a day. In return, they received a basic salary of 1500 RM and a 300 RM overtime allowance each month. 

6) Lack of Sick Leave: Even when the workers fell ill, they were forced to work, as the owner wouldn't allow them to stay in the hostel. 



Moreover, during salary payment time, the owner would abuse the workers and suspend them for minor mistakes. The owner often used the workers as a target for his frustrations, taking out his stress related to the business on them. Whenever the business is slow he will start abusing the worker for no reason.

Hence, we went back to Kepong to take his belongings.

I requested Mr Shin Jae Won to inform me when big boss return I would like to meet big boss together with POC but I was told not to come as they would want to sort out themselves.

After much discussion employer agreed to pay for POC’s flight ticket and do his COM when POC decided to go home.

To protect the POC I drafted a letter and requested employer to sign according to what they promised on paying flight, return passport and ensure COM is done that he stay with his friends while waiting for his COM, passport and flight ticket.  A Nepali staff and myself is the witness of the letter.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that he was recruited as an MOU worker by Touch Manak Manpower Supply recruitment agency, and he paid around 650 USD for the recruitment fees. He came to work with CPF in July  2021. He was only reimbursed 6000 THB from CPF. He said CPF still keeps recruiting many new batches of Cambodian workers and CPF also uses different RAs to recruit workers so the workers paid different amounts (12,000-20,000 THB).

- Clearly communicate to workers about the recruitment cost breakdown and what costs will be covered by the employer and what the worker is expected to pay
- Ensure workers don't pay more than what is expected and stated in the terms and conditions; reimburse all costs that workers paid that they shouldn't have

description: Pregnancy dismissal or hazardous conditions for pregnant worker

call_details.description: A Cambodian worker reached out to the Cambodia  Issara FB page to report the issues and made a call to the hotline number regarding Weak company policies and/or poor communication of policies,  Unresponsive grievance mechanism / no action being taken.

O&E called to validate with a worker who shared that, CPF Saraburi TH36 (Formerly BKP) terminated the pregnant Cambodian( around 30 workers) worker's contract before the 2-year MOU contract was finished. CPF also informed the workers that they would not renew the MOU 2-year contract for another batch of Cambodian workers( around 100 workers).
call_details.next_steps: According to the detail, the description of the issue of Contract renewal or dismissal, and the Lack of professional conduct of the recruitment agency and/or employer, we can consider closing these issues.

call_details.description:
O&E called back to the workers to explain to them that currently we couldn't help much in remediating the cases. Even though we have tried to work out with the buyer to be engaged with CPF, CPF rejected it as they mentioned that they already work with LPN. On the other hand, Issara also tried to reach out to LPN to discuss and refer to the case, but at the moment, we are not able to do that yet.

So, O&E suggests to workers that they reach out and seek an assistant from others, such as LA (O&E shared the contact number with the workers), and/or LPN workers can try to find their contact at the information board if not; for their information, LPN might have a field visit at CPF soon, in mid-March; however,bear in mind that Issara doesn't know how those two (LA and LPN) handle the case in terms of safeguard and risk assessment. So, workers need to carefully discuss with them how they are going to handle the case before deciding whether to proceed with it.

Note: we will still keep in touch with workers and ask them to update with us if there is any news.
call_details.next_steps: Issara tries to reach out to the LPN to discuss the case details.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A Cambodian worker reported that 30 pregnant Cambodian workers' contracts before their 2-year MOU contract end date. The worker added workers paid a lot of money for the recruitment fees to work with CPF (12,000-20,000 THB). 

Recommendations
- The workers should be formally informed by the business about the terms and conditions of their dismissal
- CPF Saraburi to pay the full wages for the time left until their contracts expire, given they are being dismissed earlier than what is stated in the contract
remediation_business_steps_taken:
1. Contract renewal or dismissal
If the business does not want to renew their contracts, we cannot do anything with it because it's up to the business but Khun Tithipol will try to see with CPF Saraburi if those pregnant workers in Cambodia get paid or not if their contracts are not renewed. If the business doesn't want to renew their contracts, at least they should get paid according to the Thai law which will comply with the legal requirement. The workers should be formally informed by the business about the terms and conditions about dismissal or renewal of contract and compensation. If CPF Saraburi decides to pay the full amount for the time being until their contracts are finished, that's the best. The same approach can apply to all 107 workers whom the business does not want to renew their contracts. O&E officer to find out with the workers how the renewal of contracts are informed to the workers and if they get the compensation. 

2. Recruitment fee
CPF does not cover passport fee, accommodation in Cambodia, and transport costs from the village to Panompen. These costs that CPF doesn;t cover, the workers have to pay by themselves. O&E will need to find more information and the specific cost breakdown of the recruitment fees that the workers have paid. What exactly are those costs? If the costs incur in Myanmar, the workers will have to pay. By Jan next year, Tesco will try to push the CPF Saraburi to cover the passport fee.

3. Unresponsive grievance mechanism 
Khun Tithipol needs more information. O&E to get back to the workers and ask them about the LPN to understand if the workers are aware of the LPN grievance mechanism and their experience in using it, for example, hotline and what kinds of announcement are being made at the factory.

call_details.next_steps: The next step O&E will make follow up on the issue that the worker reported regarding issues BFI systems

call_details.description: O&E called the workers in another line to cross check the issue reported regarding issues BFI systems to register working hours.
call_details.next_steps: Following the follow-up call with the workers from another line they got reimbursed and the business already took action to communicate with the workers we can consider closing this case.

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue. Workers have confirmed that those that were owed OT pay because of the errors with the new work time recording system have received their reimbursement.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that since the business started using a new system to manage the workers and record working hours and overtime, the Cambodian workers have been losing their OT pay. BFI's system calculates the workers OT incorrectly and does not reflect the actual working hours. The workers have been facing this issue for a few months already. The workers also reported this issue to the line supervisor and HR but there is no solution yet. 

TPs
- How are the working hours recorded?  Is there a scanner to clock-in and clock-out? Are actual working hours and OT hours recorded manually?

Recommendations:
- Investigate this matter and identify why the system is not reflecting the actual hours worked by the workers
- Communicate with workers clearly about how the working hours are actually recorded, and also announce channels whereby workers can report any problems with how their work time is being recorded.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 5 Jan 2024

K. Sopida, HR manager, explained that the new record system began operation on October 21, 2023, and that they are aware that there may be some errors and missing payments. HR manually checked the records and discovered that some workers were not paid. They repaid the workers who had not received their wages or overtime pay. Before implementing this system, HR trained all employees about how it works and that if any workers have any questions or do not receive their payment correctly, they can contact their supervisor or HR directly. They will, however, communicate to the workers through the Facebook closed group once more that if any worker has any questions or receives missing payment, they can contact HR directly by January 7, 2024.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that since the business started using a new system a few months ago to record working hours and overtime, they have been losing their OT pay as the system records do not reflect their actual working hours.
remediation_action: HR explained that the new record system came into effect on October 21, 2023, and that they are aware that there may be some errors and missing payments. HR manually checked the records and discovered that some workers were not paid. They repaid the workers who had not received their wages or overtime pay. If any worker has any questions or hasn't received their missing payment, they can contact HR directly from January 7, 2024.
remediation_validation:
Workers updated Issara that workers in some lines have been reimbursed for missing wages and the business announced to the workers that if anyone has any questions or did not receive their payment correctly, they can contact their supervisor or HR directly. However, workers in another line reported that this issue was still occurring.

In the latest update, Issara got the update that workers in other lines have also received reimbursements for OT hours that had not been correctly recorded.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue. Workers have confirmed that those that were owed OT pay because of the errors with the new work time recording system have received their reimbursement.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Review the system for recording work time of employees; minimize risk of errors and reduce dependence on manual recording by line supervisors

And Wint encourage the worker for emotional support although they are not satisfied about the V.S. cancellation as they lost their hope.

description: Unfair dismissal

call_details.description: This call is from one of our mobilisers from CMC, in this call Ko Hein, our mobilisers from CMC reported the unfair dismissal case.
This call is to KO Hein who reported the Level 3 case from CMC to get updated information.
Call to Ko Hein who reported the unfair dismissal case from CMC. This call is to inform them the business response and to get the update information.
call_details.next_steps: John to close the case

call_details.description: Ko Hein from CMC called back to us as he got a missed call from us. In this call, Issara requested him to clarify the number of workers and amount the workers received for severance pay.
call_details.next_steps: John to close the case and record the amount of severance pay in remediated amount list

closed_notes: Issara is closing this issue. Although the business did not clarify with the workers that the business was not renewing their contracts, the business provided severance pay to all the workers.
remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker (mobilizer Ko Hein) reported that on 8th Jan 2024, the business called 270 CI workers (including him) and informed them that they will be laid off and their last working day will be 15 Jan 2024. The reason given for the layoff was that they had not met the 98% work attendance target. When the workers asked for severance, the business said that it won't provide severance because workers are dismissed not for low production. However, the business said that they will provide necessary documents for those who would like to move to a new employer before 13 Feb 2024. In this situation, most of the workers regarded this dismissal as unfair dismissal because there is no 98% attendance requirement mentioned in the worker manual or employment contract.

NOTE: Initially this was affecting 270 workers.  In a follow-up call, around 50 workers will be allowed to continue working at CMC because they are at 97% attendance rate.  Now, this issue is affecting 220 workers.

TPs:
- When is the end date of these workers' current contracts?
- What are the reasons for these workers being dismissed? Workers understand it's for not having worked 98% of the time, which is not something that can be seen as legal grounds for dismissal
- Why were they notified on such short notice?

Recommendations:
- Review whether this decision to dismiss these workers can be considered fair dismissal. If unfair, workers should be retained and employment continued for this group of workers.
- Communicate clearly to workers what the decision is.  If the workers are to be dismissed, the reason for dismissal should be stated and if there are no valid legal grounds for dismissal, appropriate severance payments are to be paid to all workers. If the workers will be retained after review, communicate this change clearly
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 24 Jan 2024

K Itchaya, HR manager, responded via email with the available remediation call times of 22 February and 18 March 2024, which are too long according to the ILM case management protocol. BHR had a phone call to her. She responded that she needed to notify CMC management about Issara's proposal. Because CMC previously worked with Issara for MARS pet care, but MARs is no longer a strategic partner with Issara. BHR explained that there was an ALDI in the ILM that was still SP. She responded that ALDI is no longer one of our customers. There have been no orders from ALDI in a long time. So, if Issara wishes to make a formal call, they must first understand the nature and scope of the issue. BHR explained that CMC and Issara can collaborate while remaining in the ILM supply chain even if SPs are not present. So BHR briefly explained the issue. So she responded that all migrant workers whose contracts will expire and CMC will not extend the contracts or documents. In January 2024, DLPW and DOE convened a meeting with CMC and workers.  So CMC will proceed with 100% severance pay for the workers in accordance with the law.  She stated that Issara can validate this matter with the workers. CMC cannot share the amount and details.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that they were informed that they would be dismissed in a week's time, and the reason given was that they had not met the 98% work attendance rate, which they didn't know previously was a requirement or that it would lead to their dismissal.
remediation_action: Issara was able to contact the business, with considerable difficulty and delay. HR responded that for all migrant workers whose contracts will expire, CMC will not extend their contracts. In January 2024, the Thai Department of Labor Protection and Welfare and Department of Employment convened a meeting with the business and workers.  CMC will proceed with 100% severance pay for the workers in accordance with the law.
remediation_validation: Workers updated Issara that the business did not explain the reason for the dismissal but all workers received severance pay.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue. Although the business did not clarify with the workers that the business was not renewing their contracts, the business provided severance pay to all the workers.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Review HR procedures for employment contract terms and conditions, how contract terminations are to be decided and handled, and how/when they are communicated to employees

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported that he needed to get surgery for which he was in the hospital for 15 days, with costs covered by the employer. He said it seems he was discharged at the urging of the employer who wanted him to return to work.  However, his surgical wound has not healed and it seems the stitches are tearing apart. He has also received less than what his monthly salary should be last month, and his passport is being withheld by the employer.

Recommendations:
- Advise the worker to go to the hospital and seek medical attention directly. Also, he should contact the Nepal embassy for assistance.
- Option 1: Issara to contact the employer directly to advise him of his responsibilities that the worker is given the proper medical care and time to fully heal before returning to work and that the costs should be covered by insurance or the employer rather than the worker.  This is of primary concern.  However, there is also the issue of withholding of wages and document retention, which the employer should be advised to correct. This advice may need to be given after the worker has received the proper medical attention first, lest there be a risk that the employer may refuse to support the worker on all counts.
- Option 2: Issara to refer to partner CSOs if such appropriate partners are available
remediation_business_steps_taken:
He received one week of sick leave because of Issara intervention.

remediation_action: Issara contacted the employer who explained that the worker had his appendix removed and needs to get the wound dressed every other day. Therefore, his boss informed him that he could rejoin work once the Nepal Embassy confirmed his fitness to work.
remediation_results: Issara is closing this issue. The worker has confirmed that he has received the assistance he sought and grateful to Issara for support.

description: Proper tools/safety equipment/other equipment not provided: minor or isolated issue

call_details.description: This call is from one of the workers from Xian Ning,she reported a series of issues happening in Xian Ning.
call_details.next_steps: To write up talking points

call_details.description:
On January 31, 2024, the worker from Xian-Ning called Issara and informed her about the business coaching session near the HR office around 3:00 p.m.

The business said that they did not know who reported the issues to Issara, but the Issara team would come to the factory on February 1. All the workers should cover up the issues. "The business looks after you to get a job, and you all should look after the employer too. If Issara asks, answer that you get a daily wage and OT, six days of annual leave, double wages for working on holidays, and the employer pays for the document extension cost and provides the PPE at no cost at all."

In the past, the workers had the experience of covering up the issues in front of the visitors (not sure about the audit or DOE), and then the business provided them with 300 THB for not telling the truth.
call_details.next_steps: To update the issue to BHR and BHR to reach out to the business

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that workers are paid by piece rate, around 200-250 Baht per 8 hour shift but they should have received the minimum daily wage of 344 Baht per day. When they worked on public holidays, they were not paid at the double rate. In 2023, the business didn't fully give 13 public holidays as required by law. The business also does not cover the cost of document processing costs. Finally, workers have to pay out of pocket to buy tools needed for work and they have to pay 100 Baht to rent lockers at the factory. The business asked them to lie about all this during a recent factory audit.

Recommendations:
- Workers should be provided with all tools that are required for the workers to complete their tasks, at no cost to the workers.  Lockers where workers can keep their belongings safely should also be provided free of charge.
- Make this an official policy, and make the announcement clearly to all workers.
- Ensure all managers and supervisors implement this policy and there is no instance where workers need to pay for tools at their own expense.
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 1 Feb 2024

K. Orawan HR responded that they provide free of charge for the workers' lockers and also all the equipment and tools for working. they will investigate what is happening on the ground and get back to us next week.

DATE: 7 Feb 2024

Workers' lockers are considered company property. For the first and only time, the company asked for a 100 baht fee for damaged lockers and keys. The worker has already signed the acknowledgment name. If a worker resigns, the company has returned the money to the worker who signed to get the refund. The company communicated clearly with all employees, and please view the signed sample document.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that they have to pay out of pocket to buy tools needed for work and they have to pay 100 Baht to rent lockers at the factory.
remediation_action: The business noted that all tools and locker use is provided to workers at no charge to the workers.  The lockers are company property, so the company requires a 100 baht deposit in the case of damage to the lockers or keys. When a worker resigns, the company will return the deposit to the worker. The company has communicated this clearly with all employees, and workers have signed acknowledgement for this. The acknowledgement form, however, is only in Thai and it is unclear whether the foreign workers really understood what they were signing.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Have a clear policy that tools will be provided to workers free of charge
