description: Issue with holidays or other benefits: violation of law

call_details.description: This call is from one of the workers from Xian Ning,she reported a series of issues happening in Xian Ning.
call_details.next_steps: To write up talking points

call_details.description:
On January 31, 2024, the worker from Xian-Ning called Issara and informed her about the business coaching session near the HR office around 3:00 p.m.

The business said that they did not know who reported the issues to Issara, but the Issara team would come to the factory on February 1. All the workers should cover up the issues. "The business looks after you to get a job, and you all should look after the employer too. If Issara asks, answer that you get a daily wage and OT, six days of annual leave, double wages for working on holidays, and the employer pays for the document extension cost and provides the PPE at no cost at all."

In the past, the workers had the experience of covering up the issues in front of the visitors (not sure about the audit or DOE), and then the business provided them with 300 THB for not telling the truth.
call_details.next_steps: To update the issue to BHR and BHR to reach out to the business

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that workers are paid by piece rate, around 200-250 Baht per 8 hour shift but they should have received the minimum daily wage of 344 Baht per day. When they worked on public holidays, they were not paid at the double rate. In 2023, the business didn't fully give 13 public holidays as required by law. The business also does not cover the cost of document processing costs. Finally, workers have to pay out of pocket to buy tools needed for work and they have to pay 100 Baht to rent lockers at the factory.  The business asked them to lie about all this during a recent factory audit.

Recommendations:
- Workers should be provided with at least 13 public holidays each year as required by law.  
- Check the HR records and reimburse the number of public holidays that were not given to the workers last year
remediation_business_steps_taken:
DATE: 1 Feb 2024

K. Orawan HR responded that they insist and confirm that all employees get the 13 public holidays according to the law. they will investigate what is happening on the ground and get back to us next week.

DATE: 7 Feb 2024

The investigation found that there was a misunderstanding caused by the announcement of public holidays, which had previously been closed on 2-3 Jan 2024, as well as the customer pressing the company to deliver the supplies on time. Then on January 5, 2024, the company announced the change of a new 13 public holiday to all employees. So the 2-3 Jan 2024 are working days and all employees have a full 13 public holidays in 2024. However, the foreign workers misinterpreted the old public holiday notification and assumed it was a holiday with double wages.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that in 2023, the business didn't fully give all 13 public holidays as required by law.
remediation_action: The business conducted an investigation and found that there was a misunderstanding caused by the announcement of public holidays, which had previously noted 2-3 Jan 2024 as holidays but due to customer demands, the factory stayed open for production. On January 5, 2024, the company announced the new public holiday list to all employees, with 2-3 Jan 2024 now considered as working days and 13 public holidays scheduled in 2024. However, the foreign workers was going by the the original public holiday list and so thought 2-3 Jan 2024 were holidays worked to be paid at double wages.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - HR needs to publish the 13 public holidays well in advance of the start of each new year

call_details.referral_notes: as the issue has already been discussed with the business and followed up with the client, currently Issara will continue engaging with the client to monitor any positive changes and steps taken by the business to remediate the issue and follow up with the business at the end of the month.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A worker reported for the past couple months, they have not been given OT hours, with the manager citing a lack of orders but when there is OT, it is not given to Bangladeshi workers but given to Nepali and Myanmar workers.  The business also force them to meet daily targets which have been increased. When workers raise the issue of these increased targets, the employer will tell them they can leave and go back to Bangladesh if they can't keep up.

NOTE: The worker would like Issara to raise this issue with the business but doesn't want his identity to be disclosed.

Recommendations for the employer: 
- The employer should communicate clearly to workers about the production demands and the forecast for OT hours in the coming months. 
- The employer should clarify that daily targets are not tied to the daily wage. Workers are to be paid per 8-hour shift as per the contract, whether or not targets are met. Any time worked beyond the 8-hour period should be paid as OT.
- The employer should have an equitable and non-coercive OT system that doesn't favor workers from any nationality over another. Communicate how OT hours are offered to workers to show that it is fairly distributed and non-discriminatory
remediation_notes: A worker reported for the past couple months, they have not been given OT hours, with the manager citing a lack of orders but when there is OT, it is not given  to workers from one country but given to workers from other countries.  The business also force them to meet daily targets which have been increased. When workers raise the issue of these increased targets, the employer will tell them they can leave and go back home if they can't keep up.
remediation_action: The business acknowledged that the line supervisor may have spoken in a way that is not appropriate and they will be reminded to explain the reasons for how OT is allocated to workers and how targets are set rather than simply dismissing worker's concerns. The business will make an announcement to all workers, with translation into the workers' languages about how the OT is given and how targets are set, so that they understand the company policies.

description: Workers placed in workplace and jobs different from what they were recruited for

call_details.description: The workers reported that they were recruited by Pyae Paing Hmue and sent to Thailand on 1st Dec were sent to various places that are different from the one they had contracted for.
call_details.referral_notes: Will contact the Myanmar RA and also provided the client MOEA number
call_details.next_steps: Jonah to contact Wint

remediation_issara_recommendation:
14 workers were recruited by Pyae Paing Hmue RA to work in TMCL Energy Service Company and sent to Thailand on 1 Dec 2023 but placed in other workplaces. They were sent to  Daw Bi Bi in Rayong, and told they would be sent to a Nakhon Ratchasima construction company for a temporary job. They started work on 7 Dec 2023 but due to daily wage issues, they went back to  Daw Bi Bi on 28 December 2023. The workers got only 2,000 baht for daily wages from the construction work. This time, Daw Bi Bi said that they will get a job in TMCL only in April 2024 so they would need to work at a construction site in Rama 2 until then, which the workers agreed to. However, at the construction site, they were forced to sign 6-month contracts.

TPs (for the RA):
- Did TMCL have an agreement with you to send these MOU workers to their workplace? Why were they not sent there but ended up with Daw Bi Bi in Rayong?
- Why is it that the workers have been told that they can only start work with TMCL in April 2024 but arrived in Thailand in Dec 2023?
- Is the RA aware that the workers have been moved to different construction sites and now supposedly coerced into working for 6 months at the latest site?

Recommendations:
- The workers should be delivered to the workplace as agreed with the employer that contracted the RA and as stated in the employment contract
- The RA to coordinate with the employer so that the workers can be employed at the workplace as per their contract immediately.
- Workers to be encouraged to reach out to MOEAA or the LA for assistance if the RA cannot or unwilling to assist
remediation_notes: Workers hired to work for a certain company found upon arrival in Thailand that they had to work in workplaces different from what they were promised.
remediation_action: Issara contacted the recruitment agency, and the Managing Director noted that the Thai factory broke its promise and did not accept these workers citing low orders and decreasing company profits. That is why the agency had to find other jobs for these workers in Thailand. TMCL said it will hire the workers when needed but couldn't provide a timeframe. The MD also contacted his staff based in Thailand and instructed her to solve this issue as soon as possible.
next_description:
Reach out to the RA
Check back with the RA on workers' status

description: Lack of access to safe and credible grievance mechanism

call_details.next_steps: The worker has requested us not to escalate the issue within the company for a few days because he raised his voice during the meeting and informed the employer that he intends to file a complaint. As a result, the company may easily identify him as the reporter. We need to wait till we get consent from the reporter.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Workers reported that since February 7th, 2024, Gimmill announced workers will now only receive 50 RM for their medical checkups. Simply put, if a worker falls ill and visits the hospital's clinic, the company will reimburse them only 50 RM and any additional medical expenses will be the responsibility of the worker. The worker stated that the typical cost of a clinic visit ranges from 80 to 90 RM so this will become a financial burden and this policy is against the terms in their employment contract, which explicitly states that the employer is responsible for medical expenses. The company announced this change during a meeting with the workers. Despite protests from the worker, the company dismissed the objections. 

TPs:
- What are the requirements in terms of buying health insurance for migrant workers? If all workers are to be ensured, why has this policy change been instituted?

Recommendations:
- Any changes in the policy of wages and benefits should not go against what is stated in the employment contract and medical expenses should be covered as part of the insurance scheme, as required by law
- Communicate clearly to all workers about the details of the health insurance coverage and that medical expenses will be covered according to the insurance policy
- Any issues raised by the workers should be received professionally and responded to in a timely manner, rather than being dismissed immediately.
remediation_notes: Workers reported that since February 7th, 2024, the business announced that workers will now only receive 50 RM for health care visits and any additional medical expenses will be the responsibility of the worker. The workers understand that the employment contract explicitly states that the employer is responsible for medical expenses.  When workers protested this policy change, the business simply dismissed the objections.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: - Conduct annual review of the internal grievance mechanism system, and ensure the designated responders are properly trained to be appropriately receive and respond to all worker reports.
next_description: Reach out to the business, after getting consent from the worker

- What is the business' set ratio for number of persons per square meter to determine the appropriate number of people to fit into a dorm room, including kitchen space provided

- Get direct feedback from the workers on the current living arrangement.  Consider housing workers in such a way that they don't feel like it is too overcrowded for them

remediation_issara_recommendation:
A group of jobseekers were hired at zero fees to work at this business through Golden Plant RA.  However, out of 200 workers, 37 workers were sent to Malaysia and the remaining 163 workers have been left in limbo when Golden Plant were informed by the Malaysian RA that this recruitment was cancelled and the job openings already filled by worker from other countries. Golden Plant offered to call these workers back if they get other demands for workers.

Recommendations:
- The business to provide an explanation as to what happened and why they reneged on contract offers that had already been given to these workers. Provide compensation for the lost opportunity and time that these workers have suffered due to the cancellation 
- Golden Plant to connect these workers to other zero fee jobs ASAP, whether it is with Golden Plant or referred to another RA

call_details.description:
Mr.Htet Aung (ID:387094) has been working in MDL line in MCL facilities for almost 3 years. The supervisor P'Kwite is discriminating in terms of assigning the task to him. While he is focusing on his current task, the supervisor asked him to go and assist with other tasks. He used to cover this without complaint. But, this morning, while he was trying to focus on his  point, the supervisor asked him to go and assist with other points like before. Before he finished the second point, the supervisor asked to go and assist the third point again. Actually, there are still many workers and the supervisor just asks him to wander around like this. The supervisor's behavior irritated him and  he cannot control his emotions anymore. So he told the supervisor that, if you don't like me, you can dismiss me. Without any consultation or discussion with the worker, the supervisor said, I will give you the resignation letter this afternoon. Then the supervisor asked him to go home without finishing the morning shift. He said, at least, the supervisor should call the translator and solve the problem at HR. He didn't expect the supervisor's behavior to happen like that. He called me this morning and I suggested that he go and report to the HR office.
But, as he is from MCL facilities, the security doesn't allow him to go to the TGM HR office. He tried to call Ko Moe Aung, Burmese translator. But, he is not helpful and he just told the worker that the problem happened in the production line, and should be solved in the production line. He is just wondering if we can help him access HR so that he would like to report what he would like to present to HR according to how the line supervisor treats him. He will also request to change his line or provide him with a job changeable cancellation letter if they don't want to hire him anymore.
call_details.next_steps: Have to escalate to ILM team and to check with HR

call_details.description:
This is a call from TGM worker who was poorly treated by the line supervisor and has some difficulties to access to grievance mechanism. 

Today, TGM' HR with short hair (Probaby K'Dan), the Burmese Official Interpreter (Ko Moe Aung) and the line Supervisor (P' Kwite) and the worker had a tri-party meeting today at 2:00 PM in MCL Canteen.

HR:            "What's the problem with you? Any problem with your colleagues at your workplace?", she asked the worker interpreted by the interpreter.

Worker:    "No, I have no problem with my colleagues at all. But, I want to work peacefully like other workers. But, I don't know why I was asked to go around in the line and do the unspecific task. Before I finished, I was asked to move to another point again. So, I am not happy. So please tell me, what's wrong with me. So I can prepare or amend myself. In case if there is something I need to follow and apply, I will note it or if I should also do a record, I will record this.

**Then the Burmese Interpreter interpreted what the worker said to HR. The worker doesn't understand what the interpreter interpreted. After that, HR said something with a sense of anger in a high tone. She speaks in Thai a lot, but the worker does not understand at all. He understood that it also included "Issara" in her speech. He just estimated that HR talking you can talk or report to any organization, including Issara, we don't care. But, the interpreter didn't interpret back what HR said. 
(Then both of them left the canteen. Without telling the worker if he should change the line or continue working in the same line. Then the supervisor also left. So only the worker is left alone and he has no idea if he should continue in his current job and he is about to leave the workplace. Then he called me and he said, if I should go home or continue working, I told him to calm down, please ask the supervisor if he has to do something. Then he asked the supervisor and the supervisor said, she has no idea either. So I just told him, please focus and continue working with your current task. Now, he is settled back. He doesn't know why HR behavior changed like that and left without solving the problem. He is wondering what has been interpreted and why the interpreter didn't interpret back what HR said. And then he doesn't know how to continue working tomorrow. )
So he asked if we could talk with HR and asked
1. Why does she get upset and behave like that without solving the issue?
2. Should he  stop working or continue working? Where should he work?
3. What has the interpreter interpreted to HR?
4. What does HR tell back to the worker as the interpreter did not translate it?
call_details.next_steps: Have to update ILM team and checking to follow up with HR

remediation_notes:
An MoU worker called to report an issue with the cancellation letter provided to a group of 57 workers working at the plant that they are not able to use it to apply for jobs in different provinces, as the new employer have rejected their candidature stating that the cancellation letters are not eligible for changing jobs. Two separate batches of workers are impacted by this issue.

BHR spoke with an electronics factory to hire these workers and they require a list of names and other details to process the cases. However, on two days later that factory advised that they have already found the necessary number of workers as they had a walk-in of over 7000 workers for 200 positions they were hiring. So jobs for these workers are no longer available.

The management at this plant have acknowledged that in some provinces the "resignation" remarks on the cancellation letters are interpreted differently so it is possible that the workers are having issues with new employers. In that event, management is open to modification of remarks in the cancellation letter.

The following week, some workers did try to reach the business about this problem however they were denied access. Plant management has requested Issara to find out from MoL/DoE about the process to re-issue cancellation letters so they can advise all impacted workers and handle the cases accordingly. We did so and letters were re-issued based on our guidance.
remediation_action:
Plant management have acknowledged that in some provinces the "resignation" remarks on the cancellation letters are interpreted differently so it is possible that the workers are having issues with new employers. In that event, workers can contact HR and they are open to modification of remarks in the cancellation letters. Issara to schedule a formal remediation call with management for agreement on business actions for the closure of this issue.

The follwing week, some workers did try to reach the business about this problem however they were denied access. Management has requested Issara to find out from DoE about the process to re-issue cancellation letters so they can advise all impacted workers and handle the cases accordingly. We did so and letters were re-issued with this guidance.

In addition, Issara is helping the workers to find new job opportunities on Golden Dreams and from speaking with other businesses in our orbit.
remediation_validation:
Workers confirm that despite management saying that they were welcome to contact HR, they have been denied access at every turn.

They are now focused on getting cancellation letters that will allow them to switch employers without returning to Myanmar, and, finding actual jobs.
remediation_results: We successfully obtained the correct cancellation letters to allow workers to switch employers in-country without returning home. The workers are now focused on finding new jobs and avoid having to return to Myanmar given the civil war, and have a few leads. Workers have up to 60 days to find a new job with the corrected cancellation letter.

call_details.description:
The client reported that she had left the job for a year and when she came back, she was refused to be hired again.

The client is the wife of Ambassador Htet Aung in TGM. She gave birth to a baby in Apr 2021 and took the maternity leave 4 month + 10 days (3 months paid + 40 days unpaid). Then she went back to Myanmar to send her child after that. When MOU reopened in Jun 2022, she asked her sister-in-law, Htet Aung' s sister to give her name list to Ko Moe Aung, the interpreter as Htet Aung doesn't get along with the interpreter. Then the interpreter told her sister-in-law that to have her come back with an illegal channel and apply it back as she still left her passport and work permit and they are still alive. Then she can reapply as walk-in again. He also add that as the MOU channel is difficult, she may need to wait and a lot of people have provided their name list and she may need to try hard. So she came back with an illegal channel that cost her 30,000 THB + 500,000 MMK. 

When she arrived back in Thailand, she went and sit for an interview at TGM again as a walk-in in the 1st week of Jul 2022. And she also has passed  the sewing test by AAMT already as she can sew and she has worked there for 3 years already in TGM. When she contacted the interpreter after 3 days from the interview, the interpreter told her that they cannot hire her anymore as her cancellation letter has expired already.

The client said, there used to be a lot of workers who have signed out for like 1 year and more than one year and they can rejoin back easily. For her, she thought that the business just left her sign-out for a while like other workers too as she hasn't submitted any resignation letter and got the cancellation letter.  But now, the business has submitted the cancellation letter and she doesn't know anything.

On the other hand, if they do like this, the interpreter shouldn't recommend her to come back by illegal channel and apply for the job. Now, it has cost her a lot and they didn't take any responsibility back.

She wants to report this to business and she is wondering if the business can provide her second chance as the government allows the undocumented workers to do registration now. Even if she has to wait, she will wait.

She said that, if the business did not accept her, it's ok. She and her husband, who is currently working in TGM, will have to leave the job and go and walk in another place. 
She assumed that the interpreter was helping other workers to get the registration, but, for her, she cannot understand why they treated her like that. She thought it might be the reason as her husband didn't get along with the interpreter.
call_details.next_steps: Have to prepare the talking point to discuss with business.

remediation_notes: The worker reported that the business informed eight workers that their work permits would not be extended and their last day would be May 24, 2020. These workers, who joined the company in October 2018 as Walk-In MOU workers, were reportedly promised 30,000 Baht in severance pay and a cancellation letter around June. However, since their visas and work permits expire on June 5, they fear it's impossible to find a new employer. They seek Issara's help to negotiate with the business and address this poor company policy and communication.
remediation_action: Issara Institute conducted a remediation call with the supplier to discuss the company’s recent decision to lay off eight migrant workers for KPIs #xxx, xxx and xxxx. Here are the findings of the discussion: - The company called the eight workers to a meeting to inform them of the company’s decisions not to extend their contracts and carry out the MoU U-turn, which was due to the need to downsize its workforce over decreasing client orders and downward business performances. The workers were given an acknowledgement letter to sign. - Their last day of work is May 24, 2020. The company asked the worker if they want to go back to Myanmar. If so, they will provide transportation for them. The workers said they want to continue staying in Thailand. - The severance pay will be given to the workers on May 23, 2020, with the amount varying based on the period of their employment. The cancellation letter will be provided to workers on June 8th, as the DoE will take time to process it. However, it is still within the 15-day time frame required by law. - The company will likely implement further cuts in their workforce in the future due to its downward business outlook. However, they are currently unsure how many workers will be laid off and when. This depends on whether the company can finalize the pending orders with the clients in the upcoming months or not. The criteria for choosing which workers to let go is based on their work performance and skills. - The workers expressed concerns over not being able to find new jobs in time before their work permit expires. This might be because the workers are not yet aware of the 60-day grace period, which starts after their last day of work at the company and during which they can stay in Thailand to look for new employers with the cancellation letters. In this regard, the business will inform the workers of this grace period this week to help address and alleviate their concern. - Regarding the potential future lay-offs, the company will try to inform the workers as soon as possible, but it depends on the trends of client orders. In any case, they will include and reiterate the 60-day grace period policy in their communications to laid off workers in the future.
remediation_validation: Issara has communicated back to the workers why the business cannot make an announcement to the entire factory about adjusting their workforce demands. However, the business is willing to provide a job change letter if workers wish to change jobs in advance of termination and the workers are now aware that they have 60-days grace period to look for another jobs. Overall, the workers understand the situation now and are aware that the business is ready to support them with a job change letter and they have 60 days to find a new job as well. Plus the business will be providing them with severance pay. Issara is accordingly closing this case.
remediation_results: Workers raised this issue in the first place as they were not aware that they have 60-days grace period to find a new job and the business will also provide them with a job change cancellation letter and severance pay. They are satisfied with the outcome and Issara is accordingly closing this case.

description: Physical and/or other serious abuse by line supervisor/mgt (illegal)
remediation_notes: Line Manager from S4 (Malaysian Citizen) is abusing her authority and threathen workers for reporting issues to Issara taht has led to investigation against her. She had workers in her production line met with her group by group and blamed them for launching report to Issara and also checked the phone of the workers. She also targetted migrant workers for reporting about her bad behaviour to Issara, transferred one burmese line leader to the other site as she did not corperate with her when she asked her to check the phone of other burmese workers who reported to Issara. She also warned a few other workers that they would be transferred to the other site, and on Sep 5th, almost all burmese workers are not given overtime hence, workers have concern over her action.
remediation_action:
Business is now aware of the situation and planning to talk to senior management and production manager to reinstate the line leader and to also stop all the abusive behaviour and actions. HR also shared with Issara that there have been previous report of her mistreatment to workers. HR will continue with their investigation and aim to have the investigation report by next week which will be shared with Issara and discuss the action steps. On 10 Sep, business started the investigation with 20 workers however, workers shared their views that majority of the selected workers are not the ones who dare to speak. It was suggested that business to have more inclusive channels that allow any workers to report anonymously. Business shared the company grievance channel that workers can report anonamously by using the QR code. 

The business is conducting investigation and there have been issues with the Line Manager threathening the workers, abuse of authority by moving one burmese line leader to the other site and not providing overtime. As the situation is getting worse, new KPIs have been added and the case has been escalated to level 3. Business will complete the investigation on 19th Sep, and will take all the necessary action to have fair and smooth investigation. On 22nd Sep, business informed Issara that the abusive Line Manager was terminated, and the line supervisor got the warning. The termination will prevent the line supervisor from abuse the power.
remediation_validation: Workers shared that they are very happy with the action taken by the business and have gained confidence to launch the issues in the future.
remediation_results: The case is close as workers confirmed that they are very happy with the action taken by the business and have gained confidence to launch the issues in the future.

remediation_notes: The workers in the descaling line were being yelled at on a regular basis by their line supervisor, who used abusive names and put a lot of pressure on them to work faster and meet targets. The workers observed that other line supervisors are not as mean as theirs. After some struggles with being able to access the internal grievance mechanism, they finally were able to lodge their grievance but the issue was not fully addressed to their satisfaction.
remediation_action: The HR focal assigned as the grievance focal for these workers heard their complaint and said they would investigate. They did not tell the workers what to expect or if they would be kept updated.
remediation_validation: On the one hand, the workers are glad that they are no longer getting yelled intensely. On the other hand, they say they do not feel good about lodging a complaint then never being told what was done or what to expect. They also felt like it took a long time to solve the problem.
remediation_results: The workers never heard back from HR, but starting last Monday they had a new line supervisor and saw/heard that their old line supervisor had been assigned to another line. The workers think that the 2 line supervisors were just switched. Their new line supervisor does not yell at them or berate them.

description: Lack of access to safe and credible grievance mechanism
closed_notes: It took almost 2 months to address the situation even when the line was clear
remediation_notes: Workers in the descaling line reported that they have been getting really frustrated and worn down by the frequent verbal barraging from their line supervisor, who is constantly putting pressure on them to work faster. A couple of the workers got together to try to talk to HR but were spotted by the line supervisor and they felt intimidated to go. They know of no other way to contact HR because such information is not posted anywhere.
remediation_action: When this was reported to HR, they quickly responded that the HR grievance mechanism focal points have been shared with all workers before. We asked where workers could find this information so that they could contact their focal, and after some back and forth it was acknowledged that updated grievance focals were not posted anywhere in the factory currently - so HR said they would do it within 7 days but they would not tell us who it is so we could not pass the information back to the workers.
remediation_validation: Workers reported that they saw an updated grievance mechanism focals chart posted in the canteen this past week. They tried contacting the focal and confirmed that they were able to have a conversation with them about their line supervisor.
remediation_results: HR posted the grievance mechanism focals info in the canteen, a few weeks later than originally proposed. The grievance mechanism focals did receive the grievance from some of the line worker representatives.

call_details.description:
Client called and reported about being discriminated against and targeted by the line supervisor. Client reported that all the Burmese workers in MDL (Simple Line),  including he and his sister, were being sent to another line (MTM line) in MCL before Songkran.  Yesterday,  P'Kan Chana asked about half of the Burmese workers to go back and work in MDL (Simple Line), their original line. Here, the informant, the translator and his sister who was being promoted as garment technician, wearing a pink apron, were not asked to go back to their original line. Actually, they both have their task in their working line. But, P'Kan Channa is asking other Thai workers and teaching them how to handle their points. And then she just let the translator and his sister to assist to MTM line as regular sewing workers. 

The translator added that she just did it deliberately as a punishment for them as he used to talk back to her if she treated other Burmese workers in an unprofessional way. If there is nothing to do with their points in their original line, it's acceptable. But now, they have the work to do in their points and she doesn't allow them to go back and teach other workers instead of them is unacceptable. Then he confronted P'Kan Chana directly and asked her why she did this. P'Kan Chana told him that she can do it as a manager as she wished. All the workers are entitled to work in different areas as far as the manager assigned. Then they debated and they both went to the HR office. 

When they arrived at the HR office, they didn't meet with K'Sahasa. They met with another HR officer, who looks like Chinese lady with short hair around the shoulder. In the meeting, he raised that, if the manager is mocking the workers, staring the workers with degrading looks when they did something wrong, shouting or scolding them in front of the crowd, is it ethical or acceptable as a manager? Then this HR said yes, she has the right to do so. Then he asked if the manager has the right to ask them to go and support another line as he used to work as the translator and her sister used to work as garment technician, HR said yes, she also has the right to do as a manager to allocate human resources based on workload. Then he explained how P'Kan Chana replaced other Thai workers and taught them with their points they used to work, she replied the workers that it is concerned with the factory requirement and they should go and meet with K'Tant, Branch Manager in MCL who will handle this. The translator replied that if no one from HR will be involved, he will not meet with him directly. If HR does not solve this, he will report to Issara. Then HR told him  they will call and discuss that again in the afternoon. They will give him a call when HR is ready. But, yesterday, he waited the whole evening and nobody called him. Although he called Ko Moe Aung, Burmese translator in the HR office, he didn't hold the call. So he was disappointed and he didn't go and meet HR again. He also would like to raise the behavior of HR. In his opinion, HR should neglect workers' voices like this. He expected Issara to solve this too.
call_details.referral_notes: Provide him information that his update will be escalate to the ILM team and will get back to him for the update
call_details.next_steps: Have to Update ILM Team

P'Kanchana also took the pink apron of her sister and gave it to another Thai worker without letting his sister know about that. Yesterday, the translator took leave and P'Kanchana was meeting with those workers, her sisters and 4 workers who still left in MTM. She told her sister that sorry for not letting you know that I took your shirt and gave it to another worker. She also says that as you do not quite understand Thai, it is not convenient for you to handle the technician position. Actually, his sister had to take the test to get this position and officially promoted her as technician (wearing a pink apron) one year ago. She has also to sign a document as acknowledgement of getting promotion. He disappointed the supervisor because she is so childish for doing like that with the excuse that she dislikes him. The supervisor also went and talked to his colleagues that she will consider visa and work permit extension for her sister only and not him.

call_details.description:
Clients call and report about the abusive line supervisor behavior.

The client name is  Ms.Phyu Thazin, ID:903853 and she is working in the line no.of 303 (Before known as 118) managed by Green Line supervisor, P'Ar-Bar.  She has the issue with line supervisor P'Ar-Bar and the garment technician P' Ja-Nar wearing a pink apron. 
She and another one worker, are assigned the task of attaching the part of the waist belt and belt loop of the pants. These kinds of points need a lot of patience as the sewer needs to make sure the loops  and pants pockets (originally attached by the former assigned worker) are aligned with each other. The supervisors blamed the workers that some sewing pieces are not qualified although these sewing pieces haven't passed QC yet. The workers tried to explain to her that it was not only her fault but also depend on the former focal assigned tasks who have attached the pant pockets and the lace of the belt. So based on their attachment, they are trying to attach the belt loops. But, she didn't accept that and she just blamed them. Even the technician, P'Jar-Nar, herself,  took around 10-15 min per piece.  And she also has the issue with this point and has to unstitch and restitch too. She finds the problem of the workers when the worker made a mistake and has to unstitch and correct it. They asked the workers to do 15 pieces per hour and they also had to try to reach the target. The workers try their best, and they are not going to the toilet and drink and try to focus on the target.  But it's been everyday they came to the workers and told them to do quickly and maintain the quality since this order started. Two days ago,  they found three sewing pieces of QC failed by the workers and they came and blamed the workers again. Then the workers went to the HR office two times and they requested the translator Ko Moe Aung to come and solve the problem. Ko Moe Aung said he is busy and he asked them to solve it with another translator in the line. When they were trying to find the translator in the production line, the supervisor P'Ar-Bar and P'Jar-Nar, told them that you don't need to do that anymore.  And then they called out Ms.Phyu Thazin and took her to another line no.302, in the same PU. At that line, they also met the new line supervisor (the worker doesn't know the name) and P'Kwan (Chief supervisor). P'Jar-Nar reported to the new line supervisor and chief supervisor that the worker can not sew qualified points and please take care of her by showing the sewing piece which was returned from QC. Although Ms. Phyu Thazin would like to show what was originally wrong with those pieces, the P'Jar-Nar is not letting her touch those pieces. 

Although Ms.Phyu Thazin was sent to a different line and it was in the same PU, P'Jar-Nar still comes and reminds the client to please take care of quality. And other new supervisors also keep monitoring with the client all the time. Yesterday, O&E suggested to the worker if she can find another friend who can speak Thai and go to the HR office again, she said she will try. But, on the other hand, as she was keeping an eye on all the times, she was not able to find friends.
She requested Issara if Issara can help her discuss with the HR/ business to change her to another PU, as P'Ja-Nar and her new supervisor keep monitoring her all the time as a criminal. She felt unhappy and uncomfortable about the way they treated her and not giving her the opportunity to solve them. (Now, her friend who was left in the original line told her that the supervisor now assigned three persons to handle the points that they used to handle by only two people before.) She agreed to present her name and ID.
call_details.next_steps: Have to send alert email to ILM team.

On the other hand, as many workers are quitting the job and the business is just in the process of hiring new workers, the number of workers is less than before. description: Very late or missing payments
remediation_notes: Multiple workers in the deveining line are reporting that they have not received any of their OT payments since June and the payments have not appeared on their payslip. When they asked their line supervisor about it, the line supervisor said she would look into it so to not worry about it and to not go to HR (in an intimidating way). They feel worried to ask multiple times and also worried to go to HR.
remediation_action: Upon reporting the issue to the HR focal, they agreed to investigate the matter and noted they would get back to us within 7 days. remediation_validation: HR reassigned the deveining line supervisor to another building, it seems with no disciplinary action. They also spoke with the workers to understand their expected remediation and said they would make an adjustment in their next pay.
remediation_results: Workers reported that the correction to their pay just appeared in their pay received yesterday.

description: Unfair dismissal
remediation_notes: A group of workers who were awaiting the extension of their MOU contracts were waiting to hear how it would get done in time, since they knew their documents were close to expiring. They had given their passports to HR in June and had expected to have to get them processed in Myawaddy that month before the bridge was bombed. They did not hear what was going to be done instead, until today when they were told they were dismissed and were asked to sign a paper in Thai that they did not understand.
remediation_action: We are trying to get in touch with HR and are awaiting their return call. This case is highly time sensitive given that some of the workers with less than 1 year factory experience will fall into an undocumented status within 15 days of visa/WP cancellation.

remediation_issara_recommendation:
Case summary: The worker reported that he and 6 more friends were recruited to work at a garment factory, however when they arrived to Thailand they were placed in a different workplace for an ice company. The location of the company was also in a different province from  what they were told.


The organization has contacted MOEAF (Myanmar Recruitment Agencies Association) to report the case and remediate between the workers and the responsible reruitment agency. The recommendations provided are for the recruitment agency to place workers in the job they were promised or offer compensation and relocation to another employer if agreed by the workers.
systems_change_issara_recommendation: Recommend the recruitment agency to improve their recruitment procedures and plans to make sure workers are placed in the employer they are  promised and with the one they signed the MOU contract. The recruitment agency is recommended to attend Issara Academy trainings on Ethical Recruitment and to collaborate with CSOs in origin and destination countrie for monitoring of the recruitment process and empowerment of the workers. Additionally the recruitment agency shall revise the service agreement with the employer and comply with MOEAF code of conduct.
systems_change_business_steps_taken: The recruitment agency and workers have come to an agreement that the agency will find a new employer and workers will receive compensation and decide if they agree or not with the new employment.
next_description: To follow up with MOEAF, the recruitment agency and the workers to share updates on their case.

remediation_action: The business is now investigating this matter at this working line as well as other working lines. The HR will work with the production and finance department to make sure workers payment is not impacted by any scanner malfuntion.

description: Denial of benefits to pregnant workers
remediation_notes: Two pregnant workers has called Issara seeking for support to get necessary document to apply for social security benefits. They have requested the documents from the business to the interpreter, however, the interpreter told the workers they need to do everything by themselves and that the business will not provide any documents or support.
remediation_action: After discussing this matter with the business, the HR explained to Issara that the interpreter response was against the company policy, as the business provides necessary documents to pregnant workers as well as provide guidance on how to apply to maternity benefits with the social security fund. The business will provide training to the interpreter and make a verbal warning if necessary after conducting the investigation. The HR team will reachout to the workers to assist them as needed.
remediation_validation: Issara has notified the workers about the business response and the workers has been encourage to update Issara if there are further concerns or if there are any issues with the process of applying for the maternity benefits. The workers have replied that they will inform Issara once they receive the documents and support from the business.
next_description: - Next steps is Angga to follow up the workers and confirm the update provided by the employer.
